annotation.summary: Single-member domain wrapping mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/find-up: findUp(startDir, marker) walks parent directories via fs.existsSync checks until a marker file/dir is found, or returns null at the filesystem root.
assumptions: Single member: lib/find-up.mjs.
marker is a relative path joined onto each candidate ancestor directory; the caller supplies it, there is no hardcoded marker list.
Never throws.

sideEffects.description: fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, marker)) checked against each ancestor directory

risks: Wrong startDir yields false-negative marker discovery in nested layouts.
patterns: Small ancestor-walk helper shared across harness lib modules (graph/planner.mjs, repovine.mjs).
invariants: Deterministic given startDir and marker.
Walk terminates at the filesystem root, returning null if no ancestor matches.
extensionPoints: Callers pass whatever marker they need ('.git', a CLI-relative path); no change to find-up.mjs itself is needed to support a new marker.

fs domain (4 modules): deterministic serialization for .repovine/ cache files. mod:repovine/src/fs/keyed-json writes one sorted-by-key line per entry (mirrors the annotations file layout, so a changed entry is a one-line diff); mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic does write-to-temp + rename; mod:repovine/src/fs/containment checks path-safety; mod:repovine/src/fs/read-dir-sorted gives deterministic directory listing order.
assumptions: Member modules: keyed-json (line-per-entry sorted map), atomic (write-to-temp + rename), containment (path-safety checks), read-dir-sorted (deterministic readdir order).
Serialization order is always key-sorted, making diffs minimal and reproducible across machines.

sideEffects.description: Atomic file writes with tmp-then-rename to .repovine/ cache.

invariants: Entry keys are always sorted before serialization, so identical input produces byte-identical output regardless of insertion order.
Atomic writes guarantee no partial file states visible to concurrent readers.
All serialization is deterministic; no timestamps or random ordering.
read-dir-sorted forces filesystem-collation-independent ordering so scans are reproducible across OS/FS.
extensionPoints: New cache formats add keyed-json serializer and atomic write wrapper.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/fs/keyed-json (line-per-entry format); mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic (write-then-rename); mod:repovine/src/fs/read-dir-sorted; used by annotations/store and .repovine cache producers.
annotation.dataFlow: Object → keyed-json (sorted keys) → tmp file → atomic rename to .repovine/ path.

Domain label collapsing two unrelated 'graph' concepts: repovine's own RepositoryGraph, built in stage2 from stage1 facts, and the harness demo's LangGraph-based orchestrator graph under repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo. A scoped query must pick one by module path.
assumptions: repovine's RepositoryGraph is built in stage2 from stage1 facts.
The harness LangGraph half lives under repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph: it compiles agent-turn node functions into a runnable orchestrator, unrelated to repovine's own graph model.
Import/call edges are advisory — verify with inspect_node.

sideEffects.description: applyValidated mutates in-memory RepositoryGraph during interpreter compose

risks: Reading this domain as one subject is a mistake: a query scoped to it returns two unrelated codebases. Narrow to mod:repovine/src/graph or to repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph depending on which graph is meant.
Incomplete call-graph metadata understates dynamic coupling.
Hub tagging uses an adaptive in-degree threshold that varies by repo size.
patterns: Graph rebuild on refresh_context — agents must refresh after code edits.
invariants: getImpact and forwardImportClosure power dependency and investigate tools.
Node ids use mod:/export:/domain:/resource: prefixes.
extensionPoints: New edge kinds extend mod:repovine/src/graph linking and delta application.
annotation.integrationPoints: repovine graph model: mod:repovine/src/graph, mod:repovine/src/graph/delta, mod:repovine/src/stage2 linking. Harness orchestration: mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow and the domain:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/graph roll-up.
annotation.dataFlow: RepositoryFactsSnapshot → composeRepositoryGraph → graph query utilities → MCP handlers.

annotation.summary: Entry-script domain (5 modules, package repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo): the three channel entries onto the compiled graph — one-shot CLI, long-running HTTP, messaging bot — plus the host-side attach launcher that validates a target worktree before any container starts. The entries are thin: preflight, compile the graph once, hand off.
assumptions: Every channel runs the same compiled graph; the channel decides how a request arrives and how a reply leaves, never what the run does.
Preflight happens before anything binds or spawns, so a misconfigured run fails at startup rather than part way through.
Only real workers run on these paths; without credentials the worker reports blocked and the graph still validates and reports it.
risks: Credentials are exercised only when a worker starts, so every entry passes preflight and fails part way into a run when a provider is misconfigured.
The exit status groups unrelated preflight failures under shared codes, so only the logged line identifies which check failed.
invariants: The compiled graph is built exactly once per process.
The attach launcher makes no Docker call before every check passes, and preflight alone creates nothing.
The exit status carries the outcome, so a pipeline can gate on it without parsing output.
extensionPoints: A new channel adds an entry script and an adapter; the graph and the protocol contract stay untouched.
annotation.integrationPoints: All three channels call invokeGraph from mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow; the attach launcher pairs with the attach compose profiles and mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/target-repo.

annotation.summary: Provider-worker domain (11 modules, package repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo): the adapters that actually run an agent turn, plus the shared wiring they all need. Two provider families — the Claude SDK path and the local OpenAI-compatible path — each with a task adapter and a read-only ask adapter, over common auth, prompt composition, engine MCP wiring, usage accounting and MCP telemetry.
assumptions: A task worker and its ask counterpart share the provider but not the tool surface: the ask path runs a reduced, non-mutating set.
Prompt composition is provider-agnostic; the same policy text and result-shape contract reach every adapter.
The engine is reached as an MCP child, wired identically for every adapter through the shared descriptor builder.
risks: Read-only enforcement rests on enumerated tool lists rather than a property of the tools, so a newly added mutating engine tool is excluded until someone names it, and a permitted name that gains a mutating mode passes under its existing name.
The two provider families duplicate the turn loop shape, so a fix in one adapter does not reach the other.
invariants: Every adapter exposes the same runAgent seam, which is what lets the orchestrator pick one by provider name without knowing the family.
The ask adapters never return a protocol run result; they return answer text.
Usage is accounted per attempt and summed across retries rather than taken from the last one.
extensionPoints: A new provider adds one task adapter and one ask adapter behind the shared runAgent seam, plus a name in the worker selector.
annotation.integrationPoints: Selected by mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/model-role and invoked from the graph orchestrator; the engine MCP descriptor comes from mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/workers/mcp.

extensionPoints: New handoff template sections require prompt and telemetry formatter updates together.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by lib/graph/sub-agent.mjs (buildInterSubAgentTaskSection, finalizeHandoff, contractHandoffViolations); structure guarded by test/handoff-ssot.test.mjs.

All harness app services share egress-gw network namespace and depend on its healthcheck.

Multi-stage build separates repovine compile from slim runtime.

Additional runtime edge contributors for new infra resource kinds.

annotation.summary: Single-member domain (src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs.ts): the delivery half of the investigate-tag system — ranks and caps which inspection references carry a tag (risk > boundary > effect > wiring/hub/co-change per INVESTIGATE_PRIORITY), leaving detection to the mechanics registry.
assumptions: Two channels feed one shared cap: structural (direct imports/children, no guard) and pointer-derived (from the node's own integrationPoints prose, kept only when dependsOn confirms real dependency).
Hub threshold (computeHubInDegreeThreshold) is an adaptive p95 import in-degree with an absolute floor, computed once per build.
A pointer naming a node absent from the graph is dropped silently — a renamed target loses its flag with no report.
risks: Topology-edge tags (wiring/co-change) are capped by collection order, not signal strength, so a reference can lose its tag for its position in the response.
The direction guard (dependsOn) only applies when the caller supplies it; a caller that omits it gets tags in both directions.
patterns: Detection and delivery are separated: a new investigate reason means a new mechanic in the registry, while how much reaches the reader is decided in this one module.
Both channels are ranked together and truncated once, so the response has a single noise budget rather than one per source.
invariants: MAX_INVESTIGATE_REFS and MAX_INVESTIGATE_TAGS_PER_REF cap per response; MAX_HUB_REFS/MAX_WIRING_REFS/MAX_CO_CHANGE_REFS cap per tag.
Ties in rank resolve to the structural channel, which is collected first.
INVESTIGATE_PRIORITY ordering is sourced from the mechanics registry, so priority is defined once.
extensionPoints: New InvestigateTag values require updates to the registry (mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry) plus the ranking/caps here.
annotation.integrationPoints: Detection predicates and the hub floor come from mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry and mod:repovine/src/mechanics/types; pointer prose parsing from mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links; response shape from mod:repovine/src/graph/node-view; called by the inspect_node handler.
annotation.dataFlow: response references + the node's own annotation -> per-target mechanic detection -> per-reference tag cap by strength -> pointers filtered by the dependency guard -> one ranked truncation across both channels -> advisory tags trimmed to their caps.

annotation.summary: k8s-workload domain (1 module): mod:@repovine/plugin-iac-kubernetes/src/k8s-workload enriches Kubernetes workload (Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet/CronJob/Job) and Ingress manifests with runtime-link attributes via enrichK8sResourceAttributes — container env/image, secret/configMap refs, probe paths, ingress backend services.

list-tsconfig-files domain (1 module): mod:@repovine/plugin-source-typescript/src/list-tsconfig-files parses a package's tsconfig.json (plus followed project references) into resolved fileNames/compilerOptions via parsePackageTsConfig, supplementing an entry-only file list with a src/ directory walk.

Single-module domain wrapping mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/llm: askLLM, a lightweight completion seam used only by the planner (not the coding-agent sub-agents), dispatching to askClaude (Claude Agent SDK, tools/MCP disabled) or askLocal (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) by provider.
assumptions: Gated through the same resolveAuth check the workers use, so there is no silent spend.
Any provider failure returns { ok:false, reason }, and the caller falls back to the deterministic heuristic planner.
Default timeout comes from PLANNER_TIMEOUT_MS (fallback 90000ms); a caller-supplied timeoutMs overrides it per call.

sideEffects.description: invokes @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() for the claude provider
POST fetch to {LOCAL_BASE_URL}/chat/completions for the local provider

risks: Both providers swallow every failure into { ok:false, reason }; a caller that doesn't check .ok silently loses LLM planning and falls through to the heuristic planner without an explicit signal.
patterns: Thin shared LLM call wrapper over provider-specific ask modules (askClaude, askLocal).
annotation.flowDescription: Cheap single-turn completions for JSON plan generation only — not used by coding sub-agents.
invariants: Provider failures never throw — they resolve to { ok:false, reason } so the planner can fall back.
extensionPoints: Add a provider branch inside askLLM to extend beyond claude/local.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imports lib/workers/auth, lib/model-role, lib/workers/local-config, lib/num; used by the planner's LLM-assisted plan generation path.
annotation.dataFlow: prompt + options -> provider switch -> askClaude or askLocal -> { ok:true, text } or { ok:false, reason } returned to the planner.

annotation.summary: Path-domain for lib/log.mjs: two stderr logging helpers, logLine and logBullet, with an optional ISO timestamp prefix and configurable indent/scope, gated by an enabled flag.
assumptions: Single member: lib/log.mjs.
HARNESS_LOG_TIMESTAMPS controls the ISO timestamp prefix; timestamps are on by default, disabled only when the var is exactly '0'.
Always writes to stderr (or an overridden stream), never MCP stdout.

sideEffects.description: writes formatted log lines to process.stderr (or an overridden stream)

risks: Verbose logging in production compose can leak assignment details.
patterns: Central logging helper shared across harness lib modules for console diagnostics.
invariants: Must never write logs to stdout in MCP subprocess contexts.
extensionPoints: Add log levels or redaction helpers for new secret patterns.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used across lib/roles-catalog.mjs, lib/sandbox-procs.mjs, lib/runtime-check.mjs, lib/claude-agent.mjs, lib/channels/http-adapter.mjs, lib/channels/telegram-adapter.mjs, lib/workers/* and lib/graph/* modules.
annotation.dataFlow: logLine/logBullet(scope|message, opts) -> optional timestamp prefix + indent -> stream.write per newline-split line.

trace_flow empty results include traceFlowEmptyDiagnostic, not silent success.

False service edges from config-only matches mislead trace_flow.

trace_flow depth and pagination caps bound response size.
Architecture detectors may consume entrypoint hints when configured.

Pagination defaults for new list tools in response/pagination.

annotation.summary: mechanics domain (2 modules): mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry and mod:repovine/src/mechanics/types — the single declaration of which risk-delivery mechanics exist, in what priority, which primitive each reads, and what tag it emits. Every consumer resolves priority from here rather than restating it.
assumptions: Detection predicates are composed from the annotation-format and side-effect vocabularies rather than reimplemented in the registry.
Annotation-derived detection is referenced from the modules that own it; topology-derived detection is declared in the registry itself.
A mechanic whose required primitive is absent self-gates to false rather than defaulting, so a caller that cannot supply a primitive loses that tag rather than getting a guess.
risks: Detection is all the registry currently dispatches: the channel and direction metadata is descriptive, and the delivery machinery does not yet route through it.
The consumer mechanic emits a tag under a different name than its own, an inherited skew visible in API responses.
invariants: Array order is the tag priority, pinned by a unit test so a reorder fails loudly instead of silently changing precedence across every delivery channel.
One mechanic is reserved: its detection always returns false and no channel produces it.
extensionPoints: A new mechanic adds a registry entry with its primitive, tag and priority position; consumers pick it up without change.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry; mod:repovine/src/mechanics/types; consumed by mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs for reference tagging and by mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/inspect-node for the attention block.

annotation.summary: Delivery Protocol harness demo package (64 members: 61 modules + 3 subdomains). Runs multi-agent Claude Code / LangGraph sessions end to end: lib/graph/* (multi, nodes, sub-agent, repovine-process, planner, workflow, plan, retry, test-floor, worktree, workspace-state, workspace-revision, sessions, state, annotation-obligations, artifact-floor) orchestrates the LangGraph run; lib/workers/* (ask-claude, ask-local, local, claude, mcp, mcp-telemetry, auth, prompt, ask-prompt, usage, local-config, claude-config) drive individual agent workers; scripts/* and lib/channels/* (see domain:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/scripts) expose HTTP/Telegram/CLI entrypoints; and lib/{delivery,assignment,harness-run,repovine,handoff-loader,roles-catalog,target-repo,model-role,attach-guard,blockers,telemetry,log,sandbox-procs,env-file,find-up,harness-paths,num,task-user,runtime-check,llm,claude-agent,agents,ask} implement Delivery Protocol assignment/verification state, telemetry, and harness process management; docker/egress-gw/proxy is the sandboxed network egress proxy for the demo.
assumptions: Package name is repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo (not the older repovine-agent-harness-demo); its protocol is the Delivery Protocol (not "Agent Protocol").
annotation.integrationPoints: lib/graph/workflow is the LangGraph entrypoint scripts/* wire channel adapters into; lib/delivery + lib/assignment implement the AgentAssignment/AgentRunResult contract the parent repovine repo's Delivery Protocol docs describe.

annotation.summary: Feature domain for the demo harness's LangGraph orchestrator (16 tagged modules under lib/graph/* plus its close collaborators lib/llm, lib/telemetry and lib/workers): compiles and runs the intake -> plan -> sub-agent -> compliance -> runtime_check -> reply StateGraph (lib/graph/workflow, /nodes, /multi, /planner, /plan, /sub-agent, /retry, /state, /workspace-state, /worktree, /repovine-process), backed by the LLM provider layer (lib/llm) and dev-session telemetry (lib/telemetry).
assumptions: 16 tagged modules; membership spans the lib/graph/* directory plus lib/llm, lib/telemetry, lib/workers and lib/workers/prompt, which orchestrator nodes call directly.
This is the harness's own orchestration graph, distinct from repovine's own src/graph/* engine (domain:mcp/graph) despite the shared 'graph' basename.
invariants: The StateGraph is compiled once via lib/graph/workflow buildGraph and reused per task via invokeGraph.
Compliance is enforced by the engine (`repovine delivery compliance`), not by the orchestrator nodes.
extensionPoints: A new orchestration node adds a lib/graph/* module wired into lib/graph/workflow's StateGraph.
annotation.integrationPoints: Compiled by mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow (buildGraph/invokeGraph); CLI, HTTP and messaging entry scripts invoke it per task.

annotation.summary: Delivery Protocol harness demo's entry-point scripts and the channel adapters they load (6 modules): scripts/langgraph-http, scripts/langgraph-tg-bot, and scripts/langgraph-cli are runnable entrypoints for the demo's LangGraph workflow, scripts/attach-launcher attaches to a running harness session, and lib/channels/http-adapter + lib/channels/telegram-adapter provide the HTTP and Telegram transport implementations those scripts wire into lib/graph/workflow.
assumptions: Each script (langgraph-http, langgraph-tg-bot, langgraph-cli) selects a channel adapter and drives lib/graph/workflow end to end.
invariants: Each entry script compiles the graph once and drives it end to end via a selected channel adapter.
Entry scripts verify the repovine CLI (bare `repovine delivery`) before running.
extensionPoints: A new transport channel adds a lib/channels/<name>-adapter module and a scripts/langgraph-<name> entrypoint.
annotation.integrationPoints: Channel adapters plug into mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow; roles/target-repo config comes from lib/roles-catalog and lib/target-repo.

annotation.summary: Feature domain for the demo harness's provider worker adapters (13 tagged modules): per-provider run/config/auth modules for the local CLI provider (lib/workers/local, /local-config, /ask-local) and the Claude provider (lib/claude-agent, lib/workers/claude-config, /ask-claude, /auth), plus the shared dispatch entrypoint (lib/workers index) and prompt builders (lib/workers/prompt, /ask-prompt).
assumptions: 13 tagged modules pair each supported provider with its own config/auth/ask-* worker so run_sub_agent can dispatch by provider without a shared adapter interface file.
Provider credentials and CLI invocation details live per-provider (claude-config/local-config), not centralized.
invariants: run_sub_agent dispatches by provider name through the lib/workers index; each provider owns its config/auth/ask-* modules.
ask-* variants run a reduced, read-only tool surface and return answer text, not a protocol run result.
extensionPoints: A new provider adds its run/config/auth/ask-* modules plus a name in the worker selector.
annotation.integrationPoints: Dispatched from mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/nodes and /multi (run_sub_agent) via the lib/workers index entrypoint.

annotation.summary: Delivery Protocol core path-domain (5 modules): agents/protocol schemas, agents/manifests built-in roles, agents/validation compliance, agents/roles-source project role catalog loader, and agents/change-set git diff helper — backs MCP agent handlers, the `repovine delivery` and `repovine agents` CLI commands, and harness gates.

False compliance failures if graph not refreshed before validation.

Provenance: inspect_node same contextSessionId before module write_annotation.
Hand-editing repovine.annots.json corrupts merge metadata and contentHash freshness.
The queue and coverage answer from one walk, so a node either needs work on both or on neither.
risk-scope-candidates and carrier-link-gaps are advisory-only, never a gate on needsWork or investigate delivery.

sideEffects vocabulary kinds consumed by privileged-client-side-effect detector.
A new annotatable node kind is added to the backlog walk, where its row push and its coverage tally share one entry filter.

Argv routed from mcp/index before MCP stdio server mode.

Breaking `repovine delivery` (or the `repovine agents` utilities) CLI flags breaks harness compliance and orientation runs.

templates/ and onboarding-assets/ projections for client marketplace bundles.
`repovine delivery` subcommands for harness validate-*/compliance/run-brief; `repovine agents` for roles/orient/session-quality (kept in lockstep with DELIVERY_PROTOCOL_CLI_COMMANDS by a law test).

Optional enforcement via repovine.config contextQuality.
risks: Low quality scores warn but do not block write_annotation unless harness enforces.
patterns: In-memory session store with optional .repovine file persistence.

annotation.summary: File-system utilities for repovine (4 modules): deterministic serialization, atomic writes, path-containment checks, and platform-independent directory ordering for cache and state files.
assumptions: These modules provide low-level file I/O primitives for the cache/state layer; consumers must honor atomic-write semantics and sorted-key format.

fs/read-dir-sorted re-exports readDirSorted from @repovine/plugin-sdk so engine callers outside the discovery walk (build fingerprint, threshold groups) read directories in the same order as discovery, not raw host readdir order.

sideEffects.description: Read/write to .repovine/ cache and workspace state.

invariants: All writes are atomic: either fully written or not at all.
Serialized data is deterministically sorted by key, guaranteeing reproducible output.
Path containment checks prevent escape attacks.
Directory listings go through readDirSorted so node/file order does not depend on host filesystem readdir order.
extensionPoints: New cache formats integrate through atomic write and keyed-json serializers.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/fs/keyed-json (serialization); mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic (atomic I/O); mod:repovine/src/fs/containment (path safety); mod:repovine/src/fs/read-dir-sorted (re-export of @repovine/plugin-sdk readDirSorted); consumed by annotations/store, build/state, and MCP refresh flows.
annotation.dataFlow: Object input → keyed-json sorted encoding → atomic tmp/rename → .repovine/ file path; directory reads → readDirSorted → discovery-order-consistent listing.

annotation.summary: Built-in stage-2 semantic interpreters (12 tagged modules): code-structure base graph, infra-runtime-links runtime topology (graph + entrypoints), server-entrypoints backend routes, server-templates. Registered via INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS and stage2/interpreter/bootstrap.
assumptions: INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS stable order with explicit requiresInterpreters on infra-runtime-links.
MCP entrypoint replay order owned by mcp/lib/entrypoints — not interpreter list order.
risks: Missing semanticHints.routes on backend modules reduces server entrypoint coverage.
invariants: code-structure runs before infra-runtime-links.
Entrypoint collectors tag LAYER_ENTRYPOINT_SLOT_KEY for MCP strip/replay.
Interpreter compose runs after RepositoryFactsSnapshot is immutable.
extensionPoints: New built-in interpreter folder under src/interpreters/<name>/ with index plus optional graph/entrypoints.
Community interpreters return GraphDelta via applyValidated with trusted:false.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage2/interpreter/bootstrap; source-plugins semanticHints; stage1/infra infra modules; mcp get_entrypoints and trace_flow; entrypoint-store.
annotation.dataFlow: snapshot → code-structure graph → infra-runtime-links graph+triggers → server-entrypoints/server-templates → entrypoint-store.

annotation.summary: MCP engine subdomain (50 modules): stdio JSON-RPC server, RepovineRuntime graph pipeline, and the full public tool surface (18 tools, including decline_advisory, suggest_domains_config, get_context_session_quality and get_build_status). Handlers delegate to lib/* collectors; IndexBuildController gates tools during cold builds; context-quality sessions score agent MCP usage.

keyExports.mcp/index: stdio JSON-RPC server and CLI argv dispatcher (setup/build/status/doctor/clear/delivery/agents).
keyExports.mcp/tools/decline-advisory: decline_advisory MCP handler for domains-config/carrier-link-gaps advisory suppression.
keyExports.mcp/tools/get-config-surface: get_config_surface MCP handler for env/secret/resource surface.
keyExports.mcp/tools/registry: Tool handler registry (toolHandlers) wired from tool-defs; the complete 18-tool dispatch map.

assumptions: 50 path-tagged modules under src/mcp/: index, context, build-controller, tool-defs, tools/registry, tools/* handlers (18 tools), lib/* collectors, response/* envelope helpers, scope/* navigation, plus the annotations/* and graph/* modules this subdomain pulls in.
Cold graph build returns status:building with retryAfterSec — clients must call get_build_status.

sideEffects.description: stdio MCP server reads/writes JSON-RPC; filesystem via refresh_context and annotation tools

risks: Breaking status:building or retry_after_sec contract breaks IDE agents mid-build.
Large inspect_node includeBody responses can exceed client context budgets.
patterns: Single MCP surface for IDE agents and harness worker subprocesses.

invariants: refresh_context and refreshRepoState are post-edit sync barriers before trusting navigation.
write_annotation and merge_annotations trigger ctx.refreshRepoState after disk writes.
Tool handlers validate input via tool-defs Zod catalog before execution.

extensionPoints: New public tool: add mcp/tools handler plus registry entry plus tool-defs name.
Lib collectors in mcp/lib/* shared by multiple tools.
Navigation refs in concise mode for follow-up calls in same session.
annotation.integrationPoints: RepovineRuntime stage1/stage2 pipeline; AnnotationStore and mcp/lib/annotations; tool-defs Zod catalog; IndexBuildController cold-build gating; context-quality session-store; CLI dispatch to cli/delivery and cli/agents.
annotation.dataFlow: stdio MCP request → toolDefs validation → toolHandlers (refreshRepoState on mutation tools) → lib collectors → concise response envelope.

annotation.summary: repovine package's platform utility module family (3 modules): platform/paths handles cross-platform path normalization, platform/text handles text encoding/line-ending normalization, and platform/ordering provides deterministic sort/collation helpers (e.g. for filesystem-order-independent output).
assumptions: Depended on by graph scanning/build code that must produce the same ordering regardless of OS filesystem readdir order.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by graph/module-files and other build-stage modules needing OS-independent path/ordering behavior.

annotation.summary: repovine package's plugin-host runtime (7 modules): plugin-host/load loads plugin packages, plugin-host/runtime executes them, plugin-host/iac-set and plugin-host/declaration-catalog track the IaC/resource declarations plugins contribute, stage2/projection/compose folds plugin-derived facts into the stage2 projection, graph/model holds the graph node/edge shapes plugins populate, and cli/ui renders CLI progress during plugin load/build.
assumptions: Loaded plugins conform to the @repovine/plugin-sdk contract (plugin/descriptor, source-plugin/types).
extensionPoints: A new plugin package is picked up by plugin-host/load once it satisfies the plugin-sdk descriptor contract; no change needed here for a new plugin implementation.
annotation.integrationPoints: Depends on @repovine/plugin-sdk's src/index, plugin/descriptor, and source-plugin/types for the loaded-plugin contract.

annotation.summary: Response-shaping module family for MCP tool output (5 modules): response/empty-reason builds the emptyDiagnostic explanation on zero-result queries, response/next-call builds navigation/next-step hints, response/provenance backs context-session provenance/quality scoring, response/refusal shapes rejected-write error responses, and response/truncation builds the truncation metadata (shown/total/hint) seen on paginated queue and map_context results.
extensionPoints: A new response shape (e.g. a new diagnostic kind) is added as its own response/<name> module alongside the existing ones.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used across MCP tool handlers (search_context, get_annotation_status, map_context) to shape emptyDiagnostic, navigation, and truncation fields in tool responses.

annotation.summary: Stage-1 repository facts extraction subdomain (14 modules): discovers packages via source plugins, shards extract across worker pool, collects IaC infra modules, emits RepositoryFactsSnapshot for stage-2 graph building.

keyExports.plugin-host/iac-set: IaC parser/loader registry — installIaCPlugins, resolveLoaderForFile, file-claim dispatch by name/extension.
keyExports.stage1/cache: Incremental extract cache keyed by STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION.
keyExports.stage1/infra: collectInfraModules: walks the tree, dispatches each candidate file to the first claiming IaC parser, stamps identity/fingerprint.
keyExports.stage1/worker-pool: Package sharding and worker subprocess pool.

assumptions: STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION gates incremental cache reuse.
scanPatterns from repovine.config.json build.scan threaded to all source plugins and infra collect.

sideEffects.description: Filesystem scan, worker subprocesses, cache writes under .repovine/

risks: Worker OOM on huge unsharded monorepo packages.
Cache invalidation on STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION bump forces full re-extract.
patterns: Silent calibration picks worker count unless REPOVINE_MAX_PACKAGE_WORKERS set.
IaC parsers claim files in registration order; the first claiming parser wins even if it returns nothing.
annotation.flowDescription: discover → dedup/shard → extract → infra (plugin-host/iac-set parser dispatch) → RepositoryFactsSnapshot with linkingConfig.
invariants: Output is RepositoryFactsSnapshot with packages, modules, infraModules, linkingConfig.
Silent worker-count calibration unless REPOVINE_MAX_PACKAGE_WORKERS set.
Built-in plugin failure isolated to affected shard.
extensionPoints: build.scan and maxPackageWorkers in repovine.config.json.
Built-in source plugin registry and plugin-host/iac-set parser registry used by worker shards.
annotation.integrationPoints: source-plugins discover/extract; plugin-host/iac-set infra parsing; mcp/RepovineRuntime snapshot input; cli build progress UI; scan-filters shouldScanSourcePath.
annotation.dataFlow: discover → dedup/shard → extract → IaC (plugin-host/iac-set) → RepositoryFactsSnapshot.

annotation.summary: Stage-2 graph building subdomain (22 modules): turns a RepositoryFactsSnapshot into the served RepositoryGraph via interpreter composition, plugin-contributed projections, domain tagging/classification, and entrypoint slot storage for MCP replay. Composition runs synchronously or offloaded to a worker thread, with plugin-set reload and graph delta/extension bookkeeping crossing that boundary.

keyExports.stage2 (composeRepositoryGraph): Synchronous graph composition from a snapshot: interpreter contributions, pruning, then multi-pass domain tagging/classification.
keyExports.stage2 (composeRepositoryGraphAsync): Runs composition in a worker thread via stage2/worker, falling back to inline composition when the worker is unavailable or fails.
keyExports.stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store: Slotted entrypoint persistence for MCP replay via getInterpreterEntrypoints.

assumptions: Runs after stage1 in refresh_context; domainsConfig loaded once from repovine.domains.json.
Interpreter composition contributes structural/infra edges before domain tagging, since domain passes depend on those edges.

The async path crosses a worker_threads boundary: the worker reloads the plugin set independently and posts entrypoints/refusals back explicitly because their WeakMap/Map sidecars do not survive structured clone.

sideEffects.description: Builds and mutates one in-memory RepositoryGraph through every pass
composeRepositoryGraphAsync offloads composition to a worker isolate, which independently reloads the plugin set

risks: Missing or stale repovine.domains.json leaves modules untagged in map_context.
Silent inline fallback on worker error unless REPOVINE_STAGE2_WORKER_STRICT is set.
Entrypoint slot replay order regressions break get_entrypoints parity.
patterns: Contribute, then prune, then classify: each stage sees a graph the previous finished with.
Runtime infra edges added after base graph nodes exist.
annotation.flowDescription: Stage-2 orchestrator: interpreters enrich the graph first (modules, runtime resources, infra links, entrypoint fragments, plugin-contributed projections), then multi-pass domain tagging and classification mutate the same in-memory RepositoryGraph, synchronously or offloaded to stage2/worker.
invariants: refresh_context rebuilds graph — MCP reads RepovineRuntime copy.
Interpreter composition always precedes domain tagging.
Domain tags applied after code-structure graph exists.
extensionPoints: New interpreter registration through INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS.
repovine.domains.json patterns for tagging and infra excludes.
Plugin-contributed projections via @repovine/plugin-sdk composed alongside built-in interpreters.
annotation.integrationPoints: interpreters code-structure/infra-runtime-links/server-entrypoints/ui-entrypoints; stage2/worker for async offload; plugin-host/load and plugin-host/runtime-store for plugin-set reload; mcp/lib/entrypoints slot replay; analyze_dependencies and trace_flow MCP tools; analysis/architecture detectors.
annotation.dataFlow: facts snapshot → interpreter contributions and entrypoint fragments (sync, or offloaded via stage2/worker) → inert resources pruned → domain/content/propagation/classification/subdomain passes → validation → the served graph.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_DEV: Turns graph-validation problems into a failure instead of a warning
envDependencies.REPOVINE_STAGE2_INLINE: Forces inline composition, skipping the worker
envDependencies.REPOVINE_STAGE2_WORKER_STRICT: Turns an offload failure into a failure instead of an inline fallback
envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Reports per-domain counts and offload availability

annotation.summary: resolve-import domain (1 module): mod:@repovine/plugin-source-python/src/resolve-import resolves Python relative/intra-package/cross-package imports via resolvePythonImport directly against the Pass-1 absPathToId map and discovered PackageInfo list, mirroring the TS plugin's resolve-specifier with no disk reads.

Delegates canonicalization to canonical-json and the hash primitive/width to content-hash.

annotation.summary: Single-member hub domain over lib/graph/retry.mjs (mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/retry). Promoted by connectivity rather than grouping: the module classifies a rejected `repovine delivery compliance` report by diagnostics code (sync-only vs false-claim vs contract-handoff) and folds retry-worthy notes into the next attempt's task text; enough of the orchestration imports it to cross the basename promotion threshold.
assumptions: A one-member domain is the promotion rule working as designed — three or more importers make a basename a domain — not a naming artifact. The grouping value is nil; the signal is that this file is connective.
The content lives on mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/retry; this roll-up adds no facts of its own.
invariants: A blocked worker result is retried only when it reports a provider-transport death or the harness wall-clock kill (per the module's isRetriable); every other blocked or failed result is terminal.
extensionPoints: A new repovine diagnostics code requires a matching update to SYNC_ONLY_CODES/FALSE_CLAIM_CODES in the wrapped module, or it goes unclassified.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/retry, imported by lib/graph/workflow, lib/graph/multi and the sub-agent run loop.

annotation.summary: Single-member hub domain over lib/roles-catalog.mjs (mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/roles-catalog). Promoted by connectivity: the module resolves which agent roles this run may plan and schedule — the bundled specialist catalog in sandbox mode, or the project's committed agents.roles read from the attach launch baseline in attach mode — and every entry script plus the planner reads it.
assumptions: A one-member domain is the promotion rule working as designed — three or more importers make a basename a domain — not a naming artifact. The grouping value is nil; the signal is that this file is connective.
The content lives on mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/roles-catalog; this roll-up adds no facts of its own.
invariants: In attach mode the project role source is read from the launch baseline revision (ATTACH_BASELINE_REF), never the agent-writable working tree; an invalid opted-in role source there aborts startup rather than falling back to the bundled catalog.
extensionPoints: Adding a role requires updating the bundled catalog or the project's committed agents.roles at the attach baseline ref, not the working tree.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/roles-catalog; delegates role-source reads to lib/repovine (projectRoles) and catalog construction to lib/agents (initRoleCatalog). An unregistered role is never planned, which is what makes this the gate on the planner's vocabulary.

annotation.summary: Single-module domain (mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/runtime-check): the post-implementation runtime_check phase — discovers package.json directories, runs `npm install --ignore-scripts` per directory, then runs configured build/test commands via spawnSync in the sandbox with a redacted environment, and extracts a per-workspace failure log tail plus scope hints for automatic fix sub-agents.
assumptions: Single member: lib/runtime-check.mjs.
Runtime checks are enabled unless attach mode forces them off or HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK=0; commands default to `npm run build`/`npm test` unless HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_CMD/_CMDS override them.
Fix sub-agent attempts are optional (HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_FIX) and bounded per failed command (HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_FIX_MAX).

sideEffects.description: spawnSync for npm install --ignore-scripts per package dir and for the configured build/test commands
fs.existsSync/readdirSync to discover package.json directories and detect existing node_modules

risks: runtimeCheckEnv()'s allowlist (HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_*/NPM_CONFIG_*/npm_* prefixes) is the only thing keeping harness secrets out of the sandboxed build/test child process; a new env var under those prefixes carrying a secret-shaped value still leaks through unconditionally.
patterns: Central runtime_check result shape shared by graph nodes, telemetry, and channel summaries.
invariants: Commands run with a redacted environment (SECRET_ENV_RE strips api-key/token/secret/password/credential/oauth/auth/cookie/session-shaped vars) and a configurable timeout (HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS, default 600000ms; a timeout reports exitCode 124).

Attach targets force the check off — installing/building/testing the whole real repo after every task would fail closed under default-deny egress; the operator builds/tests on the host after promotion.
extensionPoints: Add failure classifiers alongside isMissingTestScriptFailure/isExpressParamsTypeFailure for better fix-sub-agent scope derivation.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called from mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/nodes and lib/graph/multi after a worker run; feeds telemetry and channel summary formatters.
annotation.dataFlow: worker result → runRuntimeCheck (npm install → build/test commands) → runtimeCheckPassed/runtimeCheckBlockers → optional fix sub-agent task via buildRuntimeCheckFixTask → telemetry/channel status.

annotation.summary: Single-module domain (mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/sandbox-procs): snapshots and reaps sandbox-attributed child processes, listening ports, and Docker containers after a sub-agent run or on /reset. Linux-only (via /proc), no-ops on other platforms.
assumptions: Single member: lib/sandbox-procs.mjs.
A process counts as this sandbox's when its /proc cwd is under repoRoot or its cmdline mentions repoRoot; a process with a controlling tty (the operator's own shell) is never reaped.
Used by runtime-check and provider tooling that shells out.

sideEffects.description: spawnSync docker (compose down, ps, rm -f) and ss -ltnpH
SIGTERM then SIGKILL (1500ms grace) to sandbox-attributed pids

risks: Containers are daemon-managed, so a process kill alone cannot stop them — teardown depends on `docker compose down`/`rm -f` succeeding against containers new since the sub-agent's baseline.
patterns: Shared snapshot/reconcile/reapAll trio reused by per-sub-agent cleanup (reconcile) and the full /reset sweep (reapAll).
annotation.flowDescription: Sandbox process/port/container hygiene: prevents leaked daemons and containers after a sub-agent's Bash/tool use, or on /reset.
invariants: reconcile diffs a snapshot against the caller's `before` baseline and tears down only what is new since it; reapAll unconditionally sweeps everything sandbox-attributable.
extensionPoints: Attribution and reaping are /proc-based and Linux-only; broader sandbox host support would need a new attribution mechanism.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/runtime-check calls snapshot/reconcile around a sub-agent run; /reset calls reapAll.
annotation.dataFlow: snapshot(before) → sub-agent run → snapshot(after) via reconcile diff → new pids/ports/containers → optional reap (SIGTERM/SIGKILL + docker compose down/rm -f).

annotation.summary: Harness worker adapters (13 members): the Claude SDK loop and the vendor-neutral `local` OpenAI-compatible loop, each with a task adapter and a read-only ask-* variant, over shared auth resolution, prompt composition, the repovine stdio-MCP bridge, and per-run usage/MCP-telemetry rollups.
assumptions: Two provider families remain: Claude via the SDK and `local` via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The earlier cursor and codex adapters were removed.
Workers pass REPOVINE_CONTEXT_SESSION_ID for MCP telemetry correlation.
risks: The broad `workers` path tag obscures the owning package.
Provider sandbox env overrides can weaken compose egress defaults.
Read-only enforcement on the ask-* variants rests on enumerated tool lists, so a newly added mutating tool is unavailable until named.
patterns: Provider adapters share auth, prompt, MCP, normalization modules.
annotation.flowDescription: Cross-cutting cluster for all harness modules touching LLM worker execution, cancellation, and provider adapters.
invariants: Every adapter exposes the same runAgent seam, selected by provider name.
Sub-agent telemetry rows are keyed by role/subAgent for run rollups.
extensionPoints: A new provider adds a task adapter and an ask adapter behind the shared runAgent seam, plus a name in the worker selector.
annotation.integrationPoints: repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo lib/workers; the engine MCP descriptor from lib/workers/mcp; mcp-telemetry metrics aggregation. Overlaps the path-derived domain:graph/workers roll-up.
annotation.dataFlow: invokeGraph → run_worker → provider runAgent → usage rollups → compliance.

annotation.summary: Single-member hub domain over lib/graph/workflow.mjs (mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow). Promoted by connectivity: the module compiles intake/multi_agent/build_assignment/validate_assignment/run_sub_agent/persist_result/validate_result/compliance/runtime_check/compose_reply into a LangGraph StateGraph, and every channel entry script imports it to get a compiled graph.
assumptions: A one-member domain is the promotion rule working as designed — three or more importers make a basename a domain — not a naming artifact. The grouping value is nil; the signal is that this file is connective.
The content lives on mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow; this roll-up adds no facts of its own.
invariants: An intake error never reaches a worker; a multi-agent task routes through the fan-out node straight to the reply; compliance-rejected retries loop back to run_sub_agent bounded by HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES (default one, zero disables).
extensionPoints: A new orchestrator node or route requires a matching update to nodes.mjs/multi.mjs plus the shared retry policy in lib/graph/retry.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow, imported by the CLI, HTTP and messaging entry scripts.

annotation.summary: Single-member hub domain over lib/graph/workspace-state.mjs (mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workspace-state). Promoted by connectivity: the module decides whether the sandbox reads as greenfield (no product source yet) or a continuation, and the planner, the orchestration and the protocol process all import that decision.
assumptions: A one-member domain is the promotion rule working as designed — three or more importers make a basename a domain — not a naming artifact. The grouping value is nil; the signal is that this file is connective.
The content lives on mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workspace-state; this roll-up adds no facts of its own.

Verified against the member module's current fresh annotation: 6-export surface (hasProductSourceMarkers, isGreenfieldSandbox, hasOnlyStubAnnotations, isGreenfieldContext, describeWorkspaceState, PRODUCT_SOURCE_MARKERS) and greenfield-detection role unchanged.
invariants: isGreenfieldContext is true when isGreenfieldSandbox, or when orientTrail.graphNodes is empty AND hasOnlyStubAnnotations — an empty or stub-only repovine.annots.json alone never counts as continuation.
extensionPoints: A new product-source marker requires updating PRODUCT_SOURCE_MARKERS in the wrapped module.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workspace-state, whose boolean reaches compliance enforcement and the run verdict, not planning alone.

annotation.summary: Single-member hub domain over lib/graph/worktree.mjs (mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/worktree). Promoted by connectivity: the module creates and joins the isolated git worktrees a parallel stage runs sub-agents in, and the planner, the channels and the revision-capture code all import it.
assumptions: A one-member domain is the promotion rule working as designed — three or more importers make a basename a domain — not a naming artifact. The grouping value is nil; the signal is that this file is connective.
The content lives on mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/worktree; this roll-up adds no facts of its own.

Verified against the member module's current fresh annotation: 7-export surface (available, ensureGitRepo, addWorktree, commitWorktree, mergeWorktree, removeWorktree, preserveWorktreeArtifacts) and worktree-isolation role unchanged.
invariants: mergeWorktree aborts on any conflict and reports conflict:true to the caller rather than resolving it — a caller that ignores that flag silently drops the sub-agent's work.
extensionPoints: A new sub-agent branch-naming scheme requires updating addWorktree's sub-agent/<role>-<timestamp> template.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/worktree; the fan-out gate that decides whether to use parallel worktrees lives in mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/plan (scheduleStages/applyGreenfieldParallelStages).

annotation.summary: Attach-mode overlay stacked on top of compose.yaml (docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.attach.yaml --profile attach-cli|attach-http|attach-tg-bot ...). cli-attach/http-attach/tg-bot-attach each extend harness-base and mount a pre-created host git worktree at /workspace (HARNESS_ATTACH_WORKTREE) instead of the managed .workspace sandbox, plus per-run state dirs (HARNESS_ATTACH_STATE_DIR) for HOME, the git ledger, and a read-only git-guard bind that shadows the worktree's real .git pointer.
assumptions: HARNESS_ATTACH_WORKTREE and HARNESS_ATTACH_STATE_DIR are required (`${VAR:?}`) and are set by scripts/attach-launcher.mjs, not by the operator directly.
Anchors do not cross compose files, so each service reaches the hardened shape via `extends: {file: compose.yaml, service: harness-base}` rather than a YAML anchor.

sideEffects.description: declares cli-attach/http-attach/tg-bot-attach and unions attach-* profiles onto egress-gw

risks: The .git bind is read-only so the agent cannot repoint the worktree's git dir, but the disposable repo at /state/git it points into is read-write by design (sandbox-parity posture).
annotation.integrationPoints: scripts/attach-launcher.mjs (drives the fail-closed preflight and stacks these two compose files; not part of an npm workspace, so it is not a graphed mod: node)

annotation.summary: Base compose file for the harness demo sandbox. Opt-in profiles (cli/http/tg-bot) share the harness-app anchor (hardened container: read_only rootfs, cap_drop ALL, mem/cpu/pids ceilings) and share egress-gw's network namespace so all traffic passes its default-deny allow-list. workspace-init (profile-gated) chowns the bind-mounted .workspace before the harness starts; egress-gw builds docker/egress-gw and runs the credential-custody proxy that injects the real Anthropic/Telegram secrets; harness-base is an inert never-run skeleton compose.attach.yaml extends from.
assumptions: Every service is opt-in via `profiles:`; a bare `docker compose up` starts nothing.
Host ./.workspace dir must pre-exist (bind create_host_path:false) — scripts/compose.mjs creates it before compose runs.

sideEffects.description: declares services workspace-init, egress-gw, tg-bot, http, cli, harness-base
egress-gw enforces default-deny egress except ALLOW_DOMAINS (default anthropic.com; Telegram opt-in via EGRESS_ALLOW_TELEGRAM)

risks: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/TELEGRAM_API_BASE point the harness container at 127.0.0.1 ports the egress-gw proxy owns; the real secrets never enter the harness container, only proxy-injected placeholders.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/scripts/langgraph-cli, mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/scripts/langgraph-http, mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/scripts/langgraph-tg-bot (cli/http/tg-bot service entrypoints); infra:dockerfile:examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/Dockerfile (harness-app build); infra:dockerfile:examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/docker/egress-gw/Dockerfile (egress-gw build)

annotation.summary: Two-stage harness image build. Builder stage compiles the repovine CLI from source (npm ci across the full packages/ workspace, npm run build, asserts dist/mcp/index.js exists) so the image never depends on a host-built dist/. Runtime stage installs prod deps plus the compiled packages, then the demo package (examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo), copies the full demo tree (lib/agents, lib/rules, lib/handoff baked in as defaults), creates the .workspace mountpoint, sets REPOVINE_CLI, smoke-checks the built CLI (repovine delivery), and drops privileges to the base image's node user.
assumptions: compose.yaml bind-mounts ./lib/agents over the baked-in lib/agents/ at runtime (HARNESS_AGENTS_DIR), so host edits to role briefs apply without a rebuild.
Build context is repovine/ (the repo root), not the example dir — see compose.yaml build.context.

sideEffects.description: RUN npm ci / npm run build in the builder stage; RUN node dist/mcp/index.js delivery as a build-time smoke check
RUN mkdir -p .workspace creates the bind-mount target inside the image

risks: CMD defaults to scripts/langgraph-cli.mjs --help; every compose service overrides entrypoint (cli/http/tg-bot each pick their own script).
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/scripts/langgraph-cli (default CMD entrypoint); resource:generic:examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/Dockerfile (the runtime-resource this build produces).

annotation.summary: Egress allow-list gateway image: Alpine 3.20 plus dnsmasq/ipset/iptables/ip6tables/curl/nodejs, adds an unprivileged `egw` user (uid 65000), copies entrypoint.sh and proxy.mjs. dnsmasq resolves via the configured upstream and tags allow-listed domains' IPs into an ipset; iptables default-denies egress except those IPs (+DNS+lo); proxy.mjs is a loopback origin proxy that terminates HTTP for the harness worker and holds the real Anthropic/Telegram secrets (transparent filter + secret-injecting proxy, fail-closed).
assumptions: The harness container shares this container's network namespace (network_mode: service:egress-gw in compose.yaml), so all harness traffic passes this filter.

sideEffects.description: entrypoint.sh configures dnsmasq+ipset+iptables for default-deny egress with an allow-list

risks: proxy.mjs and entrypoint.sh have no package.json in docker/egress-gw/, so they sit outside the npm/TS module graph; edits there are not tracked as graph modules.

annotation.summary: Built-in IaC plugin for docker-compose / Compose-spec manifests. Registers via definePlugin (@repovine/plugin-sdk) with id 'docker-compose', wires dockerComposeParser as its iac parser, and mounts InfraKind 'docker-compose' onto domain:infra-docker-compose.

keyExports.dockerComposeIacPlugin: The plugin descriptor built by definePlugin (also re-exported as default).

assumptions: Compose-file parsing logic lives in ./parser.ts (dockerComposeParser), not in this file.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:@repovine/plugin-iac-docker-compose/src/parser (dockerComposeParser, the manifest parser this plugin registers)

annotation.summary: IaCParser implementation for Docker Compose files: matches docker-compose*.yml/yaml and compose*.yml/yaml with a top-level `services` map, and parses each service plus secrets (top-level `secrets:` block, `*_FILE`/run/secrets convention, and env_file-synthesized) into InfraResource/InfraEnvRef records, publishing a docker-compose/build@1 fact per service that names a Dockerfile.

keyExports.dockerComposeParser: IaCParser const (kind 'docker-compose'): fileMatch regex, supports() checks services map, parse() returns { kind, resources, facts }.

assumptions: supports() requires the filename to match the compose regex AND the parsed doc to have a record-typed `services` key.
Dockerfile path resolution assumes svc.build is either a string (build context) or a record with context/dockerfile, relative to the compose file's own directory.
risks: BUILD_FACT_SCHEMA ('docker-compose/build@1') is a published fact schema string; renaming it silently breaks any reader keyed to that schema.

annotation.summary: Built-in IaC plugin registering the Dockerfile/Dockerfile.<variant> parser and a build-links projector under InfraKind 'dockerfile'.

keyExports.default: Default export — the same dockerfileIacPlugin value

annotation.summary: IaCParser for Dockerfile/Dockerfile.* files (text loader): matches by basename pattern, extracts the first `FROM` instruction's image reference (tolerating a leading `--platform=` flag) as baseImage, and emits a single 'other'-kind InfraResource identified by the normalized repo-relative path, grouped under a domainPath derived from the containing directory.

keyExports.dockerfileParser: IaCParser const (kind 'dockerfile'): fileMatch on /^Dockerfile(\..*)?$/, supports() requires the text loader's string doc, parse() builds the single resource.

assumptions: supports() requires basename to be exactly 'Dockerfile' or start with 'Dockerfile.', and the loaded doc to be a string (loaderId 'text').
risks: Only the first FROM line's base image is recorded; later FROM stages in a multi-stage Dockerfile are not represented as separate attributes.

annotation.summary: Projection contributor that links any resource naming a container image or a build context to the Dockerfile it was built from, shared by three producer schemas (docker-compose/build@1, kubernetes/object@1, helm/container-image@1) so the image-to-Dockerfile matching logic exists once instead of once per producer plugin.

keyExports.buildLinksProjector: ProjectionContributor (id 'build-links') requiring the image/build schemas; project() reads infraModules(kind:'dockerfile') plus fact records under those schemas and emits a single batch of 'builds-from' link contributions (resource -> module).

assumptions: A fourth producer joins by publishing containerImages/dockerfileRepoRelPath under its own schema and adding that schema to IMAGE_SCHEMAS/BUILD_SCHEMAS — nothing else changes.
An explicit dockerfileRepoRelPath match always wins over image-name token matching (declared build config is never overridden by a guess).
risks: Image-to-Dockerfile matching by path/name tokens returns no link when two non-default-recipe Dockerfiles tie on score — a tie is resolved only when one candidate is the plain 'Dockerfile' of its directory; otherwise the resource is left unlinked rather than guessed.

annotation.summary: Built-in IaC plugin registering Helm chart parsing: helmValuesParser and helmChartParser under InfraKind 'helm', in values-first registration order so values.yaml is matched before the (later-registered) plain k8s manifest parser could claim it.

keyExports.default: Default export — the same helmIacPlugin value
keyExports.helmIacPlugin: definePlugin() descriptor with capabilities.iac.parsers=[helmValuesParser, helmChartParser] and kindDomains for 'helm'

assumptions: Parser registration order matters: values-first ensures values.yaml/values-<env>.yaml aren't misclassified before the Helm plugin's own parsers run.

annotation.summary: IaCParser for Helm Chart.yaml/Chart.yml: supports() requires apiVersion to start with 'v2' and a string `name`, and explicitly rejects docs carrying a `Resources` key (CloudFormation shape) to avoid misclassifying unrelated YAML. parse() emits a single 'helm-release' InfraResource keyed by the chart name (falling back to the containing directory's basename) with version/appVersion/description attributes.

keyExports.helmChartParser: IaCParser const (kind 'helm'): fileMatch on Chart.yaml/Chart.yml, supports()/parse() as described in summary.

assumptions: Chart name defaults to path.basename(path.dirname(absPath)) when the doc omits `name`.
description is truncated to 200 chars via shortenText before being stored as an attribute.

annotation.summary: Helm values.yaml IaC parser: heuristic scan of a chart's values file (no template rendering) for container-image and secret references, emitting synthetic 'generic' InfraResource nodes for images and secrets and publishing a helm/container-image@1 fact naming each image for the Dockerfile-linking projector to resolve.

keyExports.HelmImageRef: { key, repository, tag? } — one collected image reference.
keyExports.HelmSecretRef: { key, secretName } — one collected secret reference.
keyExports.collectHelmImages: Recursively walks a values object collecting `{ image: { repository, tag } }` blocks into HelmImageRef[], keyed by dotted path prefix.
keyExports.collectHelmSecrets: Recursively walks a values object collecting existingSecret/secretName/secretRef string values into HelmSecretRef[].
keyExports.helmValuesParser: IaCParser (kind 'helm'); supports() requires a values*.yaml under a Helm chart dir (not itself a Chart.yaml) containing at least one image or secret reference; parse() builds image/secret InfraResource entries plus helm/container-image@1 facts.

assumptions: Detection is heuristic since chart templates are never rendered; secret detection is deliberately limited to explicit key names (existingSecret/secretName/secretRef) rather than substring heuristics on values, to keep precision high.

sideEffects.description: isUnderHelmChart calls fs.existsSync to check for a sibling Chart.yaml/yml

risks: A secret consumed only through a chart-template-derived name (not a literal existingSecret/secretName/secretRef key in values.yaml) is invisible to this parser, since templates are never rendered.
annotation.integrationPoints: Publishes helm/container-image@1 facts (subjectRef per image resource) that mod:@repovine/plugin-iac-dockerfile/src/projectors/build-links reads to link a resource to the Dockerfile it builds from.

annotation.summary: Built-in IaC plugin for Kubernetes manifests (Deployment, Service, Ingress, CronJob, CRDs); owns InfraKind 'kubernetes' and wires the workloads parser plus the ingress-routes projector through definePlugin.

keyExports.default: Default export, same value as kubernetesIacPlugin.
keyExports.kubernetesIacPlugin: const built via definePlugin({ id: 'kubernetes', capabilities: { projectors: [ingressRoutesProjector], iac: { parsers: [kubernetesParser], kindDomains: [{ kind: 'kubernetes', meta: { domainId: 'domain:infra-k8s', label: 'infra-k8s', ... } }] } } }).

assumptions: kindDomains maps IaC kind 'kubernetes' to domain:infra-k8s so facts from this plugin land in that domain roll-up.
Additional Kubernetes sub-parsers (e.g. Istio CRDs) are expected to be added under parsers/ and appended to the `parsers` array here.

annotation.summary: Enriches Kubernetes IaC resource attributes with runtime-link data from workload manifests (Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet/CronJob/Job) and Ingress: container names/images, env entries (plus secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef as InfraEnvRef), envFrom secret/configMap refs, secret-backed volumes, liveness/readiness HTTP probe paths, and Ingress path-backend service names.

keyExports.enrichK8sResourceAttributes: Entry point: resolves pod spec enrichment for workload kinds via enrichK8sWorkloadPodAttributes, then Ingress backend enrichment via enrichK8sIngressAttributes when doc.kind === 'Ingress'; returns the collected InfraEnvRef[].

assumptions: Pod spec is located at spec.template.spec, with CronJob (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec) and Job (spec.template.spec) as special cases, falling back to spec itself.
Only doc.kind values in WORKLOAD_KINDS (Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet/CronJob/Job) trigger pod-spec enrichment; 'Ingress' triggers the separate ingress path.
risks: Attribute keys (containerImage${i}, envN_NAME, livenessProbe${i}Path, etc.) are container-index-based, so reordering containers in the manifest shifts attribute keys across builds.

annotation.summary: IaCParser for Kubernetes manifests (any .yaml/.yml with both apiVersion and kind, explicitly rejecting CloudFormation/SAM-shaped docs via a `Resources` object or string `Transform` key). Maps the manifest's `kind` through k8sKindMap to a coarse InfraResourceKind (unmapped kinds default to 'k8s-crd'), builds identity as k8s/{namespace|_}/{kind}/{name} via k8sIdentity, delegates to enrichK8sResourceAttributes (src/k8s-workload.ts, same package) for container/env/probe/ingress attribute enrichment, and publishes one kubernetes/object@1 fact per object recording the manifest's own kind spelling, ref scope, Ingress backend service names, and declared container images.

keyExports.K8S_OBJECT_SCHEMA: Published fact schema id 'kubernetes/object@1' for the extra-attributes fact this parser writes.
keyExports.k8sIdentity: Builds a ResourceIdentity keyed by (namespace|cluster-scope, manifestKind, name) under the 'k8s' namespace.
keyExports.k8sRefScope: The `k8s/{namespace|_}` scope string an object's own references resolve within.
keyExports.kubernetesParser: IaCParser const (kind 'kubernetes'): fileMatch on .yaml/.yml, supports()/parse() as described in summary.

assumptions: supports() requires string apiVersion+kind and rejects docs carrying `Resources` (object) or `Transform` (string), which are CloudFormation/SAM shapes.
Object name falls back to the file's extension-stripped basename when metadata.name is absent.
risks: K8S_OBJECT_SCHEMA ('kubernetes/object@1') is a published fact schema string; renaming it breaks whichever projector reads containerImages/backends/manifestKind back out of it.

annotation.summary: Projection contributor linking Kubernetes Ingress objects to their backend Service objects: reads K8S_OBJECT_SCHEMA fact records, matches each Ingress backend name against Services in the same refScope (namespace), and emits 'routes-to' link batches for pairs already present as graph resources.

keyExports.ingressRoutesProjector: ProjectionContributor { id:'ingress-routes', requires: K8S_OBJECT_SCHEMA, project() } — contributes only links, no new resources, and drops a link whose Ingress or Service resource isn't in the graph

assumptions: A Service name is looked up scoped to refScope (namespace) — cross-namespace backend names never match.

annotation.summary: Built-in IaC plugin registering the AWS SAM/CloudFormation template parser (samParser) under InfraKind 'aws-sam' and 'cloudformation', both routed to the shared infra-sam domain.

keyExports.default: Default export — the same samIacPlugin value
keyExports.samIacPlugin: definePlugin() descriptor with capabilities.iac.parsers=[samParser] and kindDomains for aws-sam/cloudformation

assumptions: Resource/trigger kind semantics (lambda, queue, topic, table, api, bucket, role; api/sqs/schedule/event-bus/dynamodb-stream/kinesis-stream/websocket triggers) are declared in this package's package.json#repovine.declarations, not in this file.

annotation.summary: IaC parser for AWS SAM/CloudFormation templates: resolves each resource's kind and identity namespace, extracts Secrets Manager / SSM SecureString references (including dynamic {{resolve:...}} refs) as synthetic secret resources, and merges IAM policy grants (inline policy documents, managed-policy refs, SAM policy templates) onto env refs by read/write access mode.

keyExports.AWS_KIND_NAMESPACES: Identity namespace per AWS resource kind (lambda->aws-lambda, queue->aws-sqs, etc.); a kind absent from the table falls back to the account-wide 'aws' namespace.
keyExports.GRANT_TARGET_RESOURCE_TYPES: CFN resource types this parser treats as IAM-policy grant targets (DynamoDB Table, S3 Bucket, SQS Queue, SNS Topic, SecretsManager Secret, SSM Parameter); Roles/APIs/Functions are excluded because a grant names them as subject, not target.
keyExports.SAM_POLICY_TEMPLATE_ACCESS: SAM policy-template id (lowercased) to InfraAccessMode, used when a template's expanded IAM actions never literally appear in the template file.
keyExports.SAM_RESOURCE_KINDS: CloudFormation resource type string (e.g. 'AWS::Serverless::Function') to InfraResourceKind mapping.
keyExports.samParser: IaCParser implementation for SAM/CloudFormation templates; builds InfraResource/InfraTrigger/InfraEnvRef facts from parsed template resources and Lambda IAM policies.

assumptions: An SSM parameter is treated as a secret only when its Type is SecureString; plain String/StringList params are not.
Deny statements in an IAM policy document are skipped entirely — a subtraction the parser cannot evaluate must never widen a reported grant.
risks: AWS::KMS::Key is absent from GRANT_TARGET_RESOURCE_TYPES (KMS is unmodeled by SAM_RESOURCE_KINDS), so a kmsdecryptpolicy grant resolves to no resource node; conversely AWS::SSM::Parameter is a grant target here but not modelled as its own resource kind.

annotation.summary: Built-in IaC plugin registering the Terraform/OpenTofu (.tf) parser under InfraKind 'terraform', mapping recognized AWS/GCP/Azure provider resource types onto the generic InfraResourceKind set (unrecognized types fall through to 'other').

keyExports.default: Default export — the same terraformIacPlugin value

assumptions: Terraform mints its own identity namespace and declares its own lambda-handler metadata, independent of and non-colliding with the SAM plugin's.

annotation.summary: Text/regex-based Terraform (.tf) IaC parser: extracts resource/data/module blocks with a hand-written HCL block scanner (brace-balanced, heredoc-aware, comment-aware), classifies resource kind from a static Terraform-type table, and extracts env-var maps (variables/environment_variables/app_settings) into envRefs by resolving `type.name.attr` expressions to sibling block names.

keyExports.terraformParser: IaCParser (kind 'terraform', fileMatch: extension .tf, loaderId 'text'); parse() extracts blocks via extractTerraformBlocks, classifies each via resolveTerraformKind, and builds InfraResource entries with envVars/envRefs from extractTerraformEnv.

assumptions: An aws_ssm_parameter resource is a secret only when its `type` attribute equals SecureString; a Terraform type absent from TERRAFORM_TYPE_TO_KIND defaults to 'other'.

An env-map value resolves to a target only for a `${type.name.attr}` / `type.name.attr`-shaped reference; var/local/each/count/self/path/terraform-prefixed expressions are never treated as resource targets.
risks: Block and attribute extraction is a hand-written scanner rather than a real HCL parser; attribute values built from multiple interpolation expressions or unusual formatting may not match the single quoted-string attribute regex.

annotation.summary: Built-in IaC plugin registering the Vercel project-config (vercel.json) parser under InfraKind 'vercel', emitting vercel-function/vercel-cron/vercel-route resource kinds with cron entries as schedule triggers.

keyExports.default: Default export — the same vercelIacPlugin value
keyExports.vercelIacPlugin: definePlugin() descriptor with capabilities.iac.parsers=[vercelParser] and kindDomain 'vercel'

assumptions: The Vercel provider declaration in package.json#repovine answers for Vercel resources whether or not the SAM plugin is also loaded.

annotation.summary: IaCParser implementation for vercel.json: recognizes the file by name plus presence of any of version/functions/crons/rewrites/redirects/headers/routes, and parses it into a project resource (config attrs + env var names), legacy @name secret refs, per-function resources, cron resources with schedule triggers, and rewrite/redirect/header/route rule resources.

keyExports.vercelParser: IaCParser const (kind 'vercel'): fileMatch on vercel.json, supports() checks for known top-level keys, parse() builds the resource list.

assumptions: Only legacy `@name`-prefixed env values are recoverable as secret refs; modern encrypted Vercel env vars leave no in-file signal, so those secrets are invisible to this parser.
supports() requires the basename to be exactly 'vercel.json' and at least one recognized top-level key present.

annotation.summary: Public entrypoint barrel for @repovine/plugin-sdk. Re-exports the layer-1 fact surface and authoring machinery: runtime primitives (PLUGIN_API_VERSION, PluginRequirements, PluginAvailability), factories (defineSourcePlugin, defineIaCParser, plus plugin descriptor helpers via './plugin/index.js'), the source-plugin contract, the versioned semanticHints schema/validator, producer fact schemas, the conformance kit, the IaC parser vocabulary, and IaC/trigger kind-metadata types. Deliberately omits projection and ontology layers (GraphDelta, RepositoryGraph, NodeType, EdgeKind, Interpreter) — those stay engine-only.

keyExports.PLUGIN_API_VERSION: Runtime API version a plugin declares; the engine checks compatibility.
keyExports.SEMANTIC_HINTS_VERSION: Version stamp of the semanticHints producer/consumer contract.
keyExports.checkIaCPluginConformance: Conformance gate an IaC plugin runs to claim SDK compatibility.
keyExports.checkSourcePluginConformance: Conformance gate a source plugin runs to claim SDK compatibility.
keyExports.defineIaCParser: Factory authoring an IaC parser with fileMatch/supports/parse.
keyExports.defineSourcePlugin: Factory authoring a source plugin with discover/extract handlers.
keyExports.mintModuleId: Module id minting from package, relative path, and source plugin id.
keyExports.resolveDottedPathHandlerToModule: Handler resolver mapping a dotted-path handler reference to a module id.
keyExports.validateSemanticHints: Verdict-returning validator for a producer's semanticHints payload against the versioned schema.
keyExports.validateSemanticInfraDelta: Validator gating untrusted IaC parser output against zod schema.
keyExports.validateSemanticModuleDelta: Validator gating untrusted source-plugin extract output against zod schema.

assumptions: Third-party plugins import from the published entrypoints — this root barrel plus scoped ./source-plugin and ./iac-plugin subpaths — and cannot reach internal module paths.
The factories are the documented authoring path; they stamp the contract apiVersion, keeping the spec inside the object.

risks.text: Published package entrypoint: external plugin authors compile against this export list, so removing or renaming a re-export breaks builds outside this repo.

risks: New SDK contracts reach plugin authors through barrel re-exports; adding to internal modules alone leaves scoped importers without it.
patterns: Re-export barrel with a live runtime tail: importing evaluates zod schema modules behind fact and semanticHints exports, so the entrypoint needs its zod peer dependency resolvable at import time.
Deliberate omission of layer-2/3 exports keeps the plugin/engine boundary one-directional.
annotation.flowDescription: Consumer imports package entrypoint → barrel resolves/re-exports stable public symbols from internal modules.
invariants: Only stable public SDK surface is re-exported; internal projection types stay unexported.
Type-only re-exports use export type so the barrel stays erasable at runtime.
extensionPoints: New public contracts are exposed by adding a re-export here while internal paths stay encapsulated.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/runtime, src/factory, src/types, src/source-plugin/types, src/source-plugin/handler-resolver, src/source-plugin/module-id, src/source-plugin/semantic-hints-schema, src/fact-schemas, src/conformance, and src/iac-plugin/attributes.
annotation.dataFlow: External import of @repovine/plugin-sdk → barrel re-export map → concrete runtime, factory, schema, and type modules.

annotation.summary: canonicalJson(value): deterministic JSON serialization producing the same bytes for structures that must compare equal across producers, hosts and runs (e.g. a resource payload before hashing).

keyExports.canonicalJson: Serializes a value: honors toJSON() first, sorts object keys by code unit recursively, preserves array order, drops undefined-valued keys (matching JSON.stringify); throws TypeError on Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakSet

assumptions: Key sorting is by code unit, not locale collation, so the answer never depends on LANG or the host's ICU build

risks.text: canonicalJson throws TypeError on a Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakSet anywhere in the value rather than serializing it; a caller must ensure the value it passes carries no such collection, since one would otherwise canonicalize every instance to the same bytes.

annotation.summary: Self-certification kit: a plugin runs these checks to claim SDK compatibility. Exercises source plugin discovery/extraction and IaC plugin parsers against samples, mirroring engine dispatch. Every output is validated against the fact schemas and checked for semantic-only content (no mechanical metadata).

keyExports.ConformanceCheck: One named check result: { name, ok, detail? }.
keyExports.ConformanceReport: Per-check list and whether all passed: { passed, checks }.
keyExports.checkIaCPluginConformance: Runs an IaC plugin against sample documents: parser presence, file matching, support gate, first-match precedence, schema validity.
keyExports.checkSourcePluginConformance: Runs a source plugin against a sample workspace: availability, discovery, extraction, schema validity, semantics-only, determinism.

assumptions: Samples must contain at least one file the plugin claims, or the relevant check cannot exercise it.
The fact schemas (mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/fact-schemas) are the authoritative validity gate for both source and IaC deltas.
The IaC path mirrors engine dispatch: first parser that supports+parses a document wins.

sideEffects.description: reads sample files when exercising a source plugin

risks: Thin sample coverage lets a defective plugin pass conformance.
These checks can drift from the engine's own validators if the two are not updated together.
Only the first supporting parser is exercised per sample, so a later parser's handling of the same document is never checked.
patterns: Named checks aggregated; failure identifies which guarantee broke.
Determinism checked by extracting twice and comparing.
annotation.flowDescription: The plugin's hooks run against controlled samples, each output is schema-validated and inspected for mechanical keys, and the results are aggregated into a report.
invariants: The report passes only when every check passed.
Deltas must carry semantics only; no mechanical metadata.
extensionPoints: Further checks can be appended as named entries without changing the report contract.
