annotation.integrationPoints: Validates against mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/fact-schemas; plugin contracts from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types; exposed through the package barrel.
annotation.dataFlow: plugin plus samples -> matching and support gating -> the plugin's own extraction or parse -> schema validation and mechanical-key inspection -> per-check report.

annotation.summary: Canonical truncated-sha256 hashing primitive shared by the SDK so content, config, and full hashes across the engine and repovine.annots.json all use the same digest recipe and a named width per contract.

keyExports.HASH_WIDTH: { content: 16, config: 24, full: 64 } — content travels in the snapshot and repovine.annots.json; config gates the snapshot-reuse cache; full is the untruncated digest.
keyExports.sha256Hex: sha256Hex(text, width) — sha256 over an already-canonicalized UTF-8 string, kept to `width` hex characters.

invariants: The width IS the contract: a 16-char content hash and a 24-char config fingerprint compare against different stored values and mean different things.
Canonicalizing the input (JSON.stringify, sorting, joining, framing) stays at the call site, not here — this function only digests already-canonical bytes.

annotation.summary: Zod validator schemas for untrusted plugin payloads. zSemanticModuleDelta and zSemanticInfraDelta validate imports/exports/calls/attributes without throwing; validators return a FactValidationResult<T> union so callers branch on ok rather than catching.

keyExports.FactValidationResult: Type alias: { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: string }.
keyExports.zSemanticInfraDelta: Zod schema for IaC parser output: kind, resources[] with id/kind/provider/contentHash/attributes.
keyExports.zSemanticModuleDelta: Zod schema for source plugin extract output: moduleId, imports[], exports[], reExports?, calls?, semanticHints?, transient?.

assumptions: Untrusted plugins (trusted:false) must pass these validators before graph assembly.
Built-in plugins (trusted:true) skip validation; conformance tests cover them instead.
Schemas accept open-string enums (kind, provider) and forward-compatible unknown fields via .passthrough().
risks: Schema misalignment with runtime expectations can block valid plugins or leak malformed facts.
Breaking changes to SemanticModuleDelta/SemanticInfraDelta must update zod schemas and validators in lockstep.
patterns: Centralized untrusted-plugin boundary validation.
annotation.flowDescription: Plugin emits candidate delta -> validator parses against zod schema -> host uses typed output or rejects with reason.
invariants: Validation helpers return explicit success/error unions instead of throwing.
Schema definitions remain aligned with mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types contract types.
extensionPoints: New optional semantic fields can be introduced in the schema with backward-compatible defaults.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/conformance and stage1 fact ingestion; validates shapes from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types.
annotation.dataFlow: SemanticModuleDelta/SemanticInfraDelta payloads -> schema validators -> typed values for stage1 assembly.

annotation.summary: Plugin-SDK authoring factories. A plugin package's default export is a PluginRuntimeDescriptor built elsewhere; these two anchors type the pieces that go inside it — a source plugin and a single IaC parser — so authors write against the published contract rather than an ad-hoc literal. Both are runtime near-identity: defineSourcePlugin stamps apiVersion when the spec omits one, defineIaCParser just types the value.

keyExports.defineIaCParser: (parser: IaCParser) => IaCParser; typed authoring anchor for one parser declaration, returned unchanged.
keyExports.defineSourcePlugin: (spec: SourcePlugin) => SourcePlugin; stamps the current PLUGIN_API_VERSION onto the spec when it does not already declare one.

assumptions: Both factories are the intended single entry points for authoring their respective plugin piece; a hand-built literal skips the apiVersion stamping defineSourcePlugin applies.
defineIaCParser performs no normalization — it exists to type-check the literal against the IaCParser contract, not to transform it.
risks: defineSourcePlugin only fills apiVersion when absent; a spec that already sets an outdated apiVersion passes through unstamped.
patterns: Pure typed-identity factories: authoring against a published contract instead of an ad-hoc literal.
annotation.flowDescription: Author supplies a SourcePlugin or IaCParser literal -> factory type-checks it (and, for defineSourcePlugin, stamps apiVersion) -> the typed value is exported as the plugin's contribution.
invariants: defineIaCParser returns its input unchanged.
defineSourcePlugin only adds apiVersion when the spec did not set one; every other field passes through untouched.
extensionPoints: A source plugin's fileMatch/capabilities/requires fields (typed via defineSourcePlugin) are the extension surface package authors declare against; defineIaCParser is the equivalent typed anchor for a single IaC parser passed into a plugin's parsers array.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imported by plugin authors; types come from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types (SourcePlugin) and mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types (IaCParser); PLUGIN_API_VERSION comes from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/runtime.
annotation.dataFlow: author-written SourcePlugin/IaCParser literal -> factory helper -> typed (and for source plugins, apiVersion-stamped) value consumed by the plugin loader.

annotation.summary: Compiles a build.scan glob (*, **, ?; no brace expansion) into a GlobMatcher using a linear dynamic program, so the engine and a source-plugin producer match paths identically without regex backtracking.

keyExports.compileGlob: (glob: string) => GlobMatcher; tokenizes then runs an O(tokens*path length) DP over the whole string, anchored (no partial match)

assumptions: Brace expansion is not supported; every character other than *, **, ? is literal
annotation.integrationPoints: SSOT for glob matching shared by the discovery engine (compiles repovine.config.json build.scan patterns) and source-plugin producers (apply the same compiled matcher while walking); both sides must resolve the same glob to the same matches.

annotation.summary: Scoped npm subpath barrel (`@repovine/plugin-sdk/iac-plugin`) re-exporting IaC plugin factories (defineIaCParser, definePlugin), resource-identity helpers, PLUGIN_API_VERSION, SemanticInfraDelta validation, conformance checks, and IaC-related types for external plugin authors.

keyExports.DOCUMENT_CLAIMS: Registry metadata constant for document claim kinds an IaC parser declares.
keyExports.PLUGIN_API_VERSION: Runtime API version constant plugins must declare compatibility with.
keyExports.checkIaCPluginConformance: Runs SDK conformance checks on an IaC plugin descriptor.
keyExports.defineIaCParser: Factory to declare a single IaC parser implementation.
keyExports.definePlugin: Factory declaring a plugin's runtime descriptor (capabilities, requirements).
keyExports.hashResourcePayload: The one content hash a producer mints for an IaC resource payload.
keyExports.makeResourceId: Mints a resource identity string for an IaC resource.
keyExports.parseResourceId: Parses a minted resource id back into its identity components.
keyExports.validateSemanticInfraDelta: Zod-schema validation for parser output payloads.

assumptions: Publish subpath `@repovine/plugin-sdk/iac-plugin` — root package barrel remains the canonical import for in-repo consumers.
All symbols are re-exports; no runtime logic lives in this index file.
risks: Drift between this barrel and root @repovine/plugin-sdk exports breaks publish-time subpath imports.
patterns: Scoped barrel pattern: subpath for npm publish discoverability without duplicating implementation.
invariants: Re-export surface must stay aligned with root factory/runtime/types on publish.
checkIaCPluginConformance is the gate before a plugin is considered SDK-compatible.
extensionPoints: IaCParser and PluginRuntimeDescriptor types allow custom infra producers without changing engine loader signatures.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by external plugin authors and repovine plugin-loader; re-exports from ../factory.js, ../plugin/descriptor.js, ../plugin/resource-identity.js, ../runtime.js, ../fact-schemas.js, ../conformance.js, ../types.js.
annotation.dataFlow: Plugin author imports defineIaCParser/definePlugin → conformance check at build/test → engine plugin-loader registers parser at stage1.

annotation.summary: Shared rules for folding an arbitrary parsed document value (YAML/JSON/HCL) into the flat Record<string,string> shape InfraResource.attributes accepts, so every IaC parser gives the same document value the same spelling.

keyExports.addAttr: Sets attrs[key] to attrValue(value) only when that spelling is non-empty; otherwise leaves the key absent.
keyExports.attrValue: Scalar spelling of a document value: strings pass through, numbers/booleans stringify, arrays join with ',' (dropping unspellable entries), maps and null/undefined return undefined.
keyExports.isRecord: Type guard: true when value is a plain object (not null, not an array).
keyExports.pathGroupingLabel: Grouping label for a repo-relative path with container segments ('infrastructure','infra','src','app') dropped; falls back to the full path (or 'root') if dropping them would leave nothing.

assumptions: attributes is a flat, host-opaque Record<string,string>: the host stores and displays pairs and never interprets them, so every parser must agree on one scalar spelling.

annotation.summary: Host-only re-export barrel for @repovine/plugin-sdk/internal: forwards dir-layout table helpers, scan-filter halves, declaration-stamping keys, and canonical-json/sha256Hex from five sibling modules (source-plugin/dir-layout, source-plugin/scan-filters, plugin/declarations, canonical-json, content-hash) so the engine and the SDK (two packages) can share single-valued state.
assumptions: Outside the plugin contract by design: consumed only by the repovine engine reaching across the package boundary, never by a plugin; the SDK and engine ship as two packages so one subpath has to expose this host machinery.

risks.text: This subpath is host machinery outside the published plugin contract (not in docs/plugin-api-contract.json) and outside semver; no plugin (built-in, example, canary, or third party) may import it, and the boundary laws refuse the specifier by name.

annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports BASE_DIR_LAYOUT/currentDirLayoutTable/installDirLayoutTable from source-plugin/dir-layout.js, isScanExcluded/isScanIncluded from source-plugin/scan-filters.js, resourceKindMetaKey/stampDeclarationCatalog/triggerTypeMetaKey from plugin/declarations.js, canonicalJson from canonical-json.js, and sha256Hex from content-hash.js.

annotation.summary: Host-independent string comparator (compareCodeUnits) shared by the SDK so every engine sort that reaches the graph — file discovery order, package order, node payload lists, persisted artifacts — compares raw UTF-16 code units instead of locale collation (String.prototype.localeCompare varies by ICU build/LANG).

keyExports.compareCodeUnits: (a, b) => a<b?-1:a>b?1:0 — the same comparison Array.prototype.sort applies to strings with no comparator, named so a sort needing a key extractor or tie-break chain does not reach for localeCompare.

assumptions: Ships in the SDK because a producer plugin orders its own discovery output and must not depend on the host's locale/ICU build; callers wanting locale-aware display sorting must not use this.

annotation.summary: Compile-time-branded path types (HostPath, RepoRelPath, PkgRelPath) that tag which base a path string is measured from, plus assertion functions (asHostPath, asRepoRelPath, asPkgRelPath) that cast an already-correct plain string into the branded type.

keyExports.HostPath: string branded 'host' — an absolute path spelled for the current host filesystem.
keyExports.PkgRelPath: string branded 'package' — a POSIX-separated path measured from one package root.
keyExports.RepoRelPath: string branded 'repo' — a POSIX-separated path measured from the repository root.
keyExports.asHostPath: Assert a value already obtained from a host-filesystem operation is a HostPath; does not resolve or normalize.
keyExports.asPkgRelPath: Assert a value is already package-root-measured and POSIX-normalized.
keyExports.asRepoRelPath: Assert a value is already repo-root-measured and POSIX-normalized.

assumptions: The brand is compile-time only (a unique symbol phantom field) — snapshots, workers and JSON still carry a plain string, so nothing here is checked at runtime; callers must normalize/measure correctly before asserting.

annotation.summary: The path vocabulary a source-plugin producer shares with the engine: repo-relative POSIX identity, a normalized match form, the last path segment, case-folded name-matching keys, and a canonical host-path-keyed view of an absolute-path map.

keyExports.hostKeyedView: WeakMap-memoized case/host-folded view of an absPath->id map, one O(n) pass per source Map instance; on a fold collision between different ids, keeps the first entry and warns
keyExports.hostPathKey: Canonical key for absolute-host-path maps: path.resolve, case-folded only on win32; scope is resolver/map identity only
keyExports.lastPathSegment: Last POSIX segment of a repo-relative path; deliberately not path.basename (which also treats '\\' as a separator on win32)
keyExports.normalizeRelPath: Collapses duplicate '/' and strips a leading '/' for glob/map matching; dot segments (a/../b) are left alone
keyExports.pathMatchKey: Case-folded POSIX form for matching against a lowercase name vocabulary (tests/controllers/build-output heuristics); a match key, never an identity
keyExports.repoRelativePosix: Absolute path -> repo-root-relative POSIX RepoRelPath (identity form); absPath === root answers '' rather than '.'

assumptions: hostPathKey/hostKeyedView are for resolver/map identity only; security-sensitive containment checks must keep their own strict case-sensitive comparison and must not adopt this relaxed form
The source map handed to hostKeyedView is expected to be construction-frozen; the memo is invalidated only by a size change, not by in-place value mutation

sideEffects.description: module-level WeakMap memo (hostKeyedViews/hostKeyedViewSizes/producedViews) caches a folded view per source Map instance
console.warn when case/separator folding collides two different paths onto the same key

annotation.summary: Plugin authoring entrypoint barrel: the whole published contract for a package that ships a repovine plugin (manifest validation, runtime descriptor, declarations, projection/projection-schema, document loader, resource identity, json guard, conformance, path-contract).
assumptions: Nothing re-exported here reaches the engine's internal graph model, node types, or edge kinds — those stay internal to the engine.
Validators are published but their schemas are not: callers branch on a verdict (e.g. validatePluginManifest's result), and the schema shape stays free to change.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports from manifest.js (PLUGIN_MANIFEST_KIND, validatePluginManifest, validatePresetManifest), descriptor.js (PLUGIN_CAPABILITY_NAMES, definePlugin, validatePluginRuntimeDescriptor), declarations.js (ECOSYSTEM_DIR_ROLES), projection.js (ENTRYPOINT_CONTRIBUTION_KINDS, PROJECTION_REF_TYPES, SEMANTIC_LINK_RELATIONS), projection-schema.js (PROJECTION_BUDGETS, checkProjectionRefs, validateProjectionBatch, validatePublishedFact), document-loader.js types, resource-identity.js (RESOURCE_ID_PREFIX, makeResourceId, parseResourceId, resourceIdentityProblem), json.js (isJsonValue), conformance.js (checkPluginConformance), and ../path-contract.js (asHostPath, asPkgRelPath, asRepoRelPath). The root SDK barrel re-exports this subpath too, so an author may import either.

annotation.summary: checkPluginConformance() runs the unified plugin-conformance kit a plugin author (and the built-ins) uses to claim compatibility: manifest validity, descriptor validity, manifest/descriptor id agreement, then per-projector batch-schema validation, batch-id uniqueness, a two-run determinism check, and cross-batch reference resolution against known module/resource ids.

keyExports.PluginConformanceInput: Interface: { manifest: unknown; descriptor: unknown; modules?: readonly ReadonlyModuleFact[]; facts?: readonly ReadonlyFactRecord[]; resources?: readonly ResourceIdentity[]; infraModules?: readonly ReadonlyInfraModuleFact[]; repoRoot?: HostPath }.
keyExports.checkPluginConformance: (input: PluginConformanceInput) => ConformanceReport. Runs checks in the same order the host asks them at load/composition time; short-circuits after manifest/descriptor checks if either fails, and skips projection checks when the descriptor declares no projector.

assumptions: modules/facts/resources/infraModules default to empty arrays when omitted, standing in for the host's real fact view.
repoRoot defaults to asHostPath('/repo') when the caller does not supply one.
Infra documents are folded into knownModuleIds alongside modules, so a projected reference into an infra doc resolves the same way it does in the real host.

annotation.summary: Declarative half of a plugin package: the JSON facts (ecosystem dir roles, axis values, resource-kind/trigger-type/runtime-action metadata) the host reads from package.json#repovine before importing any plugin code, plus the zod schema that validates them and the stamping step that attaches host-derived ownership.

keyExports.ECOSYSTEM_DIR_ROLES: Canonical directory roles a plugin can claim: 'dependencies', 'build-output', 'tool-output', 'test-layout'.
keyExports.PluginDeclarationCatalog: Shape of one plugin's declared facts: optional ecosystem label plus dirs/values/resourceKinds/triggerTypes/runtimeActions arrays.
keyExports.resourceKindMetaKey: Builds the composite '<namespace>/<provider>/<kind>' metadata key for a resource kind declaration.
keyExports.stampDeclarationCatalog: Attaches a frozen PluginOwnerIdentity (declaredBy) to every entry of a validated catalog; the only path that produces declaredBy, since payloads are refused if they spell it themselves.
keyExports.triggerTypeMetaKey: Builds the composite metadata key for a trigger type declaration, spelling an absent namespace/provider as '*'.
keyExports.zPluginDeclarationCatalog: Strict zod schema for the whole catalog; rejects unknown keys and a payload that declares its own 'declaredBy'.

assumptions: Declarations are data and survive a disabled capability (turning a parser off does not drop its pruning facts); a fact leaves the catalog only when its package is absent or a config retraction names it.
whenContains on an EcosystemDirFact is not accepted together with role 'test-layout' (enforced by a zod .refine).

risks.text: This is the published plugin-manifest contract every plugin package declares against under package.json#repovine; changing field names/shapes here breaks every declaring plugin package.

annotation.summary: Defines the executable/runtime half of a plugin package (PluginRuntimeDescriptor) — the object a plugin's entry module default-exports, distinct from the manifest's declared half. definePlugin is a typed identity helper for authors. validatePluginRuntimeDescriptor structurally validates an untrusted default export: descriptor.id via pluginContractIdProblem, `available` must be a function when present, and each declared capability (source/iac/loaders/projectors) is checked for the shape the host will invoke (source needs discover()+extract(); iac needs a non-empty parsers array each with supports()+parse(), plus optional kindDomains entries with kind/meta.domainId/meta.label; loaders/projectors each need a valid id plus load()/project()).

keyExports.PLUGIN_CAPABILITY_NAMES: The 4 recognized capability keys: source, iac, loaders, projectors.
keyExports.PluginRuntimeDescriptor: Descriptor shape: id, optional requires/available, and capabilities.
keyExports.definePlugin: Identity function (typed anchor) a plugin author wraps its descriptor in; returns the object unchanged.
keyExports.validatePluginRuntimeDescriptor: Structural validator over an untrusted default export; returns { ok:true, descriptor, declared } or { ok:false, error }.

assumptions: descriptor.id is expected to equal the package manifest's `id`; this module does not cross-check that itself (the host refuses the package when they disagree).
A descriptor must declare at least one non-empty capability or validatePluginRuntimeDescriptor returns ok:false ('descriptor declares no capability').

risks.text: PluginRuntimeDescriptor/PluginCapabilities is the SDK's published plugin runtime contract; every installed plugin package's default export is validated against this exact shape.

annotation.summary: Declares the DocumentLoader plugin contract: turns file bytes the host already read into structured documents. Loading a format is a pure decode step, never a second filesystem authority beside the scanner.

keyExports.DocumentLoadInput: repoRelPath + raw file content (Uint8Array) handed to a loader
keyExports.DocumentLoader: Interface a plugin implements: `id` names the format it decodes, `load(input)` returns the file's LoadedDocument[]
keyExports.LoadedDocument: documentKey (unique within one file) + value (unknown) returned by a loader; one raw/JSON loader yields one document, a YAML loader yields one per source document

assumptions: value is handed unmodified to the supports/parse pair of the parser that named this loader's id — the host never reads, stores, or reshapes it
documentKey is deterministic and unique within one file, not globally

annotation.summary: Identifier and path spelling rules shared by the plugin manifest, runtime descriptor, and projection contract: validates plugin/contributor/batch/schema/namespace/provider ids and package-root-relative manifest entry paths.

keyExports.EntryPathParse: Interface { ok: true; segments: string[] } — the success shape of parseEntryPath.
keyExports.EntryPathResult: Type: EntryPathParse | { ok: false; error: string }.
keyExports.isPluginContractId: True when value is a non-empty string ≤ 64 chars matching /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/ (no ':', '/', or whitespace).
keyExports.isPluginSchemaId: True when value is ≤160 chars matching '<owner>/<name>@<version>' (SCHEMA_PATTERN), e.g. 'sam/policy-template@1'.
keyExports.parseEntryPath: Validates a manifest `entry` as a POSIX, package-root-relative path: rejects backslashes, leading '/', drive letters, NUL bytes, and '.'/'..'/empty segments; returns { ok:true, segments } or { ok:false, error }.
keyExports.pluginContractIdProblem: Human-readable reason value fails isPluginContractId (empty, too long, or bad charset), or undefined if valid.
keyExports.pluginSchemaIdProblem: Human-readable reason a schema id is invalid, or undefined if valid.
keyExports.schemaIdOwner: Extracts the owner segment (before the first '/') from a schema id.

assumptions: ':' and '/' are excluded from the id charset because every id ends up inside a composite key (provenance (pluginId,contributorId,batchId); extension (pluginId,schema,localKey); resource metadata (namespace,provider,kind)) where either character would let one plugin spell a key belonging to another owner.
Opaque plugin-invented values (a resource localKey, an extension localKey) are NOT governed by this id charset — those go through a separate identity encoder.
invariants: parseEntryPath only validates spelling; the host separately checks that the resolved absolute path stays inside the package directory.

annotation.summary: Defines the JSON-only value contract (type, zod schema, guard) shared by every declarative payload crossing the worker protocol, dump/cache, and generic MCP transports.

keyExports.JsonValue: recursive type: null | boolean | number | string | JsonValue[] | { [key: string]: JsonValue }
keyExports.zJsonValue: z.lazy zod schema validating a value is a JsonValue; z.number() already rejects NaN/Infinity

assumptions: No undefined, function, class instance, Date, or cycle is a valid JsonValue

annotation.summary: The single Zod-validated schema for `package.json#repovine`, covering both plugin packages (kind:'plugin') and preset packages (kind:'preset') — one manifest schema the SDK exports and the host imports directly rather than keeping a second copy. validatePluginManifest strict-parses the payload, checks the id contract, requires apiVersion (string or number) to coerce to the integer PLUGIN_API_VERSION, and when `entry` is present resolves it via parseEntryPath into entrySegments for the host to re-join and containment-check. validatePresetManifest validates a preset's `plugins` array (1-256 entries) and rejects a duplicate package name.

keyExports.PLUGIN_MANIFEST_KIND: Literal 'plugin' — the manifest kind discriminator for plugin packages.
keyExports.PRESET_MANIFEST_KIND: Literal 'preset' — the manifest kind discriminator for preset packages.
keyExports.PresetManifest: Preset shape: kind/id/apiVersion/plugins (npm package names, ordered).
keyExports.validatePluginManifest: Validates a plugin manifest payload; returns { ok:true, manifest, entrySegments? } or { ok:false, error }.
keyExports.validatePresetManifest: Validates a preset manifest payload; returns { ok:true, manifest } or { ok:false, error }.

assumptions: apiVersion accepts the JSON spellings `1` and `"1"`, but must equal PLUGIN_API_VERSION exactly after Number() coercion or validation fails with an incompatibility error.
A preset's `plugins` list must name each package at most once; a repeat is a validation error, not a dedup.

risks.text: This schema is the only manifest format the host reads before importing any plugin code; every published plugin/preset package's package.json#repovine must parse against zPluginManifest/zPresetManifest as written here.

annotation.summary: The public projection contract: how a source/IaC plugin turns its own facts into canonical repository semantics (resources, links, entrypoints, namespaced extensions) without ever touching the graph directly or spelling a graph node id.

keyExports.EntrypointContribution: Discriminated union of the five entrypoint contribution shapes, each carrying a moduleRef or resourceRef
keyExports.ExtensionRecord: A stored extension after the host stamps pluginId and ContributionProvenance (contributorId, batchId)
keyExports.NamespacedExtensionContribution: A fact with no canonical meaning yet: { schema, localKey, subjectRef?, payload }, unique within (pluginId, schema); no traversal/architecture algorithm interprets it
keyExports.PluginProjectionBatch: The unit of atomicity: { batchId, delta }; a rejected batch contributes nothing and does not affect the contributor's other batches
keyExports.ProjectionContributor: { id, requires?, project(input) } — requires names fact schemas (never other contributors); cross-plugin references resolve through the global index after every batch lands, so execution order carries no data
keyExports.ProjectionRef: Discriminated union addressing a module by moduleId, a resource by (namespace, localKey), or an extension by (pluginId, schema, localKey) — never a minted graph node id
keyExports.ReadonlyFactView: The immutable read API a contributor gets: hasModule/moduleIds/module, hasResource, infraModules, select — no host map or function is ever handed out
keyExports.RuntimeResourceContribution: One runtime resource: namespace+localKey identity, opaque provider/kind labels, contentHash of the declaration fragment, optional attributes/envVars
keyExports.SEMANTIC_LINK_RELATIONS: Fixed small vocabulary: publishes, consumes, binds-to, uses-env, routes-to, builds-from; anything else belongs in a namespaced extension
keyExports.SemanticLinkContribution: { from, to, relation, because? } between two ProjectionRefs

assumptions: The internal ontology (graph model, node types, edge kinds) stays unexported; a contributor only ever sees ReadonlyFactView/ReadonlyProjectionInput
A relation with no general meaning yet is a namespaced extension, not a new SEMANTIC_LINK_RELATIONS entry — promoting one is a joint SDK/host decision

annotation.summary: Zod runtime validation and size budgets for the plugin projection contract: shape/spelling checks on a projection batch or published fact, extension/fact schema-ownership enforcement, and cross-batch reference resolution.

keyExports.ENTRYPOINT_SCHEMA_KINDS: Entrypoint contribution kind literals read back off zEntrypointContribution's own union, for a totality check against a separately maintained consumer-facing list
keyExports.PROJECTION_BUDGETS: Frozen per-batch ceilings (maxResourcesPerBatch, maxLinksPerBatch, maxExtensionPayloadChars, maxStringLength, etc.) that make a runaway plugin a diagnosable refusal rather than an OOM build
keyExports.checkProjectionRefs: Builds a global resource/extension index from all accepted batches (registration order is not an input) and reports unknown-module/unknown-resource/unknown-extension for every dangling ProjectionRef, also checking against knownModuleIds/knownResourceIds already in the graph
keyExports.validateProjectionBatch: Parses a batch against zPluginProjectionBatch; with opts.pluginId also rejects extensions whose schema owner (schemaIdOwner) isn't the calling plugin
keyExports.validatePublishedFact: Parses a Stage 1 published fact against zPublishedFact and enforces that the fact's schema owner equals opts.pluginId
keyExports.zProjectionRef: Discriminated union of module/resource/extension reference shapes a plugin uses to point at something instead of minting an id

assumptions: Extension/fact schema ids are spelled '<owner>/<name>@<version>'; schemaIdOwner extracts <owner> and it must equal the publishing plugin's own id
A resource/extension localKey must not look like a minted node id (resource:/mod:/entrypoint:/template:/domain:/pkg: prefix), since identity components are input to minting, not its output

risks.text: zPluginProjectionBatch/zProjectionRef/PROJECTION_BUDGETS are the validated wire contract for every plugin's projection output; every source/IaC plugin's batches must already satisfy this shape and these budgets.

annotation.integrationPoints: Uses mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/plugin/resource-identity (makeResourceId) and mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/plugin/ids (schemaIdOwner); shares projection types with mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/plugin/projection (SEMANTIC_LINK_RELATIONS)

annotation.summary: Resource identity encode/decode contract: the plugin computes namespace+localKey, this SDK module encodes/parses the combined `resource:<namespace>:<localKey>` graph id, and the host mints it.

keyExports.RESOURCE_ID_PREFIX: The 'resource' string prefix used in minted ids.
keyExports.ResourceIdentity: { namespace: string; localKey: string } — namespace is a stable identity domain (e.g. aws-lambda, k8s, vercel); localKey is opaque, unique within the namespace, may contain '/' and ':'.
keyExports.makeResourceId: Mints `resource:<namespace>:<localKey>`; throws (via resourceIdentityProblem) on an unusable identity.
keyExports.parseResourceId: Recovers { namespace, localKey } from a minted id by splitting on the first ':', or undefined when the string isn't one.
keyExports.resourceIdentityProblem: Returns why an identity cannot be encoded (bad namespace shape, empty localKey, control chars in localKey), or undefined when it can.

risks.text: makeResourceId throws rather than returning an error value on a bad identity; callers must validate plugin-contributed ResourceIdentity (e.g. via resourceIdentityProblem) at the contribution boundary before minting, not rely on a caught exception.

invariants: Encoding splits on the first two ':' with no escaping — namespace must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]* (a contract id, no ':' or '/'), so localKey (the remainder) can itself safely contain ':' or '/' (e.g. resource:vercel:function:api/hello).

annotation.summary: Single-export module computing the content hash a source/IaC plugin mints for one runtime-resource payload, driving the engine's runtime-resource freshness comparison.

keyExports.hashResourcePayload: sha256Hex over canonicalJson(payload) at HASH_WIDTH.content; the one resource hash a producer plugin mints rather than the engine

risks.text: hashResourcePayload's byte output (canonicalization + HASH_WIDTH.content) is a published contract; every source/IaC plugin producing runtime-resource hashes must emit byte-identical output for the same resource, including reordered manifest keys.

annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates canonicalization to mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/canonical-json and the hash primitive/width to mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/content-hash

annotation.summary: Plugin API versioning and runtime availability contract: PLUGIN_API_VERSION constant (currently 1), PluginRequirements (optional runtime dependency name), and PluginAvailability (ok flag + rejection reason). Leaf module with no internal dependencies; imported by factory and conformance validators.

keyExports.PLUGIN_API_VERSION: Plugin API major version constant (=1); stamped onto plugins at definition time.
keyExports.PluginApiVersion: Type alias bound to PLUGIN_API_VERSION for compile-time compatibility checks.
keyExports.PluginAvailability: Runtime probe result: ok boolean + optional reason when availability fails.
keyExports.PluginRequirements: Plugin prerequisites shape: optional runtime field (e.g., 'python3', 'go') for graceful degradation.

assumptions: PLUGIN_API_VERSION is immutable; version bumps require loader/conformance coordination.
Absence of requirements means plugin is universally available.
Availability checks are synchronous and fast (no I/O except PATH/env inspection).
risks: Version mismatch breaks plugin loading; must align with factory and conformance validators.
Changing PLUGIN_API_VERSION invalidates all existing plugin descriptors until loaders are rebuilt.
patterns: Dependency-free leaf to avoid import cycles with sdk barrel.
annotation.flowDescription: Plugin descriptors declare requirements -> runtime constants/types define compatibility surface -> loaders/conformance compare and report availability.
invariants: PLUGIN_API_VERSION is the single source of truth for plugin API compatibility checks.
Availability checks communicate failure via structured result, not exceptions.
extensionPoints: Future runtime requirement dimensions can be added as optional fields in PluginRequirements to preserve backward compatibility.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used by factory helpers and conformance checks when validating declared plugin/runtime compatibility.
annotation.dataFlow: Factory and conformance modules import runtime constants/types -> compare plugin metadata -> return availability/compliance decisions.

annotation.summary: Scoped npm subpath barrel (`@repovine/plugin-sdk/source-plugin`) re-exporting source plugin factory, default handler resolver, semantic hints/module delta schemas, conformance checks, and source-plugin lifecycle types.

keyExports.SEMANTIC_HINTS_VERSION: Version constant for semantic hints schema evolution.
keyExports.checkSourcePluginConformance: Runs SDK conformance checks on a source plugin descriptor.
keyExports.defineSourcePlugin: Factory to declare a source-language producer plugin.
keyExports.resolveDottedPathHandlerToModule: Default resolver mapping dotted handler refs to module ids via HandlerResolveContext.
keyExports.validateSemanticHints: Validates optional semantic hint payloads attached to modules.
keyExports.validateSemanticModuleDelta: Validates source plugin extract output for a single module.

assumptions: Publish subpath `@repovine/plugin-sdk/source-plugin` — root barrel remains canonical for in-repo engine code.
resolveDottedPathHandlerToModule is the default HandlerResolver when plugins omit a custom one.
risks: Misaligned re-exports between this subpath and source-plugin/types.ts break plugin author imports.
patterns: Scoped barrel separates source-producer surface from IaC and root SDK entry.
invariants: SourcePlugin.discover and SourcePlugin.extract remain required lifecycle methods.
Re-export list must include every type external plugin authors need without reaching root barrel.
extensionPoints: SourcePluginCapabilities.resolveHandlerToModule hook for custom handler→module mapping.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports from ../factory.js, ./handler-resolver.js, ./semantic-hints-schema.js, ../fact-schemas.js, ../conformance.js, ./types.js, and shared ../types.js UI/infra shapes.
annotation.dataFlow: Plugin author imports defineSourcePlugin → discover/extract lifecycle typed via ./types.js → conformance → engine stage1 assembly.

annotation.summary: Declares CALL_INDEX_PER_DECLARATION_CAP, the shared budget on distinct call names kept per bucket (one per exported declaration, plus the module bucket) in a producer's module call index.

keyExports.CALL_INDEX_PER_DECLARATION_CAP: const 50 — max distinct call names per call-index bucket; ModuleInfo.callsTotal carries the pre-slice size so a reader can tell a capped bucket from a complete one

assumptions: A budget is a contract term shared by the producer (slices output to it) and the host (states the same number when reporting incompleteness), not a producer-private choice

risks.text: Any importer reporting the call-index completeness/budget number to a reader must read this constant rather than hardcode 50, or the reported slice and the completeness claim can drift apart.

annotation.summary: Holds the per-build DirLayoutTable a scan walks by: pruned directory names, test-layout dirs, conditional (marker-gated) prunes, and package-root markers. Installed once per isolate and replaced wholesale on install, never merged.

keyExports.BASE_DIR_LAYOUT: Engine-owned base table (vcs/cache/build-output dir names only); no package markers since no ecosystem is assumed
keyExports.DirLayoutTable: Interface: pruned, testLayout, prunedWhenContains, packageMarkers (all ReadonlySet/ReadonlyMap)
keyExports.currentDirLayoutTable: Returns the table this isolate currently walks by
keyExports.installDirLayoutTable: Replaces the isolate's installed table with a build's plugin-set-derived table (freezes and orders it)
keyExports.packageMarkersFor: Package-root marker filenames for one plugin id, from the installed table

assumptions: A build installs its table before its first walk; a caller outside a build (repovine init, a test, a plugin author's own harness) uses BASE_DIR_LAYOUT untouched
Table replacement is whole-table, not incremental — a plugin dropped from config must stop pruning immediately, which a merged/accumulating registry could not express

sideEffects.description: module-level `installed` table mutated by installDirLayoutTable and read by currentDirLayoutTable/packageMarkersFor

risks: installDirLayoutTable replaces rather than merges the isolate's table — two builds sharing one process would have the second install's plugin set silently override the first's pruned/marker names

annotation.summary: Shared deterministic filesystem walk for source-plugin discovery. Composes the engine-ignore floor and test-layout floor from the per-build currentDirLayoutTable() (sourced from …/source-plugin/dir-layout, not a static exported constant), normalizes repo-relative paths, sorts each directory by code units, and invokes a caller-supplied file callback only for admitted files.

keyExports.DirSkipReason: 'pruned' | 'test-layout' — why a directory was not descended into.
keyExports.PrunedDir: A directory the walk skipped, with its repo-relative path, name, and skip reason.
keyExports.WalkRepositoryOptions: Repository root and synchronous admitted-file callback for a discovery walk.
keyExports.WalkedFile: Absolute and repo-relative normalized path delivered to a producer callback.
keyExports.classifyDiscoveryDir: Classifies a directory as pruned, test-layout, or admitted, including conditional (ancestor-marker-gated) pruning.
keyExports.hasTestLayoutSegment: True when any path segment is a test-layout directory name (from currentDirLayoutTable().testLayout).
keyExports.matchesEngineIgnorePath: Checks whether a repo-relative path is under the engine-ignore floor (fragments from currentDirLayoutTable().pruned).
keyExports.readDirSorted: Returns fs.Dirent entries in host-independent code-unit order.
keyExports.shouldWalkDiscoveryDir: Composes engine-ignore and test-layout pruning for directory descent.
keyExports.walkRepository: Depth-first deterministic walk with shared pruning and caller-provided onFile handling.

assumptions: The caller supplies a repository root that contains startDir and a synchronous onFile callback.
Pruning is by path segment or directory name, not by language or filename convention.
A producer that bypasses shouldWalkDiscoveryDir can still submit a path; post-discovery acceptance separately enforces only the engine-ignore floor.
The ignore and test-layout name sets are read per call from currentDirLayoutTable(), a property of the active plugin set rather than a fixed constant of this module.

sideEffects.description: synchronously enumerates repository directories

risks: Unreadable directories are silently indistinguishable from empty directories because the source-plugin walk has no refusal delivery channel.
Adding a pruned directory name can hide first-party code in repositories that use that name for source.
patterns: One shared walk predicate keeps first-party package, module, template, and infra producers aligned on descent.
Code-unit sorting prevents host locale and filesystem enumeration order from changing discovery output.
invariants: No path under an engine-ignore or test-layout segment reaches onFile through walkRepository.
Directory enumeration order is corrected before recursion.
annotation.integrationPoints: Uses mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/ordering for compareCodeUnits, mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/dir-layout for the per-build ignore/test-layout table (currentDirLayoutTable), and mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/module-id for path normalization; consumed by built-in discovery producers and guarded by pruning-composition and discovery-order laws.
annotation.dataFlow: startDir + repoRoot → sorted directory entries → repo-relative normalized path → shared directory predicate (fed by currentDirLayoutTable) → recursion or onFile callback.

annotation.summary: Default resolver for dotted Lambda-style handler references on path-like runtimes: 'src/users.handler' resolves to a module at 'src/users', with host-provided artifact roots, a handler-path alias map, and bundle output roots applied before lookup. Source plugins with FQCN or package-specific handler formats provide their own resolver instead.

keyExports.resolveDottedPathHandlerToModule: Strips the trailing '.<exportName>' from a handler ref, builds candidate repo-relative paths from the handler-path map, the artifact root and common build-output roots (build/dist/dist-bundled/out mapped back to a sibling 'src'), and returns the first module id ctx.resolveModuleByRepoRelPath resolves, or undefined.

assumptions: The handler ref's export name (after the last '.') is not part of the path; only the prefix is resolved to a module.
ctx.repoRelHandlerPathMap, when present, is checked both under its bare key and under the artifact-root-prefixed key before falling back to normalized-path lookup.
A build-output segment (build/dist/dist-bundled/out) in the artifact root implies a sibling 'src' directory is also a valid source root, in addition to the artifact root itself.

Candidates are tried in order — handler-path-map hits, then the normalized path itself — against artifact roots, then a direct path, then each of ctx.repoRelSearchRoots; the first module id found wins.
risks: This is a best-effort convention resolver: a handler ref that doesn't match the assumed 'path.export' shape, or a source layout outside the common build-output roots, silently returns undefined rather than failing loudly.
patterns: Best-effort resolver with defensive fallback semantics: multiple candidate paths and roots are tried in a fixed order and the first hit wins.
annotation.flowDescription: Handler ref is decomposed into path candidates (handler-path-map first, then normalized direct path) -> each candidate is joined against artifact/source roots and search roots -> ctx.resolveModuleByRepoRelPath is tried per combination -> first matching module id is returned, else undefined.
invariants: Resolution attempts are deterministic for the same handlerRef and resolver context.
The function returns undefined instead of throwing when no mapping resolves.
extensionPoints: Source plugins with non-path handler conventions (FQCN, package-qualified names) implement their own resolver rather than extending this one.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumes the HandlerResolveContext contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types and RepoRelPath from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/path-contract; used by source-plugin handler resolution during runtime-resource/module linking.
annotation.dataFlow: handler reference string + resolver context -> candidate repo-relative paths -> module id lookup across artifact/source/search roots -> optional resolved module id.

annotation.summary: Graph-id spelling shared by every source-plugin producer and the host: normalizes path separators to POSIX, mints mod:/pkg: node ids from a package name and repo-relative path, and reads a package name back out of an id or an import specifier.

keyExports.extractPackageName: Package name at the head of a slash-separated specifier; keeps two segments for an `@scope/name` specifier, one segment otherwise.
keyExports.mintModuleId: Builds `mod:<packageName>/<relPath>` after stripping the longest matching normalize.stripSuffixes entry (case-insensitive) and collapsing a normalize.indexBasenames match down to its containing directory path.
keyExports.packageNameFromId: Strips a leading 'pkg:' prefix; returns the input unchanged when it carries none.
keyExports.toPosixPath: Replaces every backslash with a forward slash so a win32 producer's relative path compares byte-identical to a POSIX one.

assumptions: mintModuleId is called by the host, never by a producer: discover() returns a PendingModuleDraft with no id field, so id spelling cannot depend on a plugin getting the format right.
normalize.stripSuffixes is matched longest-first so a compound suffix like .d.ts is stripped whole rather than leaving a .d tail.
normalize carries the owning ecosystem's own facts, declared through that plugin's own capabilities, not a repo-wide default.
risks: relPath is assumed already repo-relative; mintModuleId does no validation, so an absolute or otherwise-foreign path mints a silently wrong id.
annotation.integrationPoints: ModuleIdNormalize's shape comes from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types; used by the source-plugin conformance kit so a plugin under test mints exactly the ids the engine will mint in a real build.
annotation.dataFlow: packageName + relPath + ModuleIdNormalize -> toPosixPath + suffix/index-basename stripping -> mod:<pkg>/<path>; packageName alone -> pkg:<pkg>; either id form reversed back to a bare package name by packageNameFromId/extractPackageName.

annotation.summary: Ecosystem-neutral half of import resolution: probes a base absolute path against a host-path-keyed map of known module ids using a caller-supplied, ordered list of candidate suffixes, and returns the first match.

keyExports.moduleCandidateSuffixes: Builds the candidate ladder: fileSuffixes in order (plus '' when includeBareBase), then each fileSuffix under each indexBasename
keyExports.resolveByCandidates: Tries baseAbsPath + each candidateSuffix in order against absPathToId (via hostKeyedView/hostPathKey folding for cross-platform/case-insensitive spelling), returning the first module id found

assumptions: absPathToId keys come from mixed sources (tsconfig enumeration, TypeScript's resolver, filesystem walkers) with different path spellings; hostPathKey is the one normalization point for all of them

risks.text: resolveByCandidates does not sort or validate candidateSuffixes; the caller must supply them already in correct preference order (e.g. '.ts' before '.d.ts') or a less-specific suffix can resolve first.

annotation.integrationPoints: Uses mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/paths (hostKeyedView, hostPathKey) for cross-platform path-key folding

annotation.summary: Compiles user-configured `build.scan` include/exclude glob patterns (compileScanPatterns) and applies them to decide whether one repo-relative path is scanned as source or infra content. shouldScanSourcePath/shouldScanInfraPath are the two entry points a discovery producer calls per candidate path: both first run admittedByLayout (matchesEngineIgnorePath + hasTestLayoutSegment) before consulting user patterns, and an include match always wins over an exclude match for the same scope.

keyExports.compileScanPatterns: Compiles raw include/exclude entries (string or {path,scope}) into matchers via compileGlob, tagged with their scan scope ('source'|'infra'|'all').
keyExports.isScanExcluded: Raw exclude-pattern match; always false when isScanIncluded is already true.
keyExports.isScanIncluded: Raw include-pattern match for a given scan scope, ignoring layout admission.
keyExports.shouldScanInfraPath: True when a path passes layout admission and is not excluded from infra scanning.
keyExports.shouldScanSourcePath: True when a path passes layout admission and is not excluded from source scanning; `.d.ts` files are excluded by default unless explicitly included.

assumptions: A pattern's scope defaults to 'all' unless the entry is an object naming 'source' or 'infra' explicitly.
The engine compiles patterns once and reuses the CompiledScanPatterns handle across every candidate path in the walk (not recompiled per path).
risks: admittedByLayout (engine-ignore paths + test-layout segments) is checked BEFORE any user include pattern, so a scan.include entry that targets an engine-ignored or test-layout path is silently never scanned.

annotation.summary: Zod-backed schema and validator for semantic hints emitted by source plugins.

keyExports.SEMANTIC_HINTS_VERSION: Version marker for semantic hints schema evolution.
keyExports.validateSemanticHints: Safe parser that validates unknown input and returns structured success/error result.
keyExports.zSemanticHints: Canonical schema defining accepted semantic hint structure.

assumptions: Plugin-produced semantic hints are validated through this schema before deeper consumption.
risks: Schema tightening can reject previously accepted plugin outputs.
Schema loosening without consumer support can allow ambiguous hint payloads.
patterns: Schema-first normalization gate in plugin fact ingestion path.
annotation.flowDescription: Untrusted hint payload enters validator -> schema safe-parse succeeds or fails -> downstream receives typed hints or structured error.
invariants: validateSemanticHints never throws; it returns explicit ok/error result.
SEMANTIC_HINTS_VERSION tracks schema evolution for compatibility checks.
extensionPoints: Schema can grow via optional properties while preserving existing plugin compatibility.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used by fact validation and plugin conformance checks to gate semantic hint payload acceptance.
annotation.dataFlow: Unknown plugin payload -> zSemanticHints.safeParse -> typed SemanticHints on success or error diagnostics on failure.

annotation.summary: Source-plugin lifecycle and contract types: the SourcePlugin interface (id, discover, extract, optional available/terminateInFlight), discovery and extract input/output shapes, file matching, compiled scan patterns (now using a matcher object instead of RegExp), handler resolution, and declared capabilities. Published plugin-SDK contract every source plugin implements.

keyExports.CompiledScanPattern: Compiled scan pattern: matcher { test(path: string): boolean }, scope: ScanScope (was { regex: RegExp }).
keyExports.SourceDiscoveryResult: Plugin discover output: packages PackageInfo[], pendingByPath Map<string, PendingModuleDraft>, extractContext?: unknown.
keyExports.SourceExtractInput: Host input to plugin extract: repoRoot, packages, pendingModules, prevByPath Map, absPathToId Map, sourceByModuleId Map, analysisVersion.
keyExports.SourceExtractResult: Plugin extract output: deltas SemanticModuleDelta[], reused count, rescanned count.
keyExports.SourcePlugin: The plugin contract: required id, discover(repoRoot, options), extract(input); optional apiVersion, requires, packageMarkers, fileMatch, capabilities, available(), terminateInFlight().
keyExports.SourcePluginCapabilities: Declared capabilities: extensions[], uiSurfaces?, looseNameSeparators?, resolveHandlerToModule?, moduleIdNormalize?.

assumptions: discover and extract are deterministic for the same repoRoot and analysisVersion.
extractContext is opaque to the host and must be structured-clone-safe.
terminateInFlight is optional; plugins with no subprocesses need not implement it.
risks: A handler resolver returning an unrecognized module id yields no infra edge; the link is silently absent.

risks.text: Implementers of SourcePlugin (stage1 loader, extraction worker, conformance kit, built-in plugins) must verify their implementation still satisfies this contract when it changes.
SourcePlugin is the published plugin-SDK contract implemented by source plugins outside this repo; changing a required field or method signature breaks every plugin built against it.

patterns: Stable plugin boundary separating host orchestration from language-specific AST work.
Two-phase lifecycle: discover does file IO; extract stays worker_threads-safe.
Opaque extractContext carries language-specific state from discover into extract.
annotation.flowDescription: The host computes scan and discovery context, the plugin's discover emits pending modules, the host builds the extract input, and the plugin's extract returns semantic deltas.
invariants: discover, extract and id are the required members; every other member is optional.
SourceExtractResult.deltas entries reference moduleIds from the same discovery set.
CompiledScanPattern.scope is one of all, source, or infra.
extensionPoints: SourcePluginCapabilities.resolveHandlerToModule overrides the default dotted-path handler mapping.
extractContext passes plugin-specific state from discover to extract without the host interpreting it.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/factory, handler-resolver, conformance, and stage1 plugin loader/extraction worker.
annotation.dataFlow: SourceDiscoveryOptions.scanPatterns -> discover -> SourceDiscoveryResult -> host builds SourceExtractInput -> extract -> SourceExtractResult.deltas -> stage1 ModuleInfo assembly.

annotation.summary: Text-truncation primitive shared by the SDK so every 'this continues' marker a plugin writes into the graph (an exported type's text, a conditional's source, a resource description) is spelled the same way.

keyExports.SHORTENED_MARKER: '…' — the one marker that says a value continues.
keyExports.shortenText: shortenText(value, maxChars) — returns at most maxChars characters, marker included.

invariants: The budget covers the marker itself: a maxChars below the marker's own width returns leading characters with no marker, because an all-marker value says nothing about the value.

annotation.summary: Shared type contracts for the plugin-sdk public surface: discovery inputs (PackageInfo, PendingModule), extraction output (SemanticModuleDelta), symbol metadata (ExportInfo, ImportInfo, ReExportInfo, ModuleInfo), and framework-neutral semantic hints (UiHints, RouteInfo, RuntimeAction) plus IaC vocabulary (IaCParser, InfraResource, InfraTrigger). Producers emit these facts; the engine owns projection and ontology.

keyExports.ExportInfo: Exported symbol record: name, kind, signature, params, returnType, fields, calls, internals, lineRange, isDefault, defaultLocalName.
keyExports.ImportInfo: Import declaration: moduleSpecifier, resolvedModuleId, importedNames, isTypeOnly, isExternal.
keyExports.ModuleInfo: Assembled module record with language semantics (imports, exports, calls, reExports, semanticHints) + mechanical metadata (id, filePath, packageName, contentHash, sourcePluginId).
keyExports.PackageInfo: Discovered package identity: name, path, version, and source plugin id.
keyExports.PendingModule: Discovered source file after engine stamps moduleId; correlation key for extraction.
keyExports.PendingModuleDraft: Discovered source file as reported by a producer: location, ownership, no identity minted yet.
keyExports.ReExportInfo: Re-export declaration (export * or export { names } from); moduleSpecifier, resolvedModuleId, names, isStar, isExternal.
keyExports.RouteInfo: Discovered route: path, component, source, kind, method, framework, fileType, rendersTemplate.
keyExports.RuntimeAction: IaC runtime action: sqs.sendMessage, sns.publish, eventbridge.putEvents, or lambda.invoke with optional envVar.
keyExports.SemanticModuleDelta: Language semantics only: producer output for one module (imports, exports, reExports, calls, semanticHints, transient flag).
keyExports.UiDataAccess: Data access signal: kind (fetch/http/query/mutation/graphql/storage/api-client), callee, target.
keyExports.UiLifecycleEffect: Lifecycle signal: kind, name, dataAccessCount, navigationCount, timerCount, subscriptionCount.

assumptions: Pure type module: declarations only, no runtime code.
SemanticModuleDelta.moduleId matches the engine-minted PendingModule.moduleId for correlation.
Open string unions (InfraKind, InfraResourceKind, InfraTriggerType, WebFramework) accept producer values the engine does not know.
SemanticHints optional sub-objects (ui, routes, security, ssr) are framework-neutral containers for plugin vocabulary.

risks.text: Importers must verify emitted facts still satisfy these shapes after any field becomes required; 67 downstream consumers and cached extracts depend on them.
Published plugin-sdk contract re-exported through src/index: third-party plugins compile against these shapes, so changing or removing a field breaks producers outside this repo.

patterns: Type module exports a closed set of payload contracts — breaking changes propagate to all plugin writers.
SemanticHints adds framework-neutral slots (routes, ui, security, ssr) so new frameworks can plug in without redefining the spec.
Open-union pairs (known/open) let producers emit unrecognized kinds while keeping autocomplete for known ones.
annotation.flowDescription: Plugin contracts define extraction/infra payloads → stage1 normalizes into snapshot types → stage2/interpreters/MCP consume graph+annotation contracts.
invariants: SemanticModuleDelta.transient=true must not produce a durable contentHash.
IaCParser.parse returns SemanticInfraDelta; the engine assembles InfraModuleInfo.
extensionPoints: Optional SemanticHints sub-objects (ui, routes, security, ssr) admit additive plugin vocabulary without schema break.
Known*/open-union pairs (KnownInfraKind + InfraKind, KnownWebFramework + WebFramework) keep autocomplete for known kinds.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exported by the package barrel mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src; validated against mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/fact-schemas.
annotation.dataFlow: discover → PendingModule[] → extract → SemanticModuleDelta → stage1 merge → ModuleInfo; IaC parse → SemanticInfraDelta → InfraModuleInfo.

annotation.summary: Package entry point for @repovine/plugin-source-python, the built-in Python source plugin; wraps pythonSourcePlugin (from ./plugin.js) in definePlugin(), lifting its requires/available interpreter check to the package descriptor.

keyExports.default: Default export, same value as plugin.
keyExports.plugin: const built via definePlugin({ id: pythonSourcePlugin.id, ...(requires if pythonSourcePlugin.requires is defined), ...(available if pythonSourcePlugin.available is defined, bound to pythonSourcePlugin), capabilities: { source: pythonSourcePlugin } }).

assumptions: The Python interpreter prerequisite is lifted from the source plugin to this descriptor so requires/available is one lifecycle check for every capability the package activates, producing one actionable message rather than a per-file failure when no interpreter is found.

annotation.summary: Python source-plugin discovery (Pass 1): resolves a trusted python3/python interpreter on PATH, then walks the repo for Python packages (pyproject.toml/setup.py markers) and their .py files, skipping test_*.py/*_test.py/conftest.py.

keyExports.PythonExtractContext: Opaque extractContext shape threaded to extract.ts: { pythonBin: string | null }
keyExports.detectPython: Resolves and memoizes an absolute python3/python path that can `import ast`, or null if none qualifies
keyExports.discoverPython: Entry point: detects the interpreter, discovers packages+.py files, returns SourceDiscoveryResult with pythonBin carried in extractContext
keyExports.isTrustedInterpreterPathEntry: True only for an absolute PATH entry that isn't the current cwd, blocking the cwd-relative interpreter search vector
keyExports.safeInterpreterCwd: Returns os.tmpdir() as the safe cwd for interpreter subprocess checks, keeping a repo-local python.exe/ast.py from being picked up

assumptions: An interpreter candidate is trusted only after it successfully runs `import ast, sys` within a 3s execFileSync timeout from a non-repo cwd.

sideEffects.description: execFileSync runs each interpreter candidate with `import ast, sys` to verify it
walks the repo for pyproject.toml/setup.py markers and .py files

risks.text: A caller resolving an interpreter from PATH must gate each entry through isTrustedInterpreterPathEntry before spawning it; empty, relative, and cwd PATH entries are the cwd-relative executable-search hijack vector this guard closes, so spawning from an ungated entry reopens it.

annotation.summary: Conservative Python-import to SideEffect-kind mapping table (EFFECT_IMPORT_TABLE) that feeds SemanticHints.effectImports, read by the annotation consistency axis's detectSideEffectKindsFromHints check (declared-pure vs detected effects). Only lists imports whose presence unambiguously implies a real behavioral effect: subprocess/threading/multiprocessing to concurrency; requests/httpx/aiohttp/urllib.request/http.client to io-read; socket to resource; boto3/botocore to external; sqlite3/psycopg2/psycopg/pymysql/pymongo/redis/sqlalchemy to io-read. Ambiguous or near-universal modules (os, sys, json, logging, asyncio, typing) are deliberately absent.

keyExports.effectImportsFromPythonImports: Filters imports to imp.isExternal, matches each against EFFECT_IMPORT_TABLE by exact or dotted-submodule prefix, dedupes by (kind, source), and returns a sorted Array<{kind, source}>.

assumptions: Intra-repo (non-external) imports never imply an effect here; the imported module is expected to carry its own hints instead.
Prefix match is `specifier === prefix || specifier.startsWith(prefix + '.')`, so submodules like `requests.adapters` match `requests`.
risks: EFFECT_IMPORT_TABLE is intentionally incomplete: a missing entry only skips detection (never asserts pure), but adding an over-broad prefix would false-flag legitimately pure modules that import it incidentally.

annotation.summary: Declares the file extensions and package/layout marker names the Python source plugin owns, as a leaf module read by discovery, import resolution, and the plugin descriptor.

keyExports.PYTHON_INDEX_BASENAMES: ['__init__'] — basenames that stand for their own directory, for id minting and the resolve ladder
keyExports.PYTHON_PACKAGE_MARKERS: ['pyproject.toml', 'setup.py'] — files whose presence makes a directory a package root

annotation.summary: Python AST extraction for the source-python plugin. runPythonAst spawns the configured Python binary against the AST-extraction script and parses its per-file JSON output; extractPython reuses prior deltas for unchanged files and calls runPythonAst only for files that changed; terminateLivePythonChildren SIGKILLs every still-tracked child process (test/shutdown cleanup).

keyExports.TrackedChild: Minimal child-process shape (exitCode/signalCode/once/kill) this module tracks and kills.
keyExports.extractPython: Entry point: diffs pending modules against prior state, re-parses only changed files via runPythonAst.
keyExports.runPythonAst: Spawns pythonBin against pyAstScriptPath for a batch of file paths, returns parsed RawModule per path.
keyExports.terminateLivePythonChildren: SIGKILLs every still-live tracked Python child process (test/shutdown cleanup).

assumptions: pythonBin and pyAstScriptPath resolve to a working Python 3 interpreter and the repo's AST-extraction script.

sideEffects.description: runPythonAst spawns the Python AST-extraction script as a child process
kills the child after a timeout (__PY_AST_TIMEOUT_MS_FOR_TEST) via an unref'd killTimer

annotation.summary: Maps AST-detected Python web-framework routes (FastAPI, Django, DRF, Flask, aiohttp) into normalized SemanticHints route entries, normalizing Django/DRF-style relative paths to absolute URLs and inferring decorator-vs-call declaration syntax per row.

keyExports.PythonWebFramework: 'fastapi' | 'django' | 'drf' | 'flask' | 'aiohttp' union of frameworks this module recognizes.
keyExports.RawFrameworkRoute: Raw route row shape the stdlib `ast` subprocess extractor emits: path, method?, component, line?, rendersTemplate?, syntax?.
keyExports.frameworkHintsFromRaw: Converts { framework?, routes? } (RawFrameworkRoute[]) into Pick<SemanticHints,'hasRoutes'|'routes'|'webFramework'>, sorted by path/method/component; returns undefined when there are no raw routes.
keyExports.normalizeApiPath: Normalizes one route path to an absolute URL: regex paths (leading '^') pass through unchanged; Django/DRF relative paths gain a leading '/'.

assumptions: aiohttp needs a per-row `syntax` because it declares routes both by decorating a handler and by a registration call; other frameworks' syntax is inferred from DECORATOR_FRAMEWORKS membership when a row omits it.
risks: rendersTemplate detection covers only same-file template renders; a route whose handler renders a template via an indirect call or a different file is not captured.

annotation.summary: Built-in Python source plugin (MVP): discovers pyproject.toml/setup.py packages and .py files, extracts symbols by running the stdlib `ast` module via a `python -c` subprocess, and degrades gracefully (one warning, no throw) when no python3/python interpreter is on PATH.

keyExports.default: pythonSourcePlugin, built via defineSourcePlugin({ id: 'python', requires: { runtime: 'python3' }, available(), packageMarkers: PYTHON_PACKAGE_MARKERS, fileMatch: { extensions: PYTHON_EXTENSIONS }, capabilities: {...}, discover(), extract(), terminateInFlight() }).

assumptions: available() probes via detectPython() and returns { ok:false, reason } instead of throwing when no interpreter is found; requires.runtime is the declarative prerequisite, available() is the real check.
looseNameSeparators:true because PEP 503 treats '-', '_' and '.' as interchangeable in Python distribution names.
moduleIdNormalize treats `__init__` as standing for its own package directory, the way `index` does for TypeScript modules.

uiSurfaces:false — Python modules never populate the TS-only frontend detectors (JSX routes, React architecture); web-framework routes (FastAPI decorators, Django urlpatterns) are still extracted when ast-provable.

sideEffects.description: extract() delegates to extractPython, which runs `python -c` as a child of the node process to parse source via the stdlib ast module.
terminateInFlight() calls terminateLivePythonChildren() so the engine can kill/reap live python subprocesses before Worker.terminate() on shutdown or build cancel.

annotation.summary: Structural Python import resolver, mirroring the TypeScript source plugin's resolve-specifier: resolves relative imports, intra-package absolute imports, and cross-package absolute imports directly against the Pass-1 absPathToId map and discovered PackageInfo list — no disk reads, no sys.path/venv simulation.

keyExports.PythonImportResolution: { resolvedModuleId: string | undefined; isExternal: boolean } — result shape.
keyExports.ResolvePythonImportInput: Input shape: importingAbsPath, level, moduleDotted, kind ('import'|'from'), absPathToId, packages, repoRoot, importingPackage.
keyExports.resolvePythonImport: Main entry: level>0 resolves relative to the importing file's directory ascended `level` times; level=0 tries intra-package resolution then cross-package resolution across all discovered Python packages, else returns isExternal:true.

assumptions: Package name matching is hyphen/underscore normalized (normalizePyName), since a package's declared name may use hyphens while its importable module name uses underscores.
Cross-package resolution tries a nested top-level directory layout first, then a flat layout (module file directly under the package root), before giving up.

annotation.summary: Package entry point for @repovine/plugin-source-typescript, the built-in TypeScript/JavaScript source plugin; wraps typescriptSourcePlugin (from ./plugin.js) in definePlugin() in the one shape the host loads.

keyExports.default: Default export, same value as plugin.
keyExports.plugin: const built via definePlugin({ id: typescriptSourcePlugin.id, capabilities: { source: typescriptSourcePlugin } }); manifest identity + lifecycle + the capabilities this package activates, read the same way whether bundled or installed independently.

assumptions: Package owns the whole TS/JS ecosystem vertical: tsconfig parsing, the ts-morph AST pass, the TypeScript module resolver, single-file-component extraction, and semantic hints — compiles against @repovine/plugin-sdk alone.

annotation.summary: Single pre-order pass over a SourceFile that attributes every forward CallExpression's callee name to its nearest enclosing exported declaration (else a module-level bucket), deduped, IGNORED_CALLS-filtered, and capped per bucket.

keyExports.CallBucket: { names: string[]; total: number } — names is the post-filter, post-cap slice; total is the pre-slice size so a consumer can report what was dropped
keyExports.collectModuleCalls: Walks the file threading the enclosing exported declaration on the recursion stack (O(nodes), no per-call ancestor re-walk); covers functions, arrow-consts, class members, HOC-wrapped consts, object-literal methods, namespace members, default exports, and non-exported local helpers

assumptions: IGNORED_CALLS excludes common builtin/utility calls (console.*, JSON.*, Object.*, Array.*, Promise.*, Math.*, Date.now, timers, encode/decodeURI*, require, Map/Set/Error/TypeError/RegExp) from attribution
Plain f() and obj.m()/this.m() are captured by name; deeper/computed-access expressions resolve to the bare property name
annotation.integrationPoints: PER_BUCKET_CAP is CALL_INDEX_PER_DECLARATION_CAP, imported from the @repovine/plugin-sdk package root but defined in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/budgets (consumer-scoped risk there: any reporter of call-index completeness must read that constant rather than hardcode the number).

annotation.summary: TypeScript/JavaScript discovery (Pass 1): enumerates each package's tsconfig file list plus SFC (Vue/Svelte) files and any explicit scanPatterns includes, registering each into one path-keyed pending-module map with deepest-package-wins ownership for overlaps.

keyExports.discoverTypeScript: Entry point: discovers packages, walks each package's parsed tsconfig fileNames + SFC files, layers in explicit-include files, returns SourceDiscoveryResult
keyExports.shouldSkipRepoRelativePath: True when any segment of a repo-relative path is inside the engine's ignored/test discovery tree

assumptions: Test files (*.test.*/*.spec.*) and *.map files are always skipped regardless of scanPatterns.
When two packages' tsconfigs both claim a file, the package with the longer matching repoRelDir prefix owns it (registerPendingModule).

sideEffects.description: reads SFC component files and walks the repo tree via walkRepository for tsconfig/explicit-include discovery

annotation.summary: Collects every exported declaration from a ts-morph SourceFile into ExportInfo records (kind, signature, params, return type, line range, calls) plus a moduleCalls bucket for calls not attributed to any exported declaration (top-level statements, non-exported helpers), which is what makes a private helper's calls visible to the reverse-by-name call index.

keyExports.CollectedExports: Return shape of collectExports: { exports: ExportInfo[]; moduleCalls: CallBucket }.
keyExports.collectExports: Walks sf.getExportedDeclarations(), keeping only declarations defined in this file (skips re-exports), and builds ExportInfo entries via collectModuleCalls/getSymbolKind/getSignatureText/etc.

assumptions: sf is a ts-morph SourceFile already loaded into a Project; declarations are only counted when decl.getSourceFile() === sf (filters out re-exported symbols from other files).
Per-declaration `calls` is only populated when the declaration body is <=500 lines; longer bodies omit calls but keep callsTotal if the bucket recorded more names than were attributed.
risks: collectFunctionInternals only descends into function bodies with >=200 lines (minLines default), so internals for shorter functions are never reported.

annotation.summary: The file-extension registry the TypeScript source plugin owns, declared once so discovery, specifier resolution, and the plugin descriptor all read it without importing the plugin itself.

keyExports.JSX_EXT_SUFFIX_RE: /\.(?:tsx|jsx)$/i — narrower than the TS family since plain .ts cannot carry JSX.
keyExports.SFC_EXTENSION_LIST: ['.vue', '.svelte'] — single-file-component extensions, deliberately excluded from TYPESCRIPT_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS.
keyExports.SFC_VIRTUAL_TS_SUFFIX_RE: Matches the virtual name discovery gives an SFC's extracted script (Button.vue -> Button.vue.ts).
keyExports.TYPESCRIPT_DECLARATION_EXTENSION: '.d.ts' — stripped longest-first by the id mint so global.d.ts does not become global.d; the resolver tries it only after implementation extensions.
keyExports.TYPESCRIPT_INDEX_BASENAMES: ['index'] — basenames that stand for their own directory.
keyExports.TYPESCRIPT_JS_EXTENSIONS: ['.js', '.jsx', '.mjs', '.cjs'] — JavaScript forms, tried after the TypeScript ones and after .d.ts.
keyExports.TYPESCRIPT_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS: Union of the two lists above.
keyExports.TYPESCRIPT_TS_EXTENSIONS: ['.ts', '.tsx', '.mts', '.cts'] — TypeScript source forms, in module-resolver preference order.

assumptions: SFC extensions (.vue/.svelte) reach discovery through their own walk (sfc-extractor.ts) and keep their own module id, so they stay out of TYPESCRIPT_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS by design, not omission.

annotation.summary: Per-package TypeScript extraction (Pass 2): builds a bounded ts-morph Project (node_modules module/type-reference resolution blocked), loads each pending module's source, and either reuses a prior module's semantic delta unchanged (content-hash hit) or re-extracts imports/exports/semantic hints via the AST.

keyExports.ExtractPackageInput: Input shape for extractPackage (pkg, pkgModules, prevByAbsPath, compilerOptions, absPathToId, packages, repoRoot, sourceByModuleId)
keyExports.createTypeScriptExtractionProject: Creates the ts-morph Project used for extraction: skipAddingFilesFromTsConfig, skipLoadingLibFiles, and a resolutionHost that excludes node_modules resolutions
keyExports.extractPackage: Classifies each pending module as cache-hit (content hash unchanged) vs miss, extracts AST deltas for misses, re-resolves import/export edges for hits (reuseDelta), returns ExtractPackageResult

assumptions: The engine has already read and content-hashed every module's source (sourceByModuleId); this plugin never reads files or fingerprints them itself.
A cache-hit module still re-resolves its import/export edges against the current build's path map, since resolution can change even when file content didn't.

sideEffects.description: console.warn on a package Project-creation failure or a per-module AST extraction error (degrades to a bare imports-only delta rather than dropping the module)

annotation.summary: TypeScript source-plugin helper that walks a ts.SourceFile's top-level statements with the raw TS AST (no ts-morph resolver) to collect static import declarations and barrel re-export declarations.

keyExports.collectImports: Walks ts.ImportDeclaration statements, extracts default/namespace/named imported names and type-only flag, resolves each specifier via resolveSpecifierFromMap
keyExports.collectReExports: Walks `export ... from` ts.ExportDeclaration statements (star / namespace / named), resolves the specifier, and skips local `export { a }` (no `from`)

assumptions: Only static import/export syntax is considered; dynamic import() calls are not collected here.

annotation.summary: Lazy loader/cache for the heavy TypeScript extract chunk (ts-morph and AST helpers), so a Python-only scan never loads ts-morph at runtime.

keyExports.isExtractModuleLoaded: () => boolean; true once the extract chunk has been requested (for tests/diagnostics)
keyExports.loadExtractModule: () => Promise<ExtractModule>; dynamic-imports './extract.js' once per process and caches the resulting module/promise for subsequent calls
keyExports.resetExtractModuleCache: () => void; clears the cached module/promise, for isolated tests

assumptions: typescript/index.ts must not statically import ./extract.js, or Python-only scans would load ts-morph anyway

sideEffects.description: module-scoped extractModule/extractModulePromise cache persists across calls within a process

risks: typescript/index.ts must keep avoiding a static import of ./extract.js; adding one would defeat the lazy split and load ts-morph on Python-only scans.

annotation.summary: Parses a TypeScript package's tsconfig.json (plus same-package referenced project fragments) into its resolved fileNames and compilerOptions, supplementing an entry-only file list (main/index/polyfills/server/app configs pointing at few files) with a full src/ directory walk.

keyExports.ParsedPackageTsConfig: { fileNames: string[]; compilerOptions: ts.CompilerOptions } — result shape shared by both exports.
keyExports.parsePackageTsConfig: Reads pkgAbsPath/tsconfig.json; when its own fileNames list is empty, merges fileNames from followed project references; then supplements an entry-only result with a raw walk of pkgAbsPath/src for TypeScript source extensions.

assumptions: A project reference is followed only when it resolves inside the package dir, is not a .spec/.test/.e2e config, and (for a non-.json ref path) does not itself contain a nested tsconfig.json.
An entry-only file list (<=3 files, each matching main/index/polyfills/server/app basenames) triggers the src/ walk supplement; test/spec files are excluded from that walk.

sideEffects.description: ts.readConfigFile, fs.existsSync, and walkRepository over the package's src directory

annotation.summary: Reads a static string module specifier from a TypeScript import/export expression, working around ts-morph's throwing string-literal-only getters.
