keyExports.importDeclarationSpecifier: (imp: ImportDeclaration) => string | undefined; reads imp.compilerNode.moduleSpecifier via staticModuleSpecifierText
keyExports.staticModuleSpecifierText: (specifier: ts.Expression) => string | undefined; returns the literal text for a string literal or no-substitution template literal, undefined otherwise

assumptions: Dynamic or computed import specifiers are skipped (return undefined), not resolved

annotation.summary: Discovers a TypeScript/JS repository's packages by walking directories for any of the caller-supplied marker files, reading package.json for name/version when present, and returning the list sorted by repoRelDir.

keyExports.discoverPackages: Walks repoRoot for directories containing a marker file, reads package.json (name/version) or derives a path slug, dedupes by normalized POSIX path, returns packages sorted by compareCodeUnits(repoRelDir)

assumptions: markers is required, not defaulted — the caller must declare what names a package root.

sideEffects.description: fs.existsSync/readFileSync/readDirSorted while walking the repo tree for marker files and package.json

annotation.summary: Built-in TypeScript/JavaScript source plugin. discover() delegates to discoverTypeScript (tsconfig walk, incl. SFC extensions); extract() lazy-loads the ts-morph extraction chunk (lazy-extract.js) and runs it per npm-scoped package with that package's parsed tsconfig compilerOptions. Declares TS/JS + SFC extensions, the uiSurfaces capability, and moduleIdNormalize (strips .d.ts/source extensions, recognizes index basenames).

keyExports.TypeScriptExtractContext: Opaque per-package extractContext type: Map<packageName, ts.CompilerOptions>.
keyExports.default: typescriptSourcePlugin — the built-in TS/JS defineSourcePlugin descriptor (id 'typescript').

assumptions: ts-morph and the 'typescript' package load lazily inside extract() only, never at discover() time or module load.

annotation.summary: String-based TypeScript module-specifier resolver for the source plugin's Pass-1 file map: resolves relative imports, tsconfig `paths` aliases, and workspace bare/sub-path specifiers directly against absPathToId, avoiding ts-morph's full module resolution (which would load shared dependencies into the Project).

keyExports.PathsContext: { compilerOptions: ts.CompilerOptions } — the importer package's parsed tsconfig, required to resolve tsconfig `paths` aliases.
keyExports.SpecifierResolution: { resolvedModuleId: string | undefined; isExternal: boolean } — result shape returned by resolveSpecifierFromMap.
keyExports.isNodeModulesPath: True when a path contains a node_modules segment.
keyExports.resolveSpecifierFromMap: Resolves one specifier in order: relative (with NodeNext .js->.ts stripping), tsconfig paths, workspace bare (-> package entry/barrel or pkg: node), workspace sub-path, else isExternal:true; returns undefined only for an unresolved relative specifier.

assumptions: RESOLVE_SUFFIX_LADDER order (TS extensions, then .d.ts, then JS extensions) is load-bearing: a .d.ts resolving ahead of its .ts would send every import to the declaration file instead of the implementation.

node_modules paths are blocked in createPathResolutionHost's exists() so tsconfig-paths resolution never walks a large monorepo's installed dependency tree (the documented source of a prior build OOM).

sideEffects.description: createPathResolutionHost falls back to ts.sys.fileExists/realpath beyond the in-memory absPathToId map when resolving tsconfig paths

risks: The suffix-ladder order and the node_modules short-circuit are both load-bearing for correctness and for avoiding the prior build OOM; reordering RESOLVE_SUFFIX_LADDER or removing the node_modules block silently changes resolution results.

annotation.summary: Collects a TypeScript/JSX source file's full SemanticHints bundle in one pass over its ts-morph SourceFile: routes across several frameworks (React Router, TanStack Router, Angular, NestJS, file-based, Fastify), env-var accesses read strictly off the syntax tree, conditional JSX renders, runtime actions, security signals, UI hints, and SSR markers (directives, Next/Remix data-fetching exports, Qwik macros).

keyExports.collectSemanticHints: (sf, relativeFilePath?) => SemanticHints | undefined; returns undefined when nothing was detected; a backend framework wins the single webFramework slot in priority fastify > nestjs > react-router > tanstack-router.

assumptions: Env-var names are read only from syntax-tree shapes (process.env.X, process.env['X'], import.meta.env.X, and destructured `{ PORT } = process.env`), never from .env files; a computed key (process.env[EXPR]) yields no name rather than a guessed one.
A `use server`/`use client` directive is detected only when it is the file's first statement, skipping a leading BOM, shebang, and comments.
risks: Qwik macro detection (routeLoader$/routeAction$/server$) matches by regex over source text excluding literals and comments; a macro name assembled dynamically (e.g. string concatenation) is not detected.

annotation.summary: Extracts TypeScript source from Vue (.vue) and Svelte (.svelte) single-file components via regex, since ts-morph cannot parse SFC wrappers directly — letting the rest of the pipeline treat SFC script blocks as plain .ts.

keyExports.ExtractedScript: { ts: string; isTypeScript: boolean } — ts is '' when the file has no script block; isTypeScript reflects a lang="ts"/"tsx"/"typescript" (or Svelte type="text/typescript") attribute
keyExports.SFC_EXTENSIONS: Set of extensions treated as SFC, sourced from SFC_EXTENSION_LIST
keyExports.extractTypeScriptFromSfc: Dispatches to a Vue or Svelte extractor by extension; null for a non-SFC extension
keyExports.isSfcFile: True when the file extension is a known SFC extension (caller must check before calling extractTypeScriptFromSfc)

assumptions: Vue: concatenates a regular <script> and a <script setup> block if both exist, setup second so its identifiers can shadow the regular script; a <template> block is appended as a hidden __REPOVINE_SFC_TEMPLATE__ const hint
Svelte: concatenates <script> and <script context="module"> blocks; template markup (non-script content) is likewise hinted
risks: Regex-based by design tradeoff for zero external deps: non-standard syntax such as Vue 3.3+ `<script setup generic="...">` with unusual whitespace may be missed.

annotation.summary: Small ts-morph helper utilities: narrowing a Node to its underlying function-like declaration, and normalizing a ts-morph type string for display.

keyExports.getFunctionNode: Returns the node itself if it's a FunctionDeclaration, or the initializer if it's a VariableDeclaration initialized directly to an ArrowFunction/FunctionExpression; undefined otherwise
keyExports.normalizeType: Strips ts-morph's import("..."). qualifier prefixes from a type text, then shortens it to maxLength (default 150) via shortenText

assumptions: getFunctionNode only unwraps one level of indirection (a variable declaration's direct initializer); it does not follow further aliasing
annotation.integrationPoints: Imports shortenText from @repovine/plugin-sdk's package entry (src/index).

annotation.summary: Formats TypeScript type/parameter/return-type text strictly from source syntax (ts-morph node.getTypeNode()/getReturnTypeNode()), never invoking the TypeChecker.

keyExports.functionTypeLabel: Formats '(params): returnType' or '(params)' when returnType is undefined
keyExports.paramTypeLabel: Formats 'name: type' or bare 'name' when type is undefined
keyExports.syntaxReturnTypeText: Return-type annotation text of a function node via getReturnTypeNode(), same normalization
keyExports.syntaxTypeText: Type annotation text of a node via getTypeNode(), normalized by ts-utils normalizeType; undefined when no annotation is present

annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates text normalization to mod:@repovine/plugin-source-typescript/src/ts-utils (normalizeType)

annotation.summary: Standalone Node script (built-ins only, no npm) run inside the egress-gw container: terminates plaintext HTTP from the worker on loopback and re-originates over HTTPS to api.anthropic.com and api.telegram.org with the real credential injected here, plus a raw byte-pipe local-model forward to host.docker.internal.
assumptions: Real secrets (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN preferred over ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) are read once from the egress-gw container env and never logged or forwarded to the worker.

The local-model forward listener is always up; fail-closed comes from the default-deny OUTPUT firewall chain, not this listener — the destination is unreachable until EGRESS_ALLOW_HOST_DOCKER_INTERNAL=1 / EGRESS_ALLOW_CIDRS allow-lists it.
*_UPSTREAM_PORT / *_UPSTREAM_INSECURE env knobs let the proxy target an on-prem endpoint or a local mock instead of the default HTTPS:443 upstream.

sideEffects.description: re-originates HTTP(S) requests to api.anthropic.com and api.telegram.org with the real credential injected
opens 4 loopback listeners (anthropic proxy, telegram proxy, health check, local-model forward) via http.createServer/net.createServer
registers SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that call process.exit(0)

risks.text: The Telegram chat_id/from_chat_id pinning against TELEGRAM_RECIPIENT_IDS and the Anthropic credential-injection are the sole boundary keeping upstream secrets and message recipients out of the worker container; an in-place change to this proxy must preserve both fail-closed checks exactly.

risks: Content-delivering Telegram methods with an unparseable JSON/urlencoded/multipart body, or with no chat_id at all, are denied (400/403) rather than forwarded; TELEGRAM_READONLY must stay in sync with which methods genuinely carry no chat_id.

annotation.summary: Role resolution for the harness's sub-agent roles: a per-process-immutable role catalog (bundled specialists in sandbox mode; project-owned roles from `repovine agents roles` in attach mode when agents.roles is configured), role prompt loading from lib/agents/*.md (or HARNESS_AGENTS_DIR override), and mapping between planner role labels, repovine manifest names, and Delivery Protocol roles.

keyExports.agentsMode: 'single' | 'auto' | 'keyword', from the AGENTS env var (defaults to 'single').
keyExports.appFrameRoles: The full-stack frame's default role set; HARNESS_APP_FRAME overrides (0/none/off disables, a comma list replaces it).
keyExports.initRoleCatalog: Builds and installs the process catalog once; attach mode with configured project roles replaces bundled specialists (utility roles stay); a project role id that shadows a harness-reserved utility role throws; re-init with a different catalog key throws.
keyExports.isKnownRole: Membership check against the active catalog.
keyExports.knownRoles: Role ids in the active catalog.
keyExports.loadRolePrompt: Loads a role's prompt prose; a project role serves its repository-owned prose byte-for-byte, a bundled role reads lib/agents/*.md and strips YAML frontmatter.
keyExports.protocolRoleForSpec: Maps a sub-agent spec's manifest name (or contextPhase as fallback) to the Delivery Protocol role enum (main/explorer/implementer/annotation-writer/architecture-auditor/code-reviewer); unknown falls back to implementer.
keyExports.resetRoleCatalogForTests: Test seam that drops the installed catalog.
keyExports.resolveRole: Resolves a full sub-agent spec (scope, manifest, prompt, contextPhase, modelRole, roleSource) for a role, with per-task overrides.
keyExports.roleCatalog: Returns the active process catalog, or the bundled one if uninitialized.
keyExports.roleRequiresTests: Whether a role's implementer must ship test source files; HARNESS_REQUIRE_TESTS_ROLES (comma list or 'none') overrides the catalog default.
keyExports.rolesFromMentions: Full-id @mention matches against the active catalog (no prefix stripping; skips 'default').

assumptions: UTILITY_ROLE_IDS (default, review, repo-explorer, annotation-writer) are harness-reserved and always present in every catalog.
The active catalog is resolved once per process and treated as immutable; identical re-init is a no-op, a differing re-init throws.
Project roles in attach mode come from `repovine agents roles` (the agents-namespace CLI), not the Delivery Protocol surface.

sideEffects.description: reads role prompt .md files from lib/agents/ or HARNESS_AGENTS_DIR
module-level activeCatalog/activeCatalogKey, init-once per process

annotation.integrationPoints: protocolRoleForSpec's return value must land in the Delivery Protocol role enum the core AgentAssignment schema validates against; an id added to MANIFEST_PROTOCOL_ROLE without a matching schema enum value fails assignment validation downstream. Project roles are sourced via lib/repovine.mjs projectRoles() (`repovine agents roles`).
annotation.dataFlow: targetMode + optional projectRoles -> initRoleCatalog builds the immutable catalog -> resolveRole/loadRolePrompt/manifestForRole read it -> sub-agent spec (scope, manifest, prompt, protocol role).

envDependencies.AGENTS: Selects mention-matching mode: single | auto | keyword (default single).
envDependencies.HARNESS_AGENTS_DIR: Overrides the directory bundled role prompts (lib/agents/*.md) are read from.
envDependencies.HARNESS_APP_FRAME: Overrides the app-frame default role set (0/none/off disables; a comma list replaces it).
envDependencies.HARNESS_REQUIRE_TESTS_ROLES: Overrides which roles require shipped test files (comma list, or 'none').

annotation.summary: Read-only /ask entrypoint: routes a question to the local or claude ask runner (same repovine MCP + read-tool stack as /task, no Delivery Protocol result contract) and chunks long replies for Telegram.

keyExports.runAsk: Validates the question and provider, dynamically imports workers/ask-local.mjs or workers/ask-claude.mjs, and forwards to that runner's runAsk with a generated or provided contextSessionId
keyExports.splitForTelegram: Splits text into <=TELEGRAM_TEXT_MAX chunks preferring paragraph, then line, then word breaks

assumptions: provider resolves via resolveProvider/isSupportedProvider to only 'local' or 'claude'; an unsupported LLM_PROVIDER returns { ok: false } rather than throwing
annotation.integrationPoints: Dynamically imports mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/workers/ask-local or lib/workers/ask-claude per provider; resolveProvider/isSupportedProvider come from lib/workers (index)

annotation.summary: Converts an internal task object (from the queue / Telegram / an issue) into the harness-facing AgentAssignment envelope (Delivery Protocol v1) that repovine schema-validates before dispatch.

keyExports.buildAssignment: Builds the AgentAssignment object: protocolVersion '1', runId, role (default 'main'), task, scope, version (default 1), acceptanceCriteria via toAcceptanceCriteria, constraints, contracts coerced to string[] via toContractStrings, requestedChecks, plus optional delivery/verificationPolicy/contextSession passthrough when the task carries them.
keyExports.toAcceptanceCriteria: Normalizes a task's acceptanceCriteria — bare strings or already-structural { id, statement, required, kind? } objects — into AcceptanceCriterion[], minting a stable `c${i+1}` id for the bare-string form.

assumptions: contracts must end up as string[]: a prior sub-agent's contractsChanged or a planner-emitted contract object is coerced through toContractStrings so it cannot fail the AgentAssignment schema gate before the sub-agent runs.
annotation.integrationPoints: Schema source of truth is repovine/src/agents/protocol.ts's AgentAssignmentSchema; this builder's output shape must satisfy that schema.

annotation.summary: Attach-mode Git pointer constants (Phase 2): the fixed gitdir: pointer bytes the host launcher writes and the in-container attach validation byte-compares against, so a container attaches to the launch-scoped disposable repo instead of the source repo's real .git.

keyExports.ATTACH_BASELINE_REF: Const 'attach-baseline' — tag the launcher pins on the baseline commit; reset-to-baseline resolves it.
keyExports.ATTACH_GIT_POINTER_CONTENT: The exact string 'gitdir: /state/git\n' written under $HARNESS_ATTACH_STATE_DIR/control/git-guard and mounted read-only at /workspace/.git.
keyExports.ATTACH_STATE_GIT_DIR: Const '/state/git' — container path of the disposable repo the pointer targets.

assumptions: The read-only mount of /workspace/.git is what keeps an in-container agent from repointing it to a different repo.

risks.text: ATTACH_GIT_POINTER_CONTENT is a byte-exact spec constant shared by the host launcher (writer) and in-container attach validation (byte-comparer); changing it in only one place breaks attach validation.

annotation.summary: Filters advisory out-of-scope infra blockers (e.g. docker-compose noise outside a subAgent's assignment) from real run-gate failures.

keyExports.filterHardBlockers: (blockers, scopeHints) => blockers with out-of-scope-infra entries removed
keyExports.isOutOfScopeInfraBlocker: (text, scopeHints) => true when text matches the OUT_OF_SCOPE_INFRA pattern and scopeHints does not include '.' or 'infra'
keyExports.subAgentGateEffectivelyOk: (subAgent) => true when a non-ok subAgent still delivered files and every recorded blocker is out-of-scope infra noise

risks: OUT_OF_SCOPE_INFRA regex hardcodes the recognized phrasings (docker-compose.yml, 'outside ... sub-agent/scope', repo-wide validate_annotations wording); a differently worded blocker will not be filtered.

annotation.summary: HTTP transport for the demo LangGraph orchestrator: a Telegram-free curl-drivable handle exposing GET /status, POST /goal (alias /task), POST /ask and POST /reset, with optional bearer auth and single in-flight episode/ask guards.

keyExports.startHttp: ({ graph, port = 8080, host = '0.0.0.0', token = '', provider, repoRoot, target }) => Promise<http.Server>. GET /status reports provider/agents/busy flags (workspace + telemetry withheld unless authorized). POST /goal|/task runs invokeGraph and reports ok/status/replyText/telemetry (runSucceeded: ok && status in ['complete','partial'], or every subAgent ok+complete/partial in multi mode). POST /ask now calls ensureTarget(resolvedTarget) before running (lazily restores the sandbox/attach target since /ask bypasses /goal's intake and /reset can leave the workspace empty; failure replies 500 before askBusy is set), then runs runAsk with per-thread session continuity (payload.thread, default 'default'). POST /reset requires {confirm:true} and idle state, else 409/400; reapAll + resetTarget + clears askThreads.

assumptions: MAX_BODY_BYTES caps the JSON request body at 1 MiB (1 << 20); an oversized body is rejected with 413.
Auth: authorized(req) passes when no token is configured, or Authorization header equals `Bearer <token>`; unauthenticated POST returns 401.
episodeBusy/askBusy are single in-process flags — only one /goal and one /ask run at a time regardless of caller.
A resetAllowed:false target policy refuses /reset before the confirm/busy checks, returning code ATTACH_RESET_DISABLED.
handleAsk's ensureTarget call is idempotent/non-destructive when the sandbox already exists and re-validates (never seeds) an attach workspace.

sideEffects.description: hosts a node:http server bound to host:port, handling GET /status and POST /goal, /ask, /reset.
handleReset() calls reapAll(repoRoot) to kill leftover worker-bound servers/containers before resetTarget wipes the sandbox.
in-memory askThreads Map plus episodeBusy/askBusy flags track per-thread /ask continuity and single-flight state for the process lifetime.

risks: authorized() compares the Authorization header to `Bearer <token>` with plain string equality (no constant-time compare); HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN is expected to run behind an isolated net/localhost bind per the startup log guidance, not as the only defense on an open network.

risks.text: handleReset() 409s while episodeBusy or askBusy but does not abort the in-flight episode/ask; the caller holding that /goal or /ask must close its own request before a retried /reset can proceed.

annotation.dataFlow: GET /status -> liveness+busy flags (+ workspace/telemetry if authorized); POST /goal|/task -> handleTask -> invokeGraph(graph, {task, repoRoot, targetMode, llmProvider}, {threadId, signal}) -> {ok, status, replyText, telemetry, turn, graphNodesTouched}; POST /ask -> handleAsk -> ensureTarget then runAsk(question, repoRoot, provider, {resume, contextSessionId}) -> {answer, contextSessionId, thread, sessionId}; POST /reset -> handleReset -> reapAll + resetTarget + askThreads.clear().

annotation.summary: Telegram transport for the demo LangGraph orchestrator: raw HTTPS long-polling (zero extra deps) that maps /goal (alias /task), /ask, /stop, /status, /new and /reset to invokeGraph/runAsk, running one background episode per chat plus a separately resumable /ask dialog.

keyExports.ATTACHMENTS_ROOT: const = path.join('.harness', 'attachments') — base dir for downloaded chat photos, split per flow into task/ and ask/ subdirs so a /task and a concurrent /ask never clear each other's files.
keyExports.startTelegram: ({ graph, token, allowedIds, provider, repoRoot, target }) => runs the getUpdates long-poll loop against a compiled graph. Only /goal and /ask invoke the agent; /help /new /reset /stop /status are fast paths that never run the graph. startAsk() now calls ensureTarget(resolvedTarget) before answering (lazily restores the sandbox/attach target since /ask bypasses /goal's graph intake and /reset can leave the workspace empty). One active run per chat (activeRuns); a photo caption carries the command/text via msg.caption.
keyExports.telegramResetPlan: (policy) => { action: 'confirm' } when policy.resetAllowed, else { action: 'refuse', reply } (attach mode: worktree is host-managed, refuses with docker:down guidance).

assumptions: Only allowlisted sender ids (allowedIds) are served; others are silently dropped (logged as IGNORED).

TELEGRAM_API_BASE defaults to https://api.telegram.org; in the hardened Docker path it points at the egress-gw custody proxy (plain http, injects the real token, pins the outbound chat_id) — http vs https follows the base scheme.
HARNESS_HEARTBEAT_FILE defaults to /tmp/harness-tg-bot.alive; the poll loop touches it every iteration so a container healthcheck can detect a wedged loop.

startAsk() calls ensureTarget(resolvedTarget) before each /ask turn: idempotent/non-destructive when the sandbox already exists, re-validates the workspace in attach mode; a throw here (e.g. attach validation failure) replies '❌ Ask workspace initialization failed' and returns before activeAsks is set.
/stop aborts the in-flight run but does not preserve LLM worker sessions for the next /task — each /task starts fresh provider sessions.

sideEffects.description: calls the Telegram Bot API (sendMessage, getUpdates, getFile, answerCallbackQuery, getMe) over the configured TELEGRAM_API_BASE.
writes the heartbeat file every poll iteration and downloaded photos under repoRoot/.harness/attachments/<task|ask>/; fs.rmSync clears a flow's attachment dir on task start/new/photo-replace.
doReset() calls reapAll(repoRoot) to kill any servers/containers a prior worker left bound before wiping the workspace.
per-chat in-memory Maps (threadGen, pendingReset, activeRuns, askSessions, sessionGen, activeAsks) track thread generation, active runs, and /ask session continuity for the process lifetime.

risks: doReset() bounds stopAndWait/stopAskAndWait at STOP_GRACE_MS (30s) before reapAll + resetTarget wipe the workspace; a worker that ignores abort past that window can still be writing when the wipe runs.
extractPhoto() only accepts the largest Telegram photo size or an image/* document; other attachment types (video, audio, generic files) are silently dropped with no chat reply.
annotation.dataFlow: getUpdates poll loop -> handleMessage routes by command: /goal|/task -> startTask -> invokeGraph(graph, {chatId, task, repoRoot, targetMode, llmProvider}, {threadId, signal}) -> reply via sendLong; /ask -> startAsk -> ensureTarget then runAsk(question, repoRoot, provider, {resume, contextSessionId, attachments}) -> reply via sendLong; /reset -> doReset -> stopAndWait/stopAskAndWait + reapAll + resetTarget.

envDependencies.HARNESS_HEARTBEAT_FILE: poll-loop heartbeat file path (default /tmp/harness-tg-bot.alive) touched every getUpdates iteration for the container healthcheck.
envDependencies.TELEGRAM_API_BASE: Bot API base URL (default https://api.telegram.org); in the hardened Docker path points at the egress-gw custody proxy over plain http.

annotation.summary: Provider worker built on the Claude Agent SDK: launches repovine as a scoped MCP server, prompts Claude to gather context and edit files, extracts the model's AgentRunResult JSON block, and normalizes it into a schema-valid, phase-consistent result (the graph still runs it through `repovine delivery compliance`).

keyExports.extractResultObject: Pulls the AgentRunResult object out of the model's final text: last fenced ```json block first, then whole-text JSON, then a best-effort {...} slice
keyExports.normalizeResult: Wraps the model's parsed claims in a schema-valid AgentRunResult envelope: forces status/scope/contextSessionId linkage, coerces contractsChanged via toContractStrings, and force-strips phase-inappropriate fields (review unless briefName is repovine-code-reviewer; deliveryVerification unless phase==='explore'; annotationsClean forced false for readOnly/implement phases)
keyExports.runAgent: Resolves auth, builds the system prompt (policy + harness brief), spawns the query() SDK call with the repovine MCP stdio server and an abort timeout, then extracts and normalizes the result
keyExports.supportsResume: true — declares this adapter supports the Agent SDK resume option for retries
keyExports.toContractStrings: Coerces non-string contract entries (e.g. structured {path,method,request}) to compact JSON strings so a malformed contract survives as text instead of breaking the run
keyExports.userPrompt: Builds the task/runId/scope/acceptanceCriteria/constraints/contracts/requestedChecks message, restating full assignment fields even when resuming (a resumed conversation may hold a different sub-agent)

assumptions: Auth is ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (checked via workers/auth.mjs); CLAUDE_AGENT_MAX_TURNS defaults to 40, CLAUDE_AGENT_VERBOSE defaults on (only '0' silences the per-tool trace)
The graph re-validates every returned result through `repovine delivery compliance`; the model is never trusted blindly.

sideEffects.description: invokes the Claude Agent SDK query() call (Anthropic API) with the repovine MCP stdio server attached
appends per-tool trace lines to a debug file when HARNESS_WORKER_STDERR is set
buildRepovineMcpStdio spawns the repovine MCP server as a child process for the SDK to talk to

risks: normalizeResult's compliance/optional-artifact stripping is keyed on assignment.contextSession.phase (explore/implement/annotate) and briefName ('repovine-code-reviewer'); adding a new phase or manifest name without updating these branches silently mis-strips or mis-preserves review/deliveryVerification/annotationsClean.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates the shared brief/policy text to mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/workers/prompt (resolveHarnessBrief, policyForAssignment, attachmentsBrief) and MCP tool wiring to lib/workers/mcp (REPOVINE_WORKER_MCP_TOOLS, buildRepovineMcpStdio); the normalized result is re-validated by `repovine delivery compliance`.
annotation.dataFlow: task + assignment -> userPrompt + system brief -> Claude Agent SDK query() with repovine MCP -> model final text -> extractResultObject -> normalizeResult -> schema-valid AgentRunResult.

envDependencies.CLAUDE_AGENT_MAX_TURNS: Caps the SDK agent's turn count (default 40).
envDependencies.CLAUDE_AGENT_VERBOSE: Per-tool trace on unless set to '0'.
envDependencies.HARNESS_WORKER_STDERR: When set, per-tool trace lines are appended to a debug file.

annotation.summary: Structured acceptance criteria and delivery-verification helpers for the demo harness: orient records sharpened criteria before implementation, and the read-only verify sub-agent's coverage claims are checked against them and against observable repository state.

keyExports.AcceptanceCriterion: JSDoc typedef: { id: string, statement: string, required: boolean }.
keyExports.buildOrientTrail: Compact orient trail (query, summary, touched graph nodes, suggested scopes, criteria, mcp tools used, contextSessionId) for assignment injection and the human reply.
keyExports.buildVerificationPolicy: Builds { assuranceProfile: 'repository', version, requirements } since this demo's verify phase is read-only and only produces repository-anchor evidence.
keyExports.criterionIdFromStatement: Stable short slug id (`c-<slug>`, or `c-<index+1>` when the slug is empty) minted from a criterion statement.
keyExports.deliveryVerificationAccepted: Fail-closed acceptance: false unless verdict.intentVerified is exactly true AND every required criterion has a `covered` result.
keyExports.inferCriteriaFromTask: Default single criterion (id 'c-user-request') built from the user task text when orient emitted none.
keyExports.mergeCriteria: Merges orient criteria with the user-task fallback, deduped by id.
keyExports.mergeCriteriaResults: Rolls criteria + their verifier results into a display list; an un-resulted criterion shows status 'pending' (display-only — the protocol's own CriterionResult.status is covered|gap|needs-developer).
keyExports.parseAcceptanceCriteria: Parses orient's contractsChanged entries ({ id?, statement, required?, kind? }, object or JSON string) into AcceptanceCriterion[]; skips non-JSON/statement-less entries; dedupes by id.
keyExports.scopesFromGraphNodes: Suggested implement scopes (infra/pkg-or-mod top segment) derived from graph node ids.

assumptions: A criterion's `kind` is 'invariant' (advisory, required:false, exempt from the change-set check) ONLY when orient tagged it explicitly ({"kind":"invariant"}); no prose heuristic classifies it, so a regression guard defaults to 'delivery' (required) rather than being silently exempted.
risks: deliveryVerificationAccepted returns false (not an error) on any malformed or incomplete input — a verifier that omits a required criterion's result silently fails acceptance rather than surfacing why.

annotation.summary: Parses a minimal KEY=value .env file and merges it into process.env, without overriding a non-empty existing value.

keyExports.loadEnvFile: Reads `file` (returns [] silently if unreadable), parses KEY=value lines (skips blank/#-comment lines, strips matching quote pairs), and for each key sets process.env[key] only when it is currently unset or empty; returns the list of key names encountered.

assumptions: An empty-string existing env value is treated as unset (not just undefined) so docker compose `${VAR:-}` placeholders get filled from the file.
An operator's explicit non-empty env value always wins over the file's value.

sideEffects.description: mutates process.env for keys that are unset or empty
fs.readFileSync(file)

annotation.summary: Walks parent directories from startDir looking for a marker file/dir, returning the containing directory (or null), used instead of a fixed-depth '../..' resolve that would break if the demo were relocated.

keyExports.findUp: (startDir, marker) => directory containing marker (checked via fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, marker))), walking up via path.dirname until the filesystem root; returns null if no ancestor has it; never throws

assumptions: marker is a relative file/dir path joined onto each candidate ancestor directory

sideEffects.description: fs.existsSync checks against each ancestor directory

annotation.summary: Read-only assembly of prior-run contracts (invariants/risks/sideEffects) from repovine.annots.json for the verify subAgent, so verification checks contracts recorded by earlier runs even if the current orient did not restate them.

keyExports.collectAnnotationObligations: (repoRoot, nodeIds, { maxItems=24, snapshot=null }) => deduped [{nodeId, kind, text}] pulled from each id's invariants/risks/sideEffects, capped at maxItems
keyExports.obligationsSection: (obligations) => markdown task section instructing the verify subAgent to add an OBLIGATION: preserved|violated line per item
keyExports.readAnnotationsSnapshot: (repoRoot) => run-start snapshot of the annotation store, read from repovine.annots.json

assumptions: repovine.annots.json is either { annotations: {...} } or a flat id-keyed map; a missing or malformed file yields {} rather than throwing

sideEffects.description: reads and JSON-parses repovine.annots.json from repoRoot

risks: The snapshot is captured once at run start; if a sub-agent writes annotations mid-run via write_annotation, obligations still reflect the pre-sync state, not the mid-run write. The annots store itself is never written from here — the write path stays MCP-only.

annotation.summary: Deterministic 'referenced artifact exists' floor: scans compose files and shallow tsconfigs for declared file references, plus two contract checks (npm ci without a lockfile, import.meta.env without a vite/client type reference), and reports missing targets as fix-ledger blockers.

keyExports.missingReferencedArtifacts: (repoRoot) => string[] of 'referenced artifact missing: ...' blockers, covering compose dockerfile:/env_file: refs, tsconfig extends, Dockerfiles running npm ci without a lockfile, and TS source using import.meta.env without a vite/client type reference

assumptions: Tolerant line-level regex parsing, not a YAML parser, since compose/tsconfig files are agent-authored with conventional formatting; a parsing miss produces a false negative, never a false blocker
env_file long-map entries with required: false are skipped (compose's sanctioned optional-env pattern); required: true or an absent required keeps the reference
Package dirs are the repo root plus directories one level deep that contain a package.json; tsconfig scan is likewise shallow (root + one level)

sideEffects.description: fs.readFileSync/readdirSync/existsSync over docker-compose*.yml, compose.yaml, tsconfig*.json, Dockerfile, and src/**/*.tsx? files under repoRoot and its one-level package dirs

annotation.summary: LangGraph run-status and review-gate logic for the delivery-protocol harness demo. Computes review freshness/acceptance (reviewIsFresh, reviewProcessValid, reviewAcceptedOf, reviewGateIsOpen), grades plan findings (gradePlanFindings), rolls sub-agent/runtime/review/verification outcomes into the final run status (deriveMultiRunStatus), and multiAgent(state, config) drives the actual LangGraph stage loop: worktree or sequential sub-agent execution, review/fix gating, runtime check, verify-claims, and annotation-sync target collection.

keyExports.annotationSyncTargets: Collects the scopes annotation-sync sub-agents must cover after implementation.
keyExports.deriveMultiRunStatus: Rolls up sub-agent/runtime/review/verification outcomes plus plan grading into the final run status.
keyExports.markReviewedRevision: Persists the reviewed workspace revision (writeJsonFile) so a later review can check freshness against it.
keyExports.multiAgent: Top-level orchestrator: plans stages, runs sub-agents (worktree or sequential), gates review/fix, runs the runtime check and verify-claims phases.
keyExports.reviewGateIsOpen: True when the last review sub-agent accepted, or a post-fix review supersedes an earlier reject.

assumptions: Review/fix/annotation-sync gating reads env flags HARNESS_PLAN_REVIEW, HARNESS_POST_FIX_REVIEW, HARNESS_POST_REVIEW_ANNOTATIONS, HARNESS_REVIEW_FIX.
Built-in repovine manifest names (via `repovine delivery manifests`) drive the per-sub-agent required-result fields the compliance gate checks.

sideEffects.description: markReviewedRevision writes the reviewed-revision JSON via writeJsonFile
multiAgent runs sub-agents via runStageWorktrees/runStageSequential
captureWorkspaceRevision/ensureGitRepo/diffChangedFiles shell out to git
runStageWorktrees runs a stage's sub-agents in parallel git worktrees

risks: useWorktreeExecution's greenfield-vs-worktree choice depends on lib/target-repo's git/workspace state being set up for the chosen mode.
annotation.integrationPoints: Runs sub-agents via lib/graph/sub-agent; retry classification via lib/graph/retry; repovine orient/verify phases via lib/graph/repovine-process; graph rebuild barriers via lib/repovine refreshGraph (`repovine build`); role/manifest data via lib/agents.
annotation.dataFlow: state + config -> plan stages -> runStageWorktrees/Sequential(sub-agents) -> review/fix gate -> runtime check -> verify-claims -> deriveMultiRunStatus rolls outcomes into the final status.

envDependencies.HARNESS_POST_FIX_REVIEW: Enables a post-fix review pass that can supersede an earlier reject.

annotation.summary: LangGraph node functions for the delivery-protocol harness demo run: intake (resolve provider/target from env, prepare the run, extract the user task), buildAssignmentNode/validateAssignmentNode (build + validate the AgentAssignment via lib/repovine), runSubAgent (invoke a worker, persist usage, reconcile retry context), persistResult/validateResultNode (write + validate the sub-agent result), complianceNode (compute delivery-protocol compliance + MCP metrics), runtimeCheckNode (run the runtime-check phase), plus reply-formatting helpers (formatReply, composeReply, clipText, subAgentBriefSummary).

keyExports.buildAssignmentNode: Builds the AgentAssignment and writes it to subAgentAssignmentPath.
keyExports.complianceNode: Computes rp.compliance()/MCP metrics for a sub-agent and writes them to subAgentMcpPath.
keyExports.intake: Resolves provider/target from env, prepares the harness run, extracts the user task.
keyExports.runSubAgent: Runs one sub-agent worker, records usage, reconciles retry context.
keyExports.runtimeCheckNode: Runs the runtime-check phase and records its pass/fail outcome.

assumptions: HARNESS_REPLY_VERBOSE controls whether formatReply includes verbose detail.

sideEffects.description: buildAssignmentNode/persistResult/runSubAgent/complianceNode write JSON via writeJson to assignment/result/usage/mcp paths
runSubAgent invokes a worker (getWorker().runAgent); runtimeCheckNode runs the configured runtime-check command
calls into lib/repovine (rp.validateAssignment/rp.validateResult/rp.compliance)

annotation.summary: Decomposes a harness task into role+scope sub-agent specs and schedules them into stages. Explicit task.subAgents/task.roles win deterministically; otherwise a keyword heuristic over task text picks roles (or, in AGENTS=auto, an LLM plan node via planSubAgentsAsync with heuristic fallback on any failure).

keyExports.applyAppFrame: Full-stack frame guarantee: injects missing frame roles (infra/backend/frontend) into a greenfield BUILD plan that already planned at least one frame role; skipped for continuation runs and non-build plans
keyExports.applyGreenfieldParallelStages: Greenfield-only: fans disjoint-scope implement roles into parallel git-worktree batches; requires gitOperationsAllowed and HARNESS_GREENFIELD_PARALLEL != '0'
keyExports.overPlannedRoles: Advisory (continuation only): flags an implement role whose scope shares no token with orient evidence; does not drop anything
keyExports.parseRolesFromText: Whole-word or @role/@prefix-role mention matcher over known roles, ordered by ROLE_ORDER (repo-explorer, infra, backend, frontend, annotation-writer, default, review)
keyExports.planSubAgents: Builds { mode, specs } from task.subAgents/task.roles (explicit) or parseRolesFromText (keyword/single)
keyExports.planSubAgentsAsync: Async planner: explicit roles skip the LLM; AGENTS=auto tries planWithLLM from ./planner.mjs and falls back to planSubAgents on any failure; also applies stripAnnotationStages, applyAppFrame, and the HARNESS_GREENFIELD_SINGLE single-agent override
keyExports.scheduleStages: Batches specs into stages by dependency depth and scope-disjointness
keyExports.stripAnnotationStages: Drops annotation-writer roles from non-explicit plans (annotation sync is harness-owned, runs post-verify, not planner-authored)

assumptions: ROLE_ORDER is the canonical stage ordering (infra -> backend -> frontend); scheduling encodes 'parallel only for disjoint scopes' in code, not in a prompt
HARNESS_GREENFIELD_PARALLEL defaults to enabled ('1'); HARNESS_GREENFIELD_SINGLE opts in to a single default sub-agent for an empty greenfield sandbox with a generic task

sideEffects.description: reads HARNESS_GREENFIELD_PARALLEL and HARNESS_GREENFIELD_SINGLE

annotation.integrationPoints: Imports lib/agents.mjs (resolveRole/isKnownRole/knownRoles/agentsMode/appFrameRoles) and lib/graph/workspace-state.mjs (isGreenfieldSandbox/isGreenfieldContext); planSubAgentsAsync dynamically imports ./planner.mjs for the LLM branch

annotation.summary: Phase-4 'implicit decomposition' planner: loads orchestration-rule prose (loadOrchestrationRule, bundled lib/rules/repovine-subagent-orchestration.mdc or HARNESS_RULES_DIR override) plus the task, asks the LLM (via lib/llm's askLLM) for a JSON array plan of {role, scope, task, dependsOn} sub-agents (buildPlanPrompt/planWithLLM), then resolves and sanitizes the result: parsePlan invalidates the WHOLE plan on any unknown role id (no silent coercion to 'default'), normalizeScopePath strips leading monorepo-layout segments and '..'/absolute-path junk from LLM-produced scopes, and finalizeSubAgentTask appends a write-only warning (or swaps in a fixed read-only task) when RUN_VERB_RE detects the LLM told a sandboxed worker to run npm/docker/lint/etc. A companion reviewPlanWithLLM/buildPlanReviewPrompt pair asks the LLM to critique a plan against task/criteria text. Any askLLM ok:false or unparsable JSON returns null so the caller falls back to the deterministic heuristic planner; this module never edits the repo (planning is a no-tools completion).

keyExports.extractJsonArray: Best-effort JSON array extraction from LLM text, trying fenced ```json blocks first, then the outermost [...] span.
keyExports.finalizeSubAgentTask: Detects RUN_VERB_RE execution verbs in a planner-produced task string and appends a write-only suffix (or replaces a review task) so a sandboxed worker isn't told to run shell commands.
keyExports.loadOrchestrationRule: Reads the orchestration rule file (HARNESS_RULES_DIR override or the bundled lib/rules/*.mdc), stripping YAML frontmatter; falls back to an empty inline rule if neither path exists.
keyExports.parsePlan: Extracts a JSON array from LLM text, invalidates the whole plan on any unrecognized role, normalizes scopes/tasks, and resolves each entry via resolveRole.
keyExports.planWithLLM: Builds the plan prompt, calls askLLM, and parses the response into resolved sub-agent specs via parsePlan; returns null on any failure to signal fallback.
keyExports.reviewPlanWithLLM: Calls askLLM with buildPlanReviewPrompt to critique a plan against task/criteria text, parsed via parsePlanReview.

assumptions: MONOREPO_ROOT is findUp(HERE, '.git') with a fixed relative-path fallback; it assumes the demo's own sandbox .git lives below HERE and never above, so the upward search cannot mistake the sandbox for the monorepo root.

A planner LLM's scope entries are expected to sometimes mirror the outer monorepo layout (e.g. 'repovine/examples/...'); sandboxPrefixSegments/normalizeScopePath strip that prefix to re-anchor scopes to the sandbox root.

sideEffects.description: reads the orchestration rule file via fs.existsSync/fs.readFileSync (bundled lib/rules/*.mdc or HARNESS_RULES_DIR override)
calls askLLM (lib/llm.mjs) to obtain the plan and plan-review text

risks: finalizeSubAgentTask only catches execution verbs matched by RUN_VERB_RE (npm/pnpm/yarn/vite/docker compose/lint/tsc/etc.); a differently worded execution instruction from the planner LLM can still reach a write-only sub-agent's task text unsanitized.

envDependencies.GRAPH_VERBOSE: Toggles verbose 'plan-llm' logging via logLine; verbose unless explicitly set to '0'.
envDependencies.HARNESS_RULES_DIR: Overrides the directory loadOrchestrationRule reads repovine-subagent-orchestration.mdc from; falls back to the bundled lib/rules/ copy.

annotation.summary: Repovine-native Delivery Protocol harness process (no Playwright): orchestrates orient (repo-explorer sub-agent) -> implement -> verify-claims phases, builds/recovers acceptance criteria, and gates a run's pass/fail across all sub-agents via repovineProcessRunOk/repovineGoalOk.

keyExports.formatOrientVerifyReplyLines: Formats a short human-readable summary line block for the orient/verify phases from run state
keyExports.isCriterionContractEntry: True when a contractsChanged entry (object or JSON string) has a non-empty .statement — the acceptance-criterion shape
keyExports.isRepovineSupportSubAgent: True for the orient or verify-claims support sub-agents
keyExports.isRunGateSubAgent: True for a core implement/review-fix/runtime-fix sub-agent — excludes orient/verify support, annotation-sync (instanceId ending '-annotations'), and role:'review' sub-agents from the run-gate set
keyExports.orientTask: Builds the orient-phase prompt: CLI pre-orient hints, greenfield-sandbox section, and the criteria/graphNodesTouched emission instructions
keyExports.recoverCriteriaContractsFromAttempts: Reads the newest prior attempt-result JSON file for a sub-agent and returns its acceptance-criterion contractsChanged entries, newest-first
keyExports.repovineGoalOk: Goal-level pass predicate combining runtimeCheck, the run-gate sub-agents, and the annotation-sync sub-agent's status
keyExports.repovineProcessEnabled: Env gate: true unless HARNESS_REPOVINE_PROCESS is set to an explicit falsy value (default on)
keyExports.repovineProcessRunOk: Process-level pass predicate: every run-gate sub-agent effectively ok, or its only failure is a CSQ-only delivery, plus greenfield-aware orient-failure tolerance
keyExports.runOrientPhase: Runs the repo-explorer orient sub-agent, merges CLI pre-orient output with the LLM's, resolves/merges acceptance criteria, writes the orient run-level artifact
keyExports.subAgentCsqOnlyDelivered: True when a sub-agent's only errors are CSQ (context-session-quality) advisory errors
keyExports.verifyClaimsTask: Builds the verify-claims-phase prompt requiring a structured deliveryVerification object (criteriaResults + split verdict) instead of free text

assumptions: HARNESS_REPOVINE_PROCESS defaults ON — only an explicit falsy value (0/false/no/off) disables the repovine-native process.
Annotation-sync sub-agents (instanceId ending '-annotations') and role:'review' sub-agents are excluded from the run-gate set; they're judged by their own gates instead.

sideEffects.description: recoverCriteriaContractsFromAttempts reads prior sub-agent attempt-result JSON files
writeOrientArtifact writes the orient run-level JSON artifact, best-effort (failure is swallowed)

risks: writeOrientArtifact swallows write failures (best-effort); a broken orient artifact write is silent.
annotation.integrationPoints: runOrientPhase/runVerifyClaimsPhase delegate through ./sub-agent.mjs (runSubAgent) to mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/target-repo, a consumer-scoped-risk dependency two hops from this module.

annotation.summary: Retry-context folding shared by the single- and multi-sub-agent harness loops: classifies a rejected `repovine delivery compliance` report by diagnostics code (sync-only annotation gap vs false graph-node claim vs contract-handoff failure), decides whether a run is worth retrying, and folds compliance notes / transient-transport / worker-timeout signals into the next attempt's task text. The harness always RESUMES the just-run session on retry (not a fresh one) except for a worker-timeout kill.

keyExports.COMPACT_RETRY_BASE: Compact retry preamble telling the resumed session not to restate scope/contracts already in its conversation.
keyExports.complianceReport: Synthesizes a report from schema-invalid AgentRunResult JSON (schemaValid:false) so schema errors reach the retry the same way compliance errors do.
keyExports.foldRetryContext: Builds the retry task text (base + notes) for a rejected report, given the prior work result.
keyExports.foldWorkerTimeoutRetry: Builds a fresh-session retry task with a hard time-box directive for a worker killed at the wall-clock limit.
keyExports.groundingRejected: True when report carries ungroundedAnnotations or inconsistentAnnotations (repovine's provenance/consistency facts).
keyExports.isRetriable: Overall retry decision combining the above, excluding failed/blocked runs that do not match a retryable pattern.
keyExports.isSyncOnlyReport: True when rejection is annotation/graph-sync only: no missing required fields, no contract-handoff prose match, and every diagnostics code is in SYNC_ONLY_CODES (or the ANNOTATION_PROPAGATION_STALE* prefix) with no FALSE_CLAIM_CODES present.
keyExports.isTransientTransportBlock: True when a blocked result with no files changed matches a transport-failure pattern (ECONNRESET, 5xx, overloaded, etc.) — the one blocked class worth a fresh retry.
keyExports.isWorkerTimeoutBlock: True when a blocked result matches the harness's own wall-clock kill message ('timed out after Ns') with no files changed.
keyExports.mergeSyncOnlyResult: Merges a sync-only retry's result back into the original work result.
keyExports.requiredFieldsRejected: True when report.missingFields is non-empty — the result itself is incomplete, never annotation-sync fixable.
keyExports.retryNotes: Compliance notes worth folding into a retry: errors + requiredFollowups + grounding-fact specifics (node ids to re-inspect, or keyExports/sideEffects to fix).
keyExports.reviewFixSubAgentAccepted: Whether a review-fix sub-agent's sync retry succeeded.
keyExports.shouldDeferImplementAnnotationRetry: True only in the implement phase with files changed and a sync-only report — defers the annotation gap to a post-review sub-agent instead of retrying and overwriting a good implementation.
keyExports.subAgentSyncRetrySucceeded: Whether a sync-only retry attempt (within the last attempts) succeeded.

assumptions: repovine diagnostics codes in the report match the SYNC_ONLY_CODES and FALSE_CLAIM_CODES hardcoded here; if the engine renames or adds a code without updating this module, it goes unclassified.
Retry always resumes the prior session's conversation history except when isWorkerTimeoutBlock is true, which signals a fresh worker attempt with a time-box directive.
A sync-only retry is NOT applied during the implement phase if files were already changed; annotation gaps must be deferred to a post-review subAgent so a good implementation pass is not overwritten.
risks: SYNC_ONLY_CODES and FALSE_CLAIM_CODES are hardcoded strings that encode harness policy on top of repovine's general validator facts; a repovine diagnostics code renamed or added without a matching update here goes unclassified and falls through to the general retry logic.
invariants: SYNC_ONLY_CODES (ANNOTATIONS_UNCLEAN, ANNOTATIONS_UNCLEAN_IN_SCOPE, ANNOTATIONS_ORPHANED, ANNOTATION_COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE, ANNOTATION_THIN, ANNOTATION_MISSING, plus any ANNOTATION_PROPAGATION_STALE*-prefixed code) are fixable without touching code.

FALSE_CLAIM_CODES (GRAPH_NODE_UNRESOLVED, REVIEW_FINDING_NODE_UNRESOLVED, ARCH_FINDING_NODE_UNRESOLVED, CONTEXT_PACK_ANCHOR_UNRESOLVED, EVIDENCE_ANCHOR_UNRESOLVED, EVIDENCE_ANCHOR_UNCHANGED) are never sync-only — the agent must re-read the graph and correct the id list.
TRANSIENT_TRANSPORT_RE matches provider/proxy deaths; WORKER_TIMEOUT_RE matches the harness's own wall-clock kill; both are blocked results with no files changed.
CONTRACT_HANDOFF prose match catches inter-sub-agent contract violations in report.errors; no diagnostics code exists for harness contract-gate failures.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by lib/graph/sub-agent.mjs (runSubAgent) and lib/graph/multi.mjs (multiAgent) to gate retry logic after repovine `delivery compliance` rejects a sub-agent result.

annotation.summary: Worker session-map helpers for the LangGraph orchestrator: builds and merges role->sessionId maps so provider conversations can resume within one invoke.

keyExports.collectSubAgentSessions: Reduces a list of finished sub-agent records into a { role: workerSessionId } map, last writer wins per role.
keyExports.mergeSessions: Shallow-merges two session maps (utility for tests/future channels); not used for cross-/task resume.

assumptions: Cross-/task resume is intentionally NOT handled here: intake resets workerSessions to {} each /task so LLM sessions start fresh; intra-task resume instead accumulates via liveSessions in multi.mjs / run_sub_agent.

annotation.summary: Defines GraphState, the LangGraph Annotation.Root state schema threaded through every node of the orchestrator graph (mirrors docs/langgraph-orchestrator-design.md).

keyExports.GraphState: Annotation.Root schema of last-value-wins channels (input, workspace, protocol artifacts, worker/session, multi-agent, control/output) with explicit defaults so a fresh or resumed thread starts from a known shape.

assumptions: targetMode ('sandbox'|'attach') is distinct from the routing mode channel ('single'|'multi'); attach invoke input must never alter mode.
Capabilities are derived per-node via targetPolicy(targetMode), not threaded through state.
turn and attempts use custom reducers that keep prev when next is nullish (turn persists across checkpointed invokes; attempts bounds the HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES loop).
usageRecords uses an accumulating-array reducer instead of last-value-wins.

annotation.summary: Runs one Delivery Protocol sub-agent to completion: builds the sub-agent task (contract handoff, role stack, contextSession), writes/validates its assignment JSON, invokes the configured worker with retry, and records telemetry + finalized handoff.

keyExports.buildSubAgentTask: Builds one sub-agent's task object (role, task text, constraints, contracts, contextSession) from parentTask + spec + priorHandoffs, embedding the inter-sub-agent contract handoff section and orient payload
keyExports.runSubAgent: Builds+validates the assignment, runs the worker (with retry per HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES), applies the harness contract gate, and returns { ok, result, report, handoff, assignmentFile }

assumptions: HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES is parsed as a non-negative integer; a non-numeric/negative value falls back to 1 to avoid a NaN retry-loop bug.
Annotate-phase sub-agents (contextPhase 'annotate') get contextSession.required:false — CSQ is advisory there, not a hard gate.
Assignment/result validation and the compliance gate come from lib/repovine.mjs (`repovine delivery validate-assignment` / `validate-result` / `compliance`).

sideEffects.description: writeSubAgentJson writes assignment/result/attempt/usage/mcp artifacts via writeJsonFile
worker.runAgent invokes the configured provider (Claude/local/etc.) to run the sub-agent
snapshot/reconcile tracks and reaps orphaned sandbox child processes around each attempt

risks: Retry loop guards HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES with Number.isInteger; a malformed env value silently falls back to 1 instead of crashing.
annotation.integrationPoints: Validation/compliance via lib/repovine.mjs (rp.validateAssignment/rp.validateResult/rp.compliance — the `repovine delivery` CLI); role resolution via lib/agents (protocolRoleForSpec); retry classification via lib/graph/retry; provider dispatch via lib/workers.
annotation.dataFlow: parentTask + spec + priorHandoffs -> buildSubAgentTask -> buildAssignment -> validate-assignment -> worker.runAgent (with retry) -> validate-result + compliance + contract gate -> { ok, result, report, handoff }.

envDependencies.HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES: Non-negative integer retry cap; a malformed value falls back to 1.

annotation.summary: Deterministic 'test floor' gate: a require-tests implementer sub-agent that changed files must leave at least one test source file under the top-level directories it self-reported writing to. Existence, not behavior coverage — testReview stays the advisory quality lens.

keyExports.hasTestFileUnder: Bounded existence scan (default maxDepth 6) for one *.test/*.spec source file under repoRoot/relDir, skipping node_modules/.git/dist/build/.harness/.repovine/.worktrees
keyExports.missingTestFloorBlockers: One blocker string per (role, scan-dir-set) whose real scope contains no test source file; a fix sub-agent that adds tests clears the blocker on re-scan
keyExports.subAgentTestScanDirs: Top-level directories from a sub-agent's self-reported result.filesChanged (not result.scope, which defaults to ['.'] and would vacuously scan the whole workspace); root-level files yield no scan dir
keyExports.testFloorEligible: True for a subAgent whose role requiresTests, is not an '-annotations' instance, and has non-empty result.filesChanged

assumptions: Verify is a read-only LLM forbidden to run tests and claims are unscoped, so this existence gate is the implementable substitute for grounding 'tests exist' as a claim
annotation-sync sub-agents keep their implementer role but write no code, so instanceId ending '-annotations' is exempted from the gate

sideEffects.description: fs.readdirSync walk under repoRoot/relDir, depth-bounded

risks: Scan dirs come from the sub-agent's self-reported filesChanged; a sub-agent that under-reports changed-file directories evades the floor (accepted asymmetry, not fixed here).

annotation.summary: Compiles the demo harness's LangGraph orchestrator: wires intake, multi_agent, build_assignment, validate_assignment, run_sub_agent, persist_result, validate_result, compliance, runtime_check and compose_reply nodes (from nodes.mjs/multi.mjs) into a StateGraph, and exposes invokeGraph to run one task through it.

keyExports.buildGraph: ({ checkpointer = new MemorySaver() } = {}) => compiles the StateGraph. Routing: routeAfterIntake sends errors straight to compose_reply, mode:'multi' to multi_agent, else to build_assignment; routeAfterAssignment only spends on run_sub_agent when assignmentValid; routeAfterCompliance retries run_sub_agent (bounded by HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES, shared isRetriable policy from retry.mjs) when a rejected run has actionable notes and isn't blocked/failed, else proceeds to runtime_check.
keyExports.invokeGraph: (graph, input, { threadId, signal, capture } = {}) => graph.invoke(input, { configurable: { thread_id: threadId || `task:${input.task?.id || Date.now()}`, signal, capture }, ...(signal ? { signal } : {}) }).

assumptions: HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES defaults to 1 when unset; set to 0 to disable retry after a rejected compliance run.

LangGraph owns step order/branching/retries/persisted state; it does not pick the LLM (run_sub_agent does, via LLM_PROVIDER) and never imports repovine internals directly — orchestrator nodes shell out to the CLI instead.
Default checkpointer (MemorySaver) is per-process/in-memory; threadId keys the checkpointer, one thread per channel conversation (e.g. one per Telegram chat).

sideEffects.description: reads process.env.HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES for the retry-after-compliance-rejection bound.
default MemorySaver checkpointer holds compiled-graph thread state in-process.

annotation.summary: Captures an observable, run-specific workspace revision as a Git tree object (backend 'git-tree') without touching HEAD, the index, or the working tree, so a baseline..current pair bounds an authoritative diff instead of trusting sub-agent-reported file unions.

keyExports.REPOVINE_ARTIFACT_RE: Matches engine-written annotations.backup.<iso>.json files, also excluded
keyExports.REPOVINE_COMMITTED_ARTIFACTS: ['repovine.annots.json', 'repovine.domains.json', 'repovine.config.json'] — excluded from changedFiles/diff since their effect is already represented via annotationsWritten
keyExports.captureWorkspaceRevision: Writes a git tree object for current non-ignored contents via a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE; returns { backend, repoRoot, digest } or null on any capture failure (fails closed)
keyExports.commitAttachRun: Attach promotion hook: commits the workspace into the disposable repo's real index as `attach/run-<runId>`, dropping harness-internal dirs first; an operator convenience, not custody
keyExports.diffChangedFiles: Normalized, sorted, deduped changed paths between two revisions, excluding REPOVINE_COMMITTED_ARTIFACTS/annotation backups/harness-internal dirs; null on backend mismatch or git failure
keyExports.diffReviewablePatch: Binary-safe diff bytes between two revisions with the same exclusions as diffChangedFiles, so patch and changedFiles agree
keyExports.revisionsEqual: Revision identity is { backend, digest }, never JS object identity

assumptions: backend must be 'git-tree'; any other value throws (the Phase 1 filesystem backend was removed with the disposable-repo design)
REPOVINE_COMMITTED_ARTIFACTS mirrors repovine's own committed-artifact filenames (src/paths.ts) by deliberate duplication, not by importing engine internals across the CLI process boundary
one backend serves both target modes: sandbox is its own repo, attach carries the launch-scoped disposable repo behind a read-only .git pointer

sideEffects.description: spawnSync git read-tree/add/write-tree/diff/commit/branch/rev-parse
writes and removes a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE under os.tmpdir() per capture

risks.text: captureWorkspaceRevision and the diff* exports return null on any capture/git failure (no HEAD, any git step non-zero); a caller must distinguish that null from an empty changeset and not finalize the run as if the workspace were unchanged.

annotation.summary: Detects whether the harness sandbox is a greenfield (no product source yet, e.g. right after /reset) or a continuation, so planner/orient-brief/process-gate logic doesn't misread an empty or stub-only repovine.annots.json as a weak-orient failure.

keyExports.PRODUCT_SOURCE_MARKERS: Const array of the path names checked by hasProductSourceMarkers.
keyExports.describeWorkspaceState: Human-readable planner guidance string: greenfield instructions (scaffold from task, defer annotations) vs continuation instructions (plan a delta, preserve graph-observed behavior).
keyExports.hasOnlyStubAnnotations: True when repoRoot/repovine.annots.json is missing, unparseable, or its annotations bucket is empty.
keyExports.hasProductSourceMarkers: True if repoRoot contains any of PRODUCT_SOURCE_MARKERS (package.json, src, app, apps, packages, lib, backend, frontend, server, client, docs, README.md).
keyExports.isGreenfieldContext: True when isGreenfieldSandbox, or when orientTrail.graphNodes is empty AND hasOnlyStubAnnotations.
keyExports.isGreenfieldSandbox: True when no product source markers exist, unless HARNESS_FORCE_MULTI=1 env forces false.

assumptions: repovine workspace stubs alone (an empty repovine.annots.json written by /reset) must not count as product memory / count as 'continuation'.

sideEffects.description: fs.existsSync for product source markers and repovine.annots.json; fs.readFileSync + JSON.parse of repovine.annots.json
reads HARNESS_FORCE_MULTI to force isGreenfieldSandbox to false

annotation.summary: Git worktree isolation for parallel sub-agents (Phase 4): gives each parallel sub-agent its own git worktree on a temp branch so concurrent LLM workers don't race on the same working tree, then merges branches back at join.

keyExports.addWorktree: Adds a worktree at .worktrees/<branch> on a fresh sub-agent/<role>-<timestamp> branch off HEAD; returns { dir, branch } or null on failure.
keyExports.available: True when `git --version` runs cleanly in repoRoot; lets the caller fall back to sequential-in-sandbox when git is absent.
keyExports.commitWorktree: git add -A + commit --allow-empty in a worktree dir so even a no-op sub-agent leaves a ref.
keyExports.ensureGitRepo: Ensures repoRoot is its own git repo (not just inside an enclosing one) with local harness identity, no gpgsign, a fresh .gitignore (node_modules/.repovine/.harness/.worktrees/dist), and at least one commit so worktrees can branch off HEAD.
keyExports.mergeWorktree: Merges a sub-agent branch back into repoRoot's current branch with --no-ff; aborts and reports conflict:true on merge conflict so the tree stays clean.
keyExports.preserveWorktreeArtifacts: Copies a worktree's .harness ledger into the durable sandbox before the worktree is removed (since .harness is gitignored and never committed to the branch).
keyExports.removeWorktree: Best-effort `git worktree remove --force` plus branch delete.

assumptions: isRepo checks for a root .git entry rather than `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, because the sandbox lives inside a monorepo and the latter would be fooled by the outer repo.
ensureGitRepo only writes .gitignore on a repo it freshly initialized (inited flag), never into a pre-existing attached workspace, so it never surfaces as an unexpected agent edit.

sideEffects.description: spawnSync('git', ...) for init/config/worktree/commit/merge/branch operations
fs.mkdirSync for worktree dirs, fs.writeFileSync for a fresh .gitignore, fs.cpSync to copy .harness artifacts out of a worktree

risks: mergeWorktree aborts on any conflict and reports it to the caller rather than resolving it, so a caller that ignores conflict:true silently drops that sub-agent's work.

annotation.summary: Loads and parses the delivery-protocol harness demo's handoff.md (frontmatter + markdown template sections) into handoff policy/config, and provides the orchestrator glue that checks contract-handoff violations and builds the inter-sub-agent context section threaded between sub-agents.

keyExports.buildInterSubAgentSectionFromTemplate: Renders the prior-sub-agents block plus a deduped contracts ledger (planner/parent contracts union prior sub-agents' contractsChanged) from the loaded template; drops same-role prior entries when resuming.
keyExports.contractHandoffViolations: Returns a violation string when an implementer role's result changed files but declared no contractsChanged, unless the role is 'review' or not in config.implementerRoles.
keyExports.finalizeHandoff: Builds the record threaded to the next sub-agent from a sub-agent's AgentRunResult; replaces an annotation-only summary (per isAnnotationOnlySummary) with a concrete one derived from filesChanged/contractsChanged.
keyExports.isAnnotationOnlySummary: Regex heuristic flagging a summary as annotation/sync busywork prose versus an actual delivered-work summary.
keyExports.loadHandoffConfig: Loads handoff.md from the first existing dir in handoffSearchDirs() (HARNESS_HANDOFF_DIR override, else the bundled lib/handoff dir), caches by file mtimeMs, falls back to DEFAULT_CONFIG.
keyExports.parseHandoffMarkdown: Parses frontmatter (requireContractsWhenFilesChanged, implementerRoles) and '# Template <name>' sections into a config object; accepts the legacy pre-rename section title 'interLeafSection' as a fallback for 'interSubAgentSection'.

assumptions: Bundled handoff.md is demo-owned prose whose structure is guarded by test/handoff-ssot.test.mjs; override only via HARNESS_HANDOFF_DIR, the same pattern lib/agents and lib/rules use.

sideEffects.description: reads handoff.md via fs.existsSync/statSync/readFileSync
module-level configCache Map keyed by search-dir join, invalidated by file mtimeMs

risks: The legacy 'interLeafSection' section-name fallback in parseHandoffMarkdown is a temporary accommodation for handoff.md copies projected before the sub-agents rename.

annotation.summary: Canonical on-disk layout and path builders for `.harness/` sandbox artifacts: active/ (ephemeral, cleared each /goal intake) vs runs/<runId>/ (durable, cleared only on /reset) vs index.jsonl (one line per archived run); plus JSON write/append helpers and the archival/migration functions that move a run from active to durable storage.

keyExports.appendRunIndex: Appends one JSON line (with archivedAt) to index.jsonl.
keyExports.archiveActiveRun: Moves active/<runId>/ to runs/<runId>/, finalizes events.jsonl, writes meta.json, appends the run index, and clears active/current-run.json.
keyExports.archiveOrphanActiveRuns: Archives in-flight run dirs left in active/ after a crash or /stop, marking them aborted/partial.
keyExports.legacyRunIdFromBasename: Recovers a runId from a legacy flat '.harness/<runId>.*.json' basename.
keyExports.migrateLegacyFlatHarness: Moves legacy flat .harness/* files into runs/<runId>/; idempotent for already-migrated names.
keyExports.runDir: activeRunDir or archivedRunDir depending on { active } (default true).
keyExports.runLevelPath: Path builder for a file inside a run's dir.
keyExports.splitSubAgentKey: Splits 'runId.subAgentId' on the first '.'; defaults subAgentId to 'default' when no dot is present.
keyExports.subAgentAssignmentPath: Path builder for a sub-agent's assignment.json, from a 'runId.subAgentId' key.
keyExports.subAgentAttemptResultPath: Path builder for a sub-agent's attempts/<n>.result.json.
keyExports.subAgentMcpPath: Path builder for a sub-agent's mcp.json.
keyExports.subAgentResultPath: Path builder for a sub-agent's result.json.
keyExports.subAgentUsagePath: Path builder for a sub-agent's usage.json.

assumptions: subAgentKey is always 'runId.subAgentId' split on the first '.'; a key with no dot is treated as runId with subAgentId 'default'.

sideEffects.description: mkdirSync/writeFileSync/appendFileSync/renameSync/rmSync/copyFileSync under .harness/
existsSync/readFileSync/readdirSync/statSync under .harness/

risks: archiveActiveRun and migrateLegacyFlatHarness are best-effort: a stray file that fails JSON.parse (safeReadJson) returns null silently rather than throwing, and telemetry copy failures are swallowed.

annotation.summary: Harness run intake boundary: aggregates the latest archived run into a compact prior-run summary, formats it for injection into the new task, and wipes .harness/active/ only (archived runs under .harness/runs/ survive until /reset).

keyExports.findLatestTaskPrefix: Compat helper returning the newest archived run id
keyExports.formatPriorRunSummaryForTask: Renders a prior-run summary as a text block capped at maxBytes (default DEFAULT_PRIOR_SUMMARY_MAX_BYTES=2048), truncating from the end
keyExports.prepareHarnessRun: Intake barrier: migrates legacy layout, archives orphaned active runs, reads the prior summary, clears .harness/active/, returns { priorRunSummary, priorRunSummaryText }
keyExports.readPriorRunSummary: Reads the latest archived run's sub-agent result files into { runId, status, summary, filesChanged, contractsChanged, blockers, subAgentCount }; filesChanged prefers the archived tree-diff signal (fail-closed: captured-but-empty stays empty) and falls back to the sub-agent filesChanged union only for pre-signal legacy archives

assumptions: Intra-task LLM worker session resume lives in multi.mjs/run_sub_agent, not here — this module only resets workerSessions at intake
A corrupt sub-agent result JSON file is skipped rather than failing the whole summary

sideEffects.description: reads archived sub-agent result files and the run-level summary JSON under .harness/runs/

risks: clearHarnessArtifacts is deprecated (kept only so tests importing the old name still resolve); callers should use clearHarnessActive from lib/harness-paths.mjs directly.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates path/archive mechanics to lib/harness-paths.mjs (RUN_LEVEL, archiveActiveRun, archiveOrphanActiveRuns, clearHarnessActive, findLatestArchivedRunId, listSubAgentResultFiles, migrateLegacyFlatHarness, runLevelPath), and re-exports several of those names for existing callers.

annotation.summary: Lightweight LLM completion seam used only by the planner (not the coding-agent workers): askLLM dispatches to askClaude (Claude Agent SDK, tools/MCP disabled, maxTurns 2) or askLocal (OpenAI-compatible chat completion) by provider, gated through the same resolveAuth check the workers use so there is no silent spend; any provider failure returns { ok:false, reason } so the caller falls back to the deterministic heuristic planner.

keyExports.askLLM: (prompt, { provider='claude', systemAppend, timeoutMs }) => dispatches to askClaude or askLocal and returns { ok:true, text } or { ok:false, reason }.

assumptions: Default timeout comes from PLANNER_TIMEOUT_MS (finitePositive fallback 90000ms); a caller-supplied timeoutMs overrides it, resolved once per call so concurrent calls with different budgets don't interfere.
'@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk' is an optional runtime dependency, dynamically imported inside askClaude; missing install yields { ok:false } rather than a throw.
askLocal requires LOCAL_BASE_URL (via localBaseUrl()) to be configured; otherwise it returns { ok:false } without attempting a request.

sideEffects.description: invokes @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() for the claude provider
POST fetch to {LOCAL_BASE_URL}/chat/completions for the local provider
AbortController timer bounds each provider call (default from PLANNER_TIMEOUT_MS)

risks: Both providers swallow every failure into { ok:false, reason }; a caller that doesn't check .ok silently loses LLM planning and falls through to the heuristic planner without an explicit signal.

envDependencies.PLANNER_TIMEOUT_MS: Overrides the default 90000ms planner call timeout (finitePositive fallback); a caller-supplied timeoutMs argument still takes precedence.

annotation.summary: Two stderr logging helpers (logLine, logBullet) with an optional ISO timestamp prefix and configurable indent/scope, gated by an `enabled` flag; used for worker/harness console diagnostics.

keyExports.logBullet: logBullet(message, { enabled, indent, scope, stream }) — same as logLine but prefixes each line with '·' and defaults indent to 4 spaces, scope to 'worker'.
keyExports.logLine: logLine(scope, message, { enabled, indent, stream }) — writes '<indent><timestamp?> [scope] <line>' per newline-split line of message to stream (default process.stderr).

assumptions: HARNESS_LOG_TIMESTAMPS controls the ISO timestamp prefix; timestamps are on by default and disabled only when the var is exactly '0'.

sideEffects.description: writes formatted log lines to process.stderr (or an overridden stream)

annotation.summary: Per-role (planner/implementer/verify/ask) model + reasoning-effort defaults for harness LLM calls, with per-provider env overrides: Claude via {PLANNER,IMPLEMENTER,VERIFY,ASK}_REASONING (plus a legacy CLAUDE_AGENT_MODEL fallback for implementer only), local OpenAI-compatible provider via LOCAL_MODEL / LOCAL_{ROLE}_MODEL.

keyExports.formatRoleLabel: Compact 'model:effort' (or bare model) label for verbose logs, per provider.
keyExports.parseRoleSetting: Parses a *_REASONING env value: 'model:effort', a bare effort token (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max), or a bare model id.
keyExports.resolveClaudeRole: Resolves { model, effort? } for a role on the Claude provider, merging env override then legacy CLAUDE_AGENT_MODEL (implementer only) then CLAUDE_DEFAULTS.
keyExports.resolveLocalRole: Resolves { model } for a role on the local provider: per-role env, else LOCAL_MODEL, else LOCAL_DEFAULT_MODEL.
keyExports.subAgentModelRole: Maps a sub-agent spec.role to a harness model role: 'review' -> verify; 'repo-explorer'/'annotation-writer' -> ask; everything else -> implementer.

assumptions: CLAUDE_DEFAULTS floors every role at sonnet or above (planner opus:high, implementer sonnet:medium, verify sonnet:low, ask sonnet:low); comment notes haiku:low was previously the read-only default for verify/ask but produced basic-tier annotations, so the floor was raised to sonnet.

annotation.summary: Fail-safe numeric env parser: finitePositive coerces a raw value to a finite positive number or returns fallback, avoiding a non-numeric timeout env silently becoming NaN.

keyExports.finitePositive: (raw, fallback) => Number(raw) if it is finite and > 0, else fallback

assumptions: raw is typically an env var string; used to guard setTimeout(fn, NaN) firing immediately

annotation.summary: Thin synchronous wrapper around the built `repovine delivery <cmd>` and `repovine agents <cmd>` CLIs (dist/mcp/index.js) — the harness's only contact surface with repovine. Delivery Protocol I/O (descriptor via bare `delivery`, manifests, run-brief, validate-assignment/validate-result, compliance) goes through delivery(); general agent utilities (roles, orient, session-quality) through agents(). Both shell out via spawnSync (32MB maxBuffer) and parse stdout JSON; refreshGraph/annotationHealth call `repovine build` / `status --json`.

keyExports.REPOVINE_CLI: Resolved path to the built CLI: env override (REPOVINE_CLI), else findUp from this file to dist/mcp/index.js, else a fixed relative fallback.
keyExports.agents: Runs `repovine agents <args>` (roles / orient / session-quality) via spawnSync and returns { status, stdout, stderr, json }.
keyExports.annotationHealth: Runs `repovine status --json` and returns { needsWork, clean } or null when the CLI is unavailable/errors.
keyExports.buildCliCommand: Pure construction of { command, args, cwd, env } for a repovine CLI child, pinning cwd and REPOVINE_ROOT to repoRoot (asserted in tests, no spawn).
keyExports.delivery: Runs `repovine delivery <args>` (Delivery Protocol I/O: descriptor, manifests, run-brief, validate-*, compliance) via spawnSync and returns { status, stdout, stderr, json }.
keyExports.getManifests: Runs `repovine delivery manifests [--role]` and returns its JSON.
keyExports.getProtocol: Runs bare `repovine delivery` and returns the DeliveryProtocol descriptor JSON.
keyExports.harnessBrief: Role brief text (from runBrief) for provider prompts.
keyExports.orientQuery: Runs `repovine agents orient` — deterministic search_context + trace_flow via the CLI (no LLM).
keyExports.projectRoles: Runs `repovine agents roles` (reads agents.roles from repovine.config.json); `at` pins the read to a committed tree-ish for attach custody.
keyExports.refreshGraph: Runs `repovine build` (optionally --cleanup-orphans) to rebuild the graph snapshot between multi-agent stages.
keyExports.runBrief: Runs `repovine delivery run-brief` for a role/name, cached per process by that key.
keyExports.validateResult: Runs `repovine delivery validate-result <file>` (schema-only); normalizes json.schemaValid from the CLI's `valid` field.

assumptions: repovine is contract + validation only — it never runs the agent; discovery/validation calls pass repoRoot as both cwd and REPOVINE_ROOT so the CLI operates on the sandbox tree.
Delivery Protocol I/O is under the `delivery` namespace and general agent utilities under `agents`; bare `delivery` prints the descriptor.

compliance()'s --greenfield-run flag exists because the harness (not the engine) knows run-start annotation state; a single sub-agent's on-disk snapshot can't tell whether shared context was empty at run start.

sideEffects.description: spawnSync('node', [REPOVINE_CLI, 'delivery'|'agents', ...]) for every discovery/validation call; refreshGraph and annotationHealth spawn `repovine build` / `status --json` directly

risks: agents()/delivery()/refreshGraph()/annotationHealth() swallow a spawnSync failure or unparseable stdout JSON into json: undefined (or annotationHealth returning null) rather than surfacing the underlying CLI error to the caller.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps the built repovine CLI (dist/mcp/index.js) — the delivery/agents dispatchers in mod:repovine/src/cli/delivery and mod:repovine/src/cli/agents.
