Consumed across the harness by lib/workers/prompt (harnessBrief), lib/graph/* (compliance/validate/runBrief), and scripts/langgraph-*.
annotation.dataFlow: caller args -> buildCliCommand([namespace, ...args]) -> spawnSync node dist/mcp/index.js -> parse stdout JSON -> { status, stdout, stderr, json }.

annotation.summary: Bootstraps the active role catalog for a resolved launch target: bundled specialist roles in sandbox mode, or the project's agents.roles read from the attach launch baseline (ATTACH_BASELINE_REF) in attach mode.

keyExports.initCatalogForTarget: mode!=='attach' delegates straight to initRoleCatalog; attach mode calls rp.projectRoles(repoRoot, {at: ATTACH_BASELINE_REF}), throws if that source is invalid/opted-in-but-broken, and otherwise falls back to the bundled catalog when the project has no agents.roles

assumptions: Attach-mode role source is read from the git ref ATTACH_BASELINE_REF (the launch baseline), not the working tree, so an agent cannot edit its own next-episode system prompt mid-episode; updating roles requires a commit plus a new prepare

sideEffects.description: calls rp.projectRoles (lib/repovine.mjs), which runs an external process reading agents.roles/briefs at ATTACH_BASELINE_REF in attach mode
logLine reports the resolved project catalog id list and per-role advisories

risks: In attach mode, a repo that opted into project roles but ships an invalid source aborts startup (fail-loud) instead of silently running the bundled fallback.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates role-source reads to mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/repovine (projectRoles) and the baseline ref constant to lib/attach-guard (ATTACH_BASELINE_REF); catalog construction is mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/agents (initRoleCatalog)

annotation.summary: Harness runtime_check: after a sub-agent's edits, installs dependencies (npm install --ignore-scripts) and runs configured build/test commands via spawnSync inside the sandbox with a redacted environment, then extracts a per-workspace failure log tail and scope hints for automatic fix sub-agents.

keyExports.buildRuntimeCheckFixTask: Builds the fix sub-agent's task text from a failed check result and its blockers.
keyExports.canAttemptRuntimeCheckFix: Whether another fix sub-agent may run for a failing command, bounded per-command by runtimeCheckFixMaxAttempts().
keyExports.deriveScopeFromRuntimeLog: Infers backend/frontend/infra scope hints from compiler/test output paths and workspace markers in a failure log.
keyExports.discoverPackageDirs: Depth-bounded (default 4) walk from repoRoot collecting directories containing package.json, skipping node_modules/.git/dist/build/.harness/.repovine.
keyExports.recordRuntimeCheckFixAttempt: Increments the per-command fix counter (mutates the Map or plain object in place).
keyExports.runRuntimeCheck: Top-level entry: runs dependency installs per discovered package dir, then the configured commands, returning per-step results and a failure log tail.
keyExports.runtimeCheckCommands: Ordered shell commands to run: HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_CMDS (multi, ;/\n-split) > HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_CMD (single) > DEFAULT_CMDS ['npm run build','npm test'].
keyExports.runtimeCheckEnabled: True unless attach mode forces it off (attachTarget()) or HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK=0.
keyExports.runtimeCheckOverriddenByAttach: True when an explicit HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK=1 was overridden off by attach mode — reported at intake, never silently swallowed.
keyExports.runtimeFailureLogTail: Failure log tail for fix sub-agents: keeps error lines from each failed monorepo workspace segment instead of a flat last-N-lines tail, so one workspace's errors don't hide another's.
keyExports.runtimeRequired: True when the check is enabled AND discoverPackageDirs finds at least one package.json; drives the tri-state runtimeAccepted so a skipped-but-required check is not a pass.

assumptions: Attach targets force the check off (attachTarget()) because installing/building/testing the whole real repo after every task would fail closed under default-deny egress; the operator builds/tests on the host after promotion.

runtimeCheckEnv() allow-lists a small fixed var set (CI, HOME, LANG, NODE_ENV, PATH, ...) plus npm_*/HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_*/NPM_CONFIG_* and credential-free proxy vars, and drops anything matching SECRET_ENV_RE (api key/token/secret/password/credential/oauth/auth/cookie/session) before spawning the check command.
runShell runs with shell:true and a configurable timeout (HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS, default 600000ms); a timeout reports exitCode 124.

sideEffects.description: spawnSync for `npm install --ignore-scripts` per package dir and for the configured build/test commands
fs.existsSync/readdirSync to discover package.json directories and detect existing node_modules

risks: runtimeCheckEnv()'s allowlist is the only thing keeping harness secrets out of the sandboxed build/test child process; a new env var that happens to start with HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_/NPM_CONFIG_/npm_ but carries a secret-shaped value would still leak through since those prefixes are allow-listed unconditionally.

annotation.summary: Sandbox process/port/container reconciliation for the harness: snapshots what a worker sub-agent's run left running, logs leftovers, and reaps them (Linux-only, via /proc; no-ops on other platforms).

keyExports.harnessReapEnabled: Always returns true — the per-sub-agent reaper is unconditionally on
keyExports.reapAll: Unconditional sweep used on /reset: kills every sandbox-attributable process and composeDown, ahead of wiping the sandbox
keyExports.reconcile: Diffs a snapshot against `before`, logs what a sub-agent left running, and (reap:true) SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs (1500ms grace) new pids plus `docker compose down`/`rm -f` for new containers
keyExports.snapshot: Captures sandbox-attributable pids/ports/containers for repoRoot (cwd-under-root or argv-mentions-root attribution)

assumptions: Attribution is by path: a process counts as this sandbox's when its /proc cwd is under repoRoot or its cmdline mentions repoRoot
A process with a controlling tty (operator's own interactive shell) is never reaped, even if its cwd is inside the sandbox
Containers are daemon-managed so a process-kill cannot stop them; teardown goes through `docker compose down` plus `rm -f` scoped to containers new since the sub-agent's baseline

sideEffects.description: reads /proc/<pid>/{cwd,cmdline,stat} to attribute processes; Linux-only, no-op elsewhere
spawnSync docker (compose down, ps, rm -f) and ss -ltnpH
SIGTERM then SIGKILL to sandbox-attributed pids

annotation.summary: Target contract: resolves whether the harness runs against a managed sandbox or an attached host Git worktree, exposes per-mode capabilities, and validates/seeds/resets each target.

keyExports.ATTACH_RESET_DISABLED: Machine-readable code for an unavailable attach reset (fail-loud baseline-missing error, or the policy-driven HTTP refusal guard).
keyExports.CSQ_CALIBRATION: Harness-owned Context Session Quality threshold calibration per phase (explore/implement/annotate: threshold, warningThreshold, byteBudget), delivered via the sandbox config stub and every sub-agent assignment's contextSession policy.
keyExports.clearWorkspaceContents: Wipes everything under workspaceRoot (default .workspace) but keeps the directory itself, since Docker bind-mount roots are often EROFS on rmdir of the mount root.
keyExports.ensureTarget: Readies a target to run against: seeds/recreates an empty sandbox, or validates an attach target via validateAttachedWorkspace.
keyExports.resetTarget: Resets a target after a run: restores the attach baseline via git, or wipes and reseeds the sandbox.
keyExports.resolveTargetFromEnv: Resolves { mode, repoRoot } from HARNESS_TARGET_MODE (sandbox|attach, default sandbox) and HARNESS_REPO_ROOT; fails loud on an unknown mode, a missing attach root, a non-/workspace root inside Docker, or a REPOVINE_ROOT that conflicts with the resolved repoRoot.
keyExports.targetPolicy: Pure per-mode capability lookup: sandbox = { resetAllowed:true, gitOperationsAllowed:true }; attach = { resetAllowed:true, gitOperationsAllowed:false } (harness-internal git-parallel worktree fan-out is sandbox-only; attach stays sequential for contract-barrier reasons).
keyExports.validateAttachedWorkspace: In-container-provable attach checks only: repoRoot exists as a directory; repovine.config.json and repovine.annots.json exist as files (annots parses as JSON); .git is a regular file (not a directory) pointing at the disposable repo; in Docker the root is pinned to requiredRoot. Never writes; the only git spawn is a read-only HEAD probe.

assumptions: Sandbox mode is a managed empty workspace under .workspace/sandbox that this module seeds with repovine.config.json/repovine.annots.json stubs and owns reset for; attach mode is a pre-created host Git worktree mounted at /workspace whose committed repovine files are authoritative and never harness-written.
Filesystem isolation between modes is enforced by the Docker Compose mount topology (compose.yaml attach services, scripts/attach-launcher.mjs), not by this module.

CSQ_CALIBRATION thresholds are advisory (never fail a sub-agent); byteBudget is raised over engine defaults because a rejected sub-agent's session is retained for retry, so bytes accumulate across roughly 2 attempts.

sideEffects.description: fs.mkdirSync/rmSync/writeFileSync to seed, wipe, and reseed the sandbox workspace and its repovine.config.json/repovine.annots.json stubs
spawnSync for git operations (attach workspace HEAD probe, resetTarget's git reset)
fs.existsSync/statSync/readFileSync to validate an attached workspace's config/annotation files and .git pointer

risks.text: validateAttachedWorkspace proves only in-container facts (files present/parseable, .git shape); proving the host path was a registered clean Git worktree is scripts/attach-launcher.mjs's job and stays host-side — callers must not treat a validateAttachedWorkspace pass as full attach-target proof.

annotation.integrationPoints: Imports ensureGitRepo from mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/worktree and ATTACH_BASELINE_REF/ATTACH_GIT_POINTER_CONTENT/ATTACH_STATE_GIT_DIR from mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/attach-guard.

annotation.summary: Extracts the user-facing task text (for orient, claims, and CLI query) with the harness's injected prior-run coordination preamble stripped out.

keyExports.stripPriorRunBlock: (text) => text with the '## Prior harness run' marker section removed, returning the content after the following blank line

assumptions: A prior-run block, when present, is followed by a blank line ('\n\n') before the real task content

annotation.summary: Demo-local dev-session telemetry: appends JSONL events and writes a current-run JSON snapshot under harness-paths, independent of the durable AgentRunResult/Delivery Protocol contract (operator feedback only).

keyExports.buildRepovineProcessSummary: Builds the compact repovine-native process block (orient/verify/criteria) for summary.json v3, loading the orient artifact from disk when state lacks it
keyExports.finishRunTelemetry: Finalizes run status via runSucceeded, writes the closing summary, and archives the active run
keyExports.readCurrentRun: Reads the active current-run snapshot, falling back to the latest archived run's summary if none is active
keyExports.recordRunEvent: Appends an event to the JSONL log, replays it onto the current run via applyEvent, and rewrites the current-run snapshot
keyExports.runSucceeded: Derives pass/fail for multi sub-agent runs from processOk/goalOk (not a raw subAgents.every(ok)) so a review sub-agent that found and fixed a blocker is not counted as a run failure
keyExports.startRunTelemetry: Initializes a run's telemetry state (baseRun) and writes the first run_started event plus the current-run snapshot

assumptions: Telemetry schema is versioned (TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_VERSION = 3); readers tolerate older archived schemas via safeReadJson returning null on parse failure
Workspace path stored in run state is the in-container path (/workspace), never a host source path

sideEffects.description: writeJson/appendJsonl write current-run JSON and events JSONL under harness-paths active telemetry dir; archiveActiveRun (harness-paths) moves them on finish
safeReadJson reads current-run and archived run-level summary/orient files

annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates run-level file paths to mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/harness-paths (activeTelemetryPath, archiveActiveRun, runLevelPath) and criteria merging to mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/delivery (mergeCriteriaResults)

annotation.summary: Worker (LLM provider) selection for the LangGraph path: resolves the provider from LLM_PROVIDER, validates support, and dynamically imports the matching adapter module so unused SDKs/CLIs never load.

keyExports.getWorker: Dynamic-imports the adapter module for a provider (import('./claude.mjs') or import('./local.mjs')); throws synchronously on process.platform==='win32' before importing.
keyExports.isSupportedProvider: True when knownProvider(provider) (from ./auth.mjs) and provider is in PROVIDERS.
keyExports.resolveProvider: Returns the given provider, else LLM_PROVIDER env, else DEFAULT_PROVIDER.

assumptions: Every adapter module implements the same async seam: runAgent(task, assignment, repoRoot, opts?: { resume?, capture? }) => Promise<AgentRunResult>; auth is resolved once in lib/workers/auth.mjs so adapters never duplicate it.
Native Windows host mode is unsupported; getWorker directs callers to WSL2 or the Docker sandbox (docs/usage.md).

sideEffects.description: dynamic import() of the selected provider adapter module at call time

annotation.integrationPoints: getWorker() dynamically imports mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/workers/claude (provider 'claude', default) or lib/workers/local.mjs (provider 'local') at call time; being a dynamic import(), neither has a static import edge in the graph.

annotation.summary: Read-only /ask worker built on the Claude Agent SDK: runs a Read/Glob/Grep plus read-only repovine MCP tool session behind a deny-by-default permission gate that hard-blocks writes and Bash even if a preset tool list re-adds them.

keyExports.askReadOnlyGate: canUseTool permission callback: allows a tool only if it is in ASK_ALLOWED_TOOLS, else denies with an explicit read-only message.
keyExports.runAsk: Entry point (question, repoRoot, opts) => { ok:true, text, contextSessionId } | { ok:false, reason }; dynamically imports @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk's query(), wires abort/timeout/resume and a stdio repovine MCP server, and streams the response into a final result/assistant text.

assumptions: Auth is checked via resolveAuth('claude') before the SDK is even imported; missing auth short-circuits with a reason instead of invoking the SDK.
Timeout comes from claudeTimeoutMs({ primaryEnv: 'ASK_TIMEOUT_MS' }), distinct from the primary worker's own timeout config.

sideEffects.description: calls the Claude Agent SDK's query() (Anthropic API)
SDK spawns `node REPOVINE_CLI` as a stdio MCP server per the mcpServers config

risks: Read-only enforcement relies on two lists staying in sync (ASK_ALLOWED_TOOLS for canUseTool, ASK_DISALLOWED_TOOLS for disallowedTools); a new write/exec tool added to a preset must be added to ASK_DISALLOWED_TOOLS or it is only blocked by the allow-list check.

annotation.summary: Read-only /ask runner for LLM_PROVIDER=local: runs the same OpenAI-compatible chat loop as the local worker but restricted to read_file plus the read-only repovine MCP tool subset (REPOVINE_ASK_MCP_TOOLS), returning a prose answer instead of an AgentRunResult.

keyExports.runAsk: (question, repoRoot, opts) drives the chat loop against LOCAL_BASE_URL with a read-only tool allowlist, dispatching read_file locally and mcp__repovine__* over a scoped McpStdioClient; returns {ok:true,text,contextSessionId} or {ok:false,reason}

assumptions: LOCAL_BASE_URL must be configured or the call fails immediately.
The local provider is stateless — no resumable server session id is captured, unlike the Claude ask runner.

sideEffects.description: chatCompletion() HTTP calls to LOCAL_BASE_URL
starts a repovine MCP stdio subprocess (McpStdioClient) restricted to REPOVINE_ASK_MCP_TOOLS, no refresh_context/write_annotation
execReadFile serves the read_file tool

risks: The MCP tool allowlist (mcpAllow) is the only thing preventing a mutating MCP call — dispatch refuses any mcp__repovine__* name not in REPOVINE_ASK_MCP_TOOLS.

annotation.summary: Builds the read-only /ask prompt (IDE-chat-like agent mode): a fixed Q&A policy forbidding file edits, refresh_context/write_annotation, and any Delivery Protocol result block, followed by the question and optional attachments.

keyExports.ASK_POLICY: Read-only policy text: orient with repovine MCP, read source files, answer in prose only, no edits/refresh_context/write_annotation/shell commands, no AgentRunResult block
keyExports.buildAskPrompt: Joins ASK_POLICY, the question, an optional contextSessionId line, an attachments brief, and a resuming/first-turn instruction into the final prompt string

annotation.integrationPoints: Reuses mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/workers/prompt (attachmentsBrief) for the shared attachment-listing format

annotation.summary: Shared credential resolver for the harness's LLM providers (claude | local): checks explicit env vars only (no home-login files), returning a loggable ok/reason shape that never carries secret values.

keyExports.authBlockedReason: Human-readable one-liner combining auth.reason and auth.hints for blocked-result summaries.
keyExports.knownProvider: True when the given provider name is a key of the internal PROVIDERS map (claude | local).
keyExports.resolveAuth: Resolves credentials for a provider (default from LLM_PROVIDER env, else 'claude'): local is presence-of-endpoint via LOCAL_BASE_URL (LOCAL_API_KEY optional, not fail-closed); claude requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Returns { ok:true, mode, source } or { ok:false, reason, hints }.

assumptions: local is deliberately not fail-closed like claude: a reachable LOCAL_BASE_URL alone is a usable credential because no remote spend is possible against a local model.

sideEffects.description: reads LLM_PROVIDER, LOCAL_BASE_URL, LOCAL_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from process.env

invariants: resolveAuth never returns a secret value itself, only which env var supplied it (source), so callers can log the result directly.

annotation.summary: Claude worker adapter (LLM_PROVIDER=claude, the default): re-exports runAgent from lib/claude-agent.mjs and declares the provider id, so the graph's run_sub_agent node only talks to lib/workers/<provider>.mjs.

keyExports.provider: Literal 'claude' provider id for this adapter.

annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates execution to mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/claude-agent (runAgent), which resolves auth via resolveAuth('claude') in lib/workers/auth.mjs and launches Claude Agent SDK with a stdio MCP server (mcp__repovine__*) scoped to repoRoot.

annotation.summary: Env-driven config helpers for the Claude Agent SDK worker: resolves the agent timeout precedence and builds the SDK's OS-sandbox option object.

keyExports.claudeSandbox: CLAUDE_SANDBOX=0/false/off/none opts out (returns undefined); otherwise returns { enabled: true, failIfUnavailable: true, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed }
keyExports.claudeTimeoutMs: Reads CLAUDE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS (or a caller-given primaryEnv), falling back to WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS then fallbackMs, via finitePositive from lib/num.mjs

assumptions: Sandbox fails closed by design: if the OS sandbox is unavailable the SDK errors rather than silently running unsandboxed while bypassPermissions stays on

sideEffects.description: reads CLAUDE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS, WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS, and CLAUDE_SANDBOX

annotation.summary: Vendor-neutral 'local' worker adapter (LLM_PROVIDER=local) for the delivery-protocol harness demo: runs any tool-capable local model through an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint, implementing the full agent loop itself (no vendor SDK) including its own minimal MCP stdio client that spawns the repovine CLI and exposes its tools as OpenAI function-call tools.

keyExports.McpStdioClient: Minimal newline-delimited JSON-RPC client that spawns `node REPOVINE_CLI` as a stdio MCP server and speaks initialize/tools-list/tools-call to it.
keyExports.chatCompletion: Single request to the local OpenAI-compatible endpoint with abort-controller timeout wiring.
keyExports.resolveInSandbox: Resolves a caller-given path to stay inside the sandbox repo root; for forWrite, also checks the realpath of the parent dir to reject symlink escapes.
keyExports.runAgent: Entry point (task, assignment, repoRoot, opts) => AgentRunResult; drives the chat-completions tool loop (native tool_calls or inline ```tool_call fallback) against read_file/write_file/apply_patch/run_shell plus repovine MCP tools until a final answer, max turns, timeout, or abort.
keyExports.scrubbedEnv: Filters an env object through SECRET_ENV_RE before it reaches a spawned process.
keyExports.supportsResume: false — this adapter is a stateless loop; a retry re-folds the full task text rather than resuming a conversation.
keyExports.synthResult: Builds the final AgentRunResult by preferring observed effects (files written, MCP calls seen) over prose from a model-emitted JSON block, since weak local models rarely emit a clean result block.

assumptions: Model and endpoint are config, not code: LOCAL_MODEL/LOCAL_BASE_URL (via local-config.mjs) pick them; auth is resolveAuth('local'), gated on LOCAL_BASE_URL presence rather than a cloud API key.
<think>...</think> content is stripped from local-model output and never shown.

sideEffects.description: spawn/spawnSync for the MCP stdio server and apply_patch (git apply)
fetch to the local OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint
execReadFile reads sandbox files
execApplyPatch writes sandbox files via applied diff

risks.text: LOCAL_TOOLS (read_file/write_file/apply_patch/run_shell) names and schemas are a fixed worker tool contract per handoff §2; a caller relying on this adapter must not assume a renamed or reshaped tool schema is compatible with models already tuned against it.

annotation.summary: Config for the vendor-neutral 'local' provider (LLM_PROVIDER=local): splits client wiring (OpenAI-compatible endpoint/key) from per-run sampling/loop options and the repovine MCP stdio descriptor, so switching models is an env change only.

keyExports.localClientOptions: { baseUrl, apiKey? } for the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions client
keyExports.localContextTokens: Soft prompt-token budget (default 24000) the local tool-use loop compacts against, since (unlike Claude) the harness owns context management itself; 0 disables compaction
keyExports.localRunOptions: Per-run options for the local worker loop: resolved model for modelRole via resolveLocalRole, temperature, maxTurns, and buildRepovineMcpStdio(..., {inheritProcessEnv:true})
keyExports.stripReasoning: Strips leaked <think>/<reasoning> blocks many OSS models emit from chat content before it reaches the user or AgentRunResult summary

assumptions: LOCAL_TIMEOUT_MS falls back to WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS then 600000ms; LOCAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS defaults to 300000ms to absorb a cold local-model load on the first request

sideEffects.description: reads LOCAL_API_KEY, LOCAL_BASE_URL, LOCAL_CONTEXT_TOKENS, LOCAL_MAX_TURNS, LOCAL_MAX_WRITE_BYTES, LOCAL_OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES, LOCAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, LOCAL_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS, LOCAL_TEMPERATURE, LOCAL_TIMEOUT_MS, WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS

annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates model selection to mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/model-role (resolveLocalRole) and the MCP stdio descriptor to lib/workers/mcp (buildRepovineMcpStdio)

annotation.summary: Shared repovine MCP wiring for harness workers and /ask agents: read-only vs mutating tool-id allowlists and stdio server config (REPOVINE_ROOT/REPOVINE_CONTEXT_SESSION_ID env).

keyExports.REPOVINE_ASK_MCP_TOOLS: Read-only repovine MCP tool ids (search/map/inspect/analyze/config-surface/trace/entrypoints/build-status/annotation-status/validate) allowed on the /ask path
keyExports.REPOVINE_WRITE_MCP_TOOLS: Mutating repovine MCP tool ids (refresh_context, write_annotation, merge_annotations) denied on /ask
keyExports.buildRepovineMcpStdio: Builds the stdio MCP server descriptor (node + REPOVINE_CLI) with repovineMcpEnv for a given repoRoot/contextSessionId
keyExports.repovineMcpEnv: Builds the child-process env, optionally inheriting process.env, always setting REPOVINE_ROOT and REPOVINE_CONTEXT_SESSION_ID when provided

assumptions: Tool ids are plain strings matched against the repovine MCP server's actual tool names, not typed refs — a renamed repovine tool silently drops out of both allowlists
annotation.integrationPoints: Points REPOVINE_CLI (mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/repovine) at the stdio MCP server process

annotation.summary: Normalizes repovine MCP tool-call telemetry (call counts, response bytes, per-tool breakdown) from a compliance contextQuality report or from the on-disk ContextSessionStore session file, and rolls per-sub-agent rows into a run total.

keyExports.buildRunMcp: Rolls a run's per-sub-agent MCP rows into { total, subAgents } for .harness/<run>.run.mcp.json.
keyExports.byToolFromEchoes: Counts requestEchoes by tool name into a byTool map.
keyExports.formatMcpMetrics: One-line 'mcp: N calls · tool×count ...' summary for CLI/Telegram replies, top maxTools (default 6) by count.
keyExports.mcpMetricsFromContextQuality: Preferred source: builds metrics from a compliance report's contextQuality.requestEchoes, or falls back to its aggregates (searchCallCount/mapCallCount/inspectCallCount).
keyExports.mcpMetricsFromEchoes: Builds { toolCallCount, totalResponseBytes, byTool } from a requestEchoes array.
keyExports.mcpMetricsFromSessionFile: Reads .repovine/.cache/sessions/<sessionId>.json and builds metrics from its requestEchoes/events; returns null on missing/unparseable file.
keyExports.resolveMcpMetrics: Tries mcpMetricsFromContextQuality first, then falls back to mcpMetricsFromSessionFile when repoRoot+contextSessionId are given.
keyExports.snapshotMcpSession: Reads the session file directly — call before compliance consumes/rotates the session store.
keyExports.totalMcpMetrics: Sums toolCallCount/totalResponseBytes and merges byTool maps across sub-agent records.

assumptions: Session id must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,128}$/ (sessionCacheFile returns null otherwise) so a session id can't escape .repovine/.cache/sessions/ via path traversal.

sideEffects.description: reads .repovine/.cache/sessions/<sessionId>.json via fs.readFileSync in mcpMetricsFromSessionFile/snapshotMcpSession

risks: mcpMetricsFromSessionFile swallows any read/parse error and returns null, so a corrupt or missing session file silently yields no MCP telemetry rather than surfacing an error.

annotation.summary: Assembles the combined prompt string (role brief + phase policy + engine harness brief + task body) for prompt-string CLI worker agents, mirroring the same brief/policy contract the Claude Agent SDK adapter uses.

keyExports.WRITE_ONLY_POLICY: Implement-phase policy text: no execution, and no write_annotation call — annotation sync is deferred to a dedicated annotate-phase sub-agent
keyExports.attachmentsBrief: Renders task.attachments as a numbered list of sandbox-relative paths for the agent to open with its own read tool
keyExports.buildWorkerPrompt: Joins roleBrief, policyForAssignment(assignment) and resolveHarnessBrief(...) into the brief, then appends task/runId/scope/acceptanceCriteria/constraints/contracts/requestedChecks and attachments as the body
keyExports.policyForAssignment: Picks ANNOTATION_ONLY_POLICY / READ_ONLY_POLICY / WRITE_ONLY_POLICY from assignment.contextSession.phase ('annotate' / 'explore' / default write-only)
keyExports.resolveHarnessBrief: Fetches the single-source engine brief via harnessBrief({name}) or harnessBrief({role}) from lib/repovine.mjs; falls back to FALLBACK_BRIEF (with a logged warning) only when the engine brief resolves to nothing

assumptions: The engine role names are exactly main | explorer | implementer | annotation-writer | architecture-auditor | code-reviewer; a briefName/role outside that set makes harnessBrief() resolve to nothing

risks.text: harnessBriefRole only special-cases contextSession.phase 'annotate' and 'explore'; a caller adding a new phase value must confirm it is mapped here or it silently resolves to the implementer write-only brief/policy.

invariants: The assembled brief is deterministic for a given (roleBrief, assignment phase, engine brief) triple.
The engine harness brief is the single source; this module concatenates, it does not author brief prose.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates the actual brief prose to mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/repovine (harnessBrief, sourced from `repovine delivery run-brief`).
annotation.dataFlow: task + assignment -> roleBrief + policyForAssignment(phase) + resolveHarnessBrief(engine brief) + task body/attachments -> combined worker prompt string.

annotation.summary: Normalizes per-provider token/cost usage (Claude Agent SDK result messages, OpenAI-compatible chat/completions usage) into one additive shape and rolls per-sub-agent rows into run totals for the delivery harness's .harness usage ledger.

keyExports.buildRunUsage: Rolls a run's per-sub-agent usage rows into { total, freshTotal, resumeTotal, subAgents } for .harness/<run>.run.usage.json.
keyExports.claudeModelId: Picks the model that did the sub-agent's work from a Claude SDK result message: result.model, else the heaviest entry in modelUsage (to skip cheap helper-model calls listed first).
keyExports.claudeUsage: Normalizes a Claude Agent SDK result message's usage/cost/duration into the common shape, with derived cacheHitRatio.
keyExports.emptyUsage: Builds an all-null usage row for a provider/model (e.g. a blocked run that never called the API).
keyExports.localUsage: Normalizes an OpenAI-compatible usage object (prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/cached_tokens) into the same additive shape, converting the subset cache convention to the additive one.
keyExports.totalUsage: Sums numeric fields across usage rows, skipping nulls per field, and recomputes cacheHitRatio from the summed totals.

assumptions: Anthropic usage is additive (input_tokens is the UNCACHED remainder; total = input + cache_creation + cache_read); OpenAI-compatible usage is subset (prompt_tokens is the total, cached_tokens the portion within it) — both are normalized to the additive convention.
Unknown numeric fields are represented as null, never 0, so 'not reported by provider' is never confused with 'zero usage'.
invariants: cacheHitRatio = cacheReadTokens / (cacheReadTokens + cacheCreationTokens + inputTokens), correct only because every normalizer converts to the additive model first.

annotation.summary: Host mount adapter for the attach launcher preflight: parses /proc/self/mountinfo, resolves which mount each bind-source path lives on, and asserts that mount's filesystem type keeps the bind topology provable (fail-closed) before docker attach is allowed to run.

keyExports.PreflightError: Error subclass carrying a `check` tag (e.g. 'mount-table', 'fs-type'); every cannot-enumerate or cannot-prove condition throws this rather than returning an empty/best-effort result.
keyExports.assertProvableFsType: Throws PreflightError if any bind-source path's mount fsType is in UNPROVABLE_FS_TYPES (9p, drvfs, virtiofs, nfs*, cifs, smb3, smbfs, sshfs, fuse/fuse.*, overlay), or (when wsl:true) is anything other than ext4.
keyExports.isWslHost: True if WSL_DISTRO_NAME env is set, or /proc/version (or injected procVersionText) matches /microsoft/i; a read failure returns false.
keyExports.mountForPath: Finds the mount a path lives on by longest-mountPoint-prefix match; on a tie the LATER table entry wins (mountinfo lists mounts in mount order, so the last line is the actual overmount); throws PreflightError if no mount contains the path.
keyExports.parseMountinfo: Parses /proc/self/mountinfo line format into [{ mountPoint, fsType }], decoding octal escapes in mount points; throws PreflightError on any line that doesn't parse (too few fields, no '-' separator, no fs-type) because skipping a bad line could hide the mount that matters.
keyExports.pathContains: True when path p equals or lives under parent, via path.relative string containment on already-canonicalized (realpath) paths; case-sensitive, byte-exact, no filesystem access.
keyExports.readHostMountTable: Reads mountinfoText (test seam) or the file at path (default /proc/self/mountinfo); throws PreflightError on unreadable file, empty text, or zero parsed mounts.

assumptions: Projection/network filesystems (9p, nfs, cifs, sshfs, overlay, fuse.*) are rejected because they re-export a foreign namespace: a mount visible on the far side never appears in this host's own /proc/self/mountinfo, so their topology cannot be proven from here.
On WSL the requirement tightens to ext4 specifically, the only filesystem type fully on the Linux side of the WSL boundary.

sideEffects.description: fs.readFileSync of /proc/self/mountinfo and /proc/version (paths overridable via params for tests)

risks.text: This module encodes the fail-closed host-mount-safety contract for docker attach; a caller changing its throw-vs-return behavior around cannot-enumerate cases would silently let attach proceed on an unproven mount topology.

annotation.summary: CLI entrypoint for `npm run attach` (preflight/run/restart/prepare) — the executable trust boundary that validates and mounts a pre-created host Git worktree at /workspace before invoking docker compose with the attach profile.

keyExports.launchFilePath: Resolves the `.attach-launch.json` pointer path (HARNESS_ATTACH_LAUNCH_FILE override or DEMO_ROOT default)
keyExports.mountsBelow: Detects mount points strictly below given roots (leak-through-the-bind check); a mount AT a root is fine
keyExports.parseWorktreeList: Parses `git worktree list --porcelain` output into { path, bare } entries
keyExports.preflight: Fail-closed validation (host platform, env paths, path-overlap topology, .git pointer, mount table) — creates nothing; every failure throws PreflightError with a one-line diagnostic before any docker call
keyExports.prepareLaunch: Creates the launch-scoped disposable git baseline repo and writes the `.attach-launch.json` pointer file
keyExports.resolveLaunchEnv: Merges explicit env vars with the prior `prepare` launch pointer; defaults HARNESS_HOST_UID/GID to the launcher's own uid/gid
keyExports.restartLaunch: Re-preflights and re-invokes compose for a restart
keyExports.runLaunch: Re-runs preflight (a prior standalone check is never trusted), prepares the control/runtime state layout under HARNESS_ATTACH_STATE_DIR, then invokes docker compose with the attach profile for cli/http/tg-bot
keyExports.walkWorktree: lstat walk of the worktree: never follows symlinks, rejects socket/FIFO/device nodes and hardlinked regular files (nlink > 1)

assumptions: Attach requires a Linux or WSL2 host (assertLinuxHost gates every entry point before any env/git/docker work); native Windows and macOS are unsupported here
The launcher never removes worktrees, state dirs, branches or refs, and never commits/merges/pushes — teardown is manual (docker:down + git worktree remove)
Attach services stack compose.attach.yaml on compose.yaml; ATTACH_TARGETS maps cli/http/tg-bot to their compose profile/service

sideEffects.description: readdirSync/lstatSync/readFileSync over the worktree and mount table
writeFileSync for the launch pointer file and launch-scoped git baseline repo
spawnSync git and docker compose

risks.text: preflight is the sole gate before any docker mount of a host worktree; weakening a check here (path-overlap, .git-pointer, mount-table scan) reopens the mount-escape it exists to close.

annotation.integrationPoints: Imports lib/env-file.mjs (loadEnvFile), lib/attach-guard.mjs (ATTACH_BASELINE_REF, ATTACH_GIT_POINTER_CONTENT), and scripts/attach-host-adapter.mjs (mount-table primitives: parseMountinfo, pathContains, readHostMountTable, assertProvableFsType, isWslHost) — PreflightError/parseMountinfo/pathContains are re-exported from attach-host-adapter for callers that import them from this module.

annotation.summary: Host-neutral docker compose front end for the sandbox profiles (cli/http/tg-bot/down): builds structured argv (no shell) so a literal '*' and paths with spaces reach compose unglobbed on Linux/macOS/Windows; called directly by npm scripts.

keyExports.normalizeHostPaths: (env) => env with HARNESS_WORKSPACE_DIR/HARNESS_AGENTS_HOST_DIR resolved against DEMO_ROOT if relative; absolute values pass through unchanged
keyExports.planCompose: (cmd, passthrough, baseEnv) => { args, env, cwd, workspaceDir } invocation plan for a subcommand; 'down' also merges DUMMY_ATTACH_ENV since it stacks the attach compose file but mounts nothing
keyExports.runCompose: (cmd, passthrough, baseEnv, { exec=defaultExec }) => pre-creates plan.workspaceDir (fs.mkdirSync recursive) then calls exec({args, env, cwd}); default exec spawnSync's docker with stdio inherit
keyExports.workspaceHostDir: (env=process.env) => absolute host path of the sandbox workspace dir (env.HARNESS_WORKSPACE_DIR or '.workspace'), resolved against DEMO_ROOT

assumptions: SUBCOMMANDS covers exactly cli, http, tg-bot, down; an unrecognized cmd throws
Attach mode has its own entry (scripts/attach-launcher.mjs); this wrapper never touches attach services except tearing them down via 'down'

sideEffects.description: spawnSync('docker', args, { stdio: 'inherit' }) via the default exec
fs.mkdirSync(workspaceDir, { recursive: true }) before running compose

risks: down's DUMMY_ATTACH_ENV values (HARNESS_ATTACH_WORKTREE/HARNESS_ATTACH_STATE_DIR set to '/attach-unset') are safe only because down never mounts volumes for the attach overlay; if down is changed to bind those paths, the dummy values would need to become real ones.

annotation.summary: Shebang CLI entry for the demo LangGraph orchestrator (CI/local debug, Telegram-free): parses --goal (alias --task) / --roles / --review flags, loads the project .env, resolves the target and provider, builds and invokes the compiled graph once, prints the reply, and exits 0/1 on completion+compliance.
assumptions: --goal is the vocabulary-level flag; --task is accepted as an alias (the wire protocol field stays `task`).
Requires the repovine CLI already built — checks rp.getProtocol(repoRoot) before running and exits 1 with a `npm run build` hint if it can't reach the CLI.

Multi-agent mode triggers when --roles is non-empty, --review is passed, or agentsMode() !== 'single'; greenfield runs fan scaffold roles out in parallel worktrees unless HARNESS_GREENFIELD_PARALLEL=0.
Exit code is 0 only when the run (or, in multi mode, every sub-agent) completed AND passed compliance; a blocked run (e.g. missing provider credentials) is a non-zero CI-visible outcome.

sideEffects.description: loadEnvFile() reads the project .env (same file the HTTP and Telegram entries read) before evaluating env vars; inline env vars still override it.
calls process.exit() at multiple points: usage/target/provider errors (2), missing repovine CLI (1), and 0/1 on run success/failure.
invokeGraph drives the LangGraph run, whose nodes shell out to the real `repovine agents` CLI and the resolved LLM provider (no mock/dry-run path).

annotation.summary: Shebang HTTP entry for the demo LangGraph orchestrator (Telegram-free handle): loads .env, resolves provider/target, verifies the repovine CLI is built, computes port/host/token from env with a fail-closed non-loopback bind check, builds the graph once, and starts startHttp().
assumptions: PORT sets the listen port (default 8080).
host: REPOVINE_IN_DOCKER=1 binds 0.0.0.0; otherwise defaults to HARNESS_HTTP_BIND or 127.0.0.1 (loopback).
Outside Docker, binding a non-loopback, non-localhost host without HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN set exits(2) — refuses to expose /goal, /ask, /reset unauthenticated.
An unset HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN still starts (loopback/isolated-net use), but logs that POST /goal and /ask are open to anyone who can reach the port.
Requires the repovine CLI already built (getProtocol(repoRoot) check); exits 1 with a rebuild hint if unreachable.

sideEffects.description: loadEnvFile() reads the project .env; reads PORT, HARNESS_HTTP_BIND, HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN, REPOVINE_IN_DOCKER from process.env.
process.exit(2) on unsupported provider/target-resolution failure/unsafe bind without a token; process.exit(1) on missing repovine CLI or startHttp() failure.
delegates to startHttp() (lib/channels/http-adapter.mjs) to start the listening server.

annotation.summary: Shebang Telegram entry for the demo LangGraph orchestrator: loads .env then ~/telegram.env, requires TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and a non-empty TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS allowlist, resolves provider/target, verifies the repovine CLI (bare `repovine delivery` smoke check), builds the graph once, and starts startTelegram().
assumptions: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS is fail-closed: empty means the bot accepts nobody and the process exits(1) rather than silently ignoring everyone — no hardcoded owner id, so a stray launch can never accidentally accept anyone.
Reads .env then ~/telegram.env in that order for local convenience; inline env vars still override both.
Exits 1 if TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is unset, if the allowlist ends up empty, or if the repovine CLI isn't reachable at REPOVINE_CLI; exits 2 for an unsupported LLM_PROVIDER or a target-resolution error.

sideEffects.description: loadEnvFile() reads the project .env and then ~/telegram.env; reads TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS from process.env.
process.exit(1) on missing token/empty allowlist/unreachable repovine CLI/startTelegram() failure; process.exit(2) on unsupported provider or target errors.

envDependencies.TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS: Fail-closed allowlist of Telegram user ids; empty exits 1.

annotation.summary: A development script that runs both build stages against the current repository, prints what they produced, and writes the snapshot and the graph to the cache directory. Despite its name it is not the package surface: nothing imports it, it exports nothing, and it exists to exercise the pipeline without the server around it.
assumptions: Both stages are called directly, so the pipeline can be exercised without the server runtime, the annotation store or any tool wiring in the way.

The printed summary is the point: import resolution counts, node and edge totals by type and kind, and three sample queries (pathFromRoot, impact analysis, per-domain member counts) that prove the graph is navigable.
Both dumps land in the cache directory, which is not tracked, so running it leaves the working tree clean.
It runs at module top level and is invoked directly rather than imported.

sideEffects.description: scans the whole repository through the first stage
writes the snapshot and graph dumps into the cache directory
prints the stage summaries and sample query output

risks.text: The file name suggests a package entry point, but the published surface is the command-line and server entries; a consumer wiring against this path gets a script that runs a full scan and prints to standard output on import.

risks: It scans the entire repository unconditionally, so on a large tree it is a full cold build rather than a quick check.
The sample queries pick a module by name matching ('oauth'/'auth'), so on a repository without a matching path those sections print nothing and the run still looks successful.
patterns: The smallest end-to-end path through the pipeline: two stage calls and a print, with nothing in between to hide a failure.
annotation.flowDescription: Dev smoke path: resolve repoRoot → collectRepositoryFactsAsync → composeRepositoryGraph → print import resolution stats and graphStats → demo pathFromRoot/impact/domain-member queries.
invariants: It starts no server and writes no annotations.
It exports nothing.
Its output goes to the cache directory and standard output only.
annotation.integrationPoints: Calls the two stages directly through mod:repovine/src/stage1 and mod:repovine/src/stage2, queries the result through mod:repovine/src/graph, and resolves the repository and cache locations through mod:repovine/src/paths. It is not part of the server entry path.
annotation.stateShape: None; it holds the snapshot and graph only for the length of the run.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → first stage snapshot → second stage graph → printed statistics and sample queries → snapshot and graph dumps written to the cache directory.

annotation.summary: computeChangedPaths shells out to `git diff --name-only` between two revisions and returns the repo-relative changed-file set, the base for revision-linked compliance evidence.

keyExports.computeChangedPaths: Runs `git -C repoRoot diff --name-only --no-ext-diff -z baseRef [headRef]` via execFileSync and returns a Set of changed paths, or null when unavailable (no repoRoot/baseRef, non-git repo, or git failure).

assumptions: git diff output uses NUL-separated (-z) filenames to survive unusual paths; GIT_DIFF_MAX_BUFFER caps stdout at 64MB.

sideEffects.description: execFileSync('git', ['diff', '--name-only', ...]) to list changed files between two revisions

risks: Any git failure (bad revs, non-git repo, git not on PATH) is swallowed into the same null return as a legitimately missing baseRef, so a real invocation error is indistinguishable from an absent one.
invariants: null means the change-set is UNAVAILABLE, not empty; callers must not treat null as no-changes. An empty Set is a real answer (nothing changed).

annotation.summary: The built-in agent manifests: one definition per repovine role, each declaring the tools that role is allowed, the result fields it must return, the client surfaces it projects into, and per-client model hints. The definition list is the source of truth that the MCP manifest tool serves and that the onboarding path renders into client agent files.

keyExports.ANNOTATION_WRITER_DEF: The annotation specialist, whose tool set covers the annotate phase.
keyExports.BUILTIN_AGENT_DEFS: The ordered definitions, the source of truth for the specialist agents.
keyExports.BUILTIN_MANIFESTS: The manifests projected out of those definitions.
keyExports.BuiltinAgentDef: One definition: a manifest plus optional model hints.
keyExports.ManifestModelHints: Per-client model hints for an agent (claude/cursor/codexReasoningEffort).
keyExports.getManifestByRole: The canonical manifest for a protocol role.
keyExports.getModelHints: The model hints for an agent name.

assumptions: Model hints are keyed by client surface rather than by provider: a client can remain a projection target even when it is not available as a worker provider.
Tool lists are curated per role rather than derived, which is what makes a read-only role genuinely read-only.
The definitions are static data; nothing here reads configuration or the filesystem.
Every definition is built through the internal manifest() helper, which sets canEditFiles/allowedTools/expectedInputs/requiredRunResultFields/projectionTargets explicitly and dedupes the tool list.
risks: The curated tool lists drift when a new MCP tool ships without being added, so a role silently lacks a capability.

Tool lists are curated per role rather than derived from the tool registry, and they are declarative metadata: the read-only roles carry the annotation-writing tools. Read-only capability is declared by canEditFiles on the manifest, which the result validator enforces against reported file changes.
Because the manifests are projected into client files at onboarding, an edit here does not reach an already-onboarded workspace until setup runs again.
patterns: One definition list drives three consumers: the MCP manifest tool, the projection into client files, and the doctor's drift check.
invariants: A manifest name matches the identity of the client agent file it is projected into.
Every protocol role resolves to exactly one canonical manifest.
annotation.integrationPoints: Manifest and role types come from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol; the definitions are served by the delivery CLI manifest subcommand, rendered into client assets by the CLI onboarding path, and read by the projection renderers in mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection.
annotation.dataFlow: definition records -> manifest lookups for the delivery manifests command -> rendered agent files in the client trees -> read back by the doctor when checking for drift.

annotation.summary: Authoritative Zod schema module for Delivery Protocol v1. Declares the assignment a harness hands an agent, the run result an agent returns, the compliance report repovine produces about that run, the agent manifests, the context-quality artifacts and context packs, and the capability result shapes for architecture audit and code review. Exports the protocol descriptor and the JSON Schema projection for harnesses that are not TypeScript.

keyExports.AGENT_ROLES: The role vocabulary the protocol recognizes: main, explorer, implementer, annotation-writer, architecture-auditor, code-reviewer.
keyExports.AcceptanceCriterionSchema: One acceptance criterion with a stable id, statement, and required flag; frozen before implementation.
keyExports.AgentAssignmentSchema: The task a harness assigns: run id, role, task, scope, version, structured acceptance criteria, requested checks, optional delivery refs and verification policy, context session.
keyExports.AgentComplianceReportSchema: repovine's verdict: validity, errors, ungrounded and inconsistent annotations, required followups.
keyExports.AgentManifestSchema: The manifest describing a role's capabilities and obligations.
keyExports.AgentRunResultSchema: The public run artifact, including compliance flags and the optional context/audit/review and delivery-verification payloads.
keyExports.ContextPackSchema: A context pack of resolved anchors handed to an agent.
keyExports.ContextSessionPolicySchema: Context-session policy: phase, enforcement mode, thresholds.
keyExports.CriterionResultSchema: One criterion's coverage result: status, grounded evidence, explanation, and an optional custody resolution that a resolved needs-developer criterion points at.
keyExports.DeliveryVerdictSchema: The split delivery verdict: intentVerified (boolean) plus optional assuranceProfile, assurancePassed, deliveryAccepted.
keyExports.DeliveryVerificationResultSchema: The verifier's registry of per-criterion results plus the delivery verdict; distinct from open review.
keyExports.EVIDENCE_KINDS: The evidence-kind vocabulary a criterion result may cite: repository, review, test, build, typecheck, runtime, security, developer, custom.
keyExports.EvidenceReferenceSchema: A pointer to observable evidence for a criterion (kind plus optional file/line/graphNodeId/symbol/artifactRef/revision).
keyExports.PROJECTION_TARGETS: The client surfaces the protocol can be projected into: agents-md, cursor, codex, claude, json.
keyExports.REQUESTED_CHECKS: The checks an assignment may request (dependencies, config, runtime-flow, architecture, code-review, annotations, tests), which drive compliance flag validation.
keyExports.RUN_STATUSES: The terminal run statuses: complete, partial, blocked, failed.
keyExports.VerificationPolicySchema: The harness's frozen per-criterion evidence choice: assurance profile, version counter, and requirements.
keyExports.buildDeliveryProtocol: Returns the DeliveryProtocol descriptor: protocolVersion, schema ids (SCHEMA_IDS), mcpTools (DELIVERY_PROTOCOL_MCP_TOOLS, empty -- CLI-only), and cliCommands (DELIVERY_PROTOCOL_CLI_COMMANDS listing the delivery subcommands).

assumptions: Sub-agent schemas (SubagentAssignment, SubagentHandoff) are internal: an external harness consumes the aggregated AgentRunResult rather than the per-sub-agent shapes.
Context-quality types (CONTEXT_PHASES, CONTEXT_ENFORCEMENT_MODES) are re-exported from src/context-quality/types.js, which stays their source of truth.
Requested checks are the mechanism by which an assignment decides which compliance flags are validated.
Delivery Protocol is CLI-only for harness/integration (DELIVERY_PROTOCOL_MCP_TOOLS is an empty array); worker MCP exposes context tools only, not the protocol validators.

risks.text: Published protocol contract: the version literal, schema shapes and JSON Schema projection are what external harnesses and the managed AGENTS.md sections are built against, so a version bump or a field change lands outside this repo before it lands here.

risks: A requested check with no corresponding validation path silently passes, since compliance flags are driven by the requested set rather than by an exhaustive sweep.
patterns: The run result JSON block in the managed agent instructions is the harness contract itself, not illustrative prose.
Every protocol surface is a Zod schema first, with the TypeScript type inferred from it, so validation and typing cannot drift apart.
invariants: The compliance report (AgentComplianceReportSchema) is constructed by the validator and never parsed from agent-supplied input.
TypeScript types are inferred from the Zod schemas (z.infer), so the runtime validator and static types cannot drift apart.

ungroundedAnnotations and inconsistentAnnotations on the compliance report are mode-independent observable facts, not a verdict; only hard inconsistencies (keyExports/sideEffects) land there, advisory env mismatches stay in warnings.
annotation.integrationPoints: Served through the delivery-protocol CLI commands (`repovine delivery` for the descriptor, plus subcommands `delivery manifests`, `delivery run-brief`, `delivery validate-assignment`, `delivery validate-result`, `delivery validate-review-input`, `delivery compliance`), enforced by mod:repovine/src/agents/validation, projected into client surfaces by mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection, and re-exports context-quality shapes from mod:repovine/src/context-quality/types.
annotation.dataFlow: Zod schemas define AgentAssignment/AgentRunResult -> harness sends assignment, agent returns result -> compliance validator checks result against schema plus observable graph/annotation state -> AgentComplianceReport.

annotation.summary: Loads the repository's own role definitions from the roles section of the committed repovine config. It validates rather than transforms: each brief is served byte for byte including its frontmatter, and a brief carrying protocol markers or an embedded result block is reported as a structured error for the repository owner to fix rather than being cleaned up. A working-tree brief path is admitted by the shared containment guard, so a link resolving outside the repository is refused. Given a tree-ish it reads the config and every brief from that committed revision instead of the working tree.

keyExports.LoadRolesOptions: Options: an optional tree-ish to read the config and briefs from.
keyExports.ProjectRole: One role: id, optional description, ownership scope, brief path, verbatim brief bytes, their hash, and any non-blocking advisories.
keyExports.ProjectRoleSource: The load result: whether the config opted in at all, plus the roles.
keyExports.loadProjectRoleSource: Loads and validates the role definitions, returning the source or a list of errors.

assumptions: An absent roles section is a valid state meaning the repository has not opted in, not an error.
A role id must be lowercase kebab-case, and a brief path must stay inside the repository after symlink resolution.
A brief path that names a file which does not exist is reported as unreadable rather than as an escape.
The scope defaults to the repository root when a role does not declare one.
The hash is taken over the exact brief bytes, so any edit to the file changes it, including whitespace.

Contamination signatures are literal Delivery Protocol markers ('<!-- repovine:delivery-protocol', '<!-- repovine:harness-agent-briefs', '<!-- repovine:harness-handoff', '## Delivery Protocol result block').

sideEffects.description: reads the config and the brief files from the working tree
reads the config and briefs from a committed revision through git when a tree-ish is given

risks.text: The roles section of the committed repovine config is a contract repository owners author against, and the brief bytes are served verbatim to agents; changing the accepted shape or the id rules invalidates configurations that live outside this repository.

risks: Contamination detection matches a fixed set of literal markers, so a brief carrying protocol content in some other form passes validation and reaches an agent unchanged.
A scope path excluded from the scan configuration is reported only as a non-blocking advisory, so a role can be loaded successfully while owning paths the graph never indexes.
patterns: Validate and refuse rather than sanitize: preparing the file is the repository owner's job, which keeps the served bytes predictable.
The dependency direction is strictly one way, from consumer through the CLI into this loader, so no harness or client concepts appear in these types.
invariants: A brief is served byte for byte, frontmatter included; nothing is stripped or rewritten.
The hash is over the exact bytes served, so a consumer can pin the prose it received.
A tree-ish read takes both the config and every brief from that same revision.
annotation.integrationPoints: Reads the roles section of the committed repovine config; containment guard from mod:repovine/src/fs/containment; exposed read-only through the agents roles CLI command and consumed in-process when the role catalog is assembled.
annotation.dataFlow: config roles section -> per-role validation of id, scope and brief path -> verbatim brief read plus hash -> role source, or a list of structured errors.

annotation.summary: Schema validation and Delivery Protocol compliance checking. It compares result claims with the graph, annotation state, manifests, and recorded context sessions. Evidence-backed protocol and annotation findings can still fail harness compliance; the weighted context-quality score was measured against outcome-labelled sessions, did not beat a trivial baseline, and so is recomputed and reported with warnings/followups but withheld from rejecting a handoff (CONTEXT_QUALITY_HARD_GATE_VALIDATED = false) until a validated bar is met.

keyExports.CheckComplianceInput: The result and its assignment, the state, the manifest, and whether the run began greenfield.
keyExports.ComplianceState: What the check needs: the repository, graph, snapshot, annotations, and the context-quality accessors.
keyExports.SchemaValidation: A parse outcome with its errors, warnings and any unsupported version.
keyExports.checkCompliance: The compliance pass: grounding, scope, annotation state, quality and context session, producing the report.
keyExports.validateAssignment: Parses an assignment against its schema.
keyExports.validateReviewInput: Parses a review input and cross-checks its declared changes against the result.
keyExports.validateRunResult: Parses a run result against its schema.

assumptions: Enforcement mode decides severity for evidence-backed annotation and protocol findings; context-quality verdicts remain advisory in both modes until the labelled-corpus return bar is met.
The declared phase constrains what a result may claim, and a scoped sub-agent is judged against its own scope.
Aggregate roll-ups that are merely unannotated stay advisory because they are derived rather than authored.
Environment inconsistencies stay advisory because dynamic access is under-captured.
requiredRunResultFields defaults to ['summary'] when the caller does not supply its own role-derived list.

sideEffects.description: a valid report consumes the run's context session unless retention is requested

risks: The provenance gate exists because the quality score measures completeness rather than correctness: without it an agent can write plausible notes and score well.

The greenfield exemption depends on the caller: the run's own writes are known here, but a sibling sub-agent's writes land in the same shared file -- greenfieldRun must be set by the harness for every sub-agent in a multi-sub-agent run, or later siblings see an earlier sibling's writes as prior context and lose the exemption.

An omitted assignment does not skip compliance, it disarms the assignment-derived gates: runId linkage, phase and scope judgements, and the context-session requirement all go inert, while manifest fields, declared graph nodes, declared annotations and provenance still run and still hard-fail. Weak tool usage is still scored whenever the result carries a contextSessionId, but nothing can make it enforceable without an assignment, so it only ever surfaces as a warning.
Scope membership is decided from the supplied hints, so an assignment whose scope omits a form the nodes actually carry judges the wrong set.
patterns: Evidence-backed graph, protocol, annotation consistency, and provenance checks remain enforceable; the unvalidated context score is one explicit advisory exception.
A rejected advisory context report is retained for review, while accepted reports are consumed after the remaining compliance checks pass.
Pre-existing annotations are never re-judged because only writes claimed by the current run are in scope.
invariants: Context-quality acceptHandoff=false alone never makes compliance invalid until the validation return bar is met.
Rejected context reports remain available instead of being consumed as successful handoffs.
Provenance applies to code modules only; derived roll-ups are excluded.
Identifiers in a result must resolve against the graph.
An annotate-phase result never reports source edits.
annotation.integrationPoints: Schemas and the protocol version come from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol and the role manifests from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests; annotation state, quality and staleness from mod:repovine/src/annotations/store and mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance; effect vocabulary from mod:repovine/src/annotations/side-effect-vocab; module classification from mod:repovine/src/annotations/module-kind; ownership resolution from mod:repovine/src/graph/node-ids; the context-quality shapes from mod:repovine/src/context-quality/types. Exposed through the validation and compliance commands of the command line.
annotation.dataFlow: result and assignment -> schema parse -> evidence-backed phase/scope/annotation/provenance checks -> recomputed advisory context report -> errors only from validated evidence gates, plus warnings and required followups -> accepted session consumption.

annotation.summary: The entry points for architecture analysis: run the detector suite over a scope and return a balanced page of findings, or expand one finding into detail. It takes a small state slice rather than the server runtime, so the analysis can be exercised without the server around it.

keyExports.RefactoringOpportunityDetailArgs: The finding identifier plus the scope and node cap for its expansion.
keyExports.RefactoringReportArgs: Scope, categories, minimum confidence, page limit, and the two behaviour toggles.
keyExports.RefactoringState: What the analysis needs: the graph, the module index, annotations, and optionally the snapshot, thresholds, propagation settings and entrypoints.
keyExports.refactoringCategoriesFromFindingId: Resolves a finding identifier back to the categories that must be rerun to produce it.
keyExports.runRefactoringOpportunityDetail: Expands one finding by identifier, with its affected nodes and the edges between them.
keyExports.runRefactoringReport: Runs the detectors for a scope and returns a capped, category-balanced page of findings.

assumptions: An empty detector registry raises with an explanation rather than returning no findings, because registration happens through a side-effect import of ./detector-bootstrap.js and a caller that reached the analysis without it would otherwise see a clean report on an unanalyzed repository.

A detector is skipped when none of its categories were asked for, and again when it declares an applicability test that no in-scope module satisfies -- safe because such a detector emits nothing anyway. A later per-category filter then drops categories a multi-category detector produced but the caller did not request.
The detail path searches the full uncapped list and with no confidence floor, so a valid identifier resolves even when the finding sits past the report's page or below its threshold.

A finding identifier maps to its categories by prefix, and failing that by the longest matching detector identifier from the registry, so a new detector's prefix round-trips without a table to update.
Findings are deduplicated per category and primary node before any cap, so the page reflects distinct problems rather than repeated views of one.
Everything here is a read over the state; nothing is written.
risks: The page is balanced across categories rather than strictly ranked, so the highest-confidence findings overall are not necessarily the ones returned -- a caller reading the page as a priority order will misread it.
The confidence floor defaults to a middle value (0.5), so a report with no arguments silently omits everything below it; the number is reported back but the omission is not.
Detector applicability is cached per predicate for the run, so a detector whose applicability depends on anything beyond the module shape would be evaluated once and reused.
patterns: Registry dispatch with two cheap gates before running anything, so an unrequested or inapplicable detector costs nothing.
One collection path serving both modes, with the report capping what the detail path deliberately does not.
invariants: A cold registry fails loudly rather than reporting zero findings.
The detail path never misses a finding the report could have shown.
Requested categories bound what is returned, whatever a detector produced.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wrapped by the analysis tool under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/analyze-architecture; detectors are registered by mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detector-bootstrap and resolved through mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detector-registry; thresholds from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/config; scope resolution, sorting and expansion from the scope, finding and detail modules beside it; annotation state from mod:repovine/src/annotations/store and staleness from mod:repovine/src/annotations/propagation.
annotation.dataFlow: state and arguments -> scope resolved -> applicable detectors run -> findings filtered by category and confidence, sorted and deduplicated -> either a balanced capped page, or one finding expanded with its nodes and their edges.

annotation.summary: Built-in architecture detector pack catalog. INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS lists serverSurfaceDetectorPack and uiSurfaceDetectorPack for detector-bootstrap drift validation; actual registration order lives in detector-bootstrap INTERNAL_DETECTORS.
assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream imports; existing annotation prose still accurate.
risks: Pack/bootstrap drift throws at startup via assertDetectorPacksRegistered.
patterns: Catalog module — does not register detectors itself.
annotation.integrationPoints: detector-bootstrap assertDetectorPacksRegistered; server-surface and ui-surface detector packs.

annotation.summary: Server-surface architecture detector pack. serverHandlerOrchestrationDetector adapts detectServerHandlerOrchestration with serverSurfaceApplies appliesTo gate; serverSurfaceDetectorPack catalogs it for INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS drift guard.

keyExports.serverHandlerOrchestrationDetector: god-module category detector gated by serverSurfaceApplies.

assumptions: Propagation review: upstream mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors updated for shared annotation-secret and component-signals modules; contract unchanged.
risks: Backend modules without HTTP handler path signals skip this detector entirely.
patterns: Thin adapter over detectServerHandlerOrchestration with appliesTo gate.
annotation.integrationPoints: architecture/detectors detectServerHandlerOrchestration; surfaces/server serverSurfaceApplies.

annotation.summary: ui-surface detector pack: eight ArchitectureDetector adapters (client-business-logic, state-fragmentation, effect-spaghetti, prop-drilling-orchestration, duplicated-client-policy, privileged-client-side-effect, sensitive-browser-storage, server-client-boundary) gated by uiSurfaceApplies, each delegating run() to the legacy detect* body in architecture/detectors (bodies untouched). uiSurfaceDetectorPack groups them for the INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS catalog. Registration deliberately stays in detector-bootstrap at legacy positions — a pack is a grouping/identity unit, not a registration loop, because order is load-bearing.

keyExports.uiSurfaceDetectorPack: DetectorPack grouping eight UI-gated detectors for assertDetectorPacksRegistered.

assumptions: Propagation review: upstream mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors updated for shared annotation-secret and component-signals modules; contract unchanged.
risks: Adding a UI detector requires bootstrap registration at legacy position — pack alone is insufficient.
patterns: Each detector: id, categories, appliesTo: uiSurfaceApplies, run delegates to legacy detect*.
annotation.integrationPoints: architecture/detectors detect* implementations; surfaces/ui uiSurfaceApplies; detector-bootstrap INTERNAL_DETECTORS interleaving.

annotation.summary: Optional annotationReasoning support for analyze_architecture: maps SemanticQuestion to relevant annotation fields, builds AnnotationContext with per-node picked fields and a content-freshness flag, and supplies QUESTION_HINTS agent copy for interpreting findings against repovine.annots.json.

keyExports.AnnotationContext: question, relevantFields, nodes[] with picked annotation slices and annotationContentFresh flag, agent hint string.
keyExports.QUESTION_HINTS: Per-SemanticQuestion agent guidance for interpreting findings against annotations.
keyExports.RELEVANT_FIELDS: Maps each SemanticQuestion to AnnotationField keys to include in context slices.
keyExports.SemanticQuestion: Enum: same-concept, shared-invariant, real-side-effect, intentional-internal, type-only-or-barrel, etc.
keyExports.buildAnnotationContext: Builds AnnotationContext for implicated nodeIds (capped) with content freshness from AnnotationStore.

assumptions: buildAnnotationContext caps implicated nodes and skips ids without modulesById entries.
QUESTION_HINTS is agent-facing copy — not validated against graph facts.

annotationContentFresh answers only whether each note still matches its module's own text and schema, which is what comparing notes across modules needs; the propagation half of freshness is reported by inspect_node.
risks: Stale annotations on implicated nodes reduce reasoning value until queue is drained.
Over-broad RELEVANT_FIELDS bloat MCP architecture detail payloads.

risks.text: annotationContentFresh: true does not mean the note is confirmed overall — a module whose upstream moved is propagation-stale while its own text is unchanged. Read annotationMeta from inspect_node before acting on a note's cross-module claims.

patterns: annotationReasoning mode is opt-in per detector call — absent annotations yield null slices.
annotation.flowDescription: analyze_architecture detector hit → buildAnnotationContext picks fields per question → agents read hint + per-node slices.
invariants: Returns undefined when nodeIds empty or no resolvable modules.
QUESTION_HINTS text is agent-facing copy, not validated against graph.
extensionPoints: New detector categories add a SemanticQuestion, RELEVANT_FIELDS row, and QUESTION_HINTS prose block.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors; uses mod:repovine/src/annotations/store for content freshness (which decides through mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness) and mod:repovine/src/annotations/format risk helpers.
annotation.dataFlow: detector implicated nodeIds + SemanticQuestion → buildAnnotationContext → optional annotationContext attached to RefactoringFinding for analyze_architecture detail.

annotation.summary: Shared single-source-of-truth mapping of UI component local signal counts to workflow-signal kind labels; prevents drift between detectors and detail view.

keyExports.workflowSignalKinds: Maps UiComponentLocalSignals counts to workflow kind labels (local-state, effects, data-access, navigation, timers, subscriptions, service-imports, validation/mapping).

assumptions: workflowSignalKinds is invoked by detectors (detectPropDrillingOrchestration) and detail expansion (refactoringCategoryDetail) with the same UiComponentLocalSignals input.
invariants: Single source of truth to prevent detector/detail label drift.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imported by mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors (detectPropDrillingOrchestration, detectServerHandlerOrchestration) and mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detail (refactoringCategoryDetail).
annotation.dataFlow: UiComponentLocalSignals → workflowSignalKinds → filtered array of kind labels.

annotation.summary: The tunable thresholds that decide whether an architecture detector emits a finding. Settings arrive in three tiers: per call through the tool arguments, per repository through the configuration file which is what this module models, and a hardcoded research tier covering the confidence formulas, the severity mapping and the truncation budgets, which is not exposed. A named strictness profile supplies the baseline and individual knobs may be overridden on top of it.

keyExports.AnnotationRiskQualityByKind: The minimum annotation quality expected of each module kind.
keyExports.DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS: The middle profile, exposed so other layers can name the default.
keyExports.RefactoringFileConfig: What a repository may set: a profile, per-knob overrides, or both.
keyExports.RefactoringThresholds: Every threshold group, one per detector family, including the security-sensitive ones.
keyExports.resolveThresholds: Merges the chosen profile with the per-knob overrides into a complete threshold set.

assumptions: The middle profile is the calibration target; the other two are relative perturbations chosen to keep a report readable rather than independently tuned.
For most groups the direction is plain: a looser profile lowers the bar to emit and produces more findings, a stricter one raises it and produces fewer.
The per-kind annotation quality bars deep-merge rather than replace, so tightening one kind leaves the calibrated defaults for the others in place.
The derived-stale penalty does not decide whether a module is surfaced — the detector always surfaces it — it raises the bar that decides how confidently the finding is stated.
A repository that sets nothing gets the middle profile.

risks.text: Within the annotation group the direction is mixed: the per-kind quality bars, the derived-stale penalty and the stale hop limit all tighten under a stricter profile and surface more modules, while the importance floor that decides candidacy rises with it and removes modules before quality is computed at all. A caller changing strictness gets a different population of annotation findings rather than simply more or fewer, and must read those findings themselves instead of inferring a direction.

risks: The scalar quality threshold and the per-kind bars move in opposite directions across profiles, and the scalar applies only when no per-kind bar exists — so it matters solely for a custom configuration that omits them, where its direction is the reverse of what the profile name suggests.

Lowering an evidence threshold on a security group raises the false-positive rate without changing what is detected, so a report can become noisy in a way that reads as a code problem rather than a configuration one.
Nothing reports the effective thresholds, so a repository running under a profile it did not intend produces findings that look like the code changed.
patterns: Complete profiles rather than deltas: each named profile carries every threshold, so reading one shows the whole posture without composing.
Configuration covers what a repository legitimately tunes; the formulas that decide confidence and severity stay out of reach on purpose.
invariants: Resolution is profile first, then per-knob overrides.
An absent configuration resolves to the middle profile.
Overriding one kind's quality bar never clears the others.
extensionPoints: A new detector family adds its threshold group to the interface and a value to all three profiles.
A new security detector follows the same evidence-score or signal-count shape as the existing ones.
annotation.integrationPoints: The module kinds the per-kind bars are keyed by come from mod:repovine/src/annotations/module-kind; the resolved thresholds are consumed by every detector in the architecture analysis. Strictness reaches the analysis only through the repository configuration file — resolved once when configuration is loaded, named by no tool argument, so a change takes effect only after a configuration reload.
annotation.dataFlow: repository configuration → named profile as the baseline → per-knob overrides merged on top, with the per-kind quality bars deep-merged → a complete threshold set handed to every detector.

annotation.summary: analyze_architecture opportunity-detail expansion: given one RefactoringFinding, builds per-node summaries (refactoringNodeSummary), affected import edges (affectedNodeEdges), category-specific facts across 20+ finding categories (refactoringCategoryDetail), and structured follow-up MCP calls (refactoringNextCalls) — replacing hand-written `tool({json})` string literals with the shared NextCall shape.

keyExports.affectedNodeEdges: Import edges strictly between the given finding's node ids (both endpoints in nodeIds), each carrying resolved imported symbol names; capped at 100 edges.
keyExports.refactoringCategoryDetail: Expanded per-category finding payload with affected nodes/edges and category-specific facts, switch-dispatched on finding.category (boundary, god-module, god-domain/low-cohesion, client-business-logic, flow-convergence, state-fragmentation, effect-spaghetti, prop-drilling-orchestration, service-wrapper-explosion, ui-domain-coupling, route-convergence, duplicated-client-policy, design-system-leakage, event-driven-boundary, secret-config-boundary, authorization-policy-drift, trust-boundary-validation, privileged-client-side-effect, sensitive-browser-storage, server-client-boundary, source-disclosure-surface, annotation-secret-hygiene, annotation-risk, duplicate-like, unclear-architecture).
