keyExports.refactoringNextCalls: Suggested follow-up MCP tool calls (inspect_node always first; analyze_dependencies impact for module/export scopes; category-specific calls for boundary/event-driven-boundary/secret-related/trust-boundary/source-disclosure/annotation-risk/annotation-secret-hygiene findings); when finding.annotationContext is present, unshifts a no-tool instruction to read the shipped annotation excerpts before drilling into source.
keyExports.refactoringNodeSummary: Per-node summary: label/type, plus for a module: packageId, relativeFilePath, up to 12 exports, exportCount, fanIn/fanOut (runtime import edges), envVars, domains, moduleKind, and (if annotated) an annotation excerpt with freshness+quality; for a runtime-resource/domain node without a module, raw node.data.

assumptions: annotationReasoning/annotationContext is opt-in per detector invocation and, when present, is meant to be read before further tool calls (refactoringNextCalls unshifts that instruction).

refactoringCategoryDetail's per-category cases each read only the fields relevant to that category from modulesById/semanticHints — a finding whose category has no explicit case returns only the base node summaries/edges.
risks: Large implicated node sets (e.g. affectedNodeEdges) are capped without pagination in detail view — callers see only the first 100 edges.
Stale annotations reduce the value of annotation-derived detail fields (annotationExcerpt, annotation quality/freshness, policyTokens).
patterns: Detail expansion is on-demand — list view stays compact; refactoringNextCalls returns structured NextCall values instead of hand-written call strings.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imports from shared annotation-secret (annotationSecretFieldPaths), component-signals (workflowSignalKinds) and heuristics (frontendFeatureKey, policyTokens, coupledTargetRole, etc.); called from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture runRefactoringReport; consumes mod:repovine/src/annotations/store, freshness and quality.
annotation.dataFlow: RefactoringFinding → refactoringNodeSummary/affectedNodeEdges for context, refactoringCategoryDetail for category-specific facts → refactoringNextCalls for suggested follow-ups → analyze_architecture detail-mode envelope.

annotation.summary: Built-in architecture-detector bootstrap (mirrors stage1/source/bootstrap). bootstrapInternalDetectors registers INTERNAL_DETECTORS into the process-global detector-registry on first import, and is auto-invoked on module load. INTERNAL_DETECTORS preserves the original if-chain order because runRefactoringReport appends in registry order and sortFindings resolves ties by insertion order -- order is load-bearing for output parity. Wraps legacy detect* exports plus the ui-surface/server-surface detector packs (clientBusinessLogicDetector, stateFragmentationDetector, effectSpaghettiDetector, propDrillingOrchestrationDetector, duplicatedClientPolicyDetector, privilegedClientSideEffectDetector, sensitiveBrowserStorageDetector, serverClientBoundaryDetector, serverHandlerOrchestrationDetector) as thin adapters. assertDetectorPacksRegistered throws at startup if a DetectorPack (from architecture-detectors/index's INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS) lists an id missing from INTERNAL_DETECTORS. Also imports the source-plugin bootstrap so capability lookups (pluginHasUiSurfaces via uiSurfaceApplies) see a populated registry in isolated unit tests.

keyExports.assertDetectorPacksRegistered: Throws if a DetectorPack lists a detector id missing from INTERNAL_DETECTORS -- drift guard between the pack catalog and the ordered registration list; defaults to the real INTERNAL_DETECTORS/INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS lists but takes parameters so the throw path is unit-testable.

assumptions: bootstrapInternalDetectors is idempotent (a module-level `bootstrapped` flag short-circuits repeat calls) and is auto-invoked once at import time, mirroring stage1/source/bootstrap and stage1/iac's side-effect-import pattern.
Registration order is owned by INTERNAL_DETECTORS in this file, not by the DetectorPack catalog; the catalog is identity/grouping only.
uiSurfaceApplies is re-exported only so the capability gate can be toggled/inspected in tests; the dispatcher itself never reads it directly.

sideEffects.description: populates the process-global detector registry on first import via bootstrapInternalDetectors()

risks: Pack/registration drift throws at startup (assertDetectorPacksRegistered), blocking any command that loads this module until INTERNAL_DETECTORS is fixed to match the packs.
Adding a new detector without an entry in INTERNAL_DETECTORS is caught only if it is also listed in a DetectorPack; a detector added to neither silently never runs.
patterns: INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS from architecture-detectors/index catalogs expected detector ids; the ordered registration here is the single source of run order.

Legacy detect* functions (detectDuplicateLike, detectBoundary, detectGodModule, detectDomainShape, detectFlowConvergence, detectServiceWrapperExplosion, detectUiDomainCoupling, detectRouteConvergence, detectDesignSystemLeakage, detectEventDrivenBoundary, detectSecretConfigBoundary, detectAuthorizationPolicyDrift, detectTrustBoundaryValidation, detectSourceDisclosureSurface, detectAnnotationSecretHygiene, detectAnnotationRisk, detectUnclearArchitecture) are wrapped inline as ArchitectureDetector objects; ui-surface and server-surface detectors are imported as already-built detector objects from their own packs.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture index; mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detector-registry (registerDetector); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors (legacy detect* bodies); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture-detectors (ui-surface/server-surface packs and INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS catalog); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/surfaces/ui (uiSurfaceApplies).
annotation.dataFlow: module import -> bootstrapInternalDetectors() runs once -> assertDetectorPacksRegistered() checks pack/registration parity -> registerDetector() for each INTERNAL_DETECTORS entry -> global detector-registry populated for runRefactoringReport to read.

annotation.summary: In-process architecture detector registry. registerDetector collects ArchitectureDetector plugins at bootstrap; getDetectors returns the list; categoriesDisjoint and anyInScopeApplies gate which detectors run for a scoped analyze_architecture request.

keyExports.anyInScopeApplies: Cached scope check whether appliesTo predicate matches any scoped module.
keyExports.registerDetector: Appends detector to process-global registry at bootstrap.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream imports; existing annotation prose still accurate.

sideEffects.description: Process-global detectors array mutated at bootstrap

risks: Duplicate category declarations across detectors can emit multiple findings for same pattern.
patterns: Singleton registry — registration order equals run order within category.
appliesTo cache keyed by predicate function reference per DetectorContext.
annotation.integrationPoints: detector-bootstrap registers built-in and pack detectors; architecture/index orchestrates run loop.
annotation.dataFlow: detector-bootstrap registerDetector* → getDetectors → architecture/index filters by categoriesDisjoint and anyInScopeApplies.

annotation.summary: Architecture-detector plugin contract (mirrors stage1/source/registry). DetectorContext bundles everything a detector adapter might need — graph, modulesById, annotations, scope, optional snapshot, thresholds, requestedCategories, annotationReasoning/includeComponentEntrypoints flags, and precomputed derivedStaleSet — assembled once per report so the registry loop stays uniform. ArchitectureDetector = { id, categories[], optional appliesTo, run(ctx) }; DetectorPack groups detectors for bootstrap registration. Detectors are read-only; findings are advisory candidates.

keyExports.ArchitectureDetector: Plugin contract: id, categories[], optional appliesTo, run(ctx) → findings.
keyExports.DetectorContext: Shared read-only inputs: graph, modules, annotations, scope, thresholds, requestedCategories.
keyExports.DetectorPack: Bootstrap bundle { id, detectors[] } registered at engine init.

assumptions: DetectorPack appliesTo gates use surface predicates from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/surfaces.
INTERNAL_DETECTORS registration order affects finding id stability.
risks: Detector id collisions across packs overwrite registry order unpredictably.
patterns: Read-only detectors — mutate nothing; findings are advisory candidates.
requestedCategories filters which detectors run per analyze_architecture call.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture index orchestrator; mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture-detectors packs.

annotation.summary: Legacy analyze_architecture detector implementations over RepositoryGraph, ModuleInfo semantic hints, and AnnotationStore; emits RefactoringFinding[] per category (duplicateLike, boundary, godModule, serverHandlerOrchestration, domainShape, clientBusinessLogic, flowConvergence, effectSpaghetti, propDrillingOrchestration, uiDomainCoupling, and further security/UI categories). Imports shared annotation-secret and component-signals from SSoT modules for security-signal and workflow-signal deduplication; module-path evidence and grouping keys now read ModuleInfo.pkgRelPath (renamed from relativeFilePath).

keyExports.detectBoundary: Cross-package import edges violating architectural boundaries (per domain membership).
keyExports.detectClientBusinessLogic: Frontend modules with non-pure sideEffects annotations or semanticHints.effects.
keyExports.detectDomainShape: God-domain (many modules, low cohesion) or low-cohesion domain (min module count, few inter-module edges).
keyExports.detectDuplicateLike: Groups modules by normalizeResponsibilityKey; emits when minGroupSize reached across packages.
keyExports.detectEffectSpaghetti: Frontend modules with excessive lifecycle/effect/useEffect blocks (minEffects threshold).
keyExports.detectFlowConvergence: Multiple frontend entrypoints converging on same data-access target through BFS paths.
keyExports.detectGodModule: Composite score (exports*1.5 + fanIn + fanOut + envVars*2 + lines/N) exceeds minScore threshold.
keyExports.detectPropDrillingOrchestration: Components forwarding props/callbacks through many children (minProps, propTunnelDepth thresholds).
keyExports.detectServerHandlerOrchestration: Backend modules with HTTP handler signals importing many unrelated targets.
keyExports.detectUiDomainCoupling: UI modules importing domain/storage/server/api targets (uiCouplingTargetRole + minCoupledImports).
keyExports.detectUnclearArchitecture: Flags a runtime resource whose plugin declared it carries code (node.data.hasCodeHandler === true) but no code target or handler was found; generalized from a hardcoded lambda-kind check to any plugin-declared code-carrying resource kind.

assumptions: Detectors are pure over graph snapshot and annotations; no state mutation.
Security-sensitive categories (clientBusinessLogic, privilegedClientSideEffect, sensitiveBrowserStorage, authorizationPolicyDrift) honor strictness from config.thresholds.
workflowSignalKinds and componentInteractionSignals imported from shared component-signals module; annotation-secret provides containsSecretValue and annotationSecretFieldPaths helpers.
annotationReasoning option (when true) attaches buildAnnotationContext reasoning for MCP detail mode.
Module path checks use ModuleInfo.pkgRelPath throughout (package-relative path), not an absolute or repo-relative path.

risks.text: Large monolithic module (27 exports); lowering thresholds in config can cause false-positive floods. Importer must validate strictness profile and per-category thresholds against project risk tolerance.

risks: Heuristic false positives expected — findings are advisory candidates only; no automatic remediation.
Security-sensitive categories (clientBusinessLogic, secretConfigBoundary, sensitiveBrowserStorage) may silently emit on missed semanticHints if modules lack full annotation.
patterns: Monolithic legacy detector implementations; newer detector packs live under architecture-detectors/* but many categories still re-export from this module.
Shared helpers (heuristics, finding, config) used uniformly across detectors.
Optional buildAnnotationContext attached when annotationReasoning:true; cost-controlled for MCP safety.
extensionPoints: Add new detector category: define new threshold key in RefactoringThresholds (config), implement detect* function signature, register via detector-bootstrap bootstrapInternalDetectors.

New security detector: define minEvidenceScore or minSignals threshold, use annotation-secret or component-signals helpers for signal detection, attach to clientBusinessLogic or create security-specific detector pack.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imports shared annotation-secret (containsSecretValue, annotationSecretFieldPaths), component-signals (workflowSignalKinds), heuristics (isFrontendSurfaceModule, isBackendContext, coupledTargetRole, etc.), and finding (sortFindings, selectBalancedFindings); registered via detector-bootstrap; consumed by mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/analyze-architecture and harness test suite.
annotation.dataFlow: DetectorContext (graph, modulesById, annotations, scope, thresholds, options) → detect*(context) → RefactoringFinding[] → finding/sortFindings/selectBalancedFindings(limit, categories) → MCP envelope.

annotation.summary: RefactoringFinding post-processing helpers for analyze_architecture: clampConfidence (round/clip to [0,1]), detectorConfidence (base + additive − subtractive contributions, clamped to a category ceiling), evidenceAxisCount (count of independent evidence signals that fired), findingSeverity (derive severity from confidence/impact), sortFindings (order by severity/confidence before pagination), selectBalancedFindings (round-robin category-balanced MCP slice), countFindingsByCategory (histogram for aggregate queries), refactoringCategoryFromFindingId (parse category prefix from finding id for detail expansion), and dedupeByCategoryAndPrimaryNode (dedup by category+primary node for stable pagination).

keyExports.clampConfidence: Normalize a confidence value to [0, 1] with two decimal precision.
keyExports.countFindingsByCategory: Histogram of findings by RefactoringCategory for aggregate reports.
keyExports.dedupeByCategoryAndPrimaryNode: Dedup findings by (category, primaryNode=nodes[0]) pair, keeping the first (already sorted) occurrence to avoid multiple findings double-inflating one category's count for the same node.
keyExports.detectorConfidence: Computes a detector's confidence as base + additive contributions − subtractive penalties, clamped to a category ceiling, then normalized by clampConfidence; base/ceiling/add/subtract are named separately so detectors can't silently disagree about what each means.
keyExports.evidenceAxisCount: Counts how many independent evidence axes (boolean signals) fired — a gate distinct from confidence score, used to require several independent signals agreeing rather than one inflated dimension.
keyExports.findingSeverity: Derive finding severity from confidence level and refactoring impact.
keyExports.refactoringCategoryFromFindingId: Extract the category prefix from a colon-separated finding id (`<category>:...`) for detail-mode filtering.
keyExports.selectBalancedFindings: Round-robin category-balanced slice (over REFACTORING_CATEGORIES order) for MCP paginated result limits; falls back to a plain sorted slice when 0-1 categories apply.
keyExports.sortFindings: Orders findings by severity (desc), confidence (desc), then node count (desc) for stable pagination.

assumptions: Detector confidence values live in the [0,1] scale from the start — detectorConfidence composes base + per-axis additions minus penalties, clamped to a category ceiling — then clampConfidence rounds to two decimals and hard-clips to [0,1].
Sort order (severity desc, confidence desc, node count desc) is stable across pagination offsets — changing it can invalidate downstream pagination expectations.
selectBalancedFindings round-robins across REFACTORING_CATEGORIES order, restricted to the categories present in the requested `categories` set, only when more than one such category applies.
risks: Changing sort order affects pagination snapshot baselines in test/bench.
clampConfidence rounding to two decimals can mask a low-confidence detection if the delta is under 0.005.
selectBalancedFindings may skip high-value findings if a category is exhausted early in round-robin.
patterns: Pure post-processing — no graph access, no state mutation.
Finding id format: `<category>:<rest>` (colon-separated); refactoringCategoryFromFindingId matches on the `${category}:` prefix against REFACTORING_CATEGORIES.
extensionPoints: Add new RefactoringCategory in architecture/types.ts; detectors register findings with that category; selectBalancedFindings and countFindingsByCategory auto-include.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/index (runRefactoringReport), detail mode, and test/analyze-architecture.test.ts (snapshot validation).
annotation.dataFlow: Raw detector findings (confidence composed via detectorConfidence/evidenceAxisCount in [0,1], impact field) → sortFindings(stable sort) → selectBalancedFindings(paginate by category) → analyze_architecture MCP envelope.

annotation.summary: Shared path, package, and annotation-text heuristics for analyze_architecture detectors: classifies frontend/backend surfaces, flow entrypoints, convergence targets, policy tokens, and provides import-graph BFS helpers across structural and security-sensitive finding categories.

keyExports.coupledTargetRole: Classifies import targets as feature/domain/api/storage/server/state for UI coupling detectors.
keyExports.findFlowPaths: Scoped import-graph BFS from frontend entrypoints to convergence targets, filtering runtime edges and excluding tooling/primitives.
keyExports.isBackendContext: True when package name, path tokens, or semantic hints indicate server/BFF context.
keyExports.isConvergenceTargetModule: Identifies modules that aggregate multiple frontend entry flows: shared state, domain, storage, service layers.
keyExports.isFrontendFlowEntryModule: Route/screen or optional component entrypoint surfaces for flow convergence analysis.
keyExports.isFrontendSurfaceModule: Classifies modules as UI-facing: excludes backend packages/paths, routes through useClient flags, targets app/pages/routes/components paths.
keyExports.isRuntimeImportEdge: Filters type-only imports (flagged `isTypeOnly` in graph metadata) to keep architecture analysis consistent with mod.imports-based detectors.
keyExports.isUiCouplingSourceModule: Frontend surface minus pure types, barrels, and tooling — source of UI coupling dependencies.
keyExports.normalizeResponsibilityKey: Dedup key for duplicate-like and policy grouping (CamelCase split, generic term stripping, kebab-join).
keyExports.policyTokens: Extracts auth/policy vocabulary from exports, paths, and annotation text for validation/permission/rules signal detection.

assumptions: Heuristics read ModuleInfo paths/exports and StoredAnnotation text — no AST re-parse.
HUB percentile and importer floors tune hub tagging separately from this module.
Graph builder flags type-only imports via edge.metadata.isTypeOnly; isRuntimeImportEdge filters these consistently.
risks: Generically named packages (api, core, shared) can false-positive as backend or frontend.
Component entrypoint inclusion toggles flow-convergence sensitivity.
Path-based heuristics may misclassify symlinked or unusual layouts.
patterns: Regex and path-token classification over ModuleInfo — shared across structural and security-sensitive detectors.
CoupledTargetRole feeds ui-domain-coupling and flow-convergence categories.
annotation.flowDescription: analyze_architecture detectors call isFrontendSurfaceModule/isBackendContext/... before grouping or traversing import graph.
invariants: isBuildOrToolingModule excludes test/spec/config paths from UI surface detectors.
isPureTypesModule and isBarrelLikeModule gate god-module and duplicate-like false positives.
extensionPoints: New detectors add regex/path helpers here rather than duplicating classification logic.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors, mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/surfaces, and mod:repovine/src/annotations/module-kind (inferModuleKind).
annotation.dataFlow: ModuleInfo path/package/export/annotation signals -> predicate helpers -> detector grouping keys, BFS seeds, and policy token extraction.

annotation.summary: Which graph nodes the architecture detectors inspect for a given ResolvedScope. scopedGraphIds expands 'all'/'package'/'domain'/'module'/'runtime-resource' into RefactoringScope moduleIds/serviceIds(runtime-resources)/domainIds; unsupported kinds (export-symbol, template, infra, query) return kind:'unsupported' carrying the refused kind, rather than three empty sets.

keyExports.ARCHITECTURE_SCOPE_KINDS: The scope kinds the detectors read: all, package, domain, module, runtime-resource.
keyExports.architectureCanScope: Whether a scope kind is inspected; the empty-diagnostic branch reads it to refuse by name.
keyExports.isSingleNodeScope: Whether the scope holds one node (module or runtime-resource), so per-node signals apply and comparisons between in-scope nodes cannot fire.
keyExports.scopedGraphIds: Expands a ResolvedScope into detector id sets, or returns kind 'unsupported' carrying the refused scope kind. Throws if passed a raw scope string instead of an already-resolved ResolvedScope.

assumptions: Caller must pass an already-resolved ResolvedScope (an object with a string .kind) — scopedGraphIds throws otherwise rather than re-parsing a raw string, since a prior re-parse silently answered only 3 of 10 scope kinds and returned empty sets for the rest.
'module' and 'runtime-resource' scopes deliberately return empty domainIds (isSingleNodeScope) so domain-shape detectors don't run over a domain filtered to one member.
'package' scope derives serviceIds by checking modulePackageId on each runtime-resource's infra targets — a runtime-resource belongs to a package only via the modules it targets, not directly.
risks: A scope kind added to ScopeKind falls into the unsupported branch until it is answered here; test/laws/scope-resolution fails when that branch and architectureCanScope disagree.
patterns: Kind dispatch over a ResolvedScope; no scope string is parsed here.
annotation.integrationPoints: architecture/index report runner; mcp scope/resolve refactoringScopeArg for empty-diagnostics nextActions.
annotation.dataFlow: ResolvedScope → scopedGraphIds → RefactoringScope module/service/domain id sets → detector ctx.scope.

annotation.summary: Server-surface applicability predicate for architecture detectors. serverSurfaceApplies returns true when a module is in backend context and carries HTTP handler path signals from heuristics.
assumptions: Propagation review: verified upstream heuristics/types; serverSurfaceApplies predicate unchanged.
risks: Python/Go handlers without path tokens may be missed until semanticHints expand.
patterns: Thin surface gate module — keeps server-only detector scope out of heuristics barrel.
annotation.integrationPoints: heuristics isBackendContext and hasHttpHandlerSignals; detector-bootstrap server-surface pack appliesTo predicate.

annotation.summary: Shared frontend-class applicability predicate for architecture detector appliesTo gates: true when the module's owning source adapter declares UI surfaces. An undefined sourcePluginId maps to the TypeScript-default frontend surface.
assumptions: A module with no sourcePluginId is treated as coming from the default TypeScript adapter, which declares UI surfaces.
risks: A mis-declared uiSurfaces flag on a source adapter causes a whole UI-class detector to skip modules from that adapter, or to run false-positive UI analysis on modules that are not frontend code.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates to pluginHasUiSurfaces in mod:repovine/src/plugin-host/source-set; ModuleInfo comes from mod:repovine/src/types.
annotation.dataFlow: ModuleInfo.sourcePluginId -> pluginHasUiSurfaces lookup -> boolean gate consumed by UI-surface architecture detectors.

annotation.summary: Core analyze_architecture type contracts. RefactoringCategory union, RefactoringFinding advisory shape, RefactoringScope scoped id sets (modules, runtime-resources, domains), and REFACTORING_CATEGORIES stable enumeration.

keyExports.CLEAN_ORACLE_FAILING_CATEGORIES: The 3 categories ('duplicate-like', 'god-module', 'authorization-policy-drift') that fired on a counterexample fixture built to carry none of the smell; off by default.
keyExports.DEFAULT_REFACTORING_CATEGORIES: REFACTORING_CATEGORIES minus CLEAN_ORACLE_FAILING_CATEGORIES — the set a report runs when the caller names none.
keyExports.REFACTORING_CATEGORIES: Stable ordered list of all 26 RefactoringCategory string literals.
keyExports.RefactoringCategory: Union of structural, flow, UI, and security-sensitive architecture finding categories.
keyExports.RefactoringFinding: Advisory candidate shape: id, category, severity, confidence, nodes, evidence, suggestion, optional annotationContext.
keyExports.RefactoringScope: Scoped moduleIds, serviceIds (runtime-resources), domainIds, and scope kind for detector runs.

assumptions: DEFAULT_REFACTORING_CATEGORIES is derived by filtering REFACTORING_CATEGORIES against CLEAN_ORACLE_FAILING_CATEGORIES, so the two lists cannot drift apart by hand-editing one.
unsupportedKind on RefactoringScope is set only when kind is 'unsupported', naming which ScopeKind was refused.
risks: Adding a category requires updating REFACTORING_CATEGORIES, config thresholds, and detector registration.

A category added to REFACTORING_CATEGORIES without a CLEAN_ORACLE_FAILING_CATEGORIES review runs by default even if it shares the oracle-failing pattern (duplicate-like/god-module/authorization-policy-drift).
patterns: Types-only contract module — no runtime detector logic.
Category union must stay aligned with detector-registry category declarations.
annotation.integrationPoints: finding/* helpers; detector-types DetectorContext; mcp analyze_architecture envelope; detail expansion by finding id; imports mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/annotation-context for the AnnotationContext type embedded in RefactoringFinding.

annotation.summary: Estimates submitted annotation payload size for write_annotation responses and batch progress reporting: recursively counts string leaf characters and applies chars/4 token heuristic (not LLM billing).

keyExports.countAnnotationTextChars: Sums string values in nested annotation objects.
keyExports.formatSubmittedAnnotationMetrics: Human compact line for MCP success messages.

assumptions: Only string leaves count; numbers and booleans contribute zero.
estimateMethod is fixed chars/4 for agent budgeting guidance.
risks: Heuristic underestimates code-heavy annotations with many symbols.
patterns: estimatedTokens is chars/4 heuristic for batch reporting only.
invariants: Never used for billing — informational MCP feedback only.
annotation.integrationPoints: write_annotation result.submittedAnnotation; token estimates for batch reporting.
annotation.dataFlow: submitted annotation object → measureSubmittedAnnotationText → chars/estimatedTokens returned in MCP concise payload.

annotation.summary: One walk over the annotatable surface (modules, templates, IaC modules, runtime resources, domain roll-ups) producing both halves of the annotation backlog: the prioritized needs-work rows the queue returns and the coverage tallies status/onboarding report. Queue vocabulary (status, staleKind, phase, ranking) lives here too.

keyExports.BACKLOG_PHASES: The node kinds the walk emits, in queue-rank order: module, template, runtime-resource, infra, domain.
keyExports.answerableOf: total minus unconfirmable — the denominator a coverage percentage converges on.
keyExports.backlogKindCoverages: The five kind buckets enumerated, so a roll-up cannot silently omit one.
keyExports.buildAnnotationBacklog: The walk: one entry filter, one freshness verdict, one bucket per node; returns { rows, coverage }.
keyExports.classifyStale: Turns a freshness verdict into a queue row: unannotated, stale with a review depth (staleKindForReason), or null (no work).
keyExports.countBacklogPhases: Rows per node kind, in the queue's byType shape.
keyExports.countBacklogRows: The one row tally; every needsWork/stale/unannotated counter a tool publishes comes from it.
keyExports.filterRowsByStaleKind: Rows of one review depth, for derived-review and staleKind filters.
keyExports.needsWorkOf: stale + unannotated for a bucket — the number a drain runs to zero.
keyExports.publishedCoverageBucket: A bucket in the shape tools publish; unconfirmable appears only when non-zero.
keyExports.publishedDomainCoverage: The domain bucket, whose published count key is totalDomains.
keyExports.rollUpCoverage: The five kind buckets as one; the only place a cross-kind sum is written.
keyExports.sortBacklogRows: Sorts BacklogRow[] in place via compareQueueItems: content-stale first, then phase, then bottom-up by dependency depth.

assumptions: Freshness is decided by mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness and the current hash by mod:repovine/src/annotations/content-hash; this module compares nothing itself.
A runtime resource carries its parent IaC module's domain tags, so scope and per-domain coverage follow the parent.
Domain roll-up nodes are excluded from byDomain; byDomain counts the nodes tagged to a domain.

sideEffects.description: reads graph, snapshot and the stored annotation map; writes nothing

risks.text: A node counted in a coverage bucket but skipped by the row loop (or the reverse) makes the queue and coverage disagree, which an agent cannot drain. Add a node kind or an entry filter in this walk only, and keep tally() and the row push on the same branch.

patterns: Lazy hydration: classification and sort key are eager, item prose is built by row.hydrate() only for returned items.
invariants: Per kind bucket: total === fresh + stale + unannotated + unconfirmable.
Rows exist for exactly the nodes counted as stale or unannotated.
byTier is a census over every domain node and is never scoped.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness (the verdict), mod:repovine/src/annotations/content-hash (current hash per node kind, cached per snapshot), mod:repovine/src/annotations/propagation (computeEntrypointBoundedDerived for module propagation-stale), mod:repovine/src/annotations/quality (module urgency and recommendedFields), mod:repovine/src/annotations/module-kind (kind inference and recommended fields).
annotation.stateShape: KindCoverage per node kind plus byDomain/byTier maps, accumulated during the walk; BacklogRow carries nodeId, status, staleKind, phase, sort key and a hydrate closure.
annotation.dataFlow: graph + snapshot + stored annotations -> per node: entry filter (domain scope, hash source, staleness policy) -> annotationFreshness -> classifyStale -> one coverage bucket, plus a BacklogRow when the verdict is stale or unannotated -> mod:repovine/src/annotations/store projects rows into getQueue/getQueuePage/scanAnnotationHealth and coverage into getStats.

annotation.summary: Local recovery snapshots named annotations.backup.<timestamp>.json, newest MAX_ANNOTATION_BACKUPS retained per directory. AnnotationStore writes failed-load and shrink-guard snapshots beside the annotations file; mergeAnnotationsOnDisk writes conflict snapshots into .repovine/annotation-backups (covered by the managed .gitignore block) via the dir option. Content matching a retained backup reuses that file and returns its path, so a caller disclosing 'your bytes are recoverable here' keeps the disclosure when deduplication kicks in.

keyExports.MAX_ANNOTATION_BACKUPS: Retention count; older backups are rotated away after each write.
keyExports.writeAnnotationBackup: Snapshot bytes into dir (default: the annotations file's directory); returns written(path) | duplicate(path) | failed(error).

assumptions: Backups are local recovery files, never read back automatically. Those written into .repovine/annotation-backups are git-ignored; those written beside the annotations file are untracked and surface in git status.
Dedup compares size first, then bytes, over retained backups in the same directory.

sideEffects.description: Lists and reads annotations.backup.*.json for dedup
Creates the target dir, atomically writes a backup, unlinks rotated-out ones

risks.text: The writer never throws; a caller that is about to destroy the snapshotted bytes must check for status 'failed' and abort instead of proceeding.

invariants: A caller never fails because a backup failed; the status is returned, not thrown.
At most MAX_ANNOTATION_BACKUPS backups survive a write in one directory.
written and duplicate both name a path holding exactly the requested bytes.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/annotations/store createBackup; mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance mergeAnnotationsOnDisk (dir: .repovine/annotation-backups); mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic writeFileAtomicSync.
annotation.dataFlow: caller bytes -> dedup scan of retained backups in dir -> atomic write of annotations.backup.<ts>.json -> rotation to MAX_ANNOTATION_BACKUPS

annotation.summary: Detects the two ways a carrier link can be broken. One is a facade that delegates to a node carrying a consumer obligation without naming it, so an agent inspecting the facade never learns the obligation exists. The other is an annotation naming a node the graph cannot deliver, so the pointer reads as authoritative but leads nowhere. Both are advisory findings reported with counts and a bounded sample.

keyExports.CARRIER_LINK_DEP_GUARD_DEPTH: How far the forward closure walks when checking deliverability.
keyExports.CARRIER_LINK_GAP_SAMPLE_LIMIT: How many concrete pairs are returned.
keyExports.CarrierLinkGapKind: The two kinds: an unnamed delegation, and a named target that cannot be delivered.
keyExports.CarrierLinkGapSample: One concrete pair: the kind, the importer and the target.
keyExports.CarrierLinkGaps: The reported shape: both counts, the suppressed count and the sample.
keyExports.EMPTY_CARRIER_LINK_GAPS: The zero result, used when the graph cannot support the analysis.
keyExports.NODE_ID_TOKEN_RE: The token pattern for node ids appearing in prose.
keyExports.computeCarrierLinkGaps: Scans importers against consumer-risk targets and returns both gap counts, the suppressed count, and a sorted sample.
keyExports.parseIntegrationPointTargets: Pulls node ids out of annotation prose, optionally keeping only those the graph knows.

assumptions: An unnamed delegation is reported only for a runtime two-hop shape: an intermediate that is neither the importer nor the target, reached by value imports on both hops. A type-only import is erased at build time and cannot delegate behavior.

Chains longer than two hops are deliberately not reported, because every hop already carries the structural flag at its own boundary; a direct one-hop import is likewise excluded since the graph edge already carries it.
An importer inside the target's own equivalence set is skipped, which is what keeps an import cycle from reporting a node as delegating to itself.
Suppression is decided by the caller, which validates it against the target's current risk state; this module only honours the set it is handed and reports how many it excluded.

What counts as a runtime import edge is taken from the shared predicate in mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/heuristics rather than restated here, so this advisory and the architecture analysis cannot disagree about the same edge.
risks: The analysis needs the graph's import edge maps and returns an empty result without them, so a graph built without them reports no gaps at all rather than reporting that it could not look.
Node ids are recovered from prose by pattern match, so an id written inside an unrelated sentence counts as a pointer while a target described only in words does not.
The sample is capped, so a scope with many gaps shows the same small set until those are fixed and the counts are the only signal of the true size.
patterns: Two failure modes, one pass: an obligation that is reachable but unnamed, and a name that is written but unreachable.
Advisory rather than blocking: the result is counts and examples for a human or agent to review, not a gate.
The runtime-edge test is shared with the analysis layer rather than duplicated, so a change to what counts as a runtime edge lands in one place.
invariants: A direct one-hop import is never reported as a missing link.
A node is never reported as delegating to itself.
Suppressed targets are excluded from the search and counted separately rather than silently dropped.
The sample is deterministically ordered before it is truncated.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by the annotation health scan and by the validation tool under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools; the same prose parser backs pointer resolution in mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs; risk-scope predicates come from mod:repovine/src/annotations/format, graph traversal from mod:repovine/src/graph, and nodeInScopeHints from mod:repovine/src/annotations/scope-hints.
annotation.dataFlow: graph plus stored annotations -> consumer-risk targets, minus the suppressed set -> per importer, the delegation test and the named-pointer deliverability check -> counts and a bounded sorted sample.

annotation.summary: Workspace-local review state for carrier-link advisories. Records which consumer-risk targets a reviewer decided are not gaps, stamped with a hash of the target's consumer-risk texts at the moment of the decision, so a target whose risks later change re-surfaces instead of staying silently suppressed. The state lives under the engine cache directory and is not committed, so triage does not travel with a clone.

keyExports.CARRIER_REVIEW_FILENAME: Basename of the review state file inside the engine cache directory.
keyExports.CarrierReviewEntry: One decision: the risk hash at decision time, the decision timestamp, and an optional reason.
keyExports.CarrierReviewFile: The file shape: a version and the reviewed targets keyed by node id.
keyExports.carrierReviewFilePath: Absolute path of the review file for a repo root.
keyExports.carrierTargetRiskHash: The invalidation key: a truncated sha256 over the target's sorted consumer-scoped risk texts.
keyExports.mergeCarrierReviewEntries: Merges new decisions into the existing state and persists it.
keyExports.readCarrierReviewFile: Reads the state, returning an empty result for a missing, corrupt or wrong-version file.
keyExports.readValidSuppressedTargets: The set of targets still suppressed, keeping only those whose current risk hash matches the recorded one.

assumptions: Only consumer-scoped risk texts feed the hash, sorted first, so re-ordering the risks does not invalidate a decision while changing their wording does.
The state is deliberately workspace-local rather than committed: a suppression is one reviewer's judgement about one checkout, not a repository fact.
The same hash function is used both when a decision is stamped and when it is checked, which is what keeps the two from drifting apart.

sideEffects.description: reads the review state file from the engine cache directory
writes the review state atomically

risks: Reading fails open toward visibility: a missing, corrupt or wrong-version file suppresses nothing, so every reviewed pair re-surfaces rather than a damaged file silently hiding advisories.

Because the hash covers only consumer-scoped risks, editing a target's local risks leaves an existing suppression in force, which is intended but means the decision is narrower than 'this annotation was reviewed'.
The state sits in the ignored cache directory, so clearing that directory discards every review decision with no other copy.
patterns: A content hash as the invalidation key, so a suppression expires by the target changing rather than by a timestamp or a manual sweep.
invariants: A suppression survives only while the recorded hash equals the target's current consumer-risk hash.
The stamping path and the checking path compute the hash through this one function.
annotation.integrationPoints: Resolves its location through mod:repovine/src/paths, writes through mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic, and normalizes risks through mod:repovine/src/annotations/format. The decisions it stores are produced by the advisory decline tool and consulted when carrier-link gaps are validated.
annotation.dataFlow: reviewer declines a target -> the target's consumer risks are hashed -> the decision is merged into the review file -> later validation reads it back and keeps only the entries whose hash still matches.

annotation.summary: The one dispatcher for "what hash answers for this node": HASHED_NODE_KINDS enumerates the five kinds that carry a hash (module, infra, runtime-resource, template, domain), hashedNodeKind classifies a node id, and resolveNodeContentHash returns the current hash for any of them. Domain hashes roll up member hashes under the active stale policy; leaf kinds read stage-1 facts. Also holds the import-baseline primitives (direct imports, baseline snapshot, drifted upstreams) that propagation builds on.

keyExports.HASHED_NODE_KINDS: Runtime list of node kinds that carry a content hash; consumers are held to answering for each.
keyExports.buildNodeContentHashLookup: Builds module/infra/template/runtime-resource hash maps from a snapshot.
keyExports.computeDomainContentHash: Order-independent roll-up over a domain's tagged members; 'empty' sentinel when none resolve.
keyExports.computeDomainContentHashForPathOnly: Roll-up over path/pattern-tagged members only — a deliberately different scope from the full roll-up.
keyExports.computeImportBaseline: Snapshots direct-import contentHashes for propagation detection.
keyExports.hashedNodeKind: Which hashed kind a node id is, or undefined for a kind nothing hashes.
keyExports.importBaselineStaleUpstream: Direct imports whose current hash differs from a stored baseline.
keyExports.nodeContentHashLookup: Per-snapshot cached lookup maps, so a single-node caller pays O(1).
keyExports.resolveDomainContentHash: Selects full vs path-only roll-up by domainStalePolicy.
keyExports.resolveLeafNodeContentHash: Hash of a non-roll-up kind; used for domain members so hashing a domain never re-enters the domain branch.
keyExports.resolveNodeContentHash: Current hash of any hashed node, by kind.

assumptions: IaC documents are graph nodes of type 'module' under an infra: id, so the id prefix is what separates them from code modules.
The per-snapshot lookup cache is keyed by the snapshot object, so a rebuild retires it with the facts it indexes.
Domain members are leaf kinds by construction; the roll-up never nests domains.
isPackageOnlyDomain and isTaggedEdge/isAuthoredTag used to pick and filter domain-member edges are imported from mod:repovine/src/graph, not exported from this module.

risks.text: The full and path-only domain roll-ups are not interchangeable: swapping one for the other re-flags every path-only domain against hashes already persisted in repovine.annots.json.

risks: A per-kind resolver called directly instead of resolveNodeContentHash re-creates the per-tool dispatch this module exists to hold in one place; test/laws/annotation-freshness.test.ts fails on that.
patterns: Kinds are enumerated at runtime, so a new hashed kind surfaces as an unanswered case rather than as a node with no hash.
invariants: A kind that carries no hash resolves to undefined rather than to a sentinel value.
Domain roll-ups are order-independent: the same member set always yields the same hash.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness compares the resolved hash against the stored one; mod:repovine/src/annotations/store uses the lookup for queue and coverage passes; mod:repovine/src/annotations/propagation builds baselines on top; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/inspect-node-core and mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/annotations resolve one node at a time; runtime-resource hashing comes from mod:repovine/src/annotations/service-resource-hash.
annotation.dataFlow: node id -> hashedNodeKind -> per-kind source (snapshot maps for leaves, tagged-member roll-up for domains) -> current hash -> freshness rule.

annotation.summary: Declares the single set of excerpt-size budgets (ANNOTATION_EXCERPT) used to cut annotation text on two secondary display surfaces, so both cut to the same width instead of drifting apart.

keyExports.ANNOTATION_EXCERPT: const budgets: summaryChars=200 (whole-thought fields like summary/dataFlow), entryChars=150 (one list entry: invariant/risk/assumption), listItems=5, mapEntries=8 (keyExports/envDependencies), mapValueChars=100, nodesPerContext=8

assumptions: inspect_node's primary delivery path does not cut annotation text at all; only analyze_architecture's annotationContext packet and get_annotation_status's risk-scope candidate list quote at these widths
On the published benchmark corpus every boundary/consumer risk exceeds entryChars, so every quoted risk is shortened there

annotation.summary: Cross-process annotation-file lock with O_EXCL acquisition, PID ownership/liveness checks, serialized atomic stale takeover, orphan-claim recovery, typed 5s timeout, and sync/async critical-section wrappers.

keyExports.AnnotationFileLockTimeoutError: Typed failure raised when ownership cannot be acquired before the wait deadline.
keyExports.withAnnotationFileLockAsync: Runs an async callback only after verified lock ownership and releases only the caller's lock.
keyExports.withAnnotationFileLockSync: Runs a sync callback only after verified lock ownership and releases only the caller's lock.

assumptions: Lock file content is the ownership token and must equal process.pid before entry, takeover success, or release.
Stale threshold assumes a crashed writer can leave a lock without unlinking it.

sideEffects.description: Creates and deletes .lock files beside annotations JSON
Atomics.wait / setTimeout backoff while waiting for lock

risks: NFS or network filesystems may weaken O_EXCL and atomic rename semantics.
patterns: Cross-process lock with verified PID ownership and atomic stale-lock takeover.
invariants: Lock file lives beside repovine.annots.json.
The critical section never runs without verified ownership.
Deadline expiry throws without deleting a live foreign lock.
Release removes the lock only while its content still equals process.pid.
annotation.integrationPoints: AnnotationStore read/write paths acquire cross-process lock on repovine.annots.json.
annotation.stateShape: Exclusive file lock handle held for duration of read-modify-write on repovine.annots.json; no persistent in-memory state beyond lock fd.
annotation.dataFlow: exclusive create → verify own PID → read/write callback → ownership-checked release; stale owner → PID temp file → atomic rename → ownership re-check.

annotation.summary: Zod schemas and canonical serialization for repovine.annots.json: AnnotationContentSchema (with the sideEffects min(1) guard that rejects empty arrays) and propagationSlice, StoredAnnotationSchema, risk-scope helpers (normalizeRisks/risksScoped/hasConsumerScopedRisk/hasBoundaryScopedRisk + the consumerRiskMarkingHints authoring nudge), the ANNOTATABLE vs ANNOTATION_EXEMPT NodeType partition (law-enforced), hydrate-with-quarantine (hydrateAnnotationEntry/hydrateAnnotationMap/parseAnnotationFile), and deterministic canonicalAnnotation ordering for merge diffs (toDiskAnnotation strips default pass=1/schemaVersion=1).

keyExports.ANNOTATABLE_NODE_TYPES: module, export-symbol, domain, runtime-resource, template — satisfies NodeType.
keyExports.AnnotationContentSchema: Zod schema incl. propagationSlice and SideEffectSchema min(1) guard.
keyExports.consumerRiskMarkingHints: Authoring nudge: flags plain-string risks whose text reads like an importer obligation but is not marked scope:consumer.
keyExports.hasBoundaryScopedRisk: True when any risk has scope boundary.
keyExports.hasConsumerScopedRisk: True when any risk has scope consumer.
keyExports.hydrateAnnotationEntry: Validates and canonicalizes one raw annotation entry via StoredAnnotationSchema, returning ok:true/annotation or ok:false/AnnotationHydrationError.
keyExports.hydrateAnnotationMap: Splits valid data vs quarantine vs AnnotationHydrationError list.
keyExports.normalizeRisks: Coerces RiskEntry[] to NormalizedRisk[] with default scope local.
keyExports.parseAnnotationFile: Parses raw annots.json content into an AnnotationFile via hydrateAnnotationMap, labelling errors with a caller-supplied source label.
keyExports.risksScoped: Filters a RiskEntry[] down to normalized risks matching one scope (local/consumer/boundary).
keyExports.serializeAnnotationFileFromRaw: Pretty JSON with sorted node ids and stripped defaults.

assumptions: ANNOTATABLE_NODE_TYPES and ANNOTATION_EXEMPT_NODE_TYPES partition NODE_TYPES (enforced in test/laws/annotatable-surface.test.ts).
inferAnnotationNodeType maps mod:/infra:→module, export:→export-symbol, resource:→runtime-resource.
sideEffects rejects empty arrays — omit field or use [{kind:pure}].
risks: Manual JSON edits outside schema land in quarantine until merge/validate repair.
patterns: Invalid hydrate results quarantine raw value for merge_annotations review.
DISK_ANNOTATION_KEY_ORDER omits nodeId/nodeType (map key is node id).
invariants: propagationSlice {anchor, path, reviewedAt} validated when present.
canonicalAnnotation sorts content fields and importBaseline keys for merge diffs.
toDiskAnnotation omits default pass=1 and schemaVersion=1 on disk.
annotation.integrationPoints: annotations/store load/save; write_annotation validation; merge_annotations; validate_annotations; imports mod:repovine/src/annotations/side-effect-vocab SideEffectSchema.
annotation.dataFlow: repovine.annots.json → parseAnnotationFile → hydrateAnnotationMap (StoredAnnotationSchema + canonical sort) → in-memory map; serializeAnnotationFileFromRaw writes sorted disk form via toDiskAnnotation.

annotation.summary: The single rule deciding whether a stored annotation still describes its node. Takes the stored note, the node's current hash, and (when evaluated) whether its import baseline drifted; returns a discriminated verdict — fresh, stale with a named reason (content, schema, propagation, no-baseline), not-comparable, or unannotated. Also owns how a verdict is published: provenance derived from the verdict, and the fresh/staleReason pair a tool response carries.

keyExports.AnnotatedFreshnessVerdict: Every state except unannotated — what a node that has a note can be.
keyExports.AnnotationFreshnessMeta: Response shape for a verdict: optional fresh, staleReason when false, provenance.
keyExports.FRESHNESS_STATES: Runtime list of verdict states, for consumers held to answering all of them.
keyExports.FreshnessInput: annotation, currentHash, and optional propagationStale (undefined = propagation not evaluated).
keyExports.FreshnessVerdict: Discriminated verdict: fresh | stale+reason | not-comparable | unannotated.
keyExports.NodeFreshnessLookup: A verdict-by-nodeId function a projection takes instead of deciding freshness itself.
keyExports.STALE_REASONS: Runtime list of stale reasons; each names the check that decided the verdict.
keyExports.annotationFreshness: The rule. Content and schema are checked before propagation.
keyExports.annotationFreshnessMeta: Projects a verdict into the fields a response publishes.
keyExports.annotationFreshnessProvenance: Method per verdict: content-hash, import-baseline for propagation, not-comparable where nothing was compared.
keyExports.contentMoved: Narrower than not-fresh: only the node's own text drifting under the note.

assumptions: propagationStale left undefined means propagation was not evaluated, so it cannot decide the verdict — a caller that publishes freshness to a reader passes it.
A stored 'unknown' hash means the note was written when the node carried no hash; on a node that hashes now, that is the no-baseline case.

risks.text: fresh answers for the whole note, so a propagation-stale node reads as fresh:false; a consumer that needs only the node's own drift asks contentMoved instead of re-deriving a narrower rule.

patterns: States and reasons are enumerated at runtime, so a new one surfaces as an unanswered case in the law rather than as a silently unhandled branch.
invariants: Content and schema decide before propagation: a note whose node text moved needs a rewrite regardless of upstream.
Every stale verdict names its reason; fresh:false is never published without one.
not-comparable publishes no fresh value at all — reporting either would state a check that never ran.
annotation.integrationPoints: The current hash comes from mod:repovine/src/annotations/content-hash; propagation from mod:repovine/src/annotations/propagation; consumed by mod:repovine/src/annotations/store (isFresh, queue, coverage), mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/inspect-node-core, mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/domain-map and mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/index; provenance vocabulary from mod:repovine/src/response/provenance.
annotation.dataFlow: stored annotation + current hash + optional propagation verdict → annotationFreshness → verdict → classifyStale for the queue, annotationFreshnessMeta for a response.

annotation.summary: The on-disk lifecycle of the annotation file: create it, merge it after a version-control conflict, normalize it to canonical form, and report its health (staleness, orphans, merge-review markers, carrier-link gaps, risk-scope candidates, and a separate advisory 'inconsistent' count for notes whose filled fields contradict the current graph). A merge prefers exact sides from the git index over reconstructed ones, backs up whatever it replaces, and refuses guesses worse than stopping.

keyExports.buildAnnotationHealthScan: Loads config + interpreter entrypoints and runs scanAnnotationHealth to build the underlying stale/orphan scan.
keyExports.computeConsumerScopeDensity: Ratio of scope:'consumer' risks to total risks, per-node over-cap list, and risks that look consumer-scoped but are not marked.
keyExports.ensureEmptyAnnotationsFile: Create an empty annotations file for a repo without one (via ensureEmptyAnnotationsFileAtPath).
keyExports.getAnnotationMergeStatus: Pre-flight: does the file exist, parse OK, carry conflict markers, index unmerged, plus next actions.
keyExports.mergeAnnotationFiles: Three-way field-level merge (base/ours/theirs) with a per-field audit trail (AnnotationMergeConflict[]).
keyExports.mergeAnnotationsOnDisk: Merge a conflicted file under a file lock from git-index stages (preferred) or conflict markers, reporting base source and a backup path.
keyExports.normalizeAnnotationsFile: Rewrite the file in canonical form without merging.
keyExports.validateAnnotationHealth: Full health report: staleness (content/propagation), orphans, merge review, consumer-scope density, carrier-link gaps, advisory risk-scope candidates, and counts.inconsistent (computeInconsistentModuleAnnotations from ./quality.js) — the correctness axis, reported but never moving `status`.

assumptions: Merge base comes from the git index when the file is genuinely unmerged there; otherwise from reconstructed base/ours/theirs sections of the conflicted file (diff3-style markers).
Ambient version-control env vars are stripped before every execFileSync git call.
Base is compared against but never taken as an output side; pass/schemaVersion on a merged node is taken as the maximum of both sides.
A missing/unparseable base is parsed leniently and raises a baseWarning rather than failing the merge.

counts.inconsistent is advisory like consumerScopeDensity/carrierLinkGaps/riskScopeCandidates: it never flips AnnotationValidationReport.status away from 'clean', since a graph-contradiction is about note content, not queue staleness.
The mergeReview and propagationStale nextActions now carry a concrete nodeId (first offending row) rather than an argument-less write_annotation call, since write_annotation requires nodeId.

sideEffects.description: reads the annotation file and its backups
writes merged/normalized files under a file lock, snapshotting replaced bytes as a backup
runs git commands (via execFileSync) with ambient VCS env vars removed

risks.text: Caller resolving a conflict must not rely on hand-edits to the conflicted file: an index-stage merge recomputes from the pre-merge blobs, not from what is currently on disk.
Caller must hand the removed node id list (AnnotationMergeReport.deletedNodeIds) to the live store before the next refresh, or the store's never-drop-on-refresh behavior restores exactly those nodes.

patterns: Prefer the exact source (git index / a passed AnnotationStore), fall back to an approximate one (reconstructed markers / lenient parse), and always report which one was used (baseSource, baseWarning).
invariants: Each resolved field in a merge conflict records which side was chosen and why (AnnotationMergeConflict).
Array-valued annotation fields union and deduplicate across sides rather than picking one wholesale.
A marker-free file with an unmerged git-index entry is never silently normalized.
counts.inconsistent, consumerScopeDensity, carrierLinkGaps and riskScopeCandidates are all advisory: none of them can turn a queue-clean report into 'needs-review'.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used by MCP merge/validation/status tools; wraps mod:repovine/src/annotations/store (AnnotationStore) and mod:repovine/src/annotations/backlog (scanAnnotationHealth, isContentStaleItem/isPropagationStaleItem); consistency axis from mod:repovine/src/annotations/quality (computeInconsistentModuleAnnotations); scope filtering from mod:repovine/src/annotations/scope-hints (nodeInScopeHints); locking/backup/serialization from mod:repovine/src/annotations/file-lock, mod:repovine/src/annotations/backup, mod:repovine/src/annotations/format; carrier-link gap detection from mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links and mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-review; risk-scope candidates from mod:repovine/src/annotations/risk-scope-candidates.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root -> annotation path -> repository-identity check -> git-index stages, or conflict-marker sides including a reconstructed base -> lenient base parse -> field-level three-way merge -> backup of replaced bytes -> canonical serialization under lock -> AnnotationMergeReport; separately, graph+snapshot+annotations -> buildAnnotationHealthScan + computeInconsistentModuleAnnotations + carrier/risk-scope helpers -> AnnotationValidationReport, with removed nodes handed to the live store before the next refresh.

annotation.summary: Git merge conflict review markers in annotations: applyMergeReviewHints embeds merge-review: field patterns and ours/theirs assumption prefixes after scalar conflicts; clearMergeReviewHints strips them once resolved via write_annotation.

keyExports.clearMergeReviewHints: Removes review markers when field updated.
keyExports.listMergeReviewFields: Lists fields still carrying review hints.
keyExports.mergeReviewPatternForField: Stable pattern string per annotation field.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream types/format; merge-review helpers unchanged.
risks: Agents must rewrite final field content — hints are not authoritative merged text.
patterns: Git conflict markers in JSON trigger merge_annotations workflow.
invariants: Never hand-edit conflict markers in repovine.annots.json.
annotation.integrationPoints: merge_annotations MCP tool and git merge conflict resolution workflow in AGENTS.md.
annotation.dataFlow: conflict markers in JSON → parse ours/theirs assumptions → agent picks merged summary via write_annotation → validate_annotations.

annotation.summary: Classifies a node into one of ten kinds so annotation scoring and field guidance can be specific to what the node is rather than uniform. The classification is an ordered decision tree over the node type, the export shapes, the path and the semantic hints, falling through to a neutral kind when nothing is decisive.

keyExports.ModuleKind: The ten kinds, from type-only declarations through interface, handler, adapter and service shapes to the aggregate node types.
keyExports.UI_COMPONENT_EXTENSIONS_RE: Extensions treated as carrying a UI component by convention: .tsx/.jsx/.vue/.svelte.
keyExports.inferModuleKind: Returns the kind for a graph node, a module record, or both.
keyExports.recommendedFieldsForKind: The fields an annotation of that kind is expected to carry.

assumptions: The order of the checks is the classification: the first that matches wins, so moving a check changes what a module is called.
Node-type kinds are settled first because they are facts rather than guesses.
Infrastructure is recognized by identifier prefix rather than by module record, because those live outside the module index and the record is usually absent.
Type-only modules are decided early, since they need only a shape description and nothing about behaviour.
The backend check runs before the interface checks, so a weak frontend signal such as an imported client library does not turn a server module into an interface one.

Interface classification is gated on the owning language plugin declaring that it produces interface surfaces, so a module from a backend-only language is never called one even when its path happens to match.

The built-in plugins are registered by importing the bootstrap for its side effect, so this works outside a build; the import is cheap because it registers plain descriptors and leaves the heavy parser lazy.

sideEffects.description: imports the source-plugin bootstrap so plugin capabilities can be resolved

risks: A module whose plugin cannot be determined is treated as capable of interface surfaces, which preserves the historical default but means a new backend-only language mislabels its modules until its plugin is resolvable here.
Path tokens are a fixed vocabulary, so a repository using different folder names classifies everything as neutral and receives generic field guidance rather than a warning that classification failed.
The kind decides which fields are expected, so a misclassification produces a confident but wrong checklist — an annotation can score well against the wrong standard.
patterns: Facts before guesses: node type, then identifier prefix, then export shape, then heuristics over path and hints.
The detection helpers are shared with the architecture analysis rather than duplicated, so both agree on what a frontend surface or a request handler looks like.
annotation.flowDescription: inferModuleKind applies an ordered decision tree: fixed kinds for domain/service/infra nodes -> types-only -> backend-context gate -> ui heuristics -> api-handler -> adapter -> service-mgr -> generic fallback.
invariants: Every input yields a kind; the neutral one is the fallback rather than a failure.

The per-kind field list is one input to the expected-field set. The scoring pass adds demands from module facts — env vars pull in side effects and env dependencies, size pulls in risks, a wide export surface pulls in integration points — and it decides data flow by its own size-and-kind rule that ignores the list. The score itself is kind-independent: each populated field carries a fixed weight whatever the kind, and a summary is always required.
A plugin without interface surfaces never yields the interface kind.
annotation.integrationPoints: The kind and its field list are consumed by the annotation quality scoring in mod:repovine/src/annotations/store; the shared detection helpers come from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/heuristics; plugin capabilities are resolved through mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/registry after mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/bootstrap registers the built-ins.
annotation.dataFlow: graph node or module record -> fixed kinds by node type and identifier prefix -> export-shape check -> backend, interface, handler, adapter and service heuristics in order -> kind -> the expected field list for that kind.

annotation.summary: Pure propagation engine: whether a module's annotation is entrypoint-bounded derived stale, plus dependency cones, contract hubs, blast previews, and audit slices. One rule answers for a single module or for the whole repository — derivedStaleEvaluator builds the shared inputs lazily, computeEntrypointBoundedDerived iterates it, isEntrypointBoundedDerivedStale asks about one node without materializing the set.

keyExports.buildPropagationSlice: Shortest importer chain from anchor module to nearest entrypoint for write_annotation audit.
keyExports.collectEntrypointRoots: Collect moduleId roots from interpreter EntrypointFragment list.
keyExports.computeDepCone: BFS downward from entrypoints following imports outEdges.
keyExports.computeEntrypointBoundedDerived: The propagation-stale module set, from the same evaluator a single-node caller uses.
keyExports.computePropagationPreview: Read-only blast preview { hard, derived, domains, entrypoints } for a changed module.
keyExports.derivedStaleEvaluator: Shared inputs (module lookup, dep cone, hub predicate) behind an isStale(moduleId) question; hubs precomputed only for a whole-repository pass.
keyExports.getImportBaselineStaleUpstream: Direct imports whose current hash differs from the note's stored baseline.
keyExports.isDerivedStaleModule: Baseline drift on a note that still matches the module's own content and schema.
keyExports.isEntrypointBoundedDerivedStale: The propagation verdict for one module.
keyExports.isHubContractDrift: Hub content moved and its export surface no longer matches the note's keyExports.
keyExports.reachesEntrypoint: Consumer-direction BFS via importer inEdges until an entrypoint module is hit.

assumptions: Entrypoint-bounded derived stale uses importBaseline snapshots taken on write_annotation.
PropagationConfig from mod:repovine/src/config controls consumer reach depth and the hub allow/deny lists.
Content and schema freshness is decided by mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness, so a content-stale note is never also reported as propagation-stale.
The module lookup is cached per snapshot object, so a single-node caller does not rebuild it per call.
risks: Missing entrypoints under-propagates narrow derived.
Hub list omission misses contract review on widely imported modules.

risks.text: Widening happens only when one and the same drifted upstream is a contract hub whose export surface moved; reading hub-ness on one upstream together with drift on another would widen review on a hub that never moved.

patterns: Single-node and whole-repository answers come from one evaluator, so a tool describing a node and the queue ranking it cannot diverge.
invariants: A module reported propagation-stale is content-fresh and schema-current: its note still matches the text it describes.
The dependency cone and hub set are computed on first use, so a node without baseline drift costs one direct-import pass.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/annotations/backlog builds queue rows/coverage from computeEntrypointBoundedDerived and derivedStaleEvaluator (mod:repovine/src/annotations/store sits above backlog for persistence/queries); mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/annotations.ts and mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/inspect-node-core for single-node verdicts; mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/index also consumes single-node propagation checks; mod:repovine/src/annotations/content-hash for baselines/hashes; mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness for the content/schema verdict; mod:repovine/src/config propagation section.
annotation.dataFlow: EntrypointFragment list → collectEntrypointRoots → computeDepCone (lazy) → evaluator compares stored importBaseline against current hashes, then widens on a drifted contract hub or on entrypoint reachability; buildPropagationSlice records the shortest importer chain for audit.

annotation.summary: Scores a stored annotation on two orthogonal axes: completeness (a weighted field count that also names what is missing) and consistency (filled fields that contradict graph facts). Neither axis moves the other; consistency is a contradiction list, never a number.

keyExports.AnnotationQualityInput: Counts plus optional ground truth; an absent ground truth skips its check rather than fabricating one.
keyExports.StoredAnnotationSource: The one method the recompute needs from a note store, so scoring never reaches for store state.
keyExports.annotationQualityInputForModule: Builds the ground truth a module's consistency check needs: real export names and detected side-effect kinds.
keyExports.computeAnnotationQuality: 0–10 completeness by moduleKind recommendedFields, plus tier, missingFields and the attached consistency verdict.
keyExports.computeInconsistentModuleAnnotations: Recomputes consistency over every stored module note and returns those with a hard contradiction.
keyExports.isHardConsistencyIssue: Hard (keyExports/sideEffects) vs advisory (envDependencies, whose detector is known-incomplete).

assumptions: A check whose ground truth is absent from the input is skipped, never guessed — a re-export barrel records no named exports and must not be flagged.
Completeness is measured against recommendedFieldsForKind, so a kind change moves what counts as missing.

sideEffects.description: reads annotation content and module facts; writes nothing

invariants: The consistency axis never changes score or tier.
Only filled fields are checked for contradictions; an empty field is completeness's concern.
annotation.integrationPoints: annotations/module-kind (recommendedFieldsForKind), annotations/side-effect-vocab (detected effect kinds from SemanticHints); read by annotations/backlog for queue urgency and recommendedFields, by mcp/lib/annotations and mcp/lib/inspect-node-core for the published quality block, and by analysis/architecture detectors.
annotation.dataFlow: annotation content + module facts → weighted field scan → score/tier/missingFields; independently, filled fields × graph ground truth → contradiction list → attached as consistency.

annotation.summary: Computes deterministic advisory candidates for plain/local annotation risks that look like consumer or boundary scope authoring opportunities.

keyExports.computeRiskScopeCandidates: Scans stored annotations plus graph/snapshot context, returns aggregate counts, reasons, samples, and optional paged items for candidate review.

assumptions: Only risks with effective local scope are considered; explicit consumer and boundary risks are skipped.
Path and integrationPoint matches are supporting cues only and cannot create a boundary candidate without a strong text cue.
risks: Regex cue rules are conservative but can still produce false positives; reviewers must inspect source before rewriting annotations.
Candidates are advisory-only and must not feed inspect_node investigate delivery or the boundary pre-edit index.
invariants: A single risk entry emits at most one candidate; boundary precedence wins overlap and total equals consumer plus boundary.
Candidate sorting stays deterministic: boundary first, then reason count descending, nodeId, and riskIndex.
annotation.integrationPoints: Uses normalizeRisks from mod:repovine/src/annotations/format and the integrationPoints target parser from mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links.
annotation.dataFlow: annotations plus graph/snapshot context -> local risk entries -> cue reason extraction -> sorted candidates -> validation aggregate or paged status view.

annotation.summary: Checks whether a graph node id falls under a set of scope hints (repo-path prefixes, graph kinds like 'infra', or 'pkg:' package ids), with '.' matching the whole repository.

keyExports.nodeInScopeHints: True if nodeId matches any hint: exact/prefix match on the hint text, or (for non-pkg hints) a '-' joined prefix; a 'pkg:' hint additionally expands to its bare package name via packageNameFromId

assumptions: Module ids carry the package name in the path tail rather than the id prefix, so a 'pkg:' hint is matched against the bare package name, not nodeId's own prefix
annotation.integrationPoints: Uses mod:repovine/src/graph/node-ids (packageNameFromId) to derive a pkg: hint's bare package name

annotation.summary: Classifies a string in an annotation as a literal secret value (vs. a safe name of one), shared by the write-path refusal and the annotation-secret-hygiene detector so both answer identically.

keyExports.annotationSecretFieldPaths: (annotationBody, rootPath) => dotted paths of every string field in the tree that containsSecretValue flags
keyExports.containsSecretValue: (text) => true if text is a credential shape (Stripe/Slack/GitHub/AWS), a PEM private-key header, or an assigned secret=value pattern; false if text is a bare UPPER_CASE env-var-style name

assumptions: rule order is load-bearing: credential-shape/PEM checks run before the env-var-name exemption, since an AWS access key id is spelled like an all-caps name
risks: Rule order (credential/PEM before env-var-name exemption before assigned-secret pattern) must be preserved; reordering could misclassify an AWS access key id as a safe name.

annotation.summary: Resolves content-hash fingerprints for runtime-resource (resource:) nodes: buildRuntimeResourceContentHashLookup groups every snapshot declaration per id and reduces each group to an order-independent set-hash; getResourceContentHashForServiceId aggregates the same way without a lookup; resolveServiceResourceContentHash falls back to graph RuntimeResourceNodeData.contentHash.

keyExports.buildRuntimeResourceContentHashLookup: Groups snapshot.infraModules declarations per makeRuntimeResourceId; reduces each group with the set-hash (single distinct hash returned verbatim).
keyExports.getParentInfraContentHash: InfraModuleInfo.contentHash for parent infra module id.
keyExports.getParentInfraModuleId: Parent infra module id via contains inEdge on resource: node.
keyExports.getResourceContentHashForServiceId: Collects all snapshot declarations matching makeRuntimeResourceId and reduces with the same set-hash; a provided lookup value wins.
keyExports.resolveServiceResourceContentHash: Primary fingerprint: snapshot set-hash, else graph node data.contentHash.

assumptions: Set-hash = sha256 over the deduped, sorted declaration hashes, sliced to 16 hex; a single distinct hash is returned verbatim, so single-declaration and identical-duplicate resources keep byte-stable fingerprints.
risks: Parser contentHash algorithm change marks all service annotations stale until rewrite.
Adding or removing a differing declaration of an id changes the set membership, re-staling that id's annotation once.
patterns: Ties runtime-resource annotation freshness to parsed IaC resource payload hashes; multi-declaration reduces to a sorted sha256 set-hash mirroring domain member hashing.
invariants: makeRuntimeResourceId must stay stable across refreshes for hash lookup.
Lookup and no-lookup paths reduce the identical universe (snapshot.infraModules), so a multi-declared id resolves to one order-independent value on every surface: write, inspect, queue, coverage.
Returns undefined when neither snapshot nor graph node carries contentHash.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/annotations/store service and domain roll-up content hash (hashDomainMembers consumes the set-hash); uses mod:repovine/src/graph/make-runtime-resource-id.
annotation.dataFlow: resource: serviceId → resolveServiceResourceContentHash → compared on refresh for service/runtime-resource annotation freshness; multi-declared ids converge to the set-hash regardless of infra file-scan order.

annotation.summary: Canonical vocabulary, Zod schema, and query helpers for the structured sideEffects array on annotations. Declares the closed SIDE_EFFECT_KINDS list with per-kind documentation, validates writes through SideEffectSchema, offers predicates for detectors (isPure, hasKind, hasSubtype, hasKindSubtype, hasPersistentEffect), and maps graph SemanticHints into kinds so a declared-pure module can be checked against detected effects.

keyExports.SIDE_EFFECT_KINDS: The closed list of eleven kinds (io-read, io-write, state-local, state-global, process, concurrency, time, subscribe, external, resource, pure); authoritative for detectors and the agent-facing docs.
keyExports.SideEffect: One entry: required kind plus optional subtype and description.
keyExports.SideEffectSchema: Zod schema for the array; rejects an empty sideEffects list.
keyExports.detectSideEffectKindsFromHints: Derives kinds from SemanticHints runtimeActions and effectImports; undefined when no reliable signal exists.
keyExports.hasKind: True when any entry matches the given kind.
keyExports.hasKindSubtype: True when any entry matches both kind and subtype.
keyExports.hasPersistentEffect: True when an entry is state-global, or io-write with a subtype other than stdout/stderr.
keyExports.hasSubtype: True when any entry carries the given subtype, compared case-insensitively.
keyExports.isPure: True when every entry declares kind pure.
keyExports.serializeSideEffect: Canonical kind:subtype:description string used for search token indexing.
keyExports.truncateSideEffect: Clips an entry's description to a maximum length.

assumptions: Eleven SideEffectKind values including the pure sentinel; subtype is diagnostic and not part of the closed enum.
detectSideEffectKindsFromHints returns undefined rather than an empty list when hints carry no reliable runtimeActions or effectImports.
Subtype comparisons are case-insensitive.
risks: hasPersistentEffect is narrower than 'not pure': external, resource, process and concurrency entries do not satisfy it, so a detector that means 'has any effect' must not reach for it.
Adding a kind requires updating the detectors, the agent-facing docs, and existing annotations that were written against the old list.
Over-mapping hints to kinds would false-flag legitimately pure client modules as privileged.

risks.text: Callers must declare the pure sentinel rather than an empty array: the annotation content schema refuses an empty sideEffects list, and an omitted field is treated as unknown rather than pure.

patterns: kind is the primary detector signal while subtype stays diagnostic, so detectors never branch on free text.
The pure sentinel separates an intentional zero-effect declaration from a field the author forgot.
invariants: sideEffects is never written as []: the field is omitted or declares [{kind: 'pure'}].
CONSOLE_WRITE_SUBTYPES limits the io-write exemption to stdout and stderr.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by write_annotation validation, mod:repovine/src/annotations/format, and the architecture detectors that classify privileged client-side effects; imports SemanticHints from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types.
annotation.dataFlow: SemanticHints → detectSideEffectKindsFromHints → compared against the declared sideEffects in the annotation consistency axis.
