annotation.summary: Annotation persistence over repovine.annots.json: load, never-lose merge with disk under a cross-process lock, debounced durable save, orphan detection. Queue and coverage are projections of one walk in mod:repovine/src/annotations/backlog; this store owns the notes, not the backlog arithmetic. The store instance is reused across refreshes and survives state swaps.

keyExports.AnnotationExternalCorruptionError: Raised when a save finds the file changed externally into something unreadable; the save refuses rather than overwrite.
keyExports.AnnotationFileStatusSnapshot: Whether the file exists, parses, and carries conflict markers.
keyExports.AnnotationHealthScan: The needs-work half of the backlog, projected for validate/compliance/status: counts, lite rows, and a hydrating sample.
keyExports.AnnotationStore: In-memory store: set/delete, flush, reloadFromDisk({signal}) under cross-process lock, forgetDeletedOnDisk for external deletions; isFresh/freshnessOf answer through the shared freshness rule; getQueue/getQueuePage/scanAnnotationHealth/getStats project one backlog walk.
keyExports.describeMergeKeeps: One sentence for a merge that kept records the file disagreed with, naming why a revert did not stick.

assumptions: Same store reused across builds; a fresh build re-reads disk.
Quarantined parse entries must not flush until merge resolves.
Every backlog number this store publishes comes from buildAnnotationBacklog; the store adds no counting of its own.
Freshness is decided by mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness and the current hash by mod:repovine/src/annotations/content-hash; this store compares neither itself.

sideEffects.description: reads/writes repovine.annots.json under cross-process file lock

risks.text: forgetDeletedOnDisk must be called before next flush or external deletions re-appear; external rollback of annots.json needs re-apply after server exit.

patterns: importBaseline captured on write; refreshImportBaseline clears propagation-stale.
Queue paths hydrate item prose only for returned rows.
invariants: getQueue, getQueuePage, scanAnnotationHealth and getStats answer about one walk, so the queue and coverage never disagree about a node.
annotation.integrationPoints: annotations/backlog (the one walk behind every queue and coverage number), fs/atomic (durable save), annotations/file-lock (cross-process lock), annotations/backup (snapshots), annotations/freshness (single-node verdicts for isFresh/freshnessOf), annotations/format (parse and serialize).
annotation.stateShape: Map<nodeId, StoredAnnotation> with nodeType, contentHash, updatedAt, annotation object, optional mergeReview fields.
annotation.dataFlow: loadAsync → in-memory note map → queue/coverage calls hand the map to buildAnnotationBacklog and project its rows or coverage → write merges annotation + refreshes baseline → debounced save chain → JSON via fs/atomic; refresh → reloadFromDisk(signal) merges disk into memory under lock: disk is the base, pending writes overlay it field-wise, keys we hold that disk lacks or has regressed below stay ours, our deletes apply.

annotation.summary: Core annotation schema: RiskEntry (plain or scoped), AnnotationContent (15+ optional fields including summary, keyExports, sideEffects, risks), and StoredAnnotation (nodeId, contentHash, importBaseline, pass/updatedAt). Re-exported by mod:repovine/src/types for compatibility.

keyExports.AnnotationContent: 15+ fields: summary, keyExports, assumptions, sideEffects, risks, patterns, flowDescription, invariants, extensionPoints, integrationPoints, stateShape, dataFlow, envDependencies, propagationSlice.
keyExports.CURRENT_ANNOTATION_SCHEMA_VERSION: Bump when adding optional fields to trigger stale backfill (currently 1).
keyExports.StoredAnnotation: Persisted memo: nodeId, nodeType, contentHash, pass, updatedAt, annotation, importBaseline (direct-import snapshot), schemaVersion.

assumptions: RiskEntry without explicit scope defaults to local scope.
importBaseline absent = no propagation-stale tracking (non-module node types).
StoredAnnotation importBaseline is always a snapshot taken at write time, never stale or edited.

risks.text: CURRENT_ANNOTATION_SCHEMA_VERSION bump requires coord with repovine.annots.json migration; stale-trigger logic in mod:repovine/src/annotations/store.

patterns: RiskEntry scope:consumer marks importer obligations; scope:boundary marks frozen surfaces.
AnnotationContent summary is REQUIRED; all other fields optional.
invariants: StoredAnnotation.nodeType ∈ {module, export-symbol, domain, runtime-resource, template}.
AnnotationContent.sideEffects: never write []—omit or use [{ kind: pure }].
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exported by mod:repovine/src/types (compat barrel); consumed by mod:repovine/src/annotations/store, mod:repovine/src/annotations/format, and annotation validation.
annotation.dataFlow: AnnotationContent is JSON-serialized to repovine.annots.json by StoredAnnotation wrapper; RiskEntry scope controls queue/boundary machinery.

annotation.summary: Engine-internal re-export facade for the @repovine/plugin-sdk fact types (ModuleInfo, PackageInfo, InfraResource, SemanticHints, Ui* hint shapes, IaC vocabulary, and known kind-metadata). Engine and MCP layers import through here so the SDK package stays the single source of truth for the fact layer. Third-party plugins import @repovine/plugin-sdk directly, not this facade.
assumptions: Pure type re-export: erases at compile time, adds no runtime edge.
Engine call sites reach these types through this facade or the src/types barrel; the graph model and node-view modules import the SDK package directly.
The set tracks the SDK's layer-1 fact exports, excluding ReExportInfo (TypeScript source plugin only) and the graph ontology (RepositoryGraph, NodeType, EdgeKind, Interpreter).

risks.text: Frozen against the @repovine/plugin-sdk contract: a type added, renamed, or removed here must track the SDK, and it must stay limited to layer-1 fact types rather than graph ontology.

patterns: Pure type re-export barrel with no exports of its own.
annotation.flowDescription: SDK package declares the fact types → this facade re-exports them → engine and MCP layers import them here or through the internal src/types barrel.
invariants: Only fact-layer types are re-exported; RepositoryGraph, NodeType, EdgeKind, and Interpreter stay engine-internal.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src; consumed internally through the src/types compatibility barrel.

annotation.summary: Read-only, client-scoped audit of agent assets. It compares managed files byte-for-byte with canonical setup output, reports managed files that are absent without pretending they were scanned, checks every required onboarding topic across each client's combined surfaces, and scans project-owned agent files only for tool-shaped names absent from the live registry.

keyExports.AgentAssetFinding: One stable diagnostic code with file, severity, and actionable message.
keyExports.DoctorAgentAssetsReport: Resolved scope, scanned/governed file inventories, findings, protocol/projection versions, and counts.
keyExports.agentAssetDoctorCliFindings: Maps the structured report to human-facing health rows.
keyExports.doctorAgentAssets: Runs managed-content, missing-asset, topic-totality, and loose project-file tool-name checks for a resolved client scope.
keyExports.parseDoctorClientScopeArg: Validates cursor, claude, codex, or all for the doctor CLI.

assumptions: Managed assets are project-owned projections only when listCanonicalManagedAssets says so; other agent files must remain customizable.
The live registry supplies current verb families, while check_, cleanup_, doctor_, and render_ stay as intentional legacy heuristics.
Warnings do not make report.ok false; exact managed-content drift is the error class.
Auto scope with one detected client remediates narrowly; multi-client or fallback auto scope remediates with setup all because setup has no auto argument.

sideEffects.description: reads managed setup projections and project-owned agent files

risks: Loose legacy prefix heuristics can warn on project prose that resembles a removed tool name.
Topic coverage is marker-based and can accept an unrelated occurrence of a marker token.
Exact comparison marks every managed projection stale after a canonical prose change even when runtime behavior is unchanged.
patterns: Governed projections get exact comparison; project-owned files get a deliberately loose stale-tool scan.
Absent assets are findings but never enter scanned or governed counts.
Registry-derived tool prefixes and a pinned topic registry avoid silent thinning of diagnostic coverage.
invariants: The audit never writes or repairs files.
A project-owned file is never compared with a canonical template.
Every remediation command names an argument accepted by the setup argv router.
summary.assets equals the number of files actually read.
annotation.integrationPoints: Canonical assets come from mod:repovine/src/cli/managed-setup-assets; topic obligations from mod:repovine/src/cli/client-topics; client detection from mod:repovine/src/cli/client-scope; valid tools from mod:repovine/src/mcp/tool-defs via the caller; health CLI renders the result in mod:repovine/src/cli/health.
annotation.dataFlow: repo root + client scope + live tool names → resolve clients → list/read canonical managed assets → exact drift, absence, and topic checks → scan non-governed agent files for stale tool spellings → structured report → CLI rows.

annotation.summary: Pure string renderers for Delivery Protocol projections: result templates, role guidance, implementer briefs, context-quality guidance, and doctor markers. The projected context-quality text states that score thresholds are advisory until the labelled-corpus return bar is met, while evidence-backed annotation checks remain enforceable.

keyExports.DELIVERY_PROTOCOL_GUIDE_PATH: Path of the protocol guide the projections point at.
keyExports.DELIVERY_PROTOCOL_MARKER: Stable comment marker the doctor greps to read the protocol and projection versions.
keyExports.PROJECTION_VERSION: Version stamped on the projected assets.
keyExports.RESULT_BLOCK_HEADING: Heading under which the structured result block is projected.
keyExports.renderClientProtocolGuidanceSection: Per-role client asset section, with provenance and quality-axis guidance.
keyExports.renderContextQualityGuidance: The block explaining context-session scoring and how to inspect it.
keyExports.renderImplementerBrief: The autonomous worker mandate: graph as truth, annotation-constraint checkpoints, the annotate-phase workflow and the result honesty rules.
keyExports.renderMainDeliveryProtocolSection: The main-agent explicit-protocol section, including context-session guidance.
keyExports.renderRequiredArtifactHints: The required-artifact hints derived from a manifest.
keyExports.renderResultBlockSection: The result-block section combining the template and its hints.
keyExports.renderStructuredResultBlock: The run-result JSON template for harness submissions.

assumptions: The harness loads the implementer brief through its own command, and that brief is deliberately stricter than client-facing instructions.
Result blocks belong only to explicit protocol mode.
The projection version stays fixed pre-release, so content changes require re-rendering assets rather than a version bump.
Protocol and context-quality doc paths are pointers into the repovine source repository.
risks: Projected assets go stale independently of this module until re-rendered.
Context-quality guidance must not imply a hard score gate while validation remains below the return bar.
If the implementer brief omits annotation constraints, workers may treat risks as background prose rather than obligations.
patterns: The annotate phase is documented as an explicit sequence: refresh, take the queue, inspect each node, write, clean orphans, validate.

Implementation and review phases convert annotation fields into constraints before edits: invariants must hold, risks must be mitigated or explicitly accepted, declared flow and integration order must be preserved or deliberately changed, and protected side effects need a preceding gate.
Provenance rule: inspecting an export grounds a module, while naming a package or domain scope alone does not.
invariants: Projected context-quality guidance describes the score as advisory until validation succeeds.
Observable claims in a run result are validated against post-refresh graph state.
An annotate-phase run must not edit code.
Relevant annotation invariants left unresolved are blockers, not routine residual risk.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the onboarding-asset and render commands in the CLI and by the harness run-brief path; the manifests and protocol constants come from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests and mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol.
annotation.dataFlow: manifest plus protocol constants -> render helpers -> projected client instructions, rules, and briefs -> doctor drift checks and worker prompts.

annotation.summary: Projects the agent assets into their per-client locations and, when asked, writes them. It renders agent files for each supported client, the managed block for the always-on instructions file, the project subagent scaffold, and the raw manifests as a preview. The always-on file is merged rather than replaced, so instructions the project owns survive a re-render.

keyExports.RENDER_CLIENTS: The five render targets, one of which ('json') is preview-only.
keyExports.RenderAgentAssetsOptions: What to render: the repository, an optional client, and whether to write.
keyExports.RenderAgentAssetsResult: What was produced: the versions, the per-asset sizes and write status, and the full content when previewing.
keyExports.RenderClientArg: A render target or the request for all of them ('all').
keyExports.RenderedAgentAsset: One rendered file: its client, target path, content, and whether it may be written.
keyExports.computeAgentsMdDiskContent: Works out what the always-on file should contain after a render, given whatever is on disk now.
keyExports.renderAgentAssets: Renders the assets for one client or all of them, returning what was produced and writing it when the write flag is set.

assumptions: Merging the always-on file follows three branches: replace between the markers when they are present, replace the file outright when it looks like one this tool generated, otherwise leave it.
The manifest ('json') target is descriptive only and is never written, which is why every asset carries a writable flag rather than the caller inferring it from the path.

Preview returns the full rendered content, and for every asset except the always-on instructions file that content is byte-for-byte what a write would put on disk. The always-on file is the exception: its preview carries the canonical managed block alone, because reconciliation against what is already on disk runs only on the write path.
Both the protocol version and the projection version travel with the result, so a consumer can tell what produced the files.

This is a leaf: it imports the asset definitions and templates, and two callers import it -- the setup path that writes the rendered files, and the doctor's canonical asset manifest, which declares the content those same paths should carry.

sideEffects.description: creates directories and writes the rendered files when the write flag is set

risks: When the markers are absent, a heuristic decides whether the existing always-on file was generated by this tool, and if it decides yes the file is replaced whole rather than appended to; a hand-written file that resembles a generated one loses its content.
Assets are written one at a time with no staging, so an interruption partway leaves some client configurations updated and others not, with nothing recording which.
Rendering targets fixed paths, so renaming an asset leaves the previous file behind in every repository already set up.
patterns: Render and write are the same pass with a flag, which is what keeps the preview honest.
Managed content is delimited by markers so a shared file can have both an owned region and a project-owned one.
invariants: Preview-only assets are never written, whatever the write flag says.
Content outside the markers is preserved when the markers are present.
Rendered files carry no live secrets.
annotation.integrationPoints: Asset bodies and render helpers come from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; the managed block and its markers from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates; the projection version from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection; the protocol version and its buildDeliveryProtocol builder from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol; the manifests from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests. Invoked by the render command and by the setup path, and the same file list is what the doctor check inspects.
annotation.dataFlow: client selection -> assets rendered per client -> the always-on file reconciled against disk -> optional directory creation and write -> per-asset report with sizes and write status.

annotation.summary: CLI-only general agent utilities (`repovine agents <cmd>`) for harness/CI, file-in / JSON-out: `roles` reads the repository role source, `orient` runs a deterministic search_context + trace_flow (no LLM), and `session-quality` prints a Context Session Quality report. Delivery Protocol operations moved to the sibling `repovine delivery` surface. session-quality prints acceptHandoff/rejectReasons but exits zero whenever a report exists while the score is unvalidated; a missing/unreadable session exits non-zero.

keyExports.runAgentsCli: Dispatches the utility subcommands (roles, orient, session-quality) and returns the process exit code.

assumptions: JSON stays on stdout and progress on stderr so callers can parse the contract.
roles never builds a graph; orient may build one.
Callers that need the advisory context verdict read acceptHandoff/rejectReasons from JSON rather than treating the session-quality exit code as a gate.
AgentsCliEnv is defined in mod:repovine/src/cli/agents-shared and re-exported here for existing importers.

sideEffects.description: writes JSON results, with progress on the error stream
the orient command builds a graph on a thread pool
shells out to git to read a committed tree when roles is pinned to a revision (--at)
redirects the pipeline log sink to the error stream on entry and again before a build

risks: The orient command can pay full cold-build cost.
Until the context score clears its validation bar, automation that previously treated session-quality --mode harness as a hard exit-code gate must consume the JSON advisory fields instead.
patterns: Output stream for the contract, error stream for everything else, which keeps the surface pipe-safe.
invariants: The output stream carries only JSON.
roles never builds a graph.
session-quality exits zero when a report exists, even when acceptHandoff is false; a missing/unreadable session exits non-zero.
annotation.integrationPoints: The role source from mod:repovine/src/agents/roles-source; orientation from mod:repovine/src/cli/orient; session reports from mod:repovine/src/context-quality/session-store; shared JSON/flag helpers and the AgentsCliEnv env shape from mod:repovine/src/cli/agents-shared. Dispatched from mod:repovine/src/mcp/index on `repovine agents`. The Delivery Protocol surface is mod:repovine/src/cli/delivery.
annotation.dataFlow: argv -> subcommand dispatch -> role-source read, graph-backed orient, or context-session lookup -> JSON on stdout; exit code gates roles/orient while context-quality stays advisory.

annotation.summary: Shared helpers for the `repovine delivery` and `repovine agents` CLI surfaces: the repo/artifacts env shape and the JSON-out / flag-parse primitives both dispatchers use. Kept in its own module so neither dispatcher imports the other.

keyExports.AgentsCliEnv: The repository root and artifacts directory the CLI subcommands work against.
keyExports.flagValue: Returns the token following a `--flag`, or undefined.
keyExports.numberFlag: Parses a numeric `--flag` value, returning undefined when absent or non-finite.
keyExports.print: Writes a value as pretty JSON straight to stdout, keeping the surface pipe/CI-safe even when graph-build progress logs to stderr.
keyExports.readJsonFile: Reads and JSON-parses a file into { ok:true, value } or { ok:false, error }; never throws.

assumptions: print is the only stdout writer for these CLIs, so results stay one JSON document.
readJsonFile turns read/parse errors into a structured result rather than throwing.

sideEffects.description: readJsonFile reads the given file synchronously
print writes JSON to stdout

patterns: Pure helpers with no dispatcher dependency, so `delivery` and `agents` share them without an import cycle.
invariants: print is the sole stdout writer for these CLI surfaces.
readJsonFile never throws; a parse failure returns { ok:false }.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imported by mod:repovine/src/cli/delivery and mod:repovine/src/cli/agents; AgentsCliEnv is re-exported from mod:repovine/src/cli/agents for existing importers (e.g. mod:repovine/src/cli/orient).
annotation.dataFlow: argv + flag name -> parsed value; file path -> parsed JSON result; value -> stdout JSON.

annotation.summary: Runs a full build ahead of time and prints its progress, for the build command and for setup, which builds by default. It returns the live runtime so a caller that needs the freshly built state does not have to build again.

keyExports.runBuild: Builds the context for a repository, optionally sweeps orphaned annotations, prints a summary, and returns the runtime; when semantic search resolved off because the opt-in transformers peer dependency is absent (not because the user explicitly disabled it), prints a one-line advisory naming TRANSFORMERS_PACKAGE and the npm install command to enable it.

assumptions: Progress goes to the error stream and the summary to the output stream, so a caller can capture the result without the progress noise.
Progress is printed in place and continuously, because a host that sees a silent subprocess on a large repository kills it on its startup timeout — the output is what keeps the build alive.
Orphan cleanup is opt-in and flushes on both sides of the delete: pending writes land before anything is removed, and the removal itself is durable before the call returns.
It exists to move the cost of the first build to an explicit moment rather than into the first tool call.

The semantic-search-off advisory is gated on cfg.semanticSearchEmbeddingsDerived: it prints only when the false value was derived (peer absent), not when the user set semanticSearchEmbeddings: false explicitly — an explicit opt-out stays silent.

sideEffects.description: persists the snapshot cache and may rewrite annotations during cleanup
prints the build summary and, when applicable, the semantic-search-off advisory, with pipeline progress on the error stream

risks: An interrupted build leaves the previous cache in place. The snapshot is written once, after extraction finishes, through a temp file renamed over the target, so a half-written snapshot is never published and never read back. What an interrupt leaves behind is this run's worker-sizing calibration, which only advises the next build's parallelism.
Orphan cleanup deletes annotations whose nodes are absent from the freshly built graph, so a build that under-discovers — a missing plugin, a narrowed scan — removes notes for code that still exists.
On a large repository this runs for minutes with no timeout of its own; progress goes to the error stream, so a programmatic caller that discards stderr sees nothing until the summary lands.
patterns: Progress on one stream, result on the other, so the command is scriptable without losing the feedback that keeps it alive.
Cleanup is a deliberate sweep rather than a default, because agents normally clear their own scope.
annotation.flowDescription: User-facing eager build invoked by `repovine build` and `repovine setup --build`; prints module/graph/annotation counts on completion.
invariants: No tracked source is modified; writes are confined to the local cache and the annotation file.
The live runtime is returned rather than discarded.
annotation.integrationPoints: Builds through mod:repovine/src/mcp/context, reads settings through mod:repovine/src/config, formats output through mod:repovine/src/cli/ui, and names the peer package through mod:repovine/src/semantic/transformers-install TRANSFORMERS_PACKAGE.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → configuration → optional semantic-search-off advisory → full build → optional orphan sweep with flushes either side → summary printed → live runtime returned.

annotation.summary: Undoes setup. It walks every place setup touched — the per-client server entries, the hook registrations, the managed block in the always-on file, the generated agent and skill files, and the ignore-file block — and removes only what it put there, leaving everything around it intact. Each target reports its own outcome, and a dry run produces the same plan without writing.

keyExports.ClearOptions: Whether this is a dry run.
keyExports.ClearResult: One target's outcome, with any backup that was made and a reason when skipped.
keyExports.ClearStatus: The six outcomes: planned removal, planned update, removal, update, skip, or error.
keyExports.RunClearOptions: Dry-run flag plus the confirmation hook the tests substitute.
keyExports.clearWorkspace: Processes every target and returns one outcome per path.
keyExports.runClear: The command entry: prints the plan, asks for confirmation unless running unattended, then applies it.

assumptions: Recognition by content applies to the always-on pointer file and to the shared configs, where a mismatch means the file is edited in place instead. Generated client assets — agents, skills, rules, the current dispatcher hook and copy-me subagent scaffolds — are removed by path: the file is not read, so an edited generated asset is deleted like any other.
Shared files are edited rather than deleted: only the recognized server entry, the recognized hook commands or the marked region come out.
Hook removal matches on the current dispatcher command strings setup registers, so unrelated hooks in the same file are untouched.
The supported hook cleanup surface starts with repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs. Pre-release per-action hook filenames are intentionally not scanned or removed.

Backups cover the shared files edited in place: the file is copied before its repovine region is rewritten, or before an emptied file is removed, and the path appears with the outcome. Whole-file and whole-directory removals take no backup. A backup path is also reported when a prior .bak already exists; that copy holds whatever was in place when the .bak was first made.
A dry run reports planned outcomes through the same code path that performs them, so the plan and the action cannot disagree.
Confirmation declines by default when there is no interactive terminal, which keeps an unattended invocation from waiting or from proceeding blindly.

sideEffects.description: removes and rewrites generated files, creating backups first

risks: A file the user edited is skipped rather than removed when removal is guarded by generated-content recognition, which is the safe choice but means a completed run does not imply every customized file disappeared.
Targets are processed one at a time with no overall transaction, so an interruption leaves some clients unwired and others still configured.
Recognition of content-guarded generated files is exact apart from supported uniform line-ending normalization, so other content differences leave the file in place.
patterns: Remove only what was generated, and only when it is still recognizable — the check is content equality rather than a record of what was written.
Delete whole files, edit shared ones: which of the two applies is decided per target rather than per client.
Every outcome is reported, including skips and their reasons, so the result explains what it did not do.
invariants: Source trees are never touched; only files setup created or regions it inserted.
Content outside a managed region is preserved when that region is removed.
A dry run writes nothing.
The annotation memory is preserved by default.
annotation.integrationPoints: The inverse of the setup path in mod:repovine/src/cli/init; expected file contents come from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates and the generated asset list from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; the ignore-file block from mod:repovine/src/cli/repovine-gitignore; merge and marker handling from mod:repovine/src/cli/merge-config; workspace paths from mod:repovine/src/paths; output through mod:repovine/src/cli/ui.
annotation.dataFlow: workspace root → per-target recognition against the expected content → removal, region edit or skip with a reason → outcomes printed, then applied after confirmation unless this is a dry run.

annotation.summary: Single source-of-truth record (CLIENT_CAPABILITIES) of how each supported client (claude, cursor, codex) launches hook commands and declares MCP servers. Template builders, plugin rendering, setup, clear, and health derive their client-specific strings from this descriptor instead of hardcoding per-client logic.

keyExports.CLIENT_CAPABILITIES: Record<ClientId, ClientCapabilities> — the concrete contract values for claude, cursor, and codex.
keyExports.CODEX_WINDOWS_PLUGIN_ROOT_REF: '%PLUGIN_ROOT%' — Windows (cmd-style) reference to the Codex plugin install root, used in command_windows values. Comment flags verification on a real Windows Codex client as pending.
keyExports.ClientHookContract: Per-client hook shape: commandForm ('shell-string'|'exec-or-shell'), windowsOverrideField, supportsShellField, projectRootExpr/projectScriptsDir, pluginRootExpr/pluginScriptsDir.
keyExports.ClientId: 'cursor' | 'claude' | 'codex' — same union as PluginClient (plugin-render) and DoctorClient (client-scope).
keyExports.ClientMcpContract: Per-client MCP config shape: format ('json'|'toml'), stdioTypeField ('required'|'optional'|'absent'), projectRootValue.
keyExports.HOOK_ACTIONS: ['boundary-notice', 'stale-graph-notice', 'session-mcp-hint'] — hook actions the client dispatcher serves.
keyExports.hookDispatcherPath: Builds the dispatcher file path as the client addresses it for a given HookScope ('project'|'plugin'); throws if the client defines no plugin install root and scope is 'plugin'.
keyExports.shellHookCommand: Builds the full shell invocation string: `node "<dispatcherPath>" <action> <client>`.

assumptions: ClientId ('cursor'|'claude'|'codex') is duplicated as PluginClient in plugin-render and DoctorClient in client-scope; adding a client means updating all three unions plus a new CLIENT_CAPABILITIES entry.

hookDispatcherPath requires pluginRootExpr to be set on a client's ClientHookContract before that client can be invoked with HookScope 'plugin'; a client with pluginRootExpr null is restricted to scope 'project'.
risks: CODEX_WINDOWS_PLUGIN_ROOT_REF's interpolation syntax is explicitly unverified on a real Windows Codex client per the source comment.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/cli/dispatcher — imports CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME to compose hookDispatcherPath.

annotation.summary: Decides which AI client surfaces the repovine doctor inspects. Detects Cursor, Claude and Codex by looking for the repovine server entry in each client's MCP config, resolves an explicit --client choice or the auto default, and reports which surfaces are in scope plus whether AGENTS.md checks apply. Reviewed against current source: 8-export surface unchanged from the prior note.

keyExports.DOCTOR_CLIENT_MCP_LABEL: Display labels for each client's MCP config location.
keyExports.DoctorClient: The supported client ids: cursor, claude, codex.
keyExports.ResolvedDoctorClients: The resolution outcome: the clients to check, the scope that produced them, and what was detected.
keyExports.describeDoctorClientScope: Human-readable scope line for doctor output.
keyExports.detectConfiguredDoctorClients: Scans the Cursor, Claude and Codex MCP configs for a repovine server entry.
keyExports.resolveDoctorClients: Resolves auto to the detected clients (or all three when none are detected), and an explicit scope to itself.
keyExports.scopeUsesAgentsMd: True when the active scope includes a client that reads AGENTS.md.

assumptions: The repo root is the workspace holding the client config directories.
JSON clients use the mcpServers object shape; Codex uses a TOML section marker.
A client whose config exists but omits the repovine entry counts as not configured.

sideEffects.description: reads the Cursor, Claude and Codex MCP config files under the repo root

risks: A non-standard MCP config shape is skipped as 'not configured', so doctor silently narrows its scope rather than warning about a config it could not parse.

risks.text: Callers must distinguish the detected list from the resolved client list; under auto with nothing detected the resolution widens to all three, so a non-empty client list is not evidence any client is actually configured.

patterns: Auto scope widens rather than fails: no detection means check everything.
invariants: Auto scope expands to all three clients when none are detected.
A scope including Codex or Claude implies the AGENTS.md doctor checks run.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the doctor paths in the repovine CLI agent-doctor and health commands; the config shapes it detects are written by mod:repovine/src/cli/merge-config.
annotation.dataFlow: repo root → scan the client MCP configs for a repovine server entry → detected clients → resolveDoctorClients against the requested scope → client list plus the AGENTS.md flag for doctor.

annotation.summary: Canonical registry of onboarding topics that every supported client surface must carry. Each topic has a stable id, one or more case-insensitive marker strings used by the doctor, and prose explaining the user-visible cost when the topic is absent.

keyExports.ClientTopic: Stable topic id, marker alternatives, and the diagnostic rationale.
keyExports.REQUIRED_CLIENT_TOPICS: Pinned cross-client topic floor consumed by the agent-asset doctor and its totality law.

assumptions: A topic is covered when any one of its markers occurs across the concatenated managed assets for that client.
Markers are diagnostic witnesses, not parsers of the surrounding prose.
risks: Substring markers can produce a false positive when a token appears in unrelated prose; the totality law proves marker removal is detectable, not semantic equivalence of arbitrary wording.
patterns: Keep cross-client obligations in one registry and let each client satisfy them through its own file layout.
invariants: Every topic has a non-empty id, at least one non-empty marker, and a non-empty rationale.
The registry stays client-neutral; client-specific file discovery belongs to managed-setup-assets and agent-doctor.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-doctor; guarded by test/laws/client-topic-totality.test.ts; marker-bearing prose originates in mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets.
annotation.dataFlow: canonical onboarding prose → per-client managed assets → concatenated client surface → REQUIRED_CLIENT_TOPICS marker scan → topic-not-covered findings.

annotation.summary: CLI-only Delivery Protocol surface (`repovine delivery <cmd>`) for harness/CI: file-in / JSON-out. Bare `delivery` (or a lone flag such as `--schemas`) prints the DeliveryProtocol descriptor; `--help` prints usage. The switch serves manifests, run-brief, validate-assignment, validate-result, validate-review-input, and compliance. General agent utilities (roles, orient, session-quality) live in the sibling `repovine agents` surface.

keyExports.runDeliveryCli: Dispatches the delivery subcommands and the bare-descriptor path, returning the process exit code. No subcommand (or a leading flag) prints buildDeliveryProtocol(), adding AGENT_JSON_SCHEMAS with --schemas; the switch handles manifests/run-brief/validate-*/compliance.

assumptions: JSON stays on stdout and progress on stderr so callers can parse the contract.
Schema-only commands (descriptor, manifests, run-brief, validate-*) never build a graph; only compliance does.
DELIVERY_PROTOCOL_CLI_COMMANDS lists every command this dispatcher serves; a law test asserts the descriptor and the switch stay in lockstep.
compliance resolves the run's manifest from --manifest, else the assignment role, and passes the required fields and read-only flag to the role-agnostic validator.

sideEffects.description: reads the assignment/result/review-input JSON files given as arguments
writes JSON results, with progress on the error stream
builds a graph on a thread pool for the compliance command
redirects the pipeline log sink to the error stream on entry and again before a build

risks: The compliance command can pay full cold-build cost.
An unrecognised --manifest name falls back to weaker default requirements.

risks.text: Adding or renaming a subcommand here without updating DELIVERY_PROTOCOL_CLI_COMMANDS breaks the descriptor-vs-dispatcher law test.

patterns: Bare command is the descriptor; subcommands are protocol I/O — the no-subcommand path is handled before the switch.
Output stream for the contract, error stream for everything else, keeping the surface pipe-safe.
invariants: The output stream carries only JSON.
Only the compliance command builds a graph.
Schema and compliance validation failures exit non-zero.
annotation.integrationPoints: Descriptor and manifests from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol and mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests; validation and the compliance gate from mod:repovine/src/agents/validation; the pre-run brief from mod:repovine/src/cli/run-brief; the graph for compliance from mod:repovine/src/mcp/context; shared JSON/flag helpers and the env shape from mod:repovine/src/cli/agents-shared. Dispatched from mod:repovine/src/mcp/index on `repovine delivery`; the JSON shapes are consumed by the harness wrapper.
annotation.dataFlow: argv[0] = subcommand (or the descriptor when absent/a flag) -> optional JSON file reads -> schema check or graph-backed compliance -> JSON on stdout; exit code gates the validated operations.

annotation.summary: Loader for the shipped client hook dispatcher: reads the standalone ESM file repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs that setup copies verbatim into client hook directories and plugin bundles, using a URL-relative read so it resolves next to this module in both src/ (tests) and dist/ (runtime build copies the .mjs alongside).

keyExports.CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME: 'repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs' — file name of the dispatcher in every client hooks directory and plugin bundle.
keyExports.readClientDispatcherSource: Reads and returns the dispatcher's source bytes (LF) from the file shipped beside this module via fs.readFileSync + import.meta.url.

assumptions: repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs is physically present next to this module's compiled output (dist/cli/dispatcher/) — the build step must copy it there or the read throws.

sideEffects.description: fs.readFileSync of repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs resolved via import.meta.url

annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/cli/client-capabilities imports CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME to build hookDispatcherPath/shellHookCommand for setup, clear, and health across clients.

annotation.summary: Identity predicates that let setup (dedupe on re-run) and clear (removal) recognize repovine-managed hook entries in client configs by their dispatcher-invocation shape, so user-defined hooks — including exec-form hooks that happen to run plain `node` — are never matched.

keyExports.isManagedClaudeHook: True for Claude exec-form dispatcher hooks: command === 'node', args is an array, and args[0] is a string containing CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME. command === 'node' alone never matches.
keyExports.isManagedCursorHookCommand: True when a Cursor shell-string command contains CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME.

annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/cli/dispatcher — imports CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME as the match token for both predicates.

annotation.summary: Walks the user through the domain suggestions a build produced, one at a time, and applies the decisions. Each suggestion can be accepted, kept, hidden or the walk abandoned; what a decision changes depends on which it is.

keyExports.DomainsAdvisorCliResult: Those counts plus whether anything was written and where the backup went.
keyExports.runDomainsAdvisorAfterBuild: Runs the walk and reports what was accepted, kept, hidden and left pending.

assumptions: The four decisions land in two different places: accepting or keeping writes the committed domain configuration, while hiding records the suggestion locally so it stops resurfacing without the repository ever learning about it.
Keeping is offered only for the infrastructure-noise suggestions, since it means committing a marker that deliberately keeps a resource visible; it makes no sense for the other kinds.
A non-interactive run applies nothing and leaves every suggestion pending, for an agent to review as a structured diff through the tool instead.
The committed file is backed up once before either kind of write, and both sets of decisions are layered onto the same copy so a single run produces a single rewrite.
Abandoning the walk leaves the remaining suggestions pending rather than treating silence as a decision.
Verified 2026-07-23: runDomainsAdvisorAfterBuild signature and imports (stage2/domains-advisor, mcp/onboarding-state, cli/prompt, cli/ui) unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: backs up and rewrites the committed domain configuration when suggestions are accepted or kept
prints each suggestion and the outcome

risks: Accepting changes domain tagging for the whole repository, so a decision made per suggestion has repository-wide effect and the backup is the only way back.

Hidden suggestions live only in the untracked local state, so clearing the cache brings every one of them back while accepted and kept decisions persist — the two kinds of decision have very different durability.
Nothing re-validates the resulting configuration here; a suggestion accepted against a stale build writes an exclusion for a shape that may no longer exist.
patterns: Two destinations, one prompt: what the repository should agree on is committed, what one person chose to ignore stays local.
Nothing applies without an explicit answer, in either the interactive or the tool-driven path.
annotation.flowDescription: Post-build hook → runDomainsAdvisorAfterBuild reads graph + domains config → prints/returns DomainsAdvisorCliResult.
invariants: Suggestions never apply without confirmation.
The committed configuration is backed up before it is overwritten.
Declined identifiers never reach the committed file.
Unanswered suggestions remain pending.
annotation.integrationPoints: The suggestions and the functions that apply them come from mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-advisor; the declined set is read and written through mod:repovine/src/mcp/onboarding-state; the configuration path from mod:repovine/src/paths; prompting from mod:repovine/src/cli/prompt. Invoked after a build by the setup path.
annotation.stateShape: DomainsAdvisorCliResult tracks suggestion counts and whether config was applied or declined.
annotation.dataFlow: suggestions on the built state → per-suggestion decision → accepted and kept layered onto one backed-up copy of the committed configuration → hidden ids merged into the local advisory state → counts returned.

annotation.summary: EOL detection/normalization helpers for comparing and writing managed files: templates are LF constants but user checkouts may be CRLF (core.autocrlf), so compares normalize to LF and writes restore the file's dominant EOL.

keyExports.applyEol: Normalizes content to LF first, then converts to the target eol if it is CRLF — never double-converts.
keyExports.detectEol: Returns the dominant EOL of content by counting CRLF vs total LF; ties/none default to '\n'.
keyExports.isUniformEol: True when every newline in content shares one form (all CRLF or all lone LF) or there are none; mixed-EOL files fail and callers must fall back to byte-exact handling.

assumptions: Callers that need lossless round-tripping on mixed-EOL files must check isUniformEol first and take a byte-exact path when it is false.

annotation.summary: Read-only CLI health surface. repovine doctor accepts an optional explicit client scope, diagnoses repo/global MCP setup, snapshot/cache state, annotation health, managed asset projections, boundary delivery, and platform prerequisites; repovine status reports graph and annotation coverage.

keyExports.globalMcpFindings: Explains which client configs were actually read before declaring the scoped global-MCP sweep clean.
keyExports.inspectGlobalMcpConfigs: Reads only the user configs for clients in the resolved doctor scope.
keyExports.runDoctorCli: Parses --json and --client cursor|claude|codex|all, runs scoped diagnostics, prints human or JSON output, and returns the diagnostic exit code.
keyExports.runStatusCli: Reports graph, cache, MCP setup, annotations, and client setup projections.

assumptions: Doctor is diagnosis-only; setup, refresh, annotation tools, or user configuration perform remediation.
Client scope is auto-detected unless --client selects cursor, claude, codex, or all.
An empty global-MCP finding is scoped to the client configs that were opened and must not claim all clients were checked.
Boundary hook scripts and the boundary index carry compatible schema versions when setup is current.

Platform report's external-toolchain check is plugin-driven: pluginRuntimeReports() asks every registered source plugin for its requires.runtime and available() probe, replacing a hardcoded Python-only detectPython() check — a language gets a platform row only if its plugin declares a runtime prerequisite.

sideEffects.description: reads MCP configs, managed projections, AGENTS.md, cache artifacts, annotation state, boundary-index files, hook scripts, and platform state

risks: Auto-detection can intentionally choose a narrower client set than a multi-client repository owner expects; use --client all for a complete three-client sweep.
A stale graph or boundary index can make health output describe an earlier repository revision.

risks.text: Boundary index schema mismatch silences boundary advisories until setup is rerun; callers consuming doctor output must preserve the warning.

patterns: Structured findings feed both human rows and --json output.
Argument validation rejects unknown, missing, or duplicate client scopes before any diagnosis.
Clean summaries name their evidence boundary instead of implying unread configs were checked.
invariants: Doctor and status never repair repository files.
Only accepted client scope values reach client resolution.
A file missing on disk is reported by the asset doctor but is not counted as scanned.
JSON and human output are projections of the same diagnostic state.
annotation.integrationPoints: Uses mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-doctor for asset diagnostics, mod:repovine/src/cli/client-scope for detection, mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance and backlog for note health, mod:repovine/src/mcp/context and boundary-index for graph state, mod:repovine/src/plugin-host/source-set for the registered plugin list backing platform runtime checks, and mod:repovine/src/cli/ui for output.
annotation.dataFlow: argv → option validation and client resolution → scoped filesystem/runtime inspections → annotation, asset, MCP, boundary, and platform findings (platform now iterating getSourcePlugins() for toolchain probes) → JSON or human rendering → exit code.

envDependencies.WINDIR: On Windows, detectLongPaths uses it to locate System32/reg.exe for the long-paths registry check; it is ignored on other platforms.

annotation.summary: Slim CLI formatter for annotation coverage stats: CompactCoverage type records total/annotated/fresh/stale/unannotated module counts; formatModuleCoverageLine renders one summary line for health/status output.

keyExports.formatModuleCoverageLine: Returns '<fresh>/<totalModules> modules fresh, <unannotated> unannotated, <stale> stale' from a CompactCoverage.

assumptions: Used by CLI health/status paths that print module coverage.
Pure string formatter; callers handle stdout themselves.
risks: Output format is not a stable API; scripts should use JSON flags instead of parsing this line.
patterns: Thin formatter — not a stable API; prefer MCP JSON for automation.
invariants: No I/O — returns a formatted string only.
annotation.integrationPoints: CLI health and annotation coverage reporting commands.
annotation.dataFlow: CompactCoverage counts -> formatModuleCoverageLine -> string for the caller to print.

annotation.summary: Workspace onboarding CLI: inspects workspace support, bootstraps repovine.config.json and annotations file, and renders Cursor/Claude/Codex MCP configs, hooks, skills, and rules from canonical templates.

keyExports.initAll: Bootstrap all supported clients in one pass.
keyExports.inspectWorkspaceSupport: Preflight scan for package markers declared by currently loaded source plugins (packagesByPlugin keyed by pluginId, via currentDirLayoutTable), IaC files, and unsupported/project-signal files; feeds estimateColdBuild for a build-time ETA. Generalized from a hardcoded tsconfig/pyproject.toml check — an ecosystem is recognized as soon as its plugin registers a package marker.
keyExports.runWorkspaceBootstrap: CLI entry for repovine setup/init command.

assumptions: initAll writes Cursor + Claude + Codex projections unless client-specific init called.
replaceMcp overwrites existing MCP server blocks when true.
ensureWorkspaceBootstrap creates repovine.config.json and repovine.annots.json when missing.
Each client hook directory contains one managed repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs; all three hook actions are selected through generated client config rather than separate hook files.
Re-running setup merges current dispatcher registrations idempotently and does not retain duplicate managed hook entries.

WorkspaceSupportInspection.packagesByPlugin replaces the old tsconfigCount/pythonPackageCount fields; estimateColdBuild and formatWorkspaceSupportPreflight key off totalPackageMarkers() (the sum across plugins), not a single language count.

getKnownExtensions now comes from ../plugin-host/source-set.js (the loaded plugin set) rather than a side-effect import of stage1/source/bootstrap.js; nothing needs to be imported purely for registration side effects.

sideEffects.description: Writes client config, hooks, skills, rules, and default repovine.config.json

risks: replaceMcp:true clobbers user MCP customizations.
Cold build recommendation ignored when autoBuild false on large monorepos.
patterns: Idempotent merge for AGENTS.md managed block and hook markers.
annotation.flowDescription: Preflight → confirm (interactive) → bootstrap workspace → per-target MCP JSON + projected agent assets.
invariants: ensureEmptyAnnotationsFile creates repovine.annots.json only when missing, so re-running setup never overwrites accumulated annotation memory.
Setup without a client argument runs the workspace bootstrap alone, writing config and the annotations file and no client projections.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/cli/templates; mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance ensureEmptyAnnotationsFile; mod:repovine/src/config loadConfig; mod:repovine/src/plugin-host/source-set getKnownExtensions.
annotation.dataFlow: cwd + InitOptions → templates from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates and mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets → write .cursor/.claude/.codex files + hooks.

annotation.summary: Builds the list of files setup would write for a given set of clients, each with the exact content it should hold. The doctor check compares what is on disk against this list, so it has to reproduce not only what setup writes but the order in which setup overwrites shared paths.

keyExports.ManagedSetupAsset: One entry: the relative path, the expected content and what kind of asset it is.
keyExports.ManagedSetupAssetKind: The four kinds: agent, skill, rule and the always-on instructions file.
keyExports.SETUP_ALL_MERGE_ORDER: The client order a full setup writes in, which decides who wins a shared path.
keyExports.listCanonicalManagedAssets: The managed files and their expected content for the selected clients.
keyExports.mergeManagedAssetsBySetupOrder: Collapses paths claimed by more than one client the way a full setup would leave them.
keyExports.readManagedFile: Reads a managed file for comparison, returning nothing when it is absent.

assumptions: Two of the three clients project their skills into the same directory, so a full setup necessarily overwrites; the merge here reproduces that rather than reporting a conflict.
Later clients in the order win, because that is the order setup writes and therefore what ends up on disk.
Agent files are obtained by rendering with writing switched off, which is what keeps the expected content identical to what a real setup would produce instead of a second description of it.
That render is done with an empty repository root, which holds because agent target paths do not depend on the root; the always-on file does depend on it and is handled separately with the real one.
Only writable assets enter the manifest, so preview-only output is not compared against disk.
The always-on file is included only when the selected clients actually use it.

sideEffects.description: reads managed files for comparison

risks: The write order is restated here as a literal list rather than derived from the setup path, so changing the order in setup without changing it here makes the doctor expect the wrong content on exactly the paths two clients share — and it reports drift on a correctly set up workspace.
Expected content is produced by rendering, so any render input that varies by environment produces a mismatch the doctor attributes to the file rather than to the render.
A path claimed by no client is simply absent from the manifest, so a file setup once wrote under an older name is never compared and never reported.
patterns: Expected content comes from the same renderer setup uses, so the comparison cannot drift from what is written.
Overwrite semantics are modelled explicitly rather than assumed away, because shared paths are the normal case rather than an error.
invariants: The manifest reflects what a full setup leaves on disk, including which client won each shared path.
Preview-only assets never appear in it.
A missing file reads as absent rather than as empty content.
annotation.integrationPoints: Asset bodies and render helpers come from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; agent previews and the always-on file reconciliation from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-render; the client scope and whether it uses the always-on file from mod:repovine/src/cli/client-scope; the manifest is consumed by the doctor check.
annotation.dataFlow: selected clients -> per-client agent, rule and skill entries -> shared paths collapsed in setup order -> the always-on file appended when in scope -> manifest compared against disk.

annotation.summary: Safe merge of the repovine MCP server entry into a client's existing config. Inspects the target file to classify what is already there (missing, invalid, empty, only-repovine, has-other-servers), resolves that into a write plan (create, merge, replace-all, skip), and applies it with a backup. Handles both JSON clients via an mcpServers key and Codex TOML via an [mcp_servers.repovine] block plus hooks.

keyExports.REPOVINE_MCP_SERVER_NAME: Canonical 'repovine' server key written into client configs.
keyExports.formatMcpPreflight: Plain-text preflight lines describing the file, its current state, and the resolved plan.
keyExports.inspectCodexMcpConfig: Classifies a Codex TOML config as missing | has-repovine | has-other-mcp | no-repovine.
keyExports.inspectMcpJsonConfig: Classifies a JSON MCP config as missing | invalid | empty | only-repovine | has-other-servers.
keyExports.resolveCodexWritePlan: Turns a Codex inspect result plus the replaceMcp flag into a plan with a stated reason.
keyExports.resolveMcpJsonWritePlan: Turns a JSON inspect result plus the replaceMcp flag into a plan with a stated reason.
keyExports.writeCodexMcpConfig: Appends or replaces the [mcp_servers.repovine] block and hooks in Codex TOML.
keyExports.writeMcpJsonConfig: Runs inspect then plan then apply for a JSON client, honouring the confirm callback.

assumptions: The confirmExistingWrite callback comes from interactive init; non-interactive callers must handle a skipped write.
Foreign MCP servers in the target file must survive, so merge is mandatory once inspect reports has-other-servers.

sideEffects.description: reads the client MCP config file during inspect
writes the client MCP config and a backup file when a plan is applied

risks: replace-all is refused while foreign servers exist, leaving the user to reconcile manually.

risks.text: Callers must treat a skipped status as a write that did not happen; the confirm callback returning false is a normal outcome, not an error.
The written server entry is the contract other clients read to launch repovine: the REPOVINE_MCP_SERVER_NAME key and block shape are what an installed client resolves at startup.

patterns: Inspect, then plan with a reason, then apply: the plan is inspectable before any file is touched.
Every destructive path records a backup path in the result.
invariants: A backup path is recorded in the write result whenever an overwrite is planned.
replace-all is chosen only when inspect reports only-repovine or the user confirms.
annotation.integrationPoints: Driven by cli init preflight and writes; mod:repovine/src/cli/templates supplies the server blocks and mod:repovine/src/cli/clear removes the managed blocks. Preflight text is styled by styleMcpPreflight in mod:repovine/src/cli/ui.
annotation.dataFlow: client path + replaceMcp flag → inspect → resolve plan → optional interactive confirm → backup + write → ConfigWriteResult.

annotation.summary: Single source for managed client guidance and agent/skill scaffolds. Named policy fragments compose into canonical assets, then client renderers project them into Cursor rules and agents, Claude skills and agents, Codex TOML, shared AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md regions, and dispatcher hooks; generated copies must be changed here and regenerated.

keyExports.AGENTS: Built-in annotation-writer, repo-explorer, architecture-auditor, and code-reviewer definitions.
keyExports.CURSOR_RULES: Always-on Cursor policy, workflow, and orchestration rules.
keyExports.OnboardingAsset: Canonical asset name, description, body, optional skill body, and per-client model hints.
keyExports.SEARCH_CONTEXT_INTERPRETATION_POLICY: Truthful interpretation of strict, relaxed, weak, semantic-only, truncated, and stale-annotation search results.
keyExports.SHARED_SKILLS: Implementation, review, refresh, status, and annotation skill sources shared across clients.
keyExports.SUBAGENT_ORCHESTRATION_CORE: Client-neutral main-agent delegation policy reused by managed surfaces.
keyExports.renderCodexAgentToml: Renders a Codex agent definition with TOML-safe content.
keyExports.renderProjectSampleSubagentToml: Renders the default project implementer for Codex.
keyExports.renderProjectSubagentTemplateToml: Renders the placeholder Codex specialist template.
keyExports.renderSkillMarkdown: Renders skill frontmatter around an asset body.

assumptions: Guidance fragments are named and composed so one correction reaches every applicable client surface.
Clients differ in model-selection and orchestration affordances; shared prose states only the common contract and client-specific renderers carry the rest.
Tool examples must include accepted scope kinds and required arguments rather than placeholders that the argv/MCP router rejects.
Generated projections are managed artifacts and setup --force may overwrite local edits.
risks: A false statement in shared guidance is multiplied across dozens of managed files and can steer many future agents incorrectly.
Editing a generated projection directly is lost on the next setup render.
The literal scaffold path inventory makes file renames a migration concern for already-onboarded repositories.
Guidance must stay repository-neutral; stack-specific examples can become invalid instructions in consumer workspaces.
patterns: Named policy constants -> canonical asset bodies -> per-client renderers -> managed files.
Claims about response truncation, supported scope kinds, cancellation, annotations, model selection, and IaC identifiers name the exact evidence boundary instead of universal behavior.
Annotation guidance separates content-stale full re-authoring from fresh-note point merges and propagation-only baseline refresh.
annotation.flowDescription: setup/init selects canonical assets, renders each client dialect, writes managed agent/rule/skill/hook files, and doctor later compares those files with the same canonical render.
invariants: repovine.annots.json is changed only through annotation MCP tools.
Only one annotation writer runs at a time because all writers share one store.
Generated client prose never recommends a tool call the corresponding public schema rejects.
The shared orchestration bridge stays client-neutral; client-specific delegation surfaces live in client-specific assets.
Projection changes originate in this module and are followed by setup all regeneration.
annotation.integrationPoints: Rendered by mod:repovine/src/cli/init, managed-setup-assets, agent-render, and plugin-render; manifest identities come from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests; projection snippets are versioned by mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection and audited by mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-doctor plus the client projection suite.
annotation.dataFlow: policy fragments + manifest identities -> canonical asset bodies -> Markdown/TOML/client renderers -> setup/init/plugin bundles -> managed client files -> doctor and projection tests compare against the same source.

annotation.summary: Deterministic orientation: run a search for a natural-language task, pick a scope from what it found, then trace the runtime flow around it -- all without a model. Used to give a harness a factual starting context before any agent runs.

keyExports.OrientReport: The report: the query, whether anything was found, the graph nodes, the traced scope, and both tool summaries.
keyExports.buildOrientReport: Runs the search and the trace for a query and returns the combined report.
keyExports.normalizeOrientQuery: Reduces a harness prompt to the part worth searching for.
keyExports.packageScopeOf: The package a node id belongs to, as a trace scope: pkg: ids read back directly, mod: ids via extractPackageName (not a naive first-slash cut, which would break scoped npm names).

assumptions: Matching is left on the adaptive setting rather than forced strict: it requires every token first and falls back to a bounded any-token match when no single node carries them all. A natural-language task rarely lands every token on one node, and strict matching returns nothing whenever token extraction is even slightly reduced -- so orientation degrades to a looser match instead of orienting to nothing.
Search results are read from the nested match object rather than the outer envelope; reading the envelope yields an empty node list every time regardless of what was found.

The query is normalized first: a prior-run preamble (marked by '## Prior harness run') is stripped, an over-long coordination blob is reduced to its last paragraph, and the result is length-capped to 800 chars.
The trace scope comes from the caller when given, otherwise from the first module or package the search returned.
A fresh runtime is built per invocation rather than reusing a long-lived server, since this runs as a command rather than inside one.
Finding nothing is reported as such; there is no fallback query, because a repository-specific guess would be wrong everywhere else.

sideEffects.description: invokes the search and trace handlers against a freshly built runtime
builds the graph for the repository on each invocation

risks: Every invocation builds the graph from scratch, so orientation costs a full build on a cold cache -- acceptable once per run, expensive if called repeatedly.
The scope for the trace is inferred from the top search hit, so a search that lands on an unrepresentative module traces the wrong area while still reporting success.
Reporting nothing found is honest but indistinguishable from a repository where the search index is thin, since both produce an empty node list.
patterns: Two tools in sequence with no model between them, so the same query always yields the same orientation.
Degrade the match rather than the answer: a looser search beats an empty one.
invariants: No model is involved.
An empty query returns a report saying so rather than searching.
There is no hard-coded fallback query.
annotation.integrationPoints: Exposed through the orient subcommand in mod:repovine/src/cli/agents and called by the harness before a run; the tools are mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/search-context and mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/trace-flow, driven against a runtime from mod:repovine/src/mcp/context; result identifiers are extracted with mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve.
annotation.dataFlow: raw query -> normalized -> search with adaptive matching -> node identifiers from the nested matches -> scope chosen -> trace over services, resources, flows and entrypoints -> one report.

annotation.summary: Generates the distributable plugin repository from the same asset definitions setup uses. For each of the three clients it writes a bundle and a marketplace manifest, pins the server invocation to the engine's current version, and adds the shared licence and readme. The output directory is a separate repository, so the render clears its own previous output and leaves that repository's own files alone.

keyExports.REPOVINE_PLUGIN_REPOSITORY: Where the rendered bundles are published.
keyExports.RenderPluginRepoOptions: Engine root, output root, an optional version override and an optional client subset.
keyExports.RenderPluginRepoResult: Both versions, the roots, the clients rendered, the paths written and the entries cleared.
keyExports.defaultEngineRoot: The engine package root, derived from this module's own file location.
keyExports.defaultOutRoot: The default output root, a sibling of the engine checkout.
keyExports.readEngineVersion: The version from the engine's package manifest, failing loudly when absent.
keyExports.renderPluginRepo: Renders the bundles for the selected clients and reports the version, the paths written and what was cleared.
keyExports.wipePluginOutRoot: Clears prior output: everything unowned on a full render, only the selected clients' entries on a scoped one.

assumptions: A full render clears the output root so an asset dropped from the projection disappears with it; a scoped render touches only the selected clients' own entries, which is what keeps the other bundles installable while one is being reworked.
Hand-placed assets and the output repository's own version-control files are never cleared, because the output root is a real repository rather than a scratch directory.
The server invocation is pinned to an exact engine version in every bundle, so an installed plugin does not silently follow the latest release.
The install instructions share one body with a per-client preamble, so the three cannot drift apart.
The bundles are a projection: a change belongs in the asset definitions, followed by a re-render.

sideEffects.description: clears prior output under outRoot and writes the bundle trees and manifests

risks: A full render deletes everything under the output root except the small preserved set, so pointing it at a directory that holds anything else destroys that content; the default is a dedicated sibling repository for exactly this reason.
The version is read from the engine's package manifest at render time, so rendering from a checkout whose version has not been bumped publishes bundles pinned to the previous release.

Version pinning in the command-line client's configuration works by text substitution on the expected argument form, so a change to how that argument is written leaves the bundle unpinned without failing.
patterns: One asset source, three client dialects: the bundles differ in packaging rather than in content.
Clearing is scoped to what the render is about to rewrite, which is what makes a single-client render safe against a shared publish repository.
annotation.flowDescription: Release packaging pipeline: resolve engineRoot/outRoot and readEngineVersion -> wipePluginOutRoot (full wipe for every client, CLIENT_OWNED_ENTRIES only for a subset; preserve assets/.git/.gitignore) -> for each selected PluginClient render bundle files from onboarding-assets/templates/agent-projection -> emit marketplace index + LICENSE/README -> return RenderPluginRepoResult with paths and projectionVersion stamp.
invariants: Marketplace manifests reference their sources by relative path, which is what the host installers accept.
A bundle carries no project-scoped settings file; its components sit at the plugin root's default locations and its hooks run from the plugin root.
The manifest does not point at the default hook file, because the host loads that file itself and naming it again trips duplicate validation.
The generated documentation keeps installation marketplace-first and does not ask for a separate asset setup afterwards.
Every bundle documents the optional embedding install, because the server starts through the package runner and the embedding package resolves from the workspace rather than from beside the engine.
A scoped render leaves the other clients' bundles and manifests installable.
annotation.integrationPoints: Asset bodies and render helpers come from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets, file contents from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates, the projection version from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection, and the server name used for pinning from mod:repovine/src/cli/merge-config; the result feeds the publish workflow.
annotation.dataFlow: engine root and version -> output root cleared to the render's scope -> per-client bundle files with the version pinned -> marketplace manifests, licence and readme -> report of paths written and entries cleared.

annotation.summary: Synchronous one-line stdin prompt for interactive repovine init/doctor: opens /dev/tty (or CONIN$ on Windows), reads until newline, throws with caller-provided message when no TTY.

keyExports.promptLineSync: Writes prompt to stdout, returns trimmed answer or throws nonTtyMessage.

assumptions: Used only for yes/no or short confirmations in CLI commands.
EAGAIN on non-blocking fd retries with 25ms sleep.

sideEffects.description: readSync from TTY fd until newline
Writes prompt string before read

risks: Hung stdin if user never sends newline.
patterns: Sync TTY read for short confirmations only.
invariants: Throws when stdin is not a TTY — callers must catch in CI.
annotation.integrationPoints: cli/init and merge-config confirmations.
annotation.dataFlow: prompt string → /dev/tty readSync → trimmed answer or throw in non-TTY CI.

annotation.summary: The canonical .gitignore block repovine manages in a workspace: a header comment recording that the annotations file is committed while the engine cache directory is ignored, plus the ignore entry itself. The recognized header and entry sets are what lets the clear command remove exactly the block it wrote.

keyExports.REPOVINE_GITIGNORE_ENTRIES: Entry lines the clear command recognizes as repovine-managed.
keyExports.REPOVINE_GITIGNORE_ENTRY: The ignore entry for the engine cache directory, derived from the artifacts directory name.
keyExports.REPOVINE_GITIGNORE_HEADER: The comment line written by setup.
keyExports.REPOVINE_GITIGNORE_HEADERS: Header lines the clear command recognizes as repovine-managed.
keyExports.formatRepovineGitignoreBlock: Returns the newline-wrapped header and entry ready to append.

assumptions: The entry is derived from the artifacts directory name rather than hardcoded, so renaming the cache directory moves the ignore rule with it.
The recognized sets are kept plural so a previously written header can still be matched after the current wording changes.
risks: A hand-edited header stops matching the recognized set, so the clear command leaves the block behind rather than removing something it no longer recognizes.
patterns: The managed block is identified by exact header and entry membership rather than by parsing, which keeps removal conservative.
invariants: The engine cache directory stays ignored while the annotations file stays committed.
annotation.integrationPoints: The block is appended by the CLI init path and removed by the CLI clear path; the cache directory name comes from mod:repovine/src/paths.
annotation.dataFlow: formatRepovineGitignoreBlock → appended to the workspace .gitignore on init → clear removes the lines matching the recognized header and entry sets.

annotation.summary: Produces the pre-run prompt material a harness gives an agent before it starts. It looks up a built-in capability manifest by explicit name or by role, renders the implementer brief from it, and returns that text alongside the protocol and projection versions it was rendered under. Reachable through the delivery CLI only (subcommand `repovine delivery run-brief`); it is not exposed as a server tool.

keyExports.RunBriefOptions: What the caller may specify: a role, a name, or nothing.
keyExports.RunBriefResult: The rendered brief plus the role, name, protocol version and projection version behind it.
keyExports.buildRunBrief: Resolves the manifest and returns the rendered brief with its versions, or an error object naming what could not be resolved.
keyExports.resolveRunBriefManifest: Looks up the manifest: an explicit name wins, then the role, and with neither the implementer role is assumed.

assumptions: An explicit name takes precedence over a role, so a caller naming an agent gets that agent rather than whatever its role would resolve to.
Omitting both selectors is a supported call, not an error: the implementer role is the default a harness wants.
Both versions travel with the brief so a consumer can tell which protocol and which rendering produced the text it received.
Only built-in manifests are reachable here; there is no lookup path for an externally supplied one.

risks.text: The result is a union rather than a thrown error, so a caller must check for the error member before reading the brief; an unresolved name or role otherwise flows onward as a missing field rather than a failure.

patterns: Resolution and rendering are separate exports, so a caller that only needs to know whether a manifest exists does not render a brief to find out.
annotation.flowDescription: role or name → resolveRunBriefManifest (explicit name, else role, else 'implementer') → renderImplementerBrief(manifest) → RunBriefResult carrying the brief text plus protocolVersion and projectionVersion, or an error object naming the unresolved role/name. No file is written here; this module only resolves and renders text.
invariants: A missing manifest yields an error object rather than an exception.
The returned role and name come from the resolved manifest, not from what the caller asked for.
annotation.integrationPoints: Manifest lookup comes from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests, the role type and protocol version from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol, and both the projection version and the brief renderer from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection. Invoked by the `repovine delivery run-brief` CLI subcommand.
annotation.dataFlow: role or name -> manifest lookup with the implementer default -> brief rendered from the manifest -> result carrying the text and both versions, or an error object.

annotation.summary: The literal file contents setup writes: config and domains scaffolds, per-client launch blocks for the stdio server, the marker-delimited managed block for the always-on file, and the hook wiring each client runs. Everything here is a string, a data row, or a function returning one; writing it to disk belongs to the callers.

keyExports.AGENTS_MD: The managed quick-reference block merged into the always-on file.
keyExports.AGENTS_MD_BEGIN_MARKER: Opening delimiter of the managed block.
keyExports.AGENTS_MD_END_MARKER: Closing delimiter of the managed block.
keyExports.CLAUDE_HOOKS_SETTINGS: Claude hook settings built for the 'project' scope, covering the pre-edit boundary check, the post-edit stale-graph check, and the session-start MCP hint.
keyExports.CLAUDE_MD: The thin pointer file that defers to the always-on file.
keyExports.CODEX_CONFIG_TOML: The full Codex config fragment: server block plus hooks block.
keyExports.CODEX_HOOKS_BEGIN_MARKER: Opening delimiter of the managed hook region in the Codex config.
keyExports.CODEX_HOOKS_BLOCK: The Codex hook registrations, one TOML stanza per row in the internal CODEX_HOOK_ROWS table.
keyExports.CURSOR_HOOKS_SETTINGS: Cursor hook settings built from the internal CURSOR_HOOK_ROWS table.
keyExports.McpLauncher: How the server is launched: a command and its arguments.
keyExports.NPX_LAUNCHER: The default launcher for a published install.
keyExports.REPOVINE_CONFIG_JSON: Default build, server and analyzer configuration for a new workspace.
keyExports.REPOVINE_DOMAINS_JSON: Starter domain configuration: an empty map plus infrastructure excludes.
keyExports.buildClaudeHooksSettings: Builds the Claude hooks settings for a given scope ('project' or 'plugin'); each row spawns node directly against the dispatcher script rather than a shell string.
keyExports.buildClaudeMcpJson: The Claude server entry serialized to its config file.
keyExports.buildClaudeMcpServer: Server entry in the Claude dialect.
keyExports.buildCodexConfigToml: The full Codex config fragment, server block plus hook markers.
keyExports.buildCodexHooksBlock: Renders CODEX_HOOK_ROWS into TOML hook stanzas, including a Windows command_windows alternate per row.
keyExports.buildCodexMcpServerBlock: The Codex server entry as a TOML block.
keyExports.buildCursorHooksSettings: Renders CURSOR_HOOK_ROWS into the Cursor hooks.json shape.
keyExports.buildCursorMcpJson: The Cursor server entry serialized to its config file.
keyExports.buildCursorMcpServer: Server entry in the Cursor dialect.

assumptions: All three clients render hook commands from the same three action names (boundary-notice, stale-graph-notice, session-mcp-hint) declared per event in a client-local ROWS table (CODEX_HOOK_ROWS, CURSOR_HOOK_ROWS, CLAUDE_HOOK_ROWS); only the command shape differs, since Claude spawns node directly with args while Codex and Cursor build a shell command string.
The default configuration must load through the real config loader, which is what the setup tests assert.
Both marker pairs exist so setup can rewrite its own region of a file the user also edits.
