The launcher is a parameter rather than a constant so a local checkout and a published install can share these builders.
Claude's dispatcher path is anchored to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for the 'project' scope or CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT for the 'plugin' scope, per buildClaudeHooksSettings' scope argument.
AGENTS_MD is composed from renderContextQualityGuidance and renderMainDeliveryProtocolSection (mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection).
risks: These strings are copies of contracts owned elsewhere, so a change to the config schema or the server surface leaves them stale with nothing failing until onboarding produces a broken workspace.

The hook scripts resolve the workspace root from the host variable, fall back to the working directory, then walk parents for .repovine, so an unset variable leaves them working. The advisory goes quiet instead when the on-disk boundary index is missing, unparseable, or carries no entry for the edited path.

risks.text: The boundary hook only reports when the on-disk index matches the version it accepts, so an importer changing either side must confirm advisories still fire in a real workspace.

patterns: One source for every client, so onboarding stays consistent and the doctor checks have something to compare against.
Setup is stdio only: the launcher is a command and arguments, with no network transport anywhere in the generated config.
Hook wiring is table-driven: a small ROWS array of event/action pairs per client is mapped through a shared dispatcher command builder, rather than three independent hardcoded scripts.
annotation.flowDescription: Setup/init copies or merges template strings into .cursor, .claude, .codex, repovine.config.json, and repovine.domains.json; the boundary-notice, stale-graph-notice and session-mcp-hint actions are wired per client into CODEX_HOOKS_BLOCK, CURSOR_HOOKS_SETTINGS and CLAUDE_HOOKS_SETTINGS.
invariants: Managed regions are always delimited by their markers so a merge never overwrites user content around them.
The default configuration contains no network listener block.
The default launcher is the published-install form.
extensionPoints: A new client adds its own server builder plus its own ROWS array of event/action pairs.
A new hook action needs a name recognized by the shared HookAction type and by the dispatcher script; adding one to a client's ROWS table is not enough on its own.
annotation.integrationPoints: Written to disk by mod:repovine/src/cli/init, mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-render and mod:repovine/src/cli/plugin-render; the managed protocol section comes from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection; merge and marker semantics live in mod:repovine/src/cli/merge-config; hook command rendering (shellHookCommand, hookDispatcherPath, HookAction) comes from mod:repovine/src/cli/dispatcher; the generated boundary hooks read the index produced by mod:repovine/src/mcp/boundary-index.
annotation.dataFlow: template constants -> init, agent render or plugin render -> client config, hook and managed-block files; at runtime the generated hooks read the boundary index from the local cache directory.

envDependencies.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT: Claude hook dispatcher root when scope is 'plugin'
envDependencies.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: Claude hook dispatcher root when scope is 'project'

annotation.summary: Splits user-facing output from build progress. logCli writes to stdout; logCliError and the pipeline loggers write to stderr, with a settable sink so MCP stdio mode can silence pipeline logs. Also formats package/semantic-embed progress bars and file-result lines for the CLI.

keyExports.formatPackageProgressLine: Renders a per-package build progress bar with elapsed time and RSS
keyExports.formatSemanticEmbedProgressLine: Renders the semantic-embedding pass progress bar (done/total, elapsed)
keyExports.logPipelineProgress: In-place \r with pad/clip/truncate; TTY or setProgressInPlace; else newline logPipeline
keyExports.setPipelineLogSink: Routes pipeline logs to silent sink for MCP stdio mode
keyExports.setProgressInPlace: Force \r progress on piped stderr (Cursor MCP subprocess)
keyExports.styleMcpPreflight: ANSI styling for merge-config preflight lines

assumptions: Node CLI or MCP child with real WriteStreams.
Tests use stripAnsi on styled output.
MCP host pipes stderr (isTTY=false) but still renders \r updates in the log panel.

sideEffects.description: logCli writes user-facing CLI lines to process.stdout
logCliError writes red-styled error lines, and logPipeline/logPipelineProgress/logPipelineWarn write build progress, to process.stderr, including in-place \r rewrites

risks: Silent pipeline sink hides build progress during long graph builds.
Very long progress lines still need clipProgressLine when column count is unknown (default 120).

risks.text: Callers that emit machine-read output on stdout must confirm the pipeline sink is not routing progress there; stdout is the MCP stdio transport.

patterns: Dual sinks: stdout for user-facing CLI, stderr for pipeline/build progress.
MCP refreshPipelineLogSink calls setProgressInPlace when pipeline logs are visible.
invariants: MCP stdio mode must route pipeline logs away from stdout.
setProgressInPlace(true) enables in-place progress when stderr is piped.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage1/index and context.ts call logPipelineProgress; MCP sets setPipelineLogSink('silent').
annotation.dataFlow: logCli/logPipeline → FORCE_COLOR/NO_COLOR + TTY check → ANSI SGR strings → stdout/stderr; pipeline sink routes build progress away from MCP stdio.

envDependencies.COLUMNS: Terminal width for progress line clipping

annotation.summary: The configuration spine. It reads the workspace configuration file, validates it against a schema, and resolves it into a shape where every field is present, filling defaults for whatever was omitted. One resolved object serves the build, the server, the architecture analysis, the annotation propagation policy and the plugin set.

keyExports.DEFAULT_CONTRACT_HUB_THRESHOLDS: When a module counts as a shared contract hub.
keyExports.DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE: How many cards are embedded at a time.
keyExports.DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL: The embedding model, fixed rather than configurable.
keyExports.DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS: The ceiling on a serialized response.
keyExports.DomainStalePolicy: Whether domain staleness follows every tag or only the path tag.
keyExports.MIN_RESPONSE_CHARS: The floor a configured ceiling may not go below.
keyExports.PluginsConfig: Whether the built-ins apply, plus additions and exclusions.
keyExports.PropagationConfig: How annotation staleness propagates: the domain policy, whether package domains queue hard, how far consumer reach walks, and the hub overrides.
keyExports.RepoContextFileConfig: The shape a workspace may actually write.
keyExports.ResolvedConfig: The fully resolved shape, with no optional fields left.
keyExports.loadConfig: Reads and resolves the configuration from a directory.

assumptions: Unknown keys are stripped but reported: a typo produces a warning naming the path rather than being silently ignored, which is the difference between a setting that did not apply and one nobody noticed.
Every field is optional with a default, so a missing or empty configuration is a supported state rather than an error.

The response ceiling is empirically derived rather than round: it is set below the point where a dense response exceeds a host's context budget, with margin, because dense structured text tokenizes far denser than prose.
An environment override is applied only when it parses and clears the floor; otherwise the configured value stands and a warning explains why.
The embedding model is deliberately not configurable, since the index and the model have to agree.
There is no network transport in the configuration shape; the server speaks over standard streams only.
There is no migration path, which is why new fields must be optional and defaulted rather than breaking.

An `agents` key is accepted as an unvalidated record so zod stops stripping/warning on it; the Delivery Protocol layer (mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol, mod:repovine/src/agents/roles-source) validates its own role internals from the raw file rather than through this schema.

sideEffects.description: reads the configuration file from the given directory

risks: A schema-invalid configuration is discarded whole rather than repaired: the load warns, then resolves as if the file were absent. One bad value drops every valid sibling setting in the same file, and the build proceeds on defaults with nothing but a warning line to say so.
Turning the plugin defaults off leaves an empty registry, so a configuration that does so without supplying replacements yields an empty graph.
Environment overrides win over the file, so a workspace can behave differently from its committed configuration.
patterns: One resolved object for every consumer, so no component reads the file itself or reimplements a default.
Validate, warn, then resolve: unknown input is surfaced before it is discarded.
annotation.flowDescription: Single configuration spine for CLI, MCP, graph build, architecture analysis strictness, and context-session quality gates.
invariants: A resolved configuration has no absent fields.
A configured response ceiling never falls below the floor.
The configuration shape contains no network listener.
annotation.integrationPoints: Architecture thresholds are resolved through mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/config; the context-quality defaults come from mod:repovine/src/context-quality/session-store; scan patterns from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters; workspace path safety from mod:repovine/src/paths; warnings are reported through mod:repovine/src/cli/ui. The resolved object is consumed by the build stages and the server runtime.
annotation.dataFlow: configuration file -> schema validation with unknown keys reported -> defaults filled -> environment overrides applied where valid -> one resolved configuration used by the build, the server, the analysis and the annotation policy.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_ANNOTATIONS_FILE: Overrides the annotations file path after a safety check
envDependencies.REPOVINE_MCP_MAX_CHARS: Overrides the response ceiling when it parses and clears the floor
envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Enables verbose server and pipeline logging

annotation.summary: Turns one scored MCP tool response into the event the context-quality session store records. Echoes back only a whitelisted set of request fields, measures the response size, and derives the per-event metrics the scoring uses: whether a search fell back to OR, how export-symbol-dominated a response was, which stable anchor it established, whether a dependency query asked for impact, and whether the result leaned on test packages.

keyExports.BuildContextEventInput: The inputs: sequence number, tool name, arguments, parsed result, response text, and the two configured thresholds.
keyExports.buildContextEvent: Builds the event: whitelisted request echo, response size, and the derived metrics.

assumptions: The request echo is a whitelist of structural argument names, so annotation bodies and merge payloads stay out of the session record. Free-form arguments on the list — the search query and the body grep pattern — are copied verbatim and persisted with every recorded call.
The flood ratio and the recovery window come from configuration rather than being fixed here, so calibration is a config change.
A stable anchor is recorded only for the navigation tools and only when the response's confidence and scope kind make it anchor-eligible.
risks: Flood detection is a ratio heuristic over a search's returned page, so a legitimately broad search can be flagged as export-symbol dominated.
OR-search recovery is measured within a configured window, so mis-tuning that window shifts the noise penalty in both directions.
Metrics are derived from the parsed result envelope, so a tool whose envelope shape changes stops contributing its metrics without any error.
patterns: A capability-dominant search is recognized by the ratio of export symbols in the response rather than by the query text.
Empty results are scored by why they were empty: the diagnostic reason and an unresolved scope drive the low-confidence penalty.
invariants: Metrics come from the parsed result envelope, not from raw transport bytes alone.
The request echo is a whitelist, so a new argument is absent from events until it is explicitly added.
annotation.integrationPoints: Events are appended by the session store in mod:repovine/src/context-quality/session-store and read back when a session quality report is produced; the event and metric shapes come from mod:repovine/src/context-quality/types.
annotation.dataFlow: MCP tool result and response text → buildContextEvent → event appended to the session → session quality report.

annotation.summary: Stores context-quality sessions, rolls MCP responses into aggregates, persists compact session state, and produces the advisory ContextQualityReport. After D5 falsification the shipped default overall is the observable inspect_node baseline (1 after any inspect, otherwise 0); the former multi-signal weights remain configurable only for experiments, while aggregates and rejectReasons remain fully reported.

keyExports.ContextSessionStore: The store: records tool calls, produces reports, consumes or purges sessions, and optionally persists them.
keyExports.DEFAULT_CONTEXT_QUALITY_CONFIG: Fallback weights, thresholds and enforcement mode when the workspace config omits them.
keyExports.GetContextQualityReportOptions: Report options, including whether reading the report consumes the session.
keyExports.RecordToolCallInput: One recorded call: session id, tool, arguments, parsed result and response text.
keyExports.ResolvedContextSessionPolicy: The effective policy: phase, mode, thresholds, minimum anchors, byte budget, and whether the session is required and retained.
keyExports.bootstrapContextSessionsOnMcpStart: Purges stale session files at server start when the workspace asks for it.
keyExports.calculateReport: Builds the report: score, noise penalty, structure bonus, anchors, reject reasons and follow-ups.
keyExports.resolveContextSessionPolicy: Merges the per-assignment policy over the workspace defaults for the active phase.

assumptions: A session is identified by the id the caller passes on each MCP call, so a run that omits or rotates it fragments its own record.
Stable anchors are recorded as graph ids and remain provenance evidence independently of the advisory overall score.
Non-default context-quality weights are experimental until a labelled corpus meets the documented AUC, false-reject, and false-accept return bar.
Persistence is unconditional for calls carrying a session id; configuration controls event detail, retention, and purge behavior.

sideEffects.description: loads persisted sessions from the engine cache directory
persists a compact session form and removes files on purge or consume
holds the per-process session map

risks: A scope that does not resolve to graph nodes cannot establish stable anchors, so a session over off-graph work fails the anchor requirement for a structural reason rather than because the work was poor; the reject reason names the missing anchors, not the real cause.
Rotating session ids without purging accumulates session files in the cache directory.
A mis-tuned byte budget or anchor minimum turns the gate into a source of false rejections in enforcing mode.
patterns: An in-process map with optional compact persistence: the harness expects one stable session id per run rather than durable cross-run history.
A recovery discount applies when a weak search is followed by a narrowing call within the configured window, so the score measures the trajectory rather than a single bad query.
invariants: With the shipped default weights, overall is 1 exactly when inspectCallCount is non-zero and 0 otherwise.
Reject reasons and aggregate diagnostics remain available even though compliance does not hard-gate the unvalidated score.
A report carrying reject reasons never sets acceptHandoff=true.
The assignment policy is merged over workspace defaults, never the other way round.
Anchors are recorded as graph ids, so provenance checks compare like with like.
annotation.integrationPoints: Events are built by mod:repovine/src/context-quality/metrics and typed by mod:repovine/src/context-quality/types; the MCP layer records every scored call here, the annotation write path checks provenance against the recorded anchors, and the compliance check reads the resulting report.
annotation.stateShape: ContextSessionStore holds Map<sessionId, ContextSession> with rolling aggregates and optional requestEchoes.
annotation.dataFlow: contextSessionId on MCP calls -> response-derived events -> persisted aggregates and anchors -> binary default overall plus full rejectReasons/followups -> advisory MCP/CLI/compliance report.

annotation.summary: Type-only contracts for MCP context-quality scoring and Agent Protocol handoff gates: session lifecycle (ContextSession, ContextEvent), per-tool metrics (ContextEventMetrics), weighted noise/structure scoring (ContextQualityWeights), phase-specific thresholds, enforcement modes (harness vs client), and the ContextQualityReport consumed by get_context_session_quality and compliance validators.

keyExports.ContextPhase: explore | implement | annotate — drives per-phase threshold lookup.
keyExports.ContextQualityConfig: Repo defaults: weights, thresholds per phase, recoveryWindow, exportSymbolFloodRatio, purgeSessionsOnMcpStart.
keyExports.ContextQualityReport: Handoff verdict: overall score, acceptHandoff, rejectReasons, aggregates.stableAnchors.
keyExports.ContextRejectReason: Stable reject codes including NO_RECORDED_EVENTS, NO_STABLE_ANCHORS, CAPABILITY_FLOOD.
keyExports.ContextSessionPolicy: Per-assignment overrides: required, mode, phase, thresholds, minAnchors, byteBudget, retain.

assumptions: Consumers are session-store, metrics, MCP middleware, and harness compliance — no runtime logic here.
Reject reason string literals are part of the stable harness API.
ContextSessionPolicy.assignmentScope filters which graph nodes count as stable anchors.
risks: Schema drift vs repovine.config contextQuality JSON breaks policy resolution at MCP startup.
New ContextRejectReason values require harness validator updates.
patterns: Phase-specific thresholds in ContextQualityConfig.thresholds mirror repovine.config contextQuality section.
invariants: Session ids are opaque strings; metrics store scope kinds/ids, not source code.
ContextRequestEcho stores whitelisted request fields only.
annotation.integrationPoints: session-store, metrics, repovine.config contextQuality, Agent Protocol contextSessionId.
annotation.dataFlow: Config + assignment policy types → session-store scoring → ContextQualityReport → harness compliance and client warnings.

annotation.summary: A development script that builds the graph and serializes a readable projection of it to the cache directory, in one or both of two formats. It exists so the graph can be inspected as a file rather than through the tools, which is what makes a structural regression visible in a diff.
assumptions: The serialized form is a trimmed projection rather than the graph itself: domains, a legacy services list (runtime-resource id/label/handler), and packages → modules, each module carrying identity, file, domains, imports and a flattened view of its exports, with optional route, environment and conditional-render detail.

The top-level dump also carries optional extensions (namespaced plugin contributions with provenance, from graph/build-artifact) and refusals (snapshot.buildRefusals combined with stage-2 composed refusals); both keys are omitted from the file when empty.
Export detail is gathered by walking the export children of each module node, so the dump reflects what the graph holds rather than re-reading source.
Command-line flags select the format; with neither, both are written.
Output goes to the cache directory, which is untracked, so a dump never enters the working tree by accident.
It runs at module top level and exports nothing; it is invoked directly.

sideEffects.description: scans the repository through the first stage
writes the serialized graph to the cache directory
prints progress

risks: The dump contains the full structure of the analyzed repository — paths, module names, exported symbols — so a copy moved out of the untracked cache discloses the shape of a private codebase.
On a large repository the serialized output reaches multiple megabytes, which is fine as a file and unwieldy as anything else.
It rebuilds from scratch every run rather than reading an existing snapshot, so it costs a full cold build each time.
patterns: A file-shaped view of the graph, which is what lets a structural change be reviewed as a diff rather than inspected node by node.
annotation.flowDescription: Top-level CLI script: argv flags → collectRepositoryFactsAsync → composeRepositoryGraph → buildDump → write graph.yaml/json under .repovine/.cache.
invariants: It is not part of the server runtime or any published entry point.
It exports nothing.
Output is confined to the cache directory.
extensionPoints: A new node field worth reviewing is added to the projection so it appears in the dump.
annotation.integrationPoints: Builds through mod:repovine/src/stage1 and mod:repovine/src/stage2, walks the result with mod:repovine/src/graph, and resolves locations through mod:repovine/src/paths; the record shapes come from mod:repovine/src/types; extensions come from mod:repovine/src/graph/build-artifact and refusals combine snapshot.buildRefusals with stage-2's getComposedRefusals.
annotation.dataFlow: flags → first-stage snapshot → second-stage graph → trimmed per-module projection plus domains/services/extensions/refusals → one or both serialized files in the cache directory.

annotation.summary: Crash-atomic, power-loss-durable filesystem writers: async/sync writeFileAtomic use per-write PID+UUID temp files (write → fsync → rename → dir fsync), while writeJsonObjectStreamed emits one large JSON field in batches without a full in-memory stringify. The streamed path loops on bytesWritten so a short write never publishes truncated JSON, and directory fsync is fail-closed. writeFileAtomic/writeFileAtomicSync additionally retry the final rename on win32-only transient errors (EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY), up to 10 attempts with linear backoff (15ms * attempt).

keyExports.StreamedJsonField: Describes one large JSON object field streamed as array or record members.
keyExports.writeFileAtomic: Async atomic write: mkdir, temp write, fsync, rename, cleanup on failure.
keyExports.writeFileAtomicSync: Sync variant used on hot paths like annotation serialize.
keyExports.writeJsonObjectStreamed: Streams one large array/record field in byte batches; returns the byte count written.

assumptions: Same-directory temp file (.tmp.<pid>.<random>) + fsync + rename gives crash safety on the local filesystem.
The directory-open fd used for directory fsync exists on POSIX; Windows cannot open a directory this way.
Rename retry (renameWithRetry/renameWithRetrySync) only engages on process.platform === 'win32'; the same errno on POSIX is a real permission failure and is not retried.
EXDEV is deliberately excluded from the retry code set: the temp file lives in the target's directory, so cross-device rename cannot occur.

sideEffects.description: mkdir, temp write, fsync, rename, parent-directory fsync; rm temp on failure
opens the parent directory read-only to fsync it

risks: The streamed writer must loop until the whole chunk lands (write(2) may persist fewer bytes on ENOSPC / network FS) — counting intended bytes instead publishes a truncated, unparseable cache.

Directory fsync is fail-closed: the open() errno tolerance is platform-gated (EISDIR/EPERM tolerated ONLY on win32); the same errno on POSIX, every other errno, an unknown code, and a no-code exception rethrow, so a real fd-exhaustion / disk error surfaces rather than silently dropping durability.
writeJsonObjectStreamed's final rename calls fsPromises.rename directly, not renameWithRetry — it does not get the win32 transient-rename retry that writeFileAtomic/writeFileAtomicSync have.
patterns: Crash-safe persistence primitive for .repovine cache and repovine.annots.json.
invariants: Temp files use .tmp.<pid>.<random> suffix beside target path.
Parent directory fsynced after rename on supporting platforms.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used by mod:repovine/src/stage1/cache, mod:repovine/src/semantic/store, and mod:repovine/src/annotations/store for disk persistence.
annotation.dataFlow: snapshot/cache/semantic-index/annotation writers → writeFileAtomic|writeFileAtomicSync|writeJsonObjectStreamed → temp path → fsync → rename to final path → parent-dir fsync.

annotation.summary: Path containment primitives shared by every surface that must keep a read inside the repository root. Two rules are kept separate on purpose: a lexical rule that judges the name a path spells, and a symlink-resolving rule that judges the bytes the path would actually yield. Only node builtins are imported, so the module has no load-time side effects and can be pulled in from any layer.

keyExports.isLexicallyInsideRepo: Name-only containment; suits labels and cheap pre-filters, and never touches the filesystem.
keyExports.isPathInsideRepo: Read guard: the path clears the lexical test and its realpath resolves inside the resolved root.

assumptions: A relative filePath is meant relative to repoRoot, not to the process working directory.
A target that cannot be resolved yields no bytes, so it keeps the lexical verdict and the caller's own read reports the errno.
Comparison is case-sensitive, matching the rest of the engine's security-sensitive path handling.

sideEffects.description: isPathInsideRepo resolves both the target and the root through realpathSync

risks.text: isLexicallyInsideRepo is a label, not a guard: it accepts a symlink that resolves out of the repository. A caller about to read bytes wants isPathInsideRepo.

risks: The guard resolves the path and the caller reads it separately, so a target replaced between the two calls is read as the caller found it.
Hard links are invisible to realpath, so a hard link to an out-of-repo file reads as contained.
patterns: The lexical test runs first, so an obviously outside path is refused without any filesystem work.
Both rules share one relative-escape predicate, so a name that leaves the base is judged identically everywhere.
invariants: A path whose realpath resolves outside the resolved root is never reported as contained.
The root itself is contained.
annotation.integrationPoints: Guards the MCP source-body reads in mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/node-body and the brief-path validation in mod:repovine/src/agents/roles-source.
annotation.dataFlow: repoRoot + filePath -> resolve against the root -> relative-escape test -> realpath both ends -> contained or not.

annotation.summary: One-line-per-entry JSON serializer for .repovine/ cache files whose bulk is a single keyed map, mirroring the annotations file layout (serializeAnnotationFileFromRaw) so a changed entry is a one-line diff rather than a moved block.

keyExports.serializeKeyedRecordFile: (header, mapKey, entries) => string. Emits scalar header fields in insertion order, then one sorted-by-key line per map entry as `    "key": <compact-json>`. A value that stringifies to undefined is written as null. Output always ends with a trailing newline.

invariants: Entry keys (ids) are always sorted before serialization, so identical input produces byte-identical output regardless of insertion order.

annotation.summary: One-line re-export facade: forwards readDirSorted from @repovine/plugin-sdk so engine callers outside the discovery walk (build fingerprint, threshold groups) read directory entries in the same platform-independent order.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates entirely to mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk (readDirSorted), which lives beside the SDK's discovery walk so insertion order (not host filesystem order) drives node ordering.

annotation.summary: In-memory RepositoryGraph utilities and MCP projection: containment/link queries, capped/deduplicated NodeView links, breadcrumbs, bounded impact traversal with one-hop reexports, import closure, and stats. Also re-exports the validated mutation surface (graph/mutate: addNode/addEdge) and graph/node-ids helpers through the same barrel.

keyExports.MAX_NODE_VIEW_LINKS: Maximum unique links embedded in a single NodeView response.
keyExports.buildNodeView: Projects a node with children and at most MAX_NODE_VIEW_LINKS unique relation/target links, reporting total when capped.
keyExports.forwardImportClosure: BFS over import edges from a start module up to maxDepth.
keyExports.getImpact: Bounded impact BFS that includes a re-export target but does not expand through a node reached only by reexports.
keyExports.getLinks: Returns the complete non-contains outbound edge list; response capping happens only in buildNodeView.
keyExports.graphStats: Counts nodes/edges and their types/kinds for refresh deltas.
keyExports.pathFromRoot: Builds ancestor NodeView breadcrumbs to a focus node.

assumptions: Per MCP refresh cycle RepositoryGraph is the authoritative snapshot for tool responses.
buildNodeView levelMap: root=0, package/runtime-resource/domain=1, module/template=2, export-symbol=3.
getImpact downstream follows inEdges (importers), upstream follows outEdges.
risks: getImpact maxDepth and the one-hop reexport rule intentionally omit distant transitive consumers.
Capped NodeView links require analyze_dependencies or trace_flow when complete traversal is needed.
Mutable addNode/addEdge (owned by graph/mutate, re-exported through this barrel) are intended only for graph construction, not for MCP-facing read paths.
patterns: graph/index barrel re-exports addNode/addEdge and applyValidated/validateGraphDelta/emptyGraphDelta from graph/mutate and graph/delta, and owningModuleId from graph/node-ids — none of those are this file's own declarations.
invariants: getChildren follows contains edges only.
getLinks remains complete and exposes tagSource on tagged edges.
buildNodeView preserves first-seen link order while deduplicating relation+target and caps only the response projection.
A node reached through reexports is included in impact but not recursively expanded unless another non-reexport path reaches it.
Edge validation, endpoint checks, and build-time dedup remain in graph/delta applyValidated.
annotation.integrationPoints: RepovineRuntime.graph; MCP inspect_node/map_context; analyze_dependencies; re-exports mod:repovine/src/graph/delta, mod:repovine/src/graph/mutate and mod:repovine/src/graph/node-ids.
annotation.dataFlow: Stage2 mutates RepositoryGraph → buildNodeView/pathFromRoot create bounded MCP projections → getImpact feeds dependency analysis with one-hop barrel inclusion; graph/delta remains the validated mutation boundary.

annotation.summary: Sidecar accessors for a build's non-graph outputs (projected extensions, projection report), keyed by RepositoryGraph object identity, plus the RepositoryBuildArtifact shape bundling graph + entrypoints + extensions + refusals + contributors as one build result.

keyExports.RepositoryBuildArtifact: interface { graph: RepositoryGraph; entrypoints: readonly EntrypointFragment[]; extensions: ExtensionStore; refusals: readonly Refusal[]; contributors: readonly ContributorOutcome[] } — what one build produced, as one value; internal (plugin-sdk publishes the contribution/extension-record shapes, never this artifact type).
keyExports.getGraphExtensions: (graph: RepositoryGraph) => ExtensionStore. Reads a process-local WeakMap keyed by the graph object; defaults to emptyExtensionStore() when nothing was remembered for it.
keyExports.getProjectionReport: (graph: RepositoryGraph) => readonly ContributorOutcome[]. Reads a separate WeakMap keyed by graph; defaults to [].
keyExports.rememberGraphExtensions: (graph: RepositoryGraph, extensions: ExtensionStore) => void. Sets the WeakMap entry; used to re-key extensions onto a graph that crossed a worker/isolate boundary (a WeakMap does not survive structured clone).
keyExports.rememberProjectionReport: (graph: RepositoryGraph, contributors: readonly ContributorOutcome[]) => void. Sets that WeakMap entry.

assumptions: Both WeakMaps are process-local and keyed by graph object identity, the same pattern used for interpreter entrypoints and composition refusals elsewhere in the build pipeline.

A worker's WeakMap entries do not survive structured clone across the isolate boundary; the parent side must call rememberGraphExtensions/rememberProjectionReport to re-key the posted values onto the cloned graph.

sideEffects.description: extensionsByGraph and projectionReportByGraph are module-level WeakMaps shared across every caller in the process, keyed by graph object identity.

annotation.summary: Validation and merge layer for graph patches produced by the stage-2 interpreters. Validates a patch against the node and edge schemas, keeping the entries that pass and reporting the rest, then merges it into the live graph in a deterministic order with node and edge de-duplication. An untrusted merge additionally drops edges whose endpoints exist neither in the graph nor in the patch.

keyExports.ApplyGraphDeltaOptions: Merge options: the trusted flag and an optional logger.
keyExports.GraphDeltaLogLevel: The levels the logger is called with.
keyExports.GraphDeltaSchema: Schema for a patch of nodes and edges.
keyExports.GraphDeltaValidationResult: The validation outcome: overall success, the surviving patch, and the error messages.
keyExports.applyValidated: Merges a validated patch into the graph in sorted order, de-duplicating nodes and edges.
keyExports.emptyGraphDelta: The shared empty patch, used for no-op and error paths.
keyExports.validateGraphDelta: Validates a patch and returns the surviving entries alongside the errors.

assumptions: Validation is partial rather than all-or-nothing: entries that pass are kept even when siblings fail, so one bad edge does not discard an interpreter's whole contribution.
Application order is sorted rather than input order, which is what makes repeated builds byte-identical.
The default logger writes warnings and errors unconditionally; the verbose flag gates only a debug level this module never emits.

sideEffects.description: the merge mutates the repository graph in place
the default logger warns on every dropped entry, regardless of verbose settings

risks.text: trusted defaults to false, so validation runs unless a caller explicitly passes trusted: true. A caller that sets trusted: true bypasses validateGraphDelta entirely and must itself verify the delta it hands in matches the node/edge schemas.

risks: The endpoint check drops an edge whose from or to is absent from the merged graph on every path; the trusted default drops it silently, an untrusted merge logs a warning. Interpreters run one delta each in sequence, so an edge pointing at a node a later interpreter has yet to contribute is discarded with no record.
patterns: Deterministic sorted application keeps graph builds reproducible regardless of interpreter order.
invariants: Edges are de-duplicated by their endpoints, kind and stable metadata, so re-contributing the same edge is a no-op.
An untrusted merge admits an edge only when both endpoints are present in the graph or in the same patch.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exported through the graph barrel; the interpreter composer applies the built-in interpreters' patches through it, and the node and edge shapes come from mod:repovine/src/graph/model.
annotation.dataFlow: interpreter contribution -> validateGraphDelta -> applyValidated -> mutated repository graph.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Enables the default logger's debug level, which this module never emits

annotation.summary: Sidecar index for namespaced plugin extensions (facts with no canonical graph meaning yet): sorted-record store, keyed by (pluginId, schema, localKey), stored beside the graph rather than as nodes so traversal/architecture algorithms never walk into an uninterpretable payload.

keyExports.extensionSchemas: Distinct (pluginId, schema) pairs present with counts, for a generic listing that never reads payloads
keyExports.extensionStoreOf: Builds a store from accepted ExtensionRecords, sorted by (pluginId, schema, localKey) via compareCodeUnits — input order is not preserved and the sort order is the store's identity
keyExports.extensionsForNode: Records whose subjectRef resolves (via subjectNodeId) to the given graph node id, in store order
keyExports.getExtension: Finds one record by exact (pluginId, schema, localKey)
keyExports.subjectNodeId: Resolves a ProjectionRef to the graph node id it points at (module id directly, or makeResourceId for a resource ref); undefined when the ref points at another extension

assumptions: ExtensionStore is plain serializable data that crosses the Stage 2 worker boundary, the dump and the snapshot cache with the graph it describes
annotation.integrationPoints: Uses mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/plugin/resource-identity (makeResourceId) to resolve a resource ProjectionRef and mod:repovine/src/platform/ordering (compareCodeUnits) for deterministic sort/listing order

annotation.summary: Host-side pass-through for infra resource-node identity. makeRuntimeResourceId encodes an InfraResource's identity (as computed by the emitting plugin) into the stable resource:… graph node id via the SDK's makeResourceId; runtimeResourceIdentity does the reverse, parsing an already-minted id back into its namespace via the SDK's parseResourceId alongside the given provider. Provider-specific identity rules (what distinguishes a Lambda from a queue, or two Kubernetes objects in different namespaces) live entirely in @repovine/plugin-sdk, not here.

keyExports.makeRuntimeResourceId: (res: InfraResource): string — delegates to makeResourceId(res.identity) for the stable resource:… node id; must match graph construction.
keyExports.runtimeResourceIdentity: (serviceId: string, provider?: string): { namespace?: string; provider?: string } — recovers the namespace from an already-minted id via parseResourceId, and passes the given provider through unchanged.

assumptions: makeResourceId/parseResourceId (from @repovine/plugin-sdk) are inverses: parsing an id minted by makeResourceId recovers the same namespace losslessly.
Callers of runtimeResourceIdentity hold only an id and a node, not the original InfraResource, so the namespace must be read back out of the id rather than re-derived.
risks: Both functions are thin forwarders to the SDK's identity encoding; a change to makeResourceId/parseResourceId's id spelling changes graph node identity here without any code changing in this file.
patterns: Host stays a thin pass-through; ecosystem-specific identity rules are pushed into the SDK layer (resource-identity) so new providers don't require host changes.
invariants: makeRuntimeResourceId's output must equal the id graph construction uses for the same resource (stated in-source).
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates to makeResourceId/parseResourceId in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/plugin/resource-identity; consumed by stage2 runtime-resource node-id construction.
annotation.dataFlow: InfraResource.identity (from a source plugin) → makeResourceId → stable resource:… node id; an already-minted id + provider → parseResourceId → recovered namespace + passed-through provider.

annotation.summary: Core repository-graph data model: the NODE_TYPES/EDGE_KINDS taxonomy, a NodeDataByType-keyed GraphNode discriminated union, GraphEdge/GraphDelta/RepositoryGraph, and the stage1 RepositoryFactsSnapshot. Split from src/types.ts, which re-exports this as a compatibility barrel.

keyExports.EDGE_KINDS: 14 graph edge kinds const array (contains, imports, reexports, tagged, implements, publishes, consumes, binds_to, uses_env, infra, routes_to, renders, extends, includes); EdgeKind derives from it.
keyExports.GraphDelta: { nodes: GraphNode[]; edges: GraphEdge[] } — an incremental add to the graph.
keyExports.GraphEdge: { from; to; kind: EdgeKind; metadata? } — one directed edge.
keyExports.GraphNode: Discriminated union keyed by NodeType; data is typed per type via NodeDataByType.
keyExports.NODE_DATA_KEYS: Runtime mirror of NodeDataByType keys, validated at compile-time to stay in sync.
keyExports.NODE_TYPES: 7 graph node kinds const array (root, package, module, export-symbol, runtime-resource, domain, template); NodeType type derives from it.
keyExports.NodeDataByType: Discriminated record mapping NodeType to its data shape: RootNodeData, PackageNodeData, ModuleNodeData, ExportSymbolNodeData, RuntimeResourceNodeData, DomainNodeData, TemplateNodeData.
keyExports.RepositoryFactsSnapshot: Stage1 facts output: repoRoot, timestamp, packages, modules, infraModules, templates, linkingConfig, bundleOutputHandlerMap, extractionConfigFingerprint.
keyExports.RepositoryGraph: In-memory graph container: nodes, edges, out/inEdges, byType, memoized hubInDegreeThreshold.
keyExports.TAG_EDGE_SOURCES: Const array of tag-edge provenance sources; TagEdgeSource derives from it.

assumptions: Downstream consumers import PackageInfo/ModuleInfo/InfraModuleInfo/SsrMarkers from @repovine/plugin-sdk; this module shapes how those facts become graph nodes.
engineBuildId is set only in development so a rebuilt engine is not silently reused against cached facts; it is undefined in an installed package.
A GraphNode's data field is optional per type; consumers must not assume every node carries populated fields.

risks.text: Wide contract (~52 downstream importers): changing NodeData interfaces, EDGE_KINDS/NODE_TYPES, or the GraphNode shape ripples through stage1, stage2, MCP, annotations, and plugins. Off-limits to casual edits.

risks: NODE_DATA_KEYS must mirror NodeDataByType exactly; compile-time guard _assertNodeDataKeysExact fails the build on drift.
patterns: Core types split into focused modules; src/types.ts is a compatibility barrel.
invariants: NodeType derives from NODE_TYPES and EdgeKind from EDGE_KINDS — single source of truth.
NODE_DATA_KEYS is exactly the key set of NodeDataByType; enforced at compile time.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage1, stage2, graph/index, graph/node-view, annotations, MCP tools; consumes @repovine/plugin-sdk types (src/types, src/path-contract, src/plugin/projection).
annotation.dataFlow: source plugins produce facts -> stage1 snapshot assembly -> stage2 maps snapshot entries to GraphNode/GraphEdge -> stored in RepositoryGraph.

annotation.summary: Answers 'what file does this module node stand for' from the graph rather than from the node's display label. moduleRelPath/moduleDirPath read the node's pkgRelPath; isBarrelModule/isBarrelRelPath detect index.ts/__init__.py-style barrels via the registered source plugins' index basenames; resolveNodeIdByShape forgives a source-extension or trailing-index-basename mismatch when resolving a raw id string to a graph node id.

keyExports.isBarrelModule: True when the module's file is its directory's registered index/barrel file.
keyExports.isBarrelRelPath: isBarrelModule for a path already in hand.
keyExports.moduleDirPath: Directory moduleRelPath sits in, or '' for a package-root file.
keyExports.moduleRelPath: Package-relative file path of a module node, or undefined for a non-file node.
keyExports.resolveNodeIdByShape: Resolves a raw id string to a graph node id, forgiving source-extension/index-basename spelling.

assumptions: isBarrelRelPath is case-sensitive on purpose, matching mintModuleId's own case handling.

annotation.summary: The two writes that keep the graph's node/edge indexes in step: createEmptyGraph builds the empty RepositoryGraph shape (nodes/edges/outEdges/inEdges/byType); addNode adds or replaces a node and keeps the by-type index in step; addEdge appends an edge and keeps both outEdges/inEdges adjacency indexes in step.

keyExports.addEdge: Appends an edge, keeping graph.outEdges/inEdges in step.
keyExports.addNode: Adds or replaces a node, keeping graph.byType in step.

sideEffects.description: mutates the RepositoryGraph object passed in (nodes/edges/outEdges/inEdges/byType maps)

risks: addEdge appends without checking for an existing identical edge; a caller that can add the same edge twice must guard with hasEdge.

annotation.summary: Central graph node-id vocabulary. Declares NODE_ID_PREFIXES/SCOPE_PREFIXES once and provides mint/parse helpers for every node kind (domain, module, export, infra, template), plus owningModuleId mapping an export: id back to its mod: id for annotation-provenance grounding. Pure string knowledge only — no graph, no config, no runtime; resolving against a real graph is resolveScope (src/mcp/scope/resolve.ts). Also re-exports packageNameFromId/packageNodeId from @repovine/plugin-sdk so engine callers read the whole id vocabulary from one module.

keyExports.NODE_ID_PREFIXES: The prefixes that can name a node: mod, export, pkg, domain, resource, infra, template.
keyExports.SCOPE_PREFIXES: NODE_ID_PREFIXES plus query, the wider set accepted as a caller-facing scope argument.
keyExports.domainLabelFromId: Strips a domain: prefix if present; returns input unchanged otherwise.
keyExports.domainNodeId: Mints a domain:<label> id unconditionally, even when the label reads like an id.
keyExports.exportSymbolId: Builds export:<moduleTail>/<exportName> from a module id and export name.
keyExports.infraNodeId: Mints infra:<kind>:<relPath>; kind keeps two documents of different parser kinds at one path apart.
keyExports.moduleNodeId: Attaches mod: to a tail that already carries <package>/<path>.
keyExports.owningModuleId: Inverse of exportSymbolId: export: id → mod: id, used by annotation provenance and Agent Protocol grounding; undefined for non-export: ids or ids with no separable segment.
keyExports.templateNodeId: Mints template:<relPath> for a server-side template.

assumptions: export: ids are built as export:${moduleId.slice(4)}/${exportName}; owningModuleId's parse relies on that exact shape.
No exported name contains a slash — exportSymbolId/owningModuleId round-trip depends on the last '/' being the export-name boundary.
risks: Malformed export ids without a separable slash return undefined from owningModuleId rather than throwing.
domainNodeId mints unconditionally without checking for an existing domain: prefix; callers holding a possibly-already-prefixed string must compose domainNodeId(domainLabelFromId(value)).
patterns: Re-exports packageNameFromId/packageNodeId from @repovine/plugin-sdk rather than duplicating the pkg: mint, so the whole id vocabulary reads from this one module.
annotation.flowDescription: Caller (SDK plugin, engine code, or annotation provenance check) → node-ids mint/parse helper → node id string or its inverse component.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports packageNameFromId/packageNodeId from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src; owningModuleId backs the annotation-writer provenance check in write_annotation and Agent Protocol compliance grounding.
annotation.dataFlow: Caller (SDK plugin, engine code, or annotation provenance check) → node-ids mint/parse helper → node id string or its inverse component.

annotation.summary: The projection types for a node as the MCP layer returns it: the core view with its children, links and symbol detail, the detail shape adding body, search and investigate enrichments, the child entry with access metadata, and the tag union naming why a reference must be inspected. Split out of the shared types so the projection lives beside the graph that builds it.

keyExports.InvestigateTag: The must-inspect reasons a reference can carry: risk, boundary, effect, unannotated, wiring, co-change and hub.
keyExports.NodeView: The core projection: identity, level, children, links with pagination, symbol detail, and the annotation with its metadata.
keyExports.NodeViewChild: A child entry extended with access and internal-declaration metadata.
keyExports.NodeViewDetail: The view plus the MCP enrichments: body slices, body search results and their truncation reporting, and the investigate pointers.

assumptions: The projection is built beside the graph and consumed by the MCP layer, so the dependency runs one way and the MCP layer never defines the shape it receives.
Link and body payloads carry their own truncation reporting, so a caller can tell a complete list from a capped one.

risks.text: The tag union is the published vocabulary the MCP responses expose: a tag is only meaningful when the projection actually emits it, and adding one without a producing mechanic yields a value no response ever carries.

risks: The union has grown as delivery mechanics were added, so a reader working from an older description will not find the topology-derived tags.
patterns: Truncation is reported rather than hidden, so a capped projection is distinguishable from a complete one.
annotation.integrationPoints: Takes its node and edge vocabulary from mod:repovine/src/graph/model and its annotation shape from mod:repovine/src/annotations/types; built by the projection helper in the graph barrel and consumed by the MCP tool handlers. The tag union is kept in step with the mechanics declared in mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry.

annotation.summary: Scoped resolution of an infra logical id to one runtime-resource node. Candidates matching the label are narrowed by the reference's own scope — declaring template for cloud providers, namespace for Kubernetes — and ambiguity scope does not settle is returned unresolved rather than picked. Also owns the nested-stack alias table (FooTableName -> FooTable).

keyExports.InfraRefResolution: The result union: resolved with a serviceId, or unresolved with a reason (ambiguous/out-of-scope/missing) and the candidates considered.
keyExports.InfraRefScope: The scope an infra reference is resolved within: the declaring document paths, or an opaque plugin-assigned refScope string.
keyExports.resolveInfraRef: Resolves a logical id (plus nested-stack aliases) to one runtime-resource node, scoped by the reference's own document/refScope; ambiguity the scope doesn't settle stays unresolved.
keyExports.resourceLogicalIdAliases: Nested-stack identifier aliases (e.g. FooTableName -> FooTable) tried when the exact logical id matches nothing.

assumptions: Called from both the graph builder (interpreters/infra-runtime-links/graph) and the query-time projection (mcp/lib/topology), so both sides read the same resolution.
A resource declared by two documents collapses onto one node; RuntimeResourceNodeData.declaredIn carries every declaring path.

risks.text: A caller passing an empty scope gets no in-scope candidate, so a repo-wide unique label still resolves but two same-named resources return unresolved. Callers must thread the declaring document.

patterns: Prefer same-scope, fall back to repo-wide uniqueness, otherwise report a gap.
invariants: The exact label decides on its own: an alias match is only consulted when the exact label matched nothing.
A Kubernetes reference never resolves outside its own namespace; an absent namespace on both sides is the same scope.
Two or more candidates that scope does not separate yield status 'unresolved', never an arbitrary pick — resolution order must not depend on scan order.
extensionPoints: New provider scoping rules extend candidateInScope; new nested-stack identifier conventions extend resourceLogicalIdAliases.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/interpreters/infra-runtime-links/graph records unresolved results on the referencing node; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/topology reuses the same resolution for the trace_flow projection.
annotation.dataFlow: logicalId + InfraRefScope -> label match over runtime-resource nodes -> scope filter -> resolved serviceId or unresolved{reason, candidates}.

annotation.summary: Type-only barrel re-exporting stage-2 interpreter plugin contract types from interpreter/types: Interpreter, EntrypointFragment, InterpreterGraphContext, InterpreterEntrypointContext, InterpreterId, InterpreterLogLevel.
assumptions: Type-only barrel — no runtime exports; implementations live in interpreter/types.ts.
Consumers should import from interpreter/types or this index for contract types only.
risks: Adding value exports here would confuse graph moduleKind classification.
patterns: Re-export type barrel for stable import path src/interpreter.
annotation.integrationPoints: interpreter/types; stage2/interpreter and interpreters/* implement Interpreter contract.

annotation.summary: Type-only stage-2 interpreter contract. An Interpreter declares an id and a composition phase, optionally gates on semantic-hint keys or non-empty snapshot fact slots, and optionally contributes a GraphDelta and/or collects EntrypointFragment rows; contexts carry the graph, snapshot, modulesById and a structured logger, never the set of source plugins that produced the snapshot.

keyExports.EntrypointFragment: One entrypoint slot: a kind plus optional id/moduleId/path/label and arbitrary extra keys.
keyExports.INTERPRETER_PHASES: The two composition phases in application order: nodes, then links.
keyExports.Interpreter: The contract: id, phase, optional requiresSemanticHints/requiresSnapshotFacts gates, optional contributeGraph and collectEntrypoints.
keyExports.InterpreterEntrypointContext: graph, snapshot, modulesById and log, handed to collectEntrypoints.
keyExports.InterpreterGraphContext: InterpreterEntrypointContext plus the already-loaded domainsConfig, handed to contributeGraph.
keyExports.InterpreterId: String alias for an interpreter's registry key.
keyExports.InterpreterLogLevel: debug | warn | error for interpreter diagnostics.
keyExports.SnapshotFactSlot: The array-valued keys of RepositoryFactsSnapshot an interpreter may name in requiresSnapshotFacts; a renamed slot fails to compile here rather than silently gating on nothing.
keyExports.entrypointHandlerModuleId: Reads the fragment's handlerModule extra key as a string, narrowing it once instead of leaving every reader to narrow `unknown` itself.

assumptions: Neither context carries the set of source plugins that produced the snapshot: an interpreter gates on the facts a repository carries, never on who published them.
Within a phase, interpreters run in registration order, which carries no meaning; every phase-'links' contribution reads the same finished node set.
risks: A change to the Interpreter contract's optional fields ripples every built-in interpreter and the composer's phase ordering.
patterns: Two fixed phases (nodes before links) rather than an interpreter-to-interpreter dependency graph, so a contributor reads facts and never another contributor's output.
invariants: requiresSemanticHints/requiresSnapshotFacts: absent means no such prerequisite; when present, the interpreter runs if ANY named hint key or non-empty fact slot exists.
SnapshotFactSlot is a mapped type restricted to array-valued keys of RepositoryFactsSnapshot, so renaming a slot breaks this file's compile rather than silently gating on nothing.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implemented by the stage-2 interpreter composer and the built-in interpreters it composes; DomainsConfig comes from mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains and the graph/snapshot types from mod:repovine/src/types and mod:repovine/src/graph/model.
annotation.dataFlow: Interpreter registry -> composer filters each interpreter by requiresSemanticHints/requiresSnapshotFacts -> contributeGraph returns a GraphDelta (nodes phase then links phase) or collectEntrypoints returns EntrypointFragment[].

annotation.summary: Registers repovine's five built-in semantic interpreters (code-structure, infra-runtime-links, server-entrypoints, server-templates, ui-entrypoints) into INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS. Per the source's own comment, array order carries no scheduling meaning of its own — the composer applies interpreters in declared phase order (nodes phase, then links phase); entrypoint replay order is driven by the MCP shell, not by this list.

keyExports.INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS: Interpreter[] of the five built-ins: code-structure (phase 'nodes'), the other four (phase 'links').

assumptions: List order is not a scheduling contract: the composer sequences by each interpreter's own `phase` value, and within one phase every contributor reads the same finished node set regardless of registration position — there is no requiresInterpreters/topo-sort mechanism on the Interpreter type (interpreter/types.ts).

Consumed via bootstrapInternalInterpreters() (stage2/interpreter/bootstrap.ts), which registers each entry into the same interpreter registry a plugin-provided interpreter would use — this list only covers the built-ins, not any plugin-registered interpreters.
risks: Adding a sixth built-in interpreter here with the wrong `phase` value silently changes when it sees the graph (before or after node-building completes), since this list itself enforces no phase invariant.
invariants: Exactly five built-in interpreters, in a fixed array (order does not encode a dependency).
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/bootstrap.ts bootstrapInternalInterpreters(), which registers each entry via ./registry.js registerInterpreter.

annotation.summary: Built-in code-structure interpreter registration: id 'code-structure', phase 'nodes'. contributeGraph delegates to contributeStructural(ctx.graph, ctx.snapshot) (./graph.ts), which builds the package/module/export-symbol nodes and import edges; this wrapper then returns emptyGraphDelta() since contributeStructural mutates the graph directly.

keyExports.codeStructureInterpreter: Interpreter object: phase 'nodes', contributeGraph delegates to contributeStructural.

assumptions: The actual node-set construction (packages, modules, export symbols, import edges) lives in ./graph.ts's contributeStructural; this module is a thin phase:'nodes' registration wrapper.

Interpreter composition orders by phase only (nodes before links, per stage2/interpreter/composer's fixed two-phase order); Interpreter carries no per-interpreter dependency field, so a links-phase interpreter that needs these nodes relies on the phase order, not on a named requirement referencing this id.

sideEffects.description: delegates to contributeStructural, which mutates the graph directly

risks: This interpreter declares no requiresSemanticHints/requiresSnapshotFacts gate, so it always runs; a change to contributeStructural's node/edge shape affects every downstream links-phase interpreter without a declared dependency edge to catch it at composition time.
patterns: Builtin Interpreter object registered via the interpreter registry (stage2/interpreter/registry), not an exported register* function.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates to mod:repovine/src/interpreters/code-structure/graph (contributeStructural); phase:'nodes' runs before every phase:'links' interpreter in stage2/interpreter/composer's fixed phase order, which is how later interpreters (e.g. infra-runtime-links, server-templates) can assume module/export-symbol nodes already exist.

annotation.summary: Code-structure graph contribution: contributeStructural materializes root + packages + modules + import edges (type-only flagged when every contributing import is `import type`) + export-symbols + implements/re-export/barrel-import edges from RepositoryFactsSnapshot onto the live RepositoryGraph. First interpreter in compose order; mutates ctx.graph directly and preserves legacy insertion order.

keyExports.contributeStructural: Runs pass1Packages, pass2Modules, pass3ExportSymbols, pass4ImplementsEdges, passReExportEdges, passBarrelImportLinks on RepositoryGraph.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream graph/module-label; contributeStructural prose still accurate.

sideEffects.description: Mutates RepositoryGraph with structural nodes, import edges, and implements edges

risks: resolveImplementsTarget skips external/unresolved/barrel re-export interface names.
Skipping this pass leaves infra-runtime-links without module nodes to link handlers.
patterns: First interpreter in compose order — foundation graph for all downstream interpreters.
invariants: A default export reaches the graph as an export-symbol node when it carries a signature, or when the extractor recorded the local name it points at. A signature-less anonymous default is dropped, since it has no name a caller could address.
A named default is labelled `default (name)` only on the signature-less branch; a signature-bearing default keeps the bare `default` label.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/interpreters/code-structure/index contributeGraph hook; uses mod:repovine/src/graph pass helpers.
annotation.dataFlow: snapshot -> pass1Packages -> pass2Modules -> pass3ExportSymbols -> pass4ImplementsEdges -> passReExportEdges -> passBarrelImportLinks on live graph.

annotation.summary: Built-in infra-runtime-links interpreter (phase:'links'). contributeGraph delegates to contributeInfraLink to draw infra/service graph edges into the module node set that phase:'nodes' interpreters (code-structure) already built; collectEntrypoints delegates to collectServiceTriggerEntrypoints for MCP get_entrypoints/trace_flow.

keyExports.infraRuntimeLinksInterpreter: Interpreter object: id INFRA_RUNTIME_LINKS_INTERPRETER_ID, phase 'links', contributeGraph -> contributeInfraLink (returns emptyGraphDelta after mutating the graph in place), collectEntrypoints -> collectServiceTriggerEntrypoints.

assumptions: phase:'links' interpreters run after every phase:'nodes' interpreter has built the module node set; per interpreter/types.ts this is composer-owned ordering between the two phases, not a declared dependency between interpreters (there is no requiresInterpreters field on Interpreter).

Within the 'links' phase, registration order in interpreters/index.ts INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS carries no meaning of its own (stated directly in that file's comment) — every links-phase contributor reads the same finished node set.

sideEffects.description: contributeGraph mutates the shared RepositoryGraph in place via contributeInfraLink, then returns emptyGraphDelta()

risks: This file is a thin composition of contributeInfraLink/collectServiceTriggerEntrypoints with no branching logic of its own — correctness depends entirely on those two delegates and on phase:'links' actually running after code-structure's phase:'nodes' build within one graph composition.
patterns: Dual graph+entrypoint interpreter: one Interpreter object supplies both contributeGraph and collectEntrypoints, unlike server-entrypoints/ui-entrypoints which are entrypoint-only.
Powers trace_flow runtime/infra topology and service-trigger entrypoint discovery from the same infra facts.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered in mod:repovine/src/interpreters INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS list; graph mutation logic lives in ./graph.js (contributeInfraLink), entrypoint collection in ./entrypoints.js (collectServiceTriggerEntrypoints).

annotation.summary: Infra runtime trigger entrypoint collector. collectServiceTriggerEntrypoints walks graph runtime-resource nodes' trigger records and emits service-trigger slotted EntrypointFragments for MCP replay.

keyExports.collectServiceTriggerEntrypoints: Builds one service-trigger slotted fragment per trigger on each runtime-resource node.

assumptions: Iterates runtime-resource nodes via nodesOfType(graph, 'runtime-resource') (byType insertion order), emitting one entry per item in that node's data.triggers array.
handlerModule is best-effort: the first infraTargetIds() target id for the service node, used whether or not it actually resolves to a module.
The entry's kind comes from triggerEntryKind(trigger, snapshot.declarations, carrier), so unrecognized trigger shapes fall back to whatever that classifier defaults to.
risks: Missing handler resolution on triggers omits entrypoints even when graph edges exist.
A runtime-resource node with no declared triggers contributes no entrypoint here, even if it is invoked at runtime some other way.
patterns: Complements graph linking — entrypoints surface triggers for get_entrypoints/trace_flow.
annotation.integrationPoints: infra-runtime-links/index wires this as collectEntrypoints; mod:repovine/src/stage2/runtime/trigger-entry-kind (triggerEntryKind); mod:repovine/src/graph/make-runtime-resource-id (runtimeResourceIdentity); mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-slots (slot vocabulary).
annotation.dataFlow: graph runtime-resource nodes -> collectServiceTriggerEntrypoints -> service-trigger slotted fragments.

annotation.summary: Infra-link graph contribution: infra modules, runtime-resource nodes, handler/env/queue/publish/container/k8s edges, and infra-kind domain tags. Every logical-id reference resolves through the scoped resolver, so an env ref, a queue trigger and a publish target all bind within the declaring template or namespace.

keyExports.contributeInfraLink: Runs the whole contribution against the graph, the snapshot and the module index.

assumptions: The graph is mutated directly and an empty delta is returned, because the linking passes read back the resource nodes they just created and the original insertion order has to survive.

Handler references are resolved by asking each language plugin's resolver in turn; the first answer naming a module the index actually contains wins, and a resolver that throws is skipped rather than failing the pass.
Resource exclusions come from the domain configuration already loaded and threaded in, never re-read from disk here.
Both registries are populated by importing their bootstraps for the side effect, because this layer reads resource kinds, trigger metadata and known extensions from them.
Edges that need every resource to exist are deferred to a second pass over the same data.

sideEffects.description: adds nodes and edges to the graph in place

risks: Direct mutation skips the delta path's dedupe and its drop of edges whose endpoints are absent — as does every other graph-contributing interpreter, none of which returns a non-empty delta. Node payload shape is schema-checked only for third-party contributions. The composed graph is swept afterwards for dangling edges and unprojected modules, which throws under REPOVINE_DEV and warns otherwise.
Handler resolution is heuristic and ordered, so two modules whose names collide can produce a confident but wrong link.
The deferred edges assume every resource node already exists, so a resource introduced by a later interpreter gets no edge.
patterns: Resolution is delegated to whichever language plugin can answer, so a handler reference format belongs to its language rather than to this layer.
Two passes over the same snapshot: create the nodes, then draw the edges that need them all present.
invariants: The domain configuration is threaded in rather than loaded here.
Insertion order is preserved, which is what keeps the graph identical to what the previous inline arrangement produced.
A resolver that throws is skipped without ending the pass.
Every findServiceIdByLogicalId call passes the referencing resource's own scope; an ambiguous or out-of-namespace reference emits no edge and is recorded on the referencing node as unresolvedRefs.
A logical id declared by several documents keeps all declaring paths in declaredIn, so a reference from any of them still finds a same-scope target.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/graph/resolve-infra-ref for scoped resolution; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/topology reads declaredIn/namespace/unresolvedRefs back off the node data.
annotation.dataFlow: snapshot infrastructure modules → infrastructure and runtime-resource nodes (with declaredIn/namespace) → handler references resolved to source modules → deferred environment, queue, publish, container and ingress edges through the scoped resolver → unresolved references recorded → infrastructure-kind domain tags.

annotation.summary: Built-in server-entrypoints interpreter (phase:'links', entrypoint-only — no contributeGraph). serverEntrypointsInterpreter gates on requiresSemanticHints:['routes'] and delegates collectEntrypoints to collectBackendRouteEntrypoints for normalized backend route entrypoint discovery.

keyExports.serverEntrypointsInterpreter: Interpreter object: id SERVER_ENTRYPOINTS_INTERPRETER_ID, phase 'links', requiresSemanticHints ['routes'], collectEntrypoints -> collectBackendRouteEntrypoints.

assumptions: Reads the 'routes' semantic hint fact itself, not who produced it — any source adapter that normalizes route hints feeds this interpreter (stated directly in the source comment).
requiresSemanticHints gates whether the interpreter participates at all when no module carries a 'routes' hint.
risks: A repository whose adapters never emit normalized 'routes' hints (e.g. an unsupported language/framework) produces no server entrypoints from this interpreter, silently rather than as an error.
patterns: Entrypoint-only interpreter (no contributeGraph) — graph node/edge structure is owned by code-structure and infra-runtime-links, not this one.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered in mod:repovine/src/interpreters INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS list; entrypoint collection logic lives in ./entrypoints.js (collectBackendRouteEntrypoints).

annotation.summary: Server/backend entrypoint collectors for the server-entrypoints interpreter: collectFrameworkApiEntrypoints reads semanticHints.routes (syntax 'decorator' or 'call', kind 'api') into api-route slotted fragments, tagging server-rendered pages (non-empty rendersTemplate) with surface:'server-page'; collectFileApiEntrypoints reads inferFileBasedRoutes (fileType->'api') into file-api slotted fragments. collectBackendRouteEntrypoints merges both. Also re-exports LAYER_ENTRYPOINT_SLOT_KEY / stripEntrypointFragmentInternals / EntrypointSlot from stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-slots for back-compat.

keyExports.BackendRoutesEntrypointFragment: Alias for SlottedEntrypointFragment, this module's fragment type.
keyExports.collectBackendRouteEntrypoints: Merges the framework and file-based API collectors.
keyExports.collectFrameworkApiEntrypoints: semanticHints.routes (syntax decorator|call, kind api) -> api-route slotted fragments; attaches surface:'server-page' + rendersTemplate when the route renders a template.

assumptions: Framework routes require route.syntax to be 'decorator' or 'call' and route.kind==='api'; a route whose syntax is neither is not collected here regardless of framework.
Server-rendered pages (non-empty rendersTemplate) keep the api-route slot and add surface:'server-page' rather than getting a dedicated slot.

frameworkRouteSource labels the source by webFramework: fastify-route for fastify, django-urlpatterns for django/drf, '<framework>-decorator' for decorator syntax, else '<framework>-ast' or the generic decorator-route/ast-route fallback.
risks: A module whose framework emits API routes with a syntax other than 'decorator'/'call' (or without semanticHints.routes at all) produces no framework-API entrypoints for it; only file-based routing still surfaces it there.
patterns: Re-exports LAYER_ENTRYPOINT_SLOT_KEY, stripEntrypointFragmentInternals and EntrypointSlot from stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-slots.js so callers that imported the slot vocabulary from this module before it moved keep working.
invariants: LAYER_ENTRYPOINT_SLOT_KEY values produced here: 'api-route' for framework routes, 'file-api' for file-based routes.
annotation.integrationPoints: server-entrypoints/index wires collectBackendRouteEntrypoints as collectEntrypoints; file routes come from mod:repovine/src/stage2/routes/file-based (inferFileBasedRoutes, fileBasedEntryKind); slot vocabulary from mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-slots.
annotation.dataFlow: InterpreterEntrypointContext.snapshot.modules -> collectFrameworkApiEntrypoints/collectFileApiEntrypoints -> slotted BackendRoutesEntrypointFragment rows.

annotation.summary: Server-templates interpreter registration: id 'server-templates', phase 'links', gated by requiresSnapshotFacts:['templates'] (only runs when the snapshot recorded at least one discovered template). contributeGraph delegates to contributeServerTemplates (./templates.js), which projects snapshot.templates as template nodes and draws renders/extends/includes edges.

keyExports.serverTemplatesInterpreter: Interpreter object: id from SERVER_TEMPLATES_INTERPRETER_ID, phase 'links', requiresSnapshotFacts ['templates'], contributeGraph = contributeServerTemplates.

assumptions: Phase 'links' runs after every phase 'nodes' interpreter (including code-structure) in stage2/interpreter/composer's fixed two-phase order, so the module/export-symbol nodes it draws renders edges to already exist — there is no named per-interpreter dependency field, only the phase order.
requiresSnapshotFacts:['templates'] means the composer skips this interpreter entirely (recorded as skipped, not run as a no-op) for a repository whose snapshot has no discovered templates.
The interpreter is language-neutral: it reacts to snapshot.templates and RouteInfo.rendersTemplate regardless of which source plugin produced them.

sideEffects.description: delegates to contributeServerTemplates, which adds template nodes and renders/extends/includes edges directly to the graph

patterns: Neutral registration wrapper: the real graph mutation lives in ./templates.js; this index only wires id/phase/gate/hook.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates to mod:repovine/src/interpreters/server-templates/templates (contributeServerTemplates); runs in the 'links' phase after all 'nodes'-phase interpreters (e.g. code-structure) via stage2/interpreter/composer's fixed phase order.

annotation.summary: Server-templates interpreter core: materializes template graph nodes and renders/extends/includes edges from the stage1 TemplateFileInfo snapshot and route render hints. Every discovered template becomes a node first (even one reached only via inheritance), then renders/extends/includes edges are drawn through a shared name resolver.

keyExports.contributeServerTemplates: Project template nodes and renders/extends/includes edges from snapshot.templates and RouteInfo.rendersTemplate.
keyExports.makeTemplateResolver: Framework-neutral template name -> node id resolution: anchored 'templates/' folder match, then repo-relative exact match, then a unique basename-suffix match.

assumptions: Render facts come from RouteInfo.rendersTemplate on each module's semanticHints.routes; template inheritance (extends/includes) comes from stage1's template-body parser.
Ambiguous template-name resolution (0 or >1 candidates at a tier) returns undefined rather than guessing — an honest under-capture, never a wrong edge.
The view rendering a template resolves to its export-symbol node when one exists (component, or its class prefix before '.'), and falls back to the same-file module node otherwise.

sideEffects.description: adds template nodes and renders/extends/includes edges to the graph in place

risks: A template name that matches more than one candidate at the same resolution tier (or none) resolves to undefined silently — no wrong edge, but also no signal that a render or inheritance edge was skipped.
patterns: Three-tier suffix resolution ranked by specificity: anchored 'templates/' segment match, then exact repo-relative path, then a single unique '/<name>' suffix match — shared by renders, extends and includes lookups.
Edges are deduped via hasEdge before adding, so re-running the interpreter over the same snapshot never duplicates a renders/extends/includes edge.
annotation.integrationPoints: Templates come from snapshot.templates (stage1 discovery); render facts from RouteInfo.rendersTemplate; the view node id comes from mod:repovine/src/graph/node-ids (exportSymbolId).
annotation.dataFlow: snapshot.templates -> template nodes; module route rendersTemplate hints + template extends/includes -> resolved via makeTemplateResolver -> renders/extends/includes edges.

annotation.summary: Built-in ui-entrypoints interpreter (phase:'links', entrypoint-only — no contributeGraph). uiEntrypointsInterpreter gates on requiresSemanticHints:['routes','conditionalRenders'] and delegates collectEntrypoints to collectUiRouteEntrypoints for JSX route/file-page/conditional-render entrypoint discovery.

keyExports.uiEntrypointsInterpreter: Interpreter object: id UI_ENTRYPOINTS_INTERPRETER_ID, phase 'links', requiresSemanticHints ['routes','conditionalRenders'], collectEntrypoints -> collectUiRouteEntrypoints.

assumptions: Reads the 'routes' and 'conditionalRenders' semantic hint slots itself, not who produced them — any adapter that normalizes either hint feeds this interpreter (per the source comment).
risks: A repository whose adapters never emit 'routes' or 'conditionalRenders' hints (e.g. Python-only frontends, or an unsupported UI framework) produces no UI entrypoints from this interpreter.
patterns: Entrypoint-only interpreter (no contributeGraph); paired with server-entrypoints so full-stack TS repos get both UI and API entrypoints discovered from the same 'links' phase.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered in mod:repovine/src/interpreters INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS list; entrypoint collection logic lives in ./entrypoints.js (collectUiRouteEntrypoints).

annotation.summary: UI route entrypoint collector for the ui-entrypoints interpreter. Builds SlottedEntrypointFragment[] from TanStack Router AST routes, Angular route calls, jsx/config routes, conditionalRenders, and non-api file-based pages via inferFileBasedRoutes — API file routes stay with server-entrypoints.

keyExports.UI_ENTRYPOINTS_INTERPRETER_ID: Stable interpreter id 'ui-entrypoints', registered in ui-entrypoints/index.
keyExports.collectUiRouteEntrypoints: Tags fragments with tanstack-route, angular-route, jsx-route, conditional, or file-page slots.

assumptions: Skips file-based routes where fileBasedEntryKind returns 'api' — no overlap with server-entrypoints, which owns those.

TanStack (syntax 'call', framework 'tanstack-router', kind 'frontend') and Angular (syntax 'call', framework 'angular', kind 'frontend') routes get dedicated slots before falling through to the generic markup/table handling.
Remaining routes are only handled when syntax is 'markup' or 'table'; other syntaxes produce no jsx-route entry.
risks: Non-TS frontends without semanticHints may produce sparse UI entrypoints.

route.kind==='api' on a markup/table route is still routed to kind 'api' rather than skipped, so upstream semanticHints must classify frontend vs backend routes correctly to keep ownership from overlapping with server-entrypoints.
patterns: Each fragment carries LAYER_ENTRYPOINT_SLOT_KEY; the MCP shell replays fragments in the legacy global order.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/stage2/routes/file-based (inferFileBasedRoutes, fileBasedEntryKind); mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-slots (slot vocabulary); registered in ui-entrypoints/index.
annotation.dataFlow: snapshot semanticHints routes + conditionalRenders + inferFileBasedRoutes -> SlottedEntrypointFragment[] -> graph entrypoint store -> mcp/lib/entrypoints replay.
