annotation.summary: MCP server entrypoint: routes CLI subcommands (setup/build/status/doctor/clear/delivery/agents), wires RepovineRuntime, registers public graph/annotation tools, serves v1 MCP over stdio. Threads each request's AbortSignal into execution and owns graceful shutdown + single-flight config-reload lifecycles. Every exit path flushes ONNX teardown and stdout/stderr before process.exit.
assumptions: Stdio protocol stdout stays JSON-RPC-only; verbose diagnostics on stderr or silenced.
SDK delivers per-request extra.signal (aborted on notifications/cancelled); tools honor cooperatively.
initialize must not block on cold build.
Every CLI exit (help/version/build/status/doctor/clear/delivery/agents) calls exitAfterFlush(code) not process.exit directly.

sideEffects.description: serves MCP JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout
installs signal/stdin-disconnect handlers that abort builds and exit; releases ONNX sessions before process.exit
admissionClosed gate + inFlightToolCalls counter coordinate shutdown drain

risks: Any stdout logging corrupts stdio MCP protocol.
Shutdown delegates to mcp/shutdown: admission closes, builds abort, in-flight drain, annotations drain, hard-exit backstop.
reloadConfig single-flight: write_annotation/merge_annotations refused while it runs (MUTATING_ANNOTATION_TOOLS).
exitAfterFlush caps embedder disposal at 2s so wedged ONNX cannot hang exit.
patterns: MCP server bootstrap — not imported by library consumers.
exitAfterFlush centralizes teardown for CLI and MCP shutdown.
annotation.flowDescription: CLI argv dispatch handles setup/build/status/doctor/clear/delivery/agents; otherwise the process connects stdio MCP before cold build and shares the RepovineRuntime build pipeline.
invariants: Stdio protocol stdout stays JSON-RPC-only.
initialize never blocks on cold build.
get_build_status is dispatched via toolHandlers ahead of the not-ready gate, so it stays callable while the graph is building.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/context, mcp/shutdown, mcp/reload-config, mcp/tools/registry, plugin-host/source-set, cli/init, cli/build, cli/clear, cli/health, cli/delivery, cli/agents.
annotation.dataFlow: argv → CLI subcommands (delivery/agents routed to runDeliveryCli/runAgentsCli) OR stdio MCP transport → IndexBuildController.start → registerTool callback (inFlightToolCalls++, extra.signal) → executeTool admission gate → toolHandlers → recordContextQualityCall.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Enables verbose tool logging and the pipeline sink in stdio MCP mode. Compared against the exact string '1', so any other value leaves it off.

annotation.summary: Projects the boundary-scoped risks in the annotation store into a path-keyed file the pre-edit hook can read on its own. It is the push half of boundary delivery: the hook needs no running server and does one constant-time lookup per edited file, while the inspection tool delivers the same facts on the pull side.

keyExports.BoundaryIndexEntry: One boundary-carrying node a file owns: the node, a label, and the risk texts verbatim.
keyExports.BoundaryIndexFile: The file: version, build time, and entries keyed by repository-relative path.
keyExports.buildBoundaryIndex: Builds the index from the current state, deterministically.
keyExports.readBoundaryIndex: Reads it back, or nothing when it is absent.
keyExports.writeBoundaryIndex: Writes it into the local cache directory after a build.

assumptions: Both delivery channels read the same structured source — risks marked with the boundary scope — so what the hook warns about and what an inspection surfaces cannot diverge, and neither depends on ranking or fuzzy matching.

Modules and their exports are keyed by their absolute path made relative to the snapshot root, not by the stored package-relative path, because the stored one would drop the package prefix in a workspace with several packages — the hook computes its key from the repository root, so the two must agree.
Infrastructure and template paths are already repository-relative and are used as they are.
An export inherits the file of the module that owns it, so editing a file surfaces the boundaries on both.
Domains and runtime resources are absent, since neither has a single owning file; they still reach an agent through the inspection path.
Risk texts are carried verbatim and in stored order rather than summarized, because the wording is the delivery.
Output is sorted by key and within each key, so the same graph and annotations produce a byte-identical file.

sideEffects.description: writes the index into the local cache directory after a build
reads it back on request

risks: The version is checked by the hook as a literal it cannot import, so a bump made here alone pauses every boundary advisory until the installed hooks are regenerated. The pause announces itself: the hook returns an actionable notice on every edit it sees, and the doctor reports the drift from both the installed hook and the index on disk. A test locks the literal to this constant so the bump cannot land in one place only.

Both annotation-writing tools keep the index current without a rebuild, so it goes stale only against a change made behind them — a file edited by hand or by another process — and the hook then warns from the previous state.
Several nodes can share a file key, so a consumer reading only the first entry misses the rest of that file's boundaries.
patterns: Push and pull from one source: a file for the editor hook, an attention block for the agent, both derived from the same marked risks.
A build-time artifact rather than a query, so the consumer needs neither a server nor the graph.
invariants: Only boundary-scoped risks are indexed.
Keys match what the editing hook computes from the repository root.
The same input always produces the same bytes.
Risk text is reproduced unchanged.
annotation.integrationPoints: Written after a graph build by the server runtime under mod:repovine/src/mcp; risk normalization comes from mod:repovine/src/annotations/format; module ownership from mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve; the state shape from mod:repovine/src/mcp/types; the cache location from mod:repovine/src/paths. It is consumed by the generated pre-edit hooks and by the doctor check.
annotation.dataFlow: annotation store → boundary-scoped risks per node → node resolved to the file an editor would touch → entries grouped and sorted by repository-relative path → file in the cache, read by the pre-edit hook without a server.

annotation.summary: The state machine around the startup build. It runs one build at a time, tracks which stage it is in and how far along, answers status queries while it runs, and supports cancelling and restarting it without stopping the process.

keyExports.BuildHooks: The progress callbacks the pipeline invokes as it advances.
keyExports.IndexBuildController: The controller: start, cancel, rebuild, the long-poll wait, and the status snapshot.
keyExports.IndexBuildStage: The stages a build passes through and the three it can end in.
keyExports.IndexBuildStatus: The reported state: stage, progress counts, percentage, elapsed and estimated time, a retry delay and a message.

assumptions: A build is single-flight: repeated starts return the same promise, so concurrent callers all await one build.

A cancellation is recognized by a flag set when it was requested, not by the type of the error that surfaced — the stages raise whatever their abort produces, so the error alone cannot distinguish a cancel from a failure.

What a cancel leaves behind depends on whether a usable graph already existed: a previous one is kept and the controller returns to ready, while a cancelled first build ends in a terminal cancelled state with the promise cleared so a fresh start can follow.

A restart is reachable only from that cancelled state and reuses the build function captured at the first start, which is what keeps the whole cancel-and-retry cycle inside the tools rather than requiring a process restart.
A build in progress is a successful answer rather than an error, and it always carries a suggested retry delay.
The long-poll never rejects and settles on whichever comes first: the build finishing, the caller cancelling, or the wait expiring.
Verified 2026-08-02: IndexBuildController state machine (stages, single-flight, cancel/restart) and dependency on mod:repovine/src/mcp/context unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: holds the build status and the ready runtime handle
drives the single in-flight build and its cancellation

risks: The time estimate is a linear extrapolation from the modules finished so far, so it is absent until the first package lands and skews long early on, while startup time is still counted against the measured rate.
A cancelled first build leaves no graph at all, and every tool then answers from that state until something starts another build.
The controller holds the ready runtime handle, so a configuration reload publishes by replacing it here.
patterns: Progress is pushed in through hooks rather than polled out, so the pipeline stays unaware of who is watching.
Cancel and rebuild are ordinary operations rather than lifecycle events, which is what makes an abandoned cold build recoverable in place.
invariants: A status reporting a build in progress always includes a retry delay.
Only one build runs at a time and all callers share it.
A cancel never discards a graph that was already serving.
The long-poll resolves rather than throwing, whatever the outcome.
annotation.integrationPoints: Runs the build supplied by mod:repovine/src/mcp/context and holds the resulting runtime; driven by the server entry under mod:repovine/src/mcp, which exposes the status and long-poll through its tool, cancels on shutdown, and swaps the held handle on a configuration reload.
annotation.dataFlow: start with a build function → stage transitions and progress callbacks update the status → settle into ready, failed or cancelled → status queries and long-polls read that snapshot; a cancelled cold build can be restarted with the same function.

annotation.summary: The server runtime. It owns the current graph, snapshot, annotations and indexes, rebuilds them on request, and replaces the whole state at once when a build succeeds. Concurrent refreshes share one rebuild, and a build that was cancelled never becomes the served state.

keyExports.RepovineRuntime: The runtime: the current state, the single-flight refresh, the forced abort used at shutdown, and the semantic index sync.
keyExports.RepovineRuntimeOptions: Whether to start from a cold snapshot, the build progress hooks, and a signal for cancelling the startup build.

assumptions: The state is swapped as one object rather than mutated, so a handler reading it mid-rebuild sees the previous build whole rather than a half-updated one.
Refresh is single-flight: several callers arriving during a rebuild join the same promise and receive the same result.

Cancellation of that shared rebuild is reference-counted — it aborts only once every attached caller has cancelled, and a caller that supplied no signal makes it uncancellable. One client pressing escape must not end a rebuild another client is still waiting for.
The shutdown path aborts unconditionally, bypassing that count, because at that point no one is waiting for the result.

Cancellation is honoured at stage boundaries and once more immediately before the swap, since a build can finish before an abort reaches an internal checkpoint; that final gate is what preserves the previously ready graph on a late cancel.

The annotation store instance is kept across refreshes and re-read from disk rather than reconstructed, so its single pending-write timer survives the swap — a replaced store would leave an orphaned timer able to clobber or resurrect records.
The second stage is offloaded to a worker so a rebuild does not block the request path.
The embedding library is resolved from the analyzed workspace rather than the working directory, because the engine may be running from a package cache.

The resolved plugins config (defaults/add/disable/retract) is always passed into the pipeline build; there is no longer a fast path that skips the plugin loader when the config looks default-only, so the preset and any third-party plugins load through the same loader on every build.
Container/Dockerfile linking config was removed from linkingConfig; only handlers.searchRoots and bundles (scripts, autoDetect) remain.

Verified 2026-08-02: RepovineRuntime class shape and import set (stage1/stage2, annotations/store, semantic/*, mcp/onboarding-state, mcp/boundary-index) confirmed against source; plugins-config and linking-config fields updated to match current buildPipelineConfig.

sideEffects.description: runs extraction and graph composition, the latter in a worker
persists the snapshot cache, the semantic index, the onboarding state and the boundary index when a build completes

risks.text: Refresh cancellation is shared and reference-counted, so a caller must supply its own signal to participate and must not assume its cancel ends the build; another caller's signal keeps it alive.

risks: An embedder failure degrades — the previously cached vectors keep serving and a warning is logged — but a cancellation during embedding is deliberately not treated that way.
A cancel arriving during the semantic index write can still leave that file written; it is a hash-validated cache, so the next build revalidates it rather than trusting it.

The resolved build configuration is captured at construction and changes only when a refresh explicitly asks for a config reload, which swaps in a freshly built runtime. Domain patterns and the recorded advisory declines are re-read from disk on every build, so an ordinary refresh already applies edits to those.
patterns: One runtime per process, one in-flight rebuild, one state object replaced atomically.
Per-build parameters — the active signal and whether to emit build hooks — are passed down rather than stored as mutable runtime mode.
Every persisted artifact is written only after the build that produced it has succeeded.
invariants: The served state is always the last build that completed without being cancelled.
Concurrent refresh callers share one rebuild and one result.
The annotation store instance outlives every state swap.
A cancelled build performs no state swap.
annotation.integrationPoints: The startup build is serialized by mod:repovine/src/mcp/build-controller; the stages come from mod:repovine/src/stage1 and mod:repovine/src/stage2 with the snapshot cache in mod:repovine/src/stage1/cache; annotations from mod:repovine/src/annotations/store; the token index from mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-index and the semantic layer from mod:repovine/src/semantic/cards, mod:repovine/src/semantic/embedder and mod:repovine/src/semantic/store; the derived artifacts from mod:repovine/src/mcp/onboarding-state and mod:repovine/src/mcp/boundary-index; domain configuration and suggestions from mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains and mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-advisor.
annotation.dataFlow: configuration → startup build under the controller → served state; a refresh joins or starts the shared rebuild → extraction, graph composition in a worker, annotations, token and semantic indexes → cancellation gate → whole-state replacement and the derived artifacts written.

annotation.summary: MCP context-quality attribution helper: selects the context session id for tool-call recording. The harness-pinned REPOVINE_CONTEXT_SESSION_ID env takes priority over tool args, so a worker cannot accidentally record under a run id instead of the assignment context id.

keyExports.contextSessionIdFromArgs: Returns the REPOVINE_CONTEXT_SESSION_ID env pin when non-empty after trim, else the trimmed contextSessionId arg, else undefined.

assumptions: Harness-owned MCP servers set REPOVINE_CONTEXT_SESSION_ID for deterministic attribution.
Client IDEs usually omit the env pin and use explicit tool args.
sessionId is the lookup key of get_context_session_quality, which is itself excluded from recording.
risks: If the harness sets an incorrect env pin, all calls in that MCP process are attributed to that id by design.
patterns: REPOVINE_CONTEXT_SESSION_ID env pin overrides tool args for harness attribution.
invariants: Non-empty REPOVINE_CONTEXT_SESSION_ID always wins over the args value.
Whitespace-only ids are treated as absent on both paths.
annotation.integrationPoints: src/mcp/index.ts recordContextQualityCall for HTTP and stdio MCP tool paths; tested by mcp/context-session.test.ts.
annotation.dataFlow: MCP tool call args + env -> contextSessionIdFromArgs -> recordContextQualityCall in mcp/index.ts stores attribution for context-quality scoring.

annotation.summary: Shared pagination helpers for MCP domain tools (map_context/search): validates moduleLimit/offset/summaryOnly, sorts modules by link count, returns top-N summary slices or offset pages with human hints, and regroups flat module lists back by package.

keyExports.paginateDomainModules: summaryOnly returns topModules only; full list when moduleLimit omitted.
keyExports.parseDomainPaginationArgs: Throws when moduleLimit outside 1..DOMAIN_MODULE_LIMIT_MAX or offset negative.
keyExports.regroupByPackage: Re-buckets paginated entries using graph package resolver.
keyExports.sortModulesByConnectivity: Descending links, then label, then id for stable ordering.

assumptions: DomainModuleRow.links populated by caller from graph metrics.
DOMAIN_MODULE_LIMIT_MAX caps MCP response size at 200 modules per page.

risks.text: summaryOnly hides most modules — clients must pass summaryOnly:false to enumerate large domains.

patterns: Pagination totals separate from returned slice in concise mode.
invariants: offset/limit apply consistently across domain list views.
annotation.integrationPoints: handlers map_context and get_annotation_status coverage with includeAllDomains.
annotation.dataFlow: domain list + limit/offset → paginated slice + totals in result.pagination for concise responses.

annotation.summary: MCP annotation tool implementations: getAnnotationQueue (unified queue + needsWork counts), annotateModule (write_annotation core — schema validate, quality score, importBaseline snapshot, secret rejection), getAnnotationsStats (coverage buckets), orphan detect/cleanup, risk scope candidates, carrier gaps, and refreshContextCore (rebuild with before/after, now including an optional projection report). Stable field order derived exhaustively from AnnotationContentSchema.

keyExports.annotateModule: Schema validate, quality scoring, importBaseline snapshot — write_annotation core.
keyExports.getAnnotationQueue: Unified queue page projected from the store's one backlog walk; publishes needsWork and the staleKind/derived filters.
keyExports.getAnnotationsStats: Coverage view: per-kind published buckets, the allNodeTypes roll-up, and per-domain anomalies.
keyExports.refreshContextCore: Rebuild with before/after stats, orphan preview, and (when any graph extension registered) a projection report of per-plugin contributor apply/reject counts.

assumptions: annotateModule backs write_annotation exclusively.
Secret field paths rejected before persist.
Hard-consistency block on refreshImportBaseline applies only when alone; annotation fields alongside skip check.
Update carrying no fields, no propagationSlice, no refreshImportBaseline is refused.
The domain scope arrives already resolved from resolveScope, so neither view canonicalizes it again.
Every backlog number published here is read from the store's coverage or row counts; nothing is re-derived by subtracting one bucket from another.

refreshContextCore's projection field (from refresh-summary.js projectionReport) is included only when there are extension contributors or extension schemas on the post-refresh graph; otherwise it is omitted, like outsideRepo/buildRefusals.

sideEffects.description: annotations.set/flush persist repovine.annots.json
refreshContextCore triggers full graph rebuild

risks: Secret rejection is heuristic — never store real credentials.
cleanupOrphanedAnnotations flush is irreversible without git restore.
patterns: Shared between mcp/tools/annotations/* and refresh_context.
invariants: Provenance warning when export-symbol grounds mod without direct inspect in session.
refreshImportBaseline requires an existing annotation; it re-snapshots the baseline and leaves prose untouched unless fields are submitted with it.
allNodeTypes.needsWork on the coverage view equals needsWork on the queue view for the same scope.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/tools/annotations/* handlers; annotations/backlog (row counts, coverage roll-up, published bucket shape); annotations/quality (score and consistency); risk-scope-candidates; graph/node-ids; annotations/propagation; annotations/carrier-links; mcp/lib/refresh-summary (outsideRepoReport, buildRefusalReport, projectionReport).

annotation.summary: Config/resource surface collector for module env vars and graph resource/secret bindings; invalid or unsafe namePattern regexes return an explicit error instead of an unfiltered surface.

keyExports.ConfigSurfaceResult: Shape returned: items, total, optional truncation, optional error.
keyExports.collectConfigSurface: Scoped env/secret/resource-binding listing with kind, kinds[], namePattern, groupBy filters.

assumptions: Secret-ness of a resource-binding is read from the target runtime-resource's own kind ('secret'), not from a dedicated edge kind — a binds_to/uses_env edge to a non-secret resource is classified 'resource-binding'/'env' respectively.

Resource-to-resource secret edges (a runtime-resource's own uses_env edge into a secret resource) are collected in a separate pass and deduped against secrets already emitted via a module binding, to surface secrets consumed by infra with no code handler (k8s workloads, docker-compose services, Vercel project, Helm images).
risks: Graph indexes env var names but never values.
Over-broad scope on monorepos returns large unfiltered lists.
patterns: Secret-ness on target runtime-resource kind, not a dedicated edge kind.
Wired into empty-diagnostics via wireEmptyDiagnosticCollectors at registry init.
invariants: Never reads .env files or secret stores — graph-extracted names only.
Deduplicates secrets already emitted via module bindings.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/tools/get-config-surface handler; empty-diagnostics configSurfaceEmptyDiagnostic.
annotation.dataFlow: args → resolveScope → collect module envVars + binds_to/uses_env edges + runtime-resource secret edges → sort by groupBy → paginate.

annotation.summary: analyze_dependencies callgraph mode: returns direct intra-module callees for an export:function/method from stage1 ModuleInfo.calls metadata.

keyExports.analyzeCallgraph: Returns root export and direct intra-module callees from ModuleInfo.calls.

assumptions: Callgraph mode requires resolved export:function or export:method scope.
Uses stage1 ModuleInfo.calls intra-module call edges only — no cross-module resolution.
risks: Unresolved dynamic calls absent from calls[] metadata.
Cross-module calls not expanded — use impact + reverse-calls for consumers.
Call extraction is skipped entirely for functions over 500 lines (returns empty calls with a note), not truncated.
patterns: callgraph mode — shallow single-module view, not whole-program CFG.
annotation.flowDescription: resolved export-symbol node id → return node.data.calls array; skips call extraction when function body >500 lines.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/analyze-dependencies callgraph mode; mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/call-graph.
annotation.dataFlow: resolved export id → collect intra-module callees from calls[] → paginateList.

annotation.summary: analyze_dependencies impact mode: wraps graph.getImpact with downstream/upstream import lists enriched with imported symbol names (uses[]). An export-symbol scope resolves to its parent module for the impact walk and filters downstream entries by the export's own label; downstream is further supplemented with reverse call-name-index hits (getCallersByName) not captured by resolved import edges. nameMatchGap discloses the per-declaration call-index cap that can silently omit those name-matched callers.

keyExports.analyzeImpact: Returns nodeId, label, paginated downstream[]/upstream[] import-impact lists (each optionally carrying imported-symbol uses[] and, for name-matched entries, a provenance tag), plus filteredByExport/nameMatchedCallers when export scoping applied.
keyExports.nameMatchGap: Static disclosure string: name-matched callers come from a call index capped at CALL_INDEX_PER_DECLARATION_CAP distinct call names per declaration, so callers in above-cap declarations are silently absent from the response.

assumptions: export-symbol scope resolves nodeId to its parent module for getImpact and filters downstream entries by the export's own node.label, not by a separate exportName argument.
The reverse-by-name completeness backstop (getCallersByName) only runs when a filter name is set; it supplements graph-reached entries and dedupes against them, never overriding an edge-based hit.
risks: Missing modulesById import records omit the uses field for a downstream/upstream entry silently.
Name-matched callers are capped per declaration by CALL_INDEX_PER_DECLARATION_CAP; callers in declarations above the cap are absent with no signal in the response itself (see nameMatchGap).
patterns: Default analyze_dependencies mode for module and export-symbol scopes.
annotation.flowDescription: resolved node id (module or export-symbol) → export-symbol resolves to parent module + export label filter → graph.getImpact(both, maxDepth) → enrich downstream/upstream entries with imported symbol names (modulesById.imports or edge.metadata.usedNames for barrel redirects) → filter downstream by export label when set → union getCallersByName reverse-index hits → paginateList.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/analyze-dependencies impact mode; mod:repovine/src/graph getImpact/getParent/nodeLabel; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/reverse-calls getCallersByName.
annotation.dataFlow: nodeId + optional exportName → resolve export-symbol to parent module → graph.getImpact → enrich downstream/upstream with imported symbol names → filter downstream by name → union reverse call-name-index hits → paginateList.

annotation.summary: analyze_dependencies interfaces mode: finds classes implementing a named interface by walking graph `implements` edges into export-symbol nodes matching interfaceName — edge traversal, not a string scan over exports' implementsInterfaces metadata (the former method), so same-named interfaces in different modules don't collide and unresolved/external interfaces return empty rather than a false positive.

keyExports.findInterfaceImplementations: Returns interfaceName, count, and paginated implementations (classId, className, moduleId/moduleLabel, signature, calls, lineRange) found via inEdges kind 'implements' into matching export-symbol nodes.

assumptions: Mode requires an interfaceName matching an export-symbol node's label; multiple export-symbol nodes can share a name across modules, and each is walked independently.
Only classes with a resolved `implements` edge (pass4 in interpreters/code-structure/graph.ts) are returned — dynamic or type-only relationships without a graph edge are invisible here.
risks: Interface names colliding across unrelated modules are all matched (any export-symbol node with that label), so results can span multiple same-named interfaces.
Dynamic/type-only implements relationships that the pass4 resolver did not turn into a graph edge are silently absent, not reported as a gap.
patterns: interfaces mode for analyze_dependencies on export:interface nodes.
annotation.flowDescription: Graph edge traversal (not string scan): find export-symbol nodes matching interface name, collect incoming implements edges from class export-symbols.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/analyze-dependencies interfaces mode.
annotation.dataFlow: interfaceName → export-symbol nodes with that label → incoming `implements` edges → paginateList of implementer class ids.

annotation.summary: Cross-package dependency analyzer that aggregates module import edges into package-pair edges, deduplicates barrel-redirected synthetic leaf edges against a sibling symbol-bearing barrel edge from the same importer, and detects deep-import boundary violations (a symbol-bearing import of a non-barrel module whose directory holds a sibling barrel in the SAME package) with a non-empty export-statement fix when the package's entry file is unambiguous.

keyExports.analyzePackageBoundaries: Returns paginated cross-package edges and symbol-bearing boundary violations without double-counting barrel redirects.

assumptions: pkgOfModule derives package membership from modulePackageId graph edges, not path heuristics.
A symbol-less leaf edge from an importer that also has a symbol-bearing edge into that package's barrel is treated as a barrel-redirected duplicate and dropped.

A boundary violation requires the imported module's directory to hold a barrel in the same package — checked via a per-package Set of barrel directory paths (barrelDirsByPackage), not a label match — plus at least one imported symbol.
topN only bounds the previewed module-edges/importedBy sample per package-pair/violation; pagination (limit/offset) separately bounds the outer edges/violations lists.
risks: Relative-import-specifier and package-entry-file heuristics suppress suggestedFix (rather than guess) when a package has multiple same-depth barrels, so some violations carry no fix.
Boundary violations are only detected for directories with a sibling barrel; deep imports into non-barrel-sibling directories are not flagged.
patterns: Directory-keyed barrelDirsByPackage Set gives O(1) sibling-barrel lookup per candidate violation, keyed on the module's own directory path, not its label.
Deduplicate cross-package module edges before aggregation so barrel + synthetic leaf edges from the same importer don't double count.
annotation.flowDescription: graph import edges + ModuleInfo.importedNames → package-pair edge aggregation → drop barrel-redirected duplicate leaf edges → group deep-import violations by (targetPackage, targetModule) using a per-package barrel-directory Set → build suggestedFix from the package's unambiguous shallowest barrel → paginate edges and violations.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/analyze-dependencies package-boundaries and import-map modes.
annotation.dataFlow: graph import edges + ModuleInfo.importedNames → deduplicated package-pair module edges → per-package barrel-directory Set lookup for sibling-barrel check → boundary violations and non-empty export suggestions.

annotation.summary: Reverse call-graph index: inverts ModuleInfo.calls into CallersByName map for exportName-filtered analyze_dependencies impact mode; memoized per modulesById snapshot.

keyExports.callersOfName: Returns module ids that call/export-reference the given symbol name.
keyExports.getCallersByName: Builds or returns cached CallersByName reverse index from ModuleInfo.calls.

assumptions: Call graph names are unresolved export symbol names from stage1 call extraction.
WeakMap cache keyed by modulesById reference identity — rebuild when graph refreshes.
risks: Unresolved or minified symbol names produce false negatives.
Cross-module re-exports may not attribute callers to canonical defining module.
patterns: Supplements import-graph impact with dynamic call edges for exportName filtering.
invariants: getCallersByName memoizes per modulesById Map instance.
callersOfName returns empty array when name unknown.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/impact analyzeImpact; mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/call-graph collectModuleCalls output.
annotation.dataFlow: modulesById export calls[] → inverted index name → Set<callerModuleId> → callersOfName lookup for impact exportName filter.

annotation.summary: Domain mapping helpers for map_context MCP tool. buildDomainContext returns domain summary (module count, subdomains, annotation freshness) or path-from-root for node id queries. buildDomainModulesSlice lists tagged modules grouped by package with optional consumer/secondary-pattern expansion.

keyExports.buildDomainContext: map_context summary view for a domain scope; a scope naming a node is answered by the tool's own path branch.
keyExports.buildDomainModulesSlice: map_context modules view with byPackage grouping and pagination.
keyExports.moduleLinkCount: Counts buildNodeView links for a module.

assumptions: buildDomainModulesSlice uses store domain membership and optional consumer-pattern expansion.
The caller's scope is already resolved: map_context routes a domain scope here and answers a node scope on its own path branch.
risks: Large domains without pagination can produce heavy MCP payloads.
Secondary pattern matches can inflate module lists if includeSecondaryMatches is on.
patterns: Summary vs modules views share pagination helpers but differ in grouping and consumer expansion.
invariants: Input is a domain name or label; the canonical domain id comes from resolveDomainToCanonical.
buildDomainModulesSlice groups by package unless regroupByPackage disabled.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/map-context; mod:repovine/src/annotations/content-hash for the domain roll-up hash; mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness for the verdict published as annotationMeta; mod:repovine/src/config for domain patterns.
annotation.dataFlow: domainTag/domain → resolveDomainToCanonical → collect tagged modules → paginate → resolveNodeContentHash for the domain → freshness verdict → annotationMeta on the response.

annotation.summary: MCP get_entrypoints collector: replays layer-owned EntrypointFragments from the graph entrypoint store by deterministic slot keys in a fixed global order, then strips hidden slot markers. Does not construct entrypoints inline — ordering authority stays here while ui/server/infra interpreters own production of each fragment.

keyExports.collectEntrypoints: Scope/kind/layer filters, slot-key replay via indexInterpreterEntrypoints, pagination. Re-exports inferFileBasedRoutes, fileBasedEntryKind, triggerEntryKind.

assumptions: An entry with no scope anchor (moduleId/serviceId/handlerModule) is visible only when the resolved scope is 'all' or a free-text 'query'; under a narrower scope it is hidden unless one of its anchors is in scope.

Replay order is fixed by layer/kind, not registration order: per-module jsx/tanstack/angular/api-route routes, then per-module conditional renders, then file-based routes (api then page), then per-runtime-resource service triggers — followed by any interpreter-produced entrypoint with no legacy slot key, appended in one stable pass sorted by id.

REPLAYED_SLOTS names the slot kinds indexInterpreterEntrypoints looks up by `${slot}:${id}`; an entry tagged with any other slot (or none) falls through to appendedEntrypoints instead of being silently dropped.
risks: Missing interpreter entry for a slot key silently omits an entrypoint from the replay.
A replay-order regression could silently reorder or drop entrypoints relative to the previously-established global ordering.
patterns: Slot-key indirection: `${slot}:${entry.id}` map from graph-attached fragments.
pushInterpreterEntry anchors scope on moduleId, serviceId, or handlerModule, matching the legacy inline-push anchoring.
annotation.flowDescription: getInterpreterEntrypoints(graph) → index by slot:id → iterate snapshot for replay keys → stripEntrypointFragmentInternals → scope filter → paginate.
invariants: Read-only over graph and snapshot — no filesystem or graph mutation.
angularRouteLayerKey covers Angular frontend route replay alongside jsx/tanstack/api-route keys.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/tools/get-entrypoints; stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store; ui-entrypoints and server-entrypoints interpreters.
annotation.dataFlow: graph entrypoint fragments → indexInterpreterEntrypoints → fixed-order replay loop → strip → resolveScope filter → paginated items.

annotation.summary: Builds the detailed view for one node: the graph view, its annotation with freshness and quality, the investigate tags on its references, paginated children, and optionally a slice of source or a regular-expression search within it. One path serves every node kind.

keyExports.buildInspectNodeDetail: Assembles the whole response for a node from the runtime and the request arguments.
keyExports.graphEdgeCount: A one-hop edge counter by kind and direction, which is the topology input the wiring and co-change tags need.

assumptions: Freshness is one call, not a per-kind branch: the current hash comes from the node-kind dispatcher and the verdict from the shared freshness rule, so this tool reports a node the same way the annotation queue does.
Propagation is folded in for code modules only — they are the nodes that carry an import baseline — and is asked per node, so a node without baseline drift costs one direct-import pass.
Reading source is opt-in: nothing is read from disk unless a body slice or a search was requested.

Search is bounded at every step — the pattern length is capped, obviously dangerous patterns are refused, the pattern is compiled before any file is read so a malformed one fails cheaply, and execution runs in a killable worker under a deadline.
The request's cancellation signal is threaded into that worker, so a client that cancels stops the scan rather than leaving it to reach its own timeout.
Secret-looking text is redacted in both the body slice and the search results, before either leaves this module.
Every truncation is reported: an over-long line, a capped match count, a body slice with more to come. None of them is silent.
Matches carry a few lines of surrounding context, deduplicated where matches are close together and returned in line order.

sideEffects.description: reads node source only when a body slice or a search is requested
runs pattern matching in a killable worker

risks: A domain's freshness follows a hash rolled up from its members, so a domain annotation reads as stale on member churn alone, even when nothing about the domain's own description is wrong. Which members count depends on how the domain was tagged: one carrying path or pattern tags rolls up only those members, while a domain assembled purely from a package rolls up all of them. The queue's exemption for package-only domains applies to ranking, not to this verdict.
Requesting a body slice on a large node can approach the response ceiling; the slice is bounded by the requested limit and the truncation is reported.
Redaction is pattern-based, so it catches secret-shaped text rather than everything sensitive; a secret that does not look like one passes through.
patterns: Bound first, then execute: every limit is checked before the expensive step, so a bad request costs little.
Truncation is always visible in the response, which is what lets a caller tell an empty result from a trimmed one.
annotation.flowDescription: nodeId + pagination opts → buildNodeView → current hash from the kind dispatcher + propagation for modules → freshness verdict → annotation and annotationMeta attach → optional readNodeBody/grepBody → paginated result.
invariants: No source is read unless the request asks for it.
Redaction happens before anything is returned.
A refused or failed search reports its reason instead of returning nothing.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by the inspection tool handler under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools; the view comes from mod:repovine/src/graph/node-view; the current hash and node kind from mod:repovine/src/annotations/content-hash, the verdict from mod:repovine/src/annotations/freshness, and the propagation half from mod:repovine/src/annotations/propagation with entrypoints from mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store; source reading, pattern safety, redaction and the worker scan from mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/node-body; the tags from mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs; limits and child paging from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination; annotation quality from mod:repovine/src/annotations/store, classification from mod:repovine/src/annotations/module-kind.
annotation.dataFlow: node identifier and options → resolved node and its view → current hash + propagation → one freshness verdict published as fresh/staleReason/provenance, plus annotation quality → investigate tags on links and children → optional bounded search or body slice, redacted → paginated response.

annotation.summary: Decides which references in an inspection response carry an investigate flag, and how many. Detection belongs to the mechanics registry; what lives here is delivery — ordering tags by strength, capping how many reach one response, and guarding the direction of the pointers parsed out of annotation prose.

keyExports.HUB_PERCENTILE: Which percentile of the import distribution marks a hub.
keyExports.INVESTIGATE_DEP_GUARD_DEPTH: How far the dependency check walks when validating a pointer.
keyExports.INVESTIGATE_PRIORITY: The tag order, taken from the registry so there is one ranking.
keyExports.InvestigateOptions: The primitives the caller supplies: the node's own annotation, the dependency and membership tests, the import and edge counts, and the hub threshold.
keyExports.MAX_CO_CHANGE_REFS: Cap on the co-change tag per response.
keyExports.MAX_HUB_REFS: Cap on the heavily-imported tag per response.
keyExports.MAX_INVESTIGATE_REFS: How many flagged references one response may carry.
keyExports.MAX_INVESTIGATE_TAGS_PER_REF: How many tags a single reference may show.
keyExports.MAX_WIRING_REFS: Cap on the wiring tag per response.
keyExports.applyInvestigateTags: Tags the response's references in place and attaches the pointers derived from the node's own annotation.
keyExports.computeHubInDegreeThreshold: The adaptive threshold above which a target counts as heavily imported.
keyExports.priorityWeight: A tag's strength, used wherever ordering by salience is needed.

assumptions: Two channels feed one shared cap: the structural one covers direct imports and children with no guard, and the pointer one covers deeper dependencies the node's own annotation names, kept only when the node really depends on them.

The hub threshold adapts to the repository rather than being a constant, because a fixed floor floods a large repository where every shared module clears it; a floor still applies so a small repository needs a real count.
That threshold costs one pass over the graph and is computed per build rather than per request, which is what keeps the per-request check to a single hop.
A capped advisory tag is removed from the excess references while the references themselves stay, so a cap never hides a reference that carries a stronger reason.
A missing primitive disables its tag rather than defaulting it, so a caller that cannot supply import counts simply never sees that tag.
One mechanic is reserved and never fires; its place in the vocabulary is held deliberately.

sideEffects.description: writes the tags onto the response structure passed in

risks: The topology-edge tags are capped by collection order, so a reference can lose wiring or co-change for its position in the response rather than for the strength of its signal; the heavily-imported cap ranks by importer count instead and keeps the strongest.
A pointer naming a node the graph does not contain is dropped silently, so an annotation pointing at a renamed module loses its flag with no report.
The direction guard only applies when the caller supplies the dependency test, so a caller that omits it gets tags in both directions.
patterns: Detection and delivery are separated: adding a reason means adding a mechanic, while how much reaches the reader is decided in one place.
Both channels are ranked together and truncated once, so the response has a single noise budget rather than one per source.
invariants: Ties in rank resolve to the structural channel, which is collected first.
Dropping references for the cap is recorded on the response rather than left implicit.
The tag ranking comes from the registry, so priority is defined once.
annotation.integrationPoints: Detection predicates, the tag vocabulary and the hub floor come from mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry and mod:repovine/src/mechanics/types; the pointer prose parser from mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links; the response shape from mod:repovine/src/graph/node-view; called by the inspection handler under mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib, and the same ranking is reused by the response pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: response references and the node's own annotation → per-target mechanic detection → per-reference tag cap by strength → pointers filtered by the dependency guard → one ranked truncation across both channels → advisory tags trimmed to their caps.

annotation.summary: Repo-contained source reader and secret redactor for inspect_node. Body reads are admitted by the shared containment guard, which resolves symlinks, so a link that names an in-repo path but resolves outside the root is refused. Agent grep regexes are screened for catastrophic backtracking, run in a worker_thread with a hard parent timeout, bounded by per-line and match caps, and admitted through a shared bounded pool so concurrent inspect_node calls cannot spawn unbounded workers.

keyExports.displayPath: Repo-relative label for messages, or [outside-repo]; lexical, so a refused symlink still names the in-repo file.
keyExports.isUnsafeRegexPattern: Rejects catastrophic-backtracking patterns before RegExp compile.
keyExports.readNodeBody: Async read: full module file or export-symbol slice from the parent module, admitted by the containment guard.
keyExports.redactSecretLikeText: Heuristic redaction of secret-like substrings in returned source text.
keyExports.scanLinesWithRegex: Runs a screened regex in a pooled worker_thread; honors an AbortSignal and returns a bounded RegexLineScanResult.

assumptions: Never serves bytes from outside the resolved repoRoot; unsupported node types return {error} without filesystem access.
Module filePath values arriving from the graph are absolute.
The grep worker pool (createLimiter, min(4, cpu-1)) is shared across all inspect_node calls in the process.

sideEffects.description: reads module source files only when the path is inside repoRoot
runs each screened regex in a worker isolate, admitted through a shared bounded limiter

risks: A request cancelled while QUEUED behind the limiter bails immediately (does not wait for admission), and an admitted-then-cancelled request skips spawning the worker — the cancel maps to the empty/timed-out result, keeping the contract 'resolves on cancel'.

Secret redaction is heuristic — novel credential formats may leak in grepBody output, and the same heuristic can over-redact ordinary source (e.g. an assignment whose right-hand side merely looks token-like) in includeBody output.
The containment guard resolves the path and readFile re-resolves it, so a target swapped between the two is read as found.
Full module reads without a lineRange can be large — bounded by the caller's bodyLimit.
patterns: Returns {error: string} instead of throwing for missing parent, out-of-repo paths, or missing files.
A refusal names the repo-relative path, so the out-of-repo target never appears in the message.
displayPath labels a path; isPathInsideRepo decides whether it may be read.
invariants: Never serves bytes from a path whose realpath resolves outside repoRoot.
Unsupported node types return {error} without filesystem access.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/inspect-node-core (includeBody + grepBody, threads the request signal); containment guard from mod:repovine/src/fs/containment; grep concurrency primitive from mod:repovine/src/semantic/serialize.
annotation.dataFlow: nodeId + nodeType + lineRange → resolve filePath → isPathInsideRepo (realpath) → readFile → slice lines → scanLinesWithRegex (pooled worker, signal) → optional redactSecretLikeText.

annotation.summary: Builds the ToolResponse every MCP tool returns when the graph is not ready yet. A still-running build gets a success-shaped progress envelope (confidence 'low', nextAction get_build_status waitSec:45) so harness retry logic keeps polling; a 'failed' or 'cancelled' build gets an error envelope (envelopeError) naming the recovery action, since retrying an already-settled build would fail identically.

keyExports.notReadyResponse: snapshot.status 'failed'|'cancelled' -> envelopeError('all', snapshot.message, {status, stage, nextAction, errorMessage?}); otherwise -> envelope('all', snapshot.message, {...snapshot, nextAction}, {confidence:'low'}).

assumptions: scope is always 'all' in the returned envelope because there is no graph yet to resolve the caller's actual scope against.
confidence is always 'low' because the request itself did not resolve, which is what that field grades (not answer trust).

A cancelled build's nextAction points at refresh_context (a fresh build); a failed build's nextAction also points at refresh_context but describes fixing the reported error first, since a failed build stays failed for every call in this process until the server restarts.
The in-progress branch carries nextAction outside the normal `navigation` block — navigation needs a resolved scope, and this response answers before one exists.
risks: A failed build reports the same nextAction shape (refresh_context) for both failed and cancelled, but the message text is the only thing distinguishing 'fix the reported error' from 'start a fresh build' — a caller matching on nextAction.tool alone cannot tell the two apart.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps IndexBuildStatus from mod:repovine/src/mcp/build-controller; builds via mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope (envelope/envelopeError) and mod:repovine/src/response/next-call (nextCall); called by MCP tool handlers when a call arrives before/after a build that isn't in a usable ready state.
annotation.dataFlow: IndexBuildStatus snapshot -> branch on status (failed/cancelled vs building/other) -> envelope()/envelopeError() -> ToolResponse returned in place of the tool's normal result.

annotation.summary: Pure mapper from stage-3 SemanticSyncReport to compact SemanticSearchRefresh (disabled/up_to_date/updated/failed) surfaced by refresh_context output; also projects the build's refusal and plugin-projection reports for refresh_context/get_build_status/repovine status.

keyExports.buildRefusalReport: Every build refusal for refresh_context/get_build_status/repovine status; undefined when the build refused nothing.
keyExports.outsideRepoReport: Files refused because they resolve outside repo; distinguishes past-root paths from link-escape paths.
keyExports.projectionReport: Per-projector applied/skipped/failed batch tallies plus the namespaced extension inventory; undefined when no projector ran and no extension was stored.
keyExports.semanticSearchRefreshFromSync: Maps SemanticSyncReport | null plus enabled/error/cachedTotal options to SemanticSearchRefresh for refresh_context.

assumptions: outsideRepoReport matches strictly on Refusal.kind === OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE_REFUSAL, not on any refusal that happens to carry paths, so a second path-bearing refusal kind cannot shadow it.
semanticSearchRefreshFromSync defaults its whole options argument to { enabled: true } when the caller omits it, then checks enabled before error, then before a null report.

projectionReport counts a batch as applied or rejected only from getProjectionReport(graph)'s per-outcome batch list; a projector that ran and contributed nothing is still listed, distinct from one that never ran.
risks: SemanticSyncReport field drift breaks refresh_context clients expecting embedded/total/status shape.
patterns: Pure formatter — no graph mutation.
annotation.flowDescription: refreshContextCore → semanticSearchRefreshFromSync → SemanticSearchRefresh status block for refresh_context envelope; buildRefusalReport/projectionReport/outsideRepoReport project the snapshot's and graph's refusal/projection state the same way.
invariants: Output fields must remain backward compatible with refresh_context concise envelope.
extensionPoints: Add optional timing fields when semantic embed reports latency.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called from mcp/lib/annotations refreshContextCore; output lands in refresh_context semanticSearch field; buildRefusalReport reads snapshot.buildRefusals, projectionReport reads mod:repovine/src/graph/build-artifact (getProjectionReport, getGraphExtensions) and mod:repovine/src/graph/extension-store (extensionSchemas).

annotation.summary: Computes trace_flow runtimeHandoff entries that route runtime resources to editable handler modules when annotations, secret bindings, or exact runtime scoping make the handoff high-signal.

keyExports.computeRuntimeHandoff: Builds capped runtime handoff items from current trace service ids, exact resource/module scope seeds, annotation risk, and secret-binding signals.
keyExports.resolveHandlerModuleId: Resolves resource -> handler mod: via stable-sorted infra edges, with a handler-label fallback.

assumptions: serviceIds is the current trace response candidate set; broad traces omit plain resources without annotation or secret signals.
Exact resource scope, or a module scope with one primary runtime seed, may emit a scoped-resource handoff without other priority signals.
Secret detection follows graph binds_to/uses_env edges to runtime-resource nodes whose kind is secret; it never reads secret values.
risks: Stale running MCP processes need restart before the new runtimeHandoff payload appears in live tool responses.
Multiple infra handlers collapse to the first stable-sorted module in v1.
invariants: RUNTIME_HANDOFF_LIMIT remains 3; candidates beyond that cap are reported as a narrow bound under truncation.items, because the list has no offset of its own and the rest is reached by paging trace_flow or inspecting each resource.
Priority order is secret-binding before annotation before scoped-resource, with lexicographic tie-breaks.
The helper stops at the handler module; deeper domain logic remains inspect/import closure.
annotation.integrationPoints: src/mcp/tools/trace-flow attaches runtimeHandoff to the envelope and navigation; annotation risk/boundary detection goes through mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry (deliveryMechanic('risk')/('boundary').detect), the same rule predicates other consumer/boundary checks use, not a direct read of annotations/format; graph uses infra, binds_to, and uses_env edges.
annotation.dataFlow: trace_flow service ids + resolved scope -> candidate runtime resources -> handler module resolution -> trigger classification -> priority sort/cap -> runtimeHandoff result.

annotation.summary: search_context post-processor: detects annotation-matched top hits and sets gaps/navigation to escalate agents to inspect_node instead of trusting truncated search payloads.

keyExports.SEARCH_ANNOTATION_ESCALATION_GAP: Gaps line when annotation match suppresses inline annotation fields.
keyExports.SEARCH_ANNOTATION_ESCALATION_NAV_REASON: Navigation reason for deeper inspect_node after annotation hit.
keyExports.searchAnnotationEscalation: Returns shouldEscalate and top1Annotated from search hit list.

assumptions: annotationMatched on search hits means token overlap with annotation text fields.
Escalation fires when top hit is annotation-matched but gaps still recommend inspect_node.
risks: False escalation when annotation text matches query but content is stale.
Missing annotationMatched flag on hits skips escalation silently.
patterns: Prevents agents from treating annotationMatched search hits as fully understood without inspect_node.
invariants: SEARCH_ANNOTATION_ESCALATION_GAP is stable agent-facing copy for gaps array.
topResultsHaveAnnotationMatch checks configurable topN (default 3).
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/search-context handleSearchContext; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope nav gaps.
annotation.dataFlow: search_context matches → searchAnnotationEscalation checks top hits → navigation.deeper inspect_node when shouldEscalate.

annotation.summary: Deterministic search_context ranking engine. It combines token scoring and bounded AND-to-OR relaxation with optional semantic reciprocal-rank fusion, dampens noisy export-symbol floods, and projects annotation provenance onto every hit shape, including annotationStale when matched prose has outrun the node content.

keyExports.applyExportSymbolDampeningIfNeeded: Down-ranks export-symbol floods when semantic search participates.
keyExports.isSuggestedScopeCandidate: Selects domain and runtime-resource hits eligible for suggestedScopes.
keyExports.searchGraph: Builds grouped or filtered token/semantic matches, pagination, strategy diagnostics, and suggested scopes.
keyExports.tokenWeight: Weights indexed tokens with weak/common-token down-ranking.

assumptions: The caller supplies the current graph, token index, annotation store, and optional semantic ranks.
Stale annotation prose remains searchable for recall; trust is conveyed by annotationStale rather than by dropping the hit.
Semantic-only candidates are advisory and must not be treated as exact token evidence.
risks: Weak-token suppression can hide valid short queries.
Bounded per-token postings can lower confidence when a broad token truncates before global ranking.
If a response projection omits annotationStale while retaining annotationMatched, stale prose becomes indistinguishable from verified prose on that surface.
patterns: Try strict token conjunction first, then bounded disjunction with explicit strategy metadata.
Project provenance flags into grouped results, topResults, and filtered flat results from the same internal match record.
invariants: Read-only: search never mutates graph or annotations.
A stale annotation match remains in results and carries annotationMatched plus annotationStale on every public hit shape.
Fresh annotation matches omit annotationStale.
Pagination and tie breaks remain host-independent and deterministic.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by the search_context MCP handler; consumes SearchIndex and graph state from MCP runtime types, annotation freshness helpers, semantic relevance ranks, and empty-diagnostic shaping.
annotation.dataFlow: query → tokenize and candidate postings → strict/relaxed score calculation + optional semantic fusion → internal matches with annotation freshness → dampening, sorting, pagination → grouped/flat results, topResults, strategy, gaps, and suggested scopes.

annotation.summary: Inverted token index for search_context: searchTokenize splits camelCase/plain identifiers, buildTokenIndex maps graph node labels and annotationSearchText bodies to nodeIds, indexableAnnotationTokens applies length/stopword/WEAK_SEARCH_TOKENS filters, and suggestVocabulary offers prefix/substring/Levenshtein hints for unknown query tokens.

keyExports.SearchIndex: tokens: Map<token, Set<nodeId>> plus annotationText: Map<nodeId, flattened text>.
keyExports.WEAK_SEARCH_TOKENS: Short/generic tokens filtered from index and suggestions.
keyExports.annotationSearchText: Flattens all annotation content strings for token indexing.
keyExports.buildTokenIndex: Tokenizes graph labels and fresh annotation bodies into inverted index.
keyExports.suggestVocabulary: Vocabulary hints when search_context query token misses index.

assumptions: searchTokenize dedupes plain and camelCase-split token forms through a Set, so a mixed-case identifier indexes under both its plain and split forms.
annotationSearchText walks every string leaf of stored.annotation generically (arrays and nested objects included), so a new annotation field is indexed automatically without a code change here.
buildTokenIndex only indexes an annotation whose nodeId still resolves in the current graph; an orphaned annotation's text is skipped.
risks: WEAK_SEARCH_TOKENS and stopword filters may drop valid short symbols (e.g. id, api).
Stale annotations excluded from index until rewritten — search may miss recently renamed modules until refresh.
patterns: Graph label tokens and annotation tokens share the same inverted index structure.
Annotation indexing boosts search_context recall when module notes are fresh.
annotation.flowDescription: Graph modules + annotations → buildSearchIndex tokenize → inverted index for search_context.
invariants: buildTokenIndex indexes annotatable graph nodes plus annotation text keyed by nodeId.
suggestVocabulary ranks prefix > substring > bounded Levenshtein distance.
annotation.integrationPoints: RepovineState.searchIndex; mcp search-context and search-graph handlers; refresh_context searchTokens count.
annotation.dataFlow: RepositoryGraph node labels + StoredAnnotation content → buildTokenIndex inverted map → search_context token scoring and suggestVocabulary for missing query tokens.

annotation.summary: Runtime topology projection for trace_flow MCP: projectRuntimeTopology walks runtime-resource nodes, assembles triggers/envRefs/publishes/consumes, surfaces routes_to/routedFrom for ingress routing hops, reports the grant-derived access mode per resource binding, and derives queue-mediated dataFlows from resourceMap.

keyExports.RUNTIME_TOPOLOGY_SCOPE_KINDS: The scope kinds membership is decided for: all, runtime-resource, module, package, domain, query.
keyExports.projectRuntimeTopology: Returns {scope, services, resources?, dataFlows?} for the runtime-resource subgraph a ResolvedScope selects; a scope kind it cannot narrow by selects nothing.
keyExports.publishTypeForRuntimeResource: Reads the plugin-declared service label off the runtime-resource node's own data (node.data.service); a resource whose ecosystem declared no service label reports as a plain 'resource' rather than being guessed from its id.
keyExports.topologyCanScope: Whether a scope kind narrows the projection; trace_flow's empty diagnostic reads it to refuse by name.

assumptions: Scope hull from mod: seeds infra-linked runtime-resources; from resource: expands uses_env/publishes/consumes/routes_to neighbors.
routes_to edges surface k8s Ingress→Service hops as routesTo/routedFrom on each service entry.
includeApiRoutes and includeResources default true; set false to trim trigger/resource sections.
resourceMap builds producer→queue→consumer dataFlows when both sides present.
risks: Incomplete IaC scan or pruned runtime-resources yield sparse topology for k8s-only services.
A resource whose ecosystem plugin declares no service label reports uniformly as 'resource'; two differently-typed but undeclared resources are indistinguishable in the publish type field.
patterns: Pairs with infra-runtime-links pass2Infra edges (infra, uses_env, publishes, consumes, routes_to).
Queue-mediated flows use resourceMap flowConsumers; routes_to is direct resource→resource routing.
annotation.flowDescription: trace_flow MCP → projectRuntimeTopology(scope) → services[] with handler/domains/triggers/publishes/routesTo plus optional resources map and dataFlows.
invariants: publishTypeForRuntimeResource returns the graph's declared service label (node.data.service) or 'resource' when the plugin declared none; it never derives the label from the resource id's prefix.
Domain scope matches tagged edges; pkg scope walks infra→contains from package node.

Env-ref targets resolve through the scoped resolver with the service's own declaredIn/namespace, the same scope the graph builder used — a global label scan here would re-introduce the cross-template match the builder refused.

access is 'unknown' with provenance('not-declared') whenever the IaC document declared no readable grant; a read grant carries provenance('iam-policy'). The projection never substitutes a default mode.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/graph/resolve-infra-ref for scoped env-ref resolution; mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/trace-flow turns unresolvedRefs into response gaps.
annotation.dataFlow: scope filter → per runtime-resource assemble triggers, scoped envRefs with access, publishes, consumes, routes_to, unresolvedRefs → resourceMap → optional dataFlows array.

annotation.summary: Keeps a small local file describing how far onboarding has got: the graph's size and build time, annotation coverage and backlog totals, and which domain suggestions the user has declined. It is workspace-local and untracked, so it records a person's choices rather than anything the repository commits.

keyExports.OnboardingStateFile: Its shape: version, graph facts, and the onboarding counters.
keyExports.buildOnboardingState: Computes the file contents from the built state and a declined set.
keyExports.mergeDeclinedDomainsSuggestions: Combines new declines with the stored ones and returns the result without writing.
keyExports.readOnboardingState: Reads it back, or nothing when it is missing, unreadable or of another version.
keyExports.writeOnboardingState: Writes the current state after a build, preserving the declined set when the caller does not supply one.

assumptions: Every read tolerates failure: a missing file, unparseable content, or a version this build does not recognize all read as absent, so a corrupted advisory file degrades to no suggestions rather than an error.
The write is best-effort and logs rather than throwing, since failing to record advisory state must not fail the build that produced it.
Merging declines is pure and returns the combined set; persisting it is a separate call, so a caller can compute a result without committing to it.
Declined ids are deduplicated and sorted, which keeps the file stable across writes.

Coverage rolls the annotatable node kinds up through mod:repovine/src/annotations/backlog rather than summing buckets here, and an empty repository reports full coverage rather than dividing by nothing.
The coverage percentage counts only nodes the backlog asks about, so it reaches 100 exactly when queueTotal reaches 0 instead of stalling below it on nodes no annotation can confirm.
Preserving the stored declines is the default on write, so a build that does not mention them cannot silently clear a user's choices.

sideEffects.description: reads the advisory state from the local cache
writes it back after a build

risks: A failed write leaves the previous file in place, so the counters can describe an older build while looking current; the only signal is the warning at the time it happened.
The declined set lives only here and the directory is untracked, so clearing the cache restores every suggestion the user had dismissed.
The counters are a snapshot taken at build time and are not recomputed on read, so a consumer reading the file without a rebuild sees the state as of the last one.
patterns: Advisory state is local and disposable: losing it costs suggestions reappearing, never correctness.
Reads fail soft, the write fails soft, and the only strictness is the version check.
annotation.flowDescription: Read/write .repovine/onboarding-state.json tracking declined domain suggestions and annotation onboarding progress.
invariants: An unrecognized version reads as absent rather than being partially trusted.
Declined ids are always deduplicated and sorted.
A write never throws.
annotation.integrationPoints: Written by the server runtime after a build under mod:repovine/src/mcp; the declined set is consumed by the domain advisor in mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-advisor and extended through the advisory-decline tool; graph counts come from mod:repovine/src/graph and annotation counts from the store's coverage rolled up by mod:repovine/src/annotations/backlog; the cache location from mod:repovine/src/paths.
annotation.stateShape: Version, graph status with build time and counts, annotation coverage and backlog totals, and the domain suggestion counts with the declined ids.
annotation.dataFlow: built state plus the stored declines → graph counters, and the store's coverage rolled up across node kinds into queueTotal and a coverage percentage → advisory file in the local cache → read back by the domain advisor to hide what was declined.

annotation.summary: Single-flight runner for refresh_context({reloadConfig:true}): builds a fresh runtime from the re-read config, drains the outgoing annotation store, re-reads the incoming one, then swaps the ready runtime. Dependency-injected (no direct runtime/controller imports) so the swap lifecycle is unit-testable.

keyExports.ReloadConfigDeps: Injected steps: loadNextConfig, buildRuntime(cfg, signal), drainOutgoing, reloadIncoming, publish, onDrainWarning.
keyExports.ReloadConfigResult: { configReloaded: true, drainWarning? } — drainWarning surfaces a non-fatal outgoing-drain failure.
keyExports.ReloadConfigRunner: run(requestSignal?) coalesces concurrent calls onto one swap; abortActive() is the shutdown handle; isInFlight gates annotation writes during the handoff.

assumptions: Deps read the CURRENT runtime at run time (e.g. drainOutgoing hits whatever runtime is ready), not a value captured at construction.
buildRuntime honors the combined signal at its own internal checkpoints; the runner adds the outer checkpoints.

sideEffects.description: single-flight coalescing; combines request signal + owned controller via AbortSignal.any
in-flight promise + abort controller held on the runner instance

risks: publish() (replaceReadyContext) is the one non-reversible step; the post-build checkpoint and the FINAL checkpoint immediately before publish must reject a late cancel so the current runtime is preserved.
Coalesced joiners share the initiating request's signal — the initiator governs the shared build; a joiner's cancel is not independently refcounted.
annotation.integrationPoints: Constructed in mod:repovine/src/mcp/index with live deps (RepovineRuntime.create as buildRuntime, controller.replaceReadyContext as publish, current store.drain as drainOutgoing); abortActive() is invoked by mod:repovine/src/mcp/shutdown.

annotation.summary: MCP response shaping layer: concise mode compacts a standard tool envelope (resolvedScope down to {kind,id}, navigation deduped/ref-substituted, empty gaps dropped) via NavigationRefRegistry; debug mode returns the raw payload untouched; toCallToolMcpResult serializes the final tools/call JSON and withholds an oversized payload whole rather than truncating it.

keyExports.CallToolMcpResult: MCP tools/call payload: content[{type:'text',text}] plus optional isError.
keyExports.NavigationRefRegistry: refFor(value)/resolveArgs(value) — deduplicates repeated/long scope strings into short $hash refs, capped at MAX_REFS (500) with oldest-inserted-entry eviction.
keyExports.responseConfigWithOverride: Applies a per-call responseFormat override ('concise'|'debug') onto the base McpResponseConfig; any other value returns base unchanged.
keyExports.shapeToolResult: Concise-mode envelope compaction (resolvedScope/navigation/refs/gaps); returns the input unchanged for debug mode or a non-envelope payload.
keyExports.toCallToolMcpResult: Shapes, serializes, and applies the oversized-result guard; sets isError:true exactly when toolErrorMessage(result) is defined.
keyExports.toolErrorMessage: The message a result's `error` field carries, via publishedRefusalMessage, or undefined when it is not an error.

assumptions: shapeToolResult only rewrites resolvedScope, navigation, and (when empty) gaps — every other top-level envelope field passes through unchanged via spread, so it is not lost in concise mode.

compactNavigation/compactNavigationItem/compactArgs iterate whatever keys/sections are actually present (Object.entries), so a new NavigationSection or a new navigation-item field does not need a corresponding code change here.
A ref is only created for an args string that is scope-prefixed (hasScopePrefix), at least REF_MIN_LENGTH (32) chars, and either repeated >=2 times or >= REF_ALWAYS_LENGTH (96) chars.
compactReason shortens the `reason` text on each navigation item to 5 words.
risks: A new large top-level envelope field bypasses NavigationRefRegistry entirely — only navigation args strings get ref-substituted, so a large non-navigation field counts fully toward toCallToolMcpResult's maxChars ceiling.

boundOversizedResult withholds the payload whole (shown:0) rather than truncating it partially; a caller expecting a partial/truncated body instead gets a minimal replacement envelope with only scope/resolvedScope/summary/result/gaps/navigation.
patterns: Concise vs debug is a single mode switch in shapeToolResult; debug always returns the untouched payload.

Failure is read once via toolErrorMessage/publishedRefusalMessage and reused for both the withheld-result path and the normal isError flag, so a withheld failure keeps the same message as an unwithheld one.
invariants: toCallToolMcpResult sets CallToolMcpResult.isError:true exactly when toolErrorMessage(result) is defined, whether or not the result was also withheld for size.
NavigationRefRegistry never holds more than MAX_REFS (500) entries at once.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the MCP server transport wrapping every mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/* handler result; McpResponseConfig comes from mod:repovine/src/config (ResolvedConfig['mcp']['response']); reads envelope shape from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope (emptyNavigation, isEnvelope check); refusal detection from mod:repovine/src/response/refusal (publishedRefusalMessage).
annotation.dataFlow: tool handler ToolResponse -> shapeToolResult (compact envelope + build refs map) -> JSON.stringify -> if over maxChars, boundOversizedResult replaces it whole -> CallToolMcpResult.content[0].text returned to the MCP client.

annotation.summary: Turns an empty tool result into an explanation. Each tool has a factory that works out why nothing came back, states it with a confidence, and offers concrete next calls with their arguments already filled in. An agent that hits an empty result learns whether the repository lacks the thing, the scope was wrong, or its own filter removed everything.

keyExports.EmptyDiagnostic: The shape: reason, message, confidence, next actions and optional detail.
keyExports.architectureEmptyDiagnostic: Why an analysis produced no findings; categories narrowing restores with DEFAULT_REFACTORING_CATEGORIES (not []), minConfidence narrowing carries no restoreWith since it is a config knob, not a tool argument.
keyExports.configSurfaceEmptyDiagnostic: Why no configuration or resource bindings matched; kind/kinds narrowing restores with the argument's own shape (array for kinds, string for kind).
keyExports.dependenciesEmptyDiagnostic: Why a dependency query returned nothing; the cross-package-edges message only claims the scope narrowed the answer when scope.kind is package (import-map/package-boundary modes filter by package only).
keyExports.dependencyModeScopeMismatchDiagnostic: Why a mode and a scope are incompatible; impact mode suggests analyze_dependencies import-map only when scope.kind is not domain, since import-map returns the same repository-wide edges for every domain.
keyExports.emptyAction: Builds one suggested next call: the condition, the tool and its arguments.
keyExports.entrypointsEmptyDiagnostic: Why no execution starts matched; a domain scope's next actions no longer include an analyze_dependencies suggestion (import-map/package-boundaries do not narrow by domain).
keyExports.graphEmptyDiagnostic: The answer when nothing is indexed at all.
keyExports.mapContextEmptyDiagnostic: Why a map came back empty, including paging past the end.
keyExports.searchEmptyDiagnostic: Why a search returned nothing, distinguishing suppression, no token hits, a type filter and an unsatisfiable combination.
keyExports.traceFlowEmptyDiagnostic: Why no runtime topology was proven.
keyExports.wireEmptyDiagnosticCollectors: Binds the tool-layer collectors at startup, which is how the circular import between this module and the handlers is avoided.

assumptions: The checks run in order from cheapest and most decisive: an unindexed graph first, then an unresolved scope, then a filter that removed everything, then the tool-specific reasons.

Filter attribution is verified where a collector can be re-run: the entrypoint and config-surface factories ask again with a limit of one and state exclusion at high confidence. The search and architecture factories infer it from weaker evidence — token hits in the index, or the mere presence of a filter argument — and state it at medium confidence.

Domain scopes are special-cased in the entrypoint and runtime-flow factories, where the explanation states the domain tag owns no handlers, pages or runtime resources; map-context tells a tagged-but-empty domain that no modules carry the tag. The config-surface and dependency factories return their generic explanation for a domain scope; the dependency-mode-mismatch and dependencies factories additionally drop or reword suggestions that would not actually narrow a domain scope.
Confidence is stated per diagnosis: a resolved structural fact is high, an inference about why a repository lacks something is medium.
Collectors are injected at startup rather than imported, and calling one before it is wired raises a message naming the fix.

Suggested next-call arguments are built to match each tool's schema exactly (array vs scalar shape, omitting arguments a mode ignores, using a real default instead of an empty sentinel) so a suggestion never becomes a call the target tool would itself reject.
risks: The reasons are a closed set, so a genuinely new cause of emptiness is reported as the nearest existing reason rather than as an unknown one — a confident but wrong explanation.
A new tool that forgets to call its factory returns a bare empty result, and nothing detects the omission; the wiring is by convention rather than enforced.
The suggested calls carry pre-filled arguments, so a suggestion that drifts from a tool's actual schema sends an agent into a rejected call rather than a useful one.
patterns: An empty result is an answer with a reason, not a null; the reason and the next step travel together.
Distinguish absence from exclusion by asking again without the filter, so the two are never conflated.
invariants: An unindexed graph always suggests a refresh first.
Every diagnosis carries at least one next action.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called from the zero-result path of every tool under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools; scope resolution from mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve; paging defaults from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination; the token index from mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-index; the result shape from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope; DEFAULT_REFACTORING_CATEGORIES from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/types.
annotation.dataFlow: a tool returns nothing → its factory checks graph, scope, filters and kind in order → a reason with confidence and pre-filled next calls, schema-shaped per target tool → attached to the response envelope.

annotation.summary: Standard MCP tool response envelope builder: scope, resolvedScope, summary, confidence, result, gaps, navigation, attention — the shape all MCP tool handlers answer in.
