ToolResponseSchema/ToolResultSchema are the runtime (zod) contract; NavigationItem/AttentionItem's `next` field is the shared NextCall type from response/next-call.ts.

keyExports.ATTENTION_LIMIT: Max obligations surfaced in the top-level attention block (3).
keyExports.NAV_SECTION_LIMIT: Max entries kept per navigation section after boundNavigation (4).
keyExports.boundNavigation: Dedupes each of the five navigation sections by tool+args (via dedupeNextCalls) and caps each to NAV_SECTION_LIMIT (4), in one pass.
keyExports.emptyNavigation: Returns a Navigation with all five sections as empty arrays.
keyExports.envelope: Main builder: merges result with confidence, gaps, navigation (deduped+capped via boundNavigation), attention (capped to ATTENTION_LIMIT).
keyExports.envelopeError: Low-confidence error envelope; navigation falls back to scopeNavigation(scope) only when scope is a ResolvedScope object, otherwise emptyNavigation().
keyExports.nav: Factory for a NavigationItem — thin wrapper over nextCall(tool, args, reason).
keyExports.publicResolvedScope: Serializes ResolvedScope (or a raw scope string) to the client-safe {kind, id, raw, nodeId?, domainId?, packageId?, query?}.
keyExports.resultError: Builds the {error, ...details} shape used inside result on failure.

assumptions: confidence defaults to 'medium' when the caller omits options.confidence.
boundNavigation always returns all five NavigationSection keys (via emptyNavigation), even when a section ends up empty after dedupe+cap.
attention truncation is a reading-order cutoff, not a filter: obligations past ATTENTION_LIMIT still appear as investigate tags elsewhere in result (drillDown/links/investigatePointers).
risks: envelopeError only computes scopeNavigation when scope is a ResolvedScope object; a raw string scope (e.g. an unresolved/unknown scope string) gets emptyNavigation, so that error path suggests no follow-up tools.
ToolResponseSchema is z.strictObject — adding a field beside `result` instead of inside it breaks validation for every one of the tools that share this envelope, not just the one that added it.
patterns: Standard MCP tool response envelope: the type is exported so a handler's return is checked by envelope()/envelopeError(), not so responses are hand-assembled.
ToolResultSchema stays z.looseObject/unknown on purpose — only truncation/provenance/error are held to one shape; each tool's own result fields are otherwise unconstrained.
invariants: navigation always has all five NavigationSection keys after boundNavigation.
ToolResponseSchema rejects any top-level key not in {scope, resolvedScope, summary, confidence, attention, truncation, result, gaps, navigation}.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by every mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/* handler; envelopeError calls mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/navigation scopeNavigation; NextCall/dedupeNextCalls come from mod:repovine/src/response/next-call; truncation helpers from mod:repovine/src/response/truncation; ProvenanceSchema from mod:repovine/src/response/provenance.
annotation.dataFlow: handler result + ResolvedScope + optional navigation/attention/gaps -> envelope()/envelopeError() -> ToolResponse -> shaped by mod:repovine/src/mcp/response-format for the MCP transport.

annotation.summary: Shared pagination utilities and default limits for MCP tool responses: limitFrom/offsetFrom parsers, paginateList, paginateNodeViewChildren, pathFromRootPaginated, and DEFAULT_* limit constants for search, map, inspect, architecture, and validation tools.

keyExports.DEFAULT_BODY_LIMIT: 12000 — max source slice chars for inspect_node includeBody.
keyExports.limitFrom: Parses args.limit with fallback and max cap (default max 200).
keyExports.paginateList: Slices a built list to a page and returns a Truncation when the page does not reach the end.
keyExports.paginateNodeViewChildren: Slices drillDown and merges a `children` bound into the view's truncation map; optional summaryOnly mode.
keyExports.pathFromRootPaginated: Paginated ancestor path + focus node for map_context; ancestors carry a non-pageable narrow bound.

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types and graph hash changed; pagination helpers unchanged.
risks: Changing DEFAULT_* constants affects all tools simultaneously — test envelope shapes after tuning.

risks.text: summaryOnly mode empties drillDown and exposes topChildren instead — clients must handle both.

patterns: namedLimitFrom/namedOffsetFrom support non-standard arg names (exportLimit, exportOffset).
The truncation hint names the offset argument and its next value, so a caller pages without guessing which list it advances.
invariants: limit always clamped to [1, max]; offset always >= 0.
paginateNodeViewChildren never mutates input NodeView — returns new PaginatedNodeView.
A bound is emitted only when it bit: the paging rule lives in pageTruncation, and an offset past the end answers with an arg-restart rather than a cursor pointing at itself.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used by inspect_node, map_context, search_context handlers; imports mod:repovine/src/graph pathFromRoot, mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs salience ordering, and mod:repovine/src/response/truncation for the bound primitive.
annotation.dataFlow: handler args → limitFrom/offsetFrom → paginateList/paginateNodeViewChildren → truncation block beside the bounded list.

annotation.summary: Advisory semantic recovery for scope misses: withSemanticScopeSuggestions embeds the failed scope/nodeId text, ranks graph node cards via SemanticIndex, and appends up to 3 same-tool retry actions to emptyDiagnostic.nextActions. Suggested ids are filtered against the current graph so a stale index cannot suggest removed nodes.

keyExports.withSemanticScopeSuggestions: Async enrichment; no-op unless the response carries a scope-miss diagnostic (reason 'scope_unresolved', or any empty result on a resolved query: scope) and handlerArgs.scope/nodeId is a non-empty string.

assumptions: Runs post-handler for every tool; reads state via ctx.getState at call time (one snapshot for the whole call, so validation ids match the ranking generation).
Embedder failure degrades to the unchanged token-only diagnostic (never throws).

sideEffects.description: mutates the passed response envelope: appends actions to emptyDiagnostic.nextActions
semanticIndex.embedQuery when enriching a scope-miss diagnostic

risks: Suggested hit ids are filtered by graph.nodes.has against the pinned state, so a semantic index lagging the current generation cannot suggest a removed/renamed node as a retry scope.
Over-suggesting broad domains adds noise to agent navigation hints.
patterns: Post-processor on search_context/map_context/inspect_node envelopes wired centrally by executeTool.
annotation.flowDescription: MCP tool response → withSemanticScopeSuggestions when semantic search under-resolves scope.
invariants: Never resolves a scope silently — suggestions are advisory nextActions only.
Max 3 suggestions; the original raw scope/nodeId is never suggested back; retry args never carry nodeId (it would take precedence over scope and miss again).
Resolved non-query scopes (package/module/domain) with empty results are never enriched.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/index executeTool (sole caller); mod:repovine/src/semantic/store SemanticIndex; consumed by agents reading emptyDiagnostic.nextActions.
annotation.dataFlow: executeTool → handler response → scopeMissDiagnosticOf gate → semanticIndex.embedQuery(scope||nodeId) → query + score floor → filter by graph.nodes.has → dedupe → push {when, tool, args} actions.

annotation.summary: Scope-aware MCP navigation hint generator. Given a ResolvedScope, returns a Navigation object (up/deeper/sideways/crossLayer/validate sections) suggesting follow-up tool calls tailored to package, domain, module, or export-symbol scopes; used by envelope()/envelopeError() to populate the navigation block of every tool response.

keyExports.scopeNavigation: Builds a Navigation object with up to a few items per section based on scope.kind (all/package/domain/module/export-symbol).

assumptions: scope.kind 'all' returns a completely empty Navigation (no up/deeper/sideways/crossLayer/validate) — the up-link back to 'all' is only pushed when kind is NOT 'all'.

For a domain scope, no dependency-analysis link is suggested on purpose: import-map/package-boundaries return the same repo-wide edge list for every domain and impact mode refuses a domain scope, so callers should narrow to a module via map_context first.
risks: Domain navigation suggests search_context with a heuristic query (label + 'handler route lambda') — may miss runtime anchors on sparse domains.
Package scope always suggests get_entrypoints even when the package has no runtime entrypoints.
patterns: Only scopeNavigation is exported; nav()/emptyNavigation() are imported directly from response/envelope.js, not reimplemented locally.
validate section always suggests get_annotation_status coverage for package/domain scopes.
invariants: Never mutates the input scope — read-only hint generation.
kind:'all' is the one case where the returned Navigation is entirely empty, not just deeper/sideways.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by mcp/response/envelope.ts envelopeError() when scope resolved to an object, and directly by each MCP tool handler (map-context, analyze-dependencies, inspect-node, analyze-architecture, trace-flow, get-entrypoints, get-config-surface, annotations/status, annotations/write) to build its response navigation. Takes ResolvedScope from scope/resolved.ts.
annotation.dataFlow: ResolvedScope -> scopeNavigation -> Navigation (partial per scope.kind) -> merged into envelope()/envelopeError() responses.

annotation.summary: MCP scope resolution: translates human/agent scope strings and forgiving aliases into ResolvedScope for all graph tools; nodeInScope filters handler results.

keyExports.nodeInScope: Membership test for handler result filtering.
keyExports.resolvePackageId: Package scope resolution: exact match first, then a PEP 503 '-'/'_'/'.' relaxation gated to packages whose owning source plugin declares looseNameSeparators.
keyExports.resolveResourceInfraAlias: Forgiving resource:/infra: lookup by label or bare name.
keyExports.resolveScope: Main parser for mod:/export:/domain:/pkg:/resource:/infra: and path aliases.

assumptions: Ambiguous relaxed package matches return undefined — never pick arbitrarily.

The PEP 503 '-'/'_'/'.' relaxation in resolvePackageId applies only to a package whose owning source plugin declares looseNameSeparators (pluginUsesLooseNameSeparators); npm/TS packages never cross-match by separator.
Bootstrap import registers the built-in source plugins before this module asks their looseNameSeparators capability.

sideEffects.description: Bootstrap registers source plugins for loose name separators

risks: Ambiguous package name matches stay unresolved.
patterns: normalizeLookupPath for case-insensitive path matching.
firstResultId/topSearchResultIds bridge search_context to navigation.
annotation.flowDescription: Forgiving scope parser bridging human/agent shorthand (paths, package names, service labels) to canonical graph node ids.
invariants: scope 'all' never carries nodeId.
resource:/infra: alias requires exactly one matching node.
annotation.integrationPoints: Every mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/* handler; mod:repovine/src/mcp/boundary-index resolveNodeRelPath; mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/bootstrap. TypeScript tsconfig discovery (transitive): mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/list-tsconfig-files.
annotation.dataFlow: scope string + getState() → resolveScope → ResolvedScope → nodeInScope filters in all MCP handlers.

annotation.summary: Ordered graceful-shutdown sequence for the MCP server, dependency-injected so the phase ORDER is unit-testable outside the CLI entry. createShutdownSequence runs a fixed 6-phase teardown; abortMcpBuilds fans cancellation across the independent build owners.

keyExports.ShutdownBuildDeps: Injected per-owner abort handles for abortMcpBuilds.
keyExports.abortMcpBuilds: Live-owner adapter: starts startup + refresh + reloadConfig aborts concurrently before awaiting any, so a slow owner does not block the others; per-owner failures are logged and absorbed.
keyExports.createShutdownSequence: Returns a once-guarded handler running: close admission → abort all build kinds → drain in-flight tool calls → inline plugin teardown → drain annotations → after-flush hooks → transport close → exit. A reserved cleanupTailMs stops the build-abort wait and tool-call poll before the deadline so teardown/drain always run.

assumptions: exit(), log(), and the phase operations are injected — the module owns no process/global state itself.
deadlineMs defaults 8s, buildAbortGraceMs 4s, cleanupTailMs 2s of that deadline.

sideEffects.description: unref'd hard-exit backstop timer + build-abort grace timer
races build-abort against the grace budget; polls inFlightToolCalls until the cleanup boundary

risks: Phase order is load-bearing: aborting builds before the tool-call drain unblocks refresh long-polls so the drain can finish; reversing it deadlocks until the deadline.
The reserved cleanup tail is what lets a hung build plus a stuck tool call still reach annotation drain before the unref'd hard-exit backstop fires; shrinking it to zero re-opens that starvation.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wired by mod:repovine/src/mcp/index (createShutdownHandler passes live process state); abortMcpBuilds drives controller.cancel(), mod:repovine/src/mcp/context abortActiveRefresh(), and mod:repovine/src/mcp/reload-config abortActive().

annotation.summary: Module src/mcp/tool-defs.ts in repovine

keyExports.ToolDef: One entry: name, description and argument schema.
keyExports.getRequiredArgs: Derives the required argument names from the schema's own optionality.
keyExports.getToolDef: Looks a definition up by name.
keyExports.toolDefs: The ordered catalog, every entry extended with the shared response and session arguments.

assumptions: The shared arguments are added to every tool in one place rather than repeated per definition, so no tool can be published without them.
Required arguments are read off the schema rather than listed separately, so the two cannot disagree.

Descriptions are part of the contract, not documentation: they carry when to reach for a tool, what an empty result means, and which follow-up to make, and that prose is what steers an agent's choice.

Some of that prose comes from the same shared guidance constants the generated client assets use (ANNOTATION_CONSUMER_RISK_AUTHORING, ANNOTATION_INVESTIGATE_CLOSURE from cli/onboarding-assets), so a rule is worded once and appears everywhere.
RefactoringReportCategorySchema is derived from REFACTORING_CATEGORIES rather than hand-listed, so the tool's advertised category filter can't drift from the detectors' category union.
A definition and its handler are registered separately, and a definition without a handler fails at startup rather than at call time.
risks: A tool's description can promise a bound the server does not honour, and nothing checks prose against behaviour.

Adding a tool means changing the catalog, the handler and the always-on reference together. A definition and its handler are registered separately and reconciled only by a test, so a definition with no handler is advertised normally and fails on first call as an unknown tool.

risks.text: A schema that admits an argument the handler ignores validates successfully and does nothing, so the public surface should expose only parameters a handler honours.

patterns: One definition drives both registration and validation, which is what keeps the published schema and the enforced schema identical.
The behavioural contract lives beside the machine one, so a change in how a tool should be used is made where the tool is defined.
invariants: Every published tool accepts the shared response-format and session arguments.

Registration walks the catalog, so the two sets are never compared. A handler with no catalog entry is never registered and is unreachable — silently absent rather than diagnosed. A catalog entry with no handler advertises and validates normally and fails only when an agent calls it, unless the server answers that name itself before reaching the handler, which is how the build-status tool is served.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered and validated by the server entry under mod:repovine/src/mcp; shared guidance prose comes from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; the analysis categories enumerated in one schema come from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/types; session and phase vocabularies from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol.
annotation.dataFlow: definitions with schemas and descriptions → shared arguments appended → registration with the protocol library and per-call validation → the tool list and call behaviour an agent sees.

annotation.summary: MCP analyze_architecture handler: runs the read-only architectural detector suite via mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture (report or detailFindingId expansion mode), then projects the raw result into what the tool publishes -- stripping the internal confidence score, previewing a finding's nodes (capped at 10 in report mode, full in detail mode), and folding truncation/empty-result diagnostics into the envelope.

keyExports.handleAnalyzeArchitecture: Resolves scope and mode (report vs detail, the latter triggered by a detailFindingId/findingId arg), builds the RefactoringState from ctx.getState()/ctx.getConfig() plus interpreter entrypoints, runs runRefactoringReport or runRefactoringOpportunityDetail, and returns the published result with navigation, gaps and truncation.

assumptions: strictness and thresholds come from the analyze_architecture block of mod:repovine/src/config, already resolved onto ctx.getState()/ctx.getConfig().
detailFindingId (or the legacy findingId arg) switches the handler into detail mode, which calls runRefactoringOpportunityDetail instead of runRefactoringReport.
A single-node scope gets an explicit gap message (SINGLE_NODE_SCOPE_GAP) because comparison-based findings have nothing to compare within one node.

Report-mode findings preview up to REPORT_FINDING_NODE_PREVIEW (10) nodes per finding with a truncation hint pointing at detail mode; the finding's confidence score is stripped from the published shape in both modes because the 0.5 default confidence floor filters little and publishing it would overstate precision.
risks: strict vs balanced strictness (resolved upstream in config) changes which findings clear the confidence floor, so it changes security-sensitive category volume without this handler seeing that as a distinct signal.
annotationReasoning is passed through only when the caller opts in; a caller that omits it gets findings with no annotationContext even where a detector could have attached one.
patterns: Read-only candidate report -- findings are architectural hypotheses, not proven safe refactors.
publicFinding/publicArchitectureResult strip internal-only fields (confidence, minConfidence) at the boundary so the published shape cannot be read as a precision guarantee.
annotation.flowDescription: Scope + categories -> handleAnalyzeArchitecture -> ranked architectural candidates with optional detail expansion.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture (runRefactoringReport, runRefactoringOpportunityDetail); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/scope (isSingleNodeScope); mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store (getInterpreterEntrypoints); mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination (limitFrom); mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + mode + args -> state slice from ctx.getState()/ctx.getConfig() plus interpreter entrypoints -> runRefactoringReport or runRefactoringOpportunityDetail -> findings previewed/stripped for publication -> envelope with navigation, gaps and truncation.

annotation.summary: MCP analyze_dependencies handler: resolves scope, selects mode (impact, package-boundaries, interfaces, callgraph), dispatches to lib/dependencies analyzers with empty diagnostics.

keyExports.defaultDependencyMode: Selects default analyze_dependencies mode from ResolvedScope kind.
keyExports.handleAnalyzeDependencies: Dispatches mode to impact/package-boundaries/interfaces/callgraph analyzers; callgraph and impact results that come back refused (isRefused) are turned into a structured error envelope via dependencyRefusal rather than passed through.

assumptions: defaultDependencyMode picks impact for modules, package-boundaries for pkg: scopes.
Mode dispatch delegates to mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/* analyzers.

dependencyRefusal answers a callgraph/impact Refusal with the refusal's own message/reason/details plus a dependencyModeScopeMismatchDiagnostic, low confidence, and navigation — kept distinct from the generic wrapper sentence so the scope and navigation survive.
risks: Wrong mode for scope kind returns dependencyModeScopeMismatchDiagnostic.
exportName only affects impact mode downstream filtering.
patterns: Contract axis — run before editing shared exports or package boundaries.
annotation.flowDescription: scope + mode → handleAnalyzeDependencies → dispatches impact/import-map/package-boundaries/callgraph analyzers, unwrapping isRefused results through dependencyRefusal.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/impact; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/package-boundaries; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/interfaces; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/callgraph; mod:repovine/src/response/refusal isRefused.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + mode → resolveScope → analyzer → envelope with mode/analysis/emptyDiagnostic, or dependencyRefusal envelope when the analyzer itself refused.

annotation.summary: The two annotation-merge tools. One reports whether the annotation file currently carries conflict markers and what merge review is outstanding. The other runs the semantic merge on disk, optionally as a dry run, forgets entries deleted on the other side, and reloads the engine state when a write actually happened, then points the caller at the nodes that still need manual resolution.

keyExports.handleGetAnnotationMergeStatus: Reports the annotation file's merge state without touching it.
keyExports.handleMergeAnnotations: Runs the on-disk merge, optionally dry, and refreshes engine state when the file was written.

assumptions: A dry run reports what would happen and never writes, so a caller can inspect the outcome before committing to it.
A write is followed by a state reload, because the in-memory store would otherwise diverge from the file just rewritten.

A deletion the merge honors is forgotten rather than resurrected, so the reload that follows does not write it back. Honoring turns on whether the other side left the entry untouched, not on which side deleted it: a deletion the other side contested with an edit loses, and the edited entry survives with a conflict recorded.
Verified 2026-07-23: handleGetAnnotationMergeStatus/handleMergeAnnotations and the delegation to mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: the merge rewrites the annotation file unless the call is a dry run
reloads the engine state after a successful write

risks: A merge running concurrently with a git operation on the same file has no lock between them, so the two writers can interleave.
Nodes whose conflict the merge cannot resolve are listed for manual resolution; leaving them means the file still carries unresolved state even though the tool reported success.
patterns: Thin wrappers over the disk-merge helpers, with the state reload attached here because only the tool layer knows about the engine context.
invariants: A non-dry merge reloads the engine state only when it wrote the file. A merge that finds nothing to resolve reports success and leaves the loaded state untouched.
The status tool never writes.
annotation.integrationPoints: Both delegate to the merge helpers in mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance; the state reload goes through the MCP context.
annotation.dataFlow: merge request → on-disk merge or dry-run report → state reload when written → response listing what merged and what still needs manual resolution.

annotation.summary: refresh_context MCP tool wrapper — synchronization barrier after code or annotation edits. Calls lib/annotations refreshContextCore for graph rebuild with stats, optionally deletes orphaned annotations when cleanupOrphans:true.

keyExports.handleRefreshContext: Synchronization barrier after code changes — rebuilds graph and reports orphan count.

assumptions: Synchronization barrier — rebuilds graph after code/annotation edits.
cleanupOrphans:true deletes annotations for removed modules (irreversible).

Every buildRefusals entry from refreshContextCore's result is surfaced as a gap message, in the same place get_build_status reports them; the containment/outsideRepo warning is one such refusal and is not separately duplicated beside the bounded outsideRepo projection block.

sideEffects.description: Triggers full graph rebuild
Optional orphan deletion when cleanupOrphans set

risks: cleanupOrphans:true irreversibly deletes — requires git restore to undo.
patterns: Synchronization barrier.
annotation.flowDescription: Optional cleanupOrphans → refreshContextCore → optional cleanup → envelope with payloads.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/lib/annotations refreshContextCore; mcp/context IndexBuildController; mod:repovine/src/response/refusal Refusal type for buildRefusals gaps.
annotation.dataFlow: cleanupOrphans flag → refreshContextCore → optional cleanup → gaps built from orphan count and every buildRefusals message → envelope with refresh+cleanup payloads.

annotation.summary: The annotation-status tool wrapper. Resolves the requested scope, then routes the requested view to the matching helper: coverage, the unified drain queue, the propagation-only filter, the propagation preview for one upstream, the orphan list, the risk-scope candidates advisory, the carrier-gap advisory, or everything at once. Paging and domain filtering are applied here rather than in each helper.

keyExports.domainLabelForQueue: Strips the domain prefix off a resolved scope (via graph/node-ids domainLabelFromId) so the queue and coverage filters can use a bare label.
keyExports.handleGetAnnotationStatus: The tool entry: resolves scope, dispatches the view, and attaches the refresh follow-up navigation.

assumptions: The queue is one unified backlog across node types; the view selects a projection of it rather than a separate list.
The view argument is a closed set checked before the handler runs, so an unrecognized name is rejected as an invalid argument; the coverage default applies only when the view is omitted.
Scope, paging and domain arguments are resolved once for every view; each helper applies them to its own list.
The advisory views (risk-scope candidates and carrier gaps) are paged and do not affect the work counters, so a clean queue can still list them.
risks: Queue offsets shift as annotations are written, so paging deeper while draining skips items; the queue is meant to be drained from the top.
patterns: A thin dispatcher: every view's computation lives in the annotation library, and this module owns only routing, scope filtering and paging.
annotation.flowDescription: The requested view and scope select one helper, whose result is wrapped with navigation pointing at the natural follow-up.
annotation.integrationPoints: All views are computed by mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/annotations; the scope is resolved through mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve and paging defaults come from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination; the domain label helper reads mod:repovine/src/graph/node-ids.
annotation.dataFlow: resolved scope plus view → the matching annotation helper → response envelope carrying that view's payload and its follow-up navigation.

annotation.summary: The annotation-validation tool wrapper. Runs the health check of the annotation store against the current graph and returns its counts, the merge state of the file, the advisory findings, and navigation pointing at the natural follow-ups. Read-only: it reports what is wrong without repairing anything.

keyExports.handleValidateAnnotations: The tool entry: runs the health check for the whole workspace or a named scope and wraps the result with follow-up navigation.

assumptions: The check compares the stored annotations against the graph as currently built, so its verdict is only as fresh as the last graph refresh.
A scope argument narrows the reported work without changing what is validated globally, which is what lets a sub-agent see just its own slice.
risks: The queue sample in the response is truncated, so it indicates the head of the backlog rather than enumerating it; the status tool is the paged view.
Because the verdict is computed against the current graph, running it before a refresh reports staleness that a refresh would resolve, and misses staleness a refresh would reveal.
patterns: A thin wrapper: the whole computation lives in the annotation maintenance module and this handler only shapes the response.
invariants: The check never mutates the annotation file.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates to the health check in mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance, resolves an optional scope through mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve, and points follow-ups at the merge, refresh and queue paths.
annotation.dataFlow: engine state and workspace root → health check against the graph → counts, merge state and advisories → response envelope with follow-up navigation.

annotation.summary: write_annotation MCP tool wrapper. Delegates to lib/annotations annotateModule (schema validation, secret rejection, quality scoring, importBaseline, in-memory store set); the store persists via an 800ms debounced save, so the write is in memory now and on disk shortly. When args.durable===true it awaits annotations.flushAsync() and reports persistence.{durable,persisted,lastSaveError} so the response reflects a durable commit; a flush failure is reported (persistenceError) while the annotation stays safe in memory. Wraps the result in the standard envelope with a post-save inspect_node navigation hint.

keyExports.handleWriteAnnotation: MCP entry for annotation writes — never hand-edit repovine.annots.json.

assumptions: Delegates to annotateModule for schema validation and secret rejection.
Post-save navigation hints inspect_node on the written nodeId.

sideEffects.description: Persists via AnnotationStore in annotateModule

risks: Bypassing annotateModule (manual JSON edit) corrupts merge metadata and freshness.
patterns: Thin MCP wrapper — business logic lives in mcp/lib/annotations.
annotation.flowDescription: MCP args → handleWriteAnnotation → annotateModule → quality score + persistence → envelope with navigation hint.
invariants: write_annotation must merge partial updates without dropping unrelated fields.
Quality score is completeness only — consistency checked separately.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/annotations annotateModule; mod:repovine/src/annotations/store AnnotationStore. Envelope pagination (transitive): mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: nodeId + annotation JSON → annotateModule → envelope with quality score.

annotation.summary: MCP get_build_status tool handler (handleGetBuildStatus). Reports build lifecycle status (building/ready/failed/cancelled) inside a normal envelope rather than an error response, even before the graph exists. args.cancel:true stops the in-flight startup build via build.cancel(). args.waitSec (clamped to 0..MAX_WAIT_SEC=55, tied to ctx.signal) long-polls build.waitForSettled instead of returning the current snapshot immediately. On a ready build, buildStatusEnvelope attaches domainsSuggestions, outsideRepo, buildRefusals, and projection diagnostics from RepovineState.

keyExports.handleGetBuildStatus: ToolHandler for get_build_status; dispatched ahead of the not-ready gate since it reads build lifecycle, not the graph

assumptions: ctx.build may be undefined in some processes; handled by returning envelopeError('all', 'Build status is unavailable in this process.')

sideEffects.description: cancel:true calls build.cancel(), stopping the in-flight build's Stage 1 workers and settling its status
waitSec>0 awaits build.waitForSettled(waitSec, ctx.signal) before responding, up to 55s

risks: MAX_WAIT_SEC is hardcoded to 55s to stay under the MCP SDK client's 60s default request timeout; raising it without checking that client timeout would reintroduce client-side timeout-and-discard on long polls.

annotation.summary: MCP tool handler for get_context_session_quality: looks up a worker-runtime context session report from contextQualityStore with optional policy overrides (phase, mode, thresholds, assignmentScope) and consume/retain flags. Not the harness protocol compliance gate — use CLI validate/compliance for that.

keyExports.handleGetContextSessionQuality: Returns scored context session report or error when store unavailable or sessionId not found.

assumptions: sessionId defaults to '' when args.sessionId is not a string, which getReport treats as session-not-found.

Policy override fields (phase, mode, qualityThreshold, warningThreshold, minAnchors, byteBudget, maxRecoveryAttempts, assignmentScope) pass through only when they match the expected type/enum; anything else becomes undefined and the store's own default applies.
consume/retainSession booleans gate on strict === true — any other value is treated as false.

sideEffects.description: Optional consume/retainSession mutates store when args.consume or args.retainSession are true

risks: Store unavailable in lightweight CLI subprocesses returns a clear error, not a silent empty report.
Invalid sessionId returns not-found error rather than partial report.
patterns: Meta tool — excluded from its own quality recording.
annotation.flowDescription: contextSessionId → aggregate per-tool byte counts → quality score vs threshold.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered in mcp/tools registry; contextQualityStore populated by recordContextQualityCall in mcp/index.ts.
annotation.dataFlow: args.sessionId + policy → contextQualityStore.getReport → JSON report or error envelope.

annotation.summary: One MCP surface for recording that an advisory was reviewed and rejected, dispatched by a required kind argument. The domains kind merges the declined suggestion ids into the workspace onboarding state and recomputes the remaining suggestions; the carrier-link kind validates the requested targets against the pairs actually flagged, stamps each with the target's current risk hash, and merges them into the carrier review file. An unknown or missing kind returns an error naming the valid kinds and writes nothing.

keyExports.DECLINE_ADVISORY_KINDS: The accepted advisory kinds, also used to build the error message for an unknown one.
keyExports.DeclineAdvisoryKind: The union derived from that list.
keyExports.handleDeclineAdvisory: The handler: dispatches on kind to the domains or carrier-link decline path.

assumptions: Both kinds of state are workspace-local and stored separately, so declining one advisory never touches the other's record.
A carrier-link decline is stamped with the target's current risk hash, so the suppression expires when the target's consumer risks change.
The per-kind result payload shape is part of the tool contract and is asserted by the handler tests.
requestedIds resolves `all: true` to every currently visible/flagged id; otherwise it filters args.ids to strings — ids not currently visible are reported back as ignored rather than erroring.

sideEffects.description: writes the onboarding state or the carrier review file on a successful decline; nothing is written for an empty request, an ignored id, or a bad kind

risks: A decline reason is persisted only for the carrier-link kind; the domains path accepts a reason and discards it, since that state stores bare ids.
Requested targets are validated against what is currently flagged, so declining a target that is not presently a gap is silently ignored rather than rejected.
invariants: An unknown or missing kind writes nothing and returns an error listing the valid kinds.
Carrier-link declines record the risk hash alongside the decision.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered in the MCP tool dispatch table; the domains path delegates to mod:repovine/src/mcp/onboarding-state and mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-advisor, and the carrier path to mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-review and mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links.
annotation.dataFlow: tool call with a kind and target ids → validated against the current advisories → merged into the matching workspace-local state → result reporting what was recorded.

annotation.summary: get_config_surface wrapper that turns invalid/unsafe filter results into error envelopes, otherwise adds binding navigation and scoped empty diagnostics.

keyExports.handleGetConfigSurface: Scoped env/secret/resource listing with optional kind and namePattern filters.

assumptions: Reports env var names only — never secret values.
Empty scope uses configSurfaceEmptyDiagnostic helper, with confidence/gaps derived through emptyOutcome(emptyDiagnostic).
risks: Dynamic env access may be under-detected vs declared envDependencies in annotations.
patterns: Env names only — never values — extracted for agent safety.
annotation.flowDescription: scope → scan config + env var names + resource bindings → concise config surface envelope; when result.total is 0 a configSurfaceEmptyDiagnostic is attached and emptyOutcome supplies confidence/gaps, otherwise a fixed best-effort-coverage gap is used.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/config-surface collectConfigSurface; mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/navigation per-binding inspect_node hints; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/empty-diagnostics emptyOutcome/configSurfaceEmptyDiagnostic. Envelope pagination (transitive): mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + filters → collectConfigSurface → envelope.

annotation.summary: `get_entrypoints` MCP tool thin wrapper. Delegates to `lib/entrypoints.collectEntrypoints` (frontend file routes, IaC triggers, Python FastAPI/Django/DRF backend API routes), adds drill-down navigation and `entrypointsEmptyDiagnostic` on zero results.

keyExports.handleGetEntrypoints: Scoped entrypoint listing with kind/layer filters via collectEntrypoints.

assumptions: Entrypoint slots come from stage2 interpreter registry.
Empty scope returns entrypointsEmptyDiagnostic.
risks: Missing layer contributions yield empty entrypoints for non-TS stacks.
patterns: Pairs with trace_flow for user-journey anchoring.
annotation.flowDescription: scope + filters -> list runtime entrypoints (HTTP, queues, schedules) from graph entrypoint store.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/entrypoints; mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store. Envelope pagination (transitive): mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + args -> collectEntrypoints (incl. Python backend api) -> envelope with navigation hints.

annotation.summary: The inspect_node tool handler. Resolves the requested scope, delegates the detail build to the core, attaches the runtime handoff for resource nodes, assembles the navigation hints, and hoists the obligation-carrying investigate references into a top-level attention block so a caller sees what it must look at before treating the node as understood. The advisory structural tags stay inline on the reference and never reach that block.

keyExports.handleInspectNode: The tool entry: scope resolution, detail build, runtime handoff, navigation, and the attention block.
keyExports.selfBoundaryAttention: Attention when the inspected node is itself a boundary surface, gated by the boundary mechanic.
keyExports.selfWiringAttention: Attention when the node sits in the deployed runtime topology, gated by the wiring mechanic and the graph's edge counts.

assumptions: The detail build, including annotation metadata and the investigate tags, belongs to the core module; this handler arranges and hoists rather than deciding what is flagged.
Self-attention is gated through the mechanics registry, so the same predicate decides a self flag here and a neighbour flag elsewhere.
A domain scope resolves through the scope's domain id rather than by string matching.

A body/grep request the node view could not satisfy (a bodyless kind, a malformed regex) is surfaced as a gap on the response, not silently dropped; envelope confidence stays 'high' since the scope itself resolved — confidence answers whether the scope resolved, not whether every requested facet came back.

risks.text: The hub tag is deliberately excluded from the attention block to avoid flooding on a large repository, so a caller must still read the inline investigate tags on high-in-degree references.

risks: Must-inspect pointers are capped in the navigation, so a node with many obligations shows a subset and the rest are reachable only by paging.

A body search on a very large file can hit the time cap; the search then reports the deadline and carries no matches at all, so an incomplete search is distinguishable from an empty one only by that error. The line-length and match-count bounds behave differently — they return partial results and flag the truncation alongside the matches they did assemble.
patterns: Resource nodes get their handler hint pushed to the front of the navigation, so the code that owns the resource is the first thing offered.
A node inspected without a body gets a bounded body hint rather than the body itself.
annotation.flowDescription: nodeId + body/export pagination → buildInspectNodeDetail → annotation meta + navigation hints.
invariants: The hub tag never enters the attention block.
An unresolved scope returns an empty diagnostic with search and map next actions rather than an error.
annotation.integrationPoints: Builds detail through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/inspect-node-core, resolves investigate references through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs, attaches resource handoff through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/runtime-handoff, and gates self-attention through mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry.
annotation.dataFlow: scope resolution → detail build → optional runtime handoff → navigation assembly → attention hoisted from the drill-down, links and investigate pointers → response envelope, with bodyError/grepError surfaced as gaps.

annotation.summary: map_context MCP tool handler. Maps resolved scopes to code-structure overviews: all (repo stats + packages), domain (summary or modules view via lib/domain-map), query (searchGraph fallback), or node path-from-root paginated ancestry. Attaches mapContextEmptyDiagnostic on empty domain/module views.

keyExports.handleMapContext: Scope router with view=summary|modules and pagination.

assumptions: summary and modules views delegate to domain-map helpers.
Query scopes rank on the token index only; semantic ranking reaches searchGraph from search_context alone.

Confidence and gaps split two concerns: a non-empty result with its own error/gap fields still forces confidence 'low'; only when there are no such gaps does confidence fall back to emptyOutcome(emptyDiagnostic)'s verdict (high when no diagnostic, low when there is one).
risks: Domain scopes are path tags — may be runtime-empty for untagged packages.
patterns: summary view first for large domains — paginate with limit/offset.
annotation.flowDescription: scope + view → paginated domain/package summary or module list with connectivity sorting.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/domain-map; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-graph; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/empty-diagnostics emptyOutcome/mapContextEmptyDiagnostic. Domain slice pagination (transitive): mod:repovine/src/mcp/domain-pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + view → resolveScope → domain-map or pathFromRoot or searchGraph → envelope.

annotation.summary: The dispatch table for the public MCP tools: one plain map from tool name to handler, covering the navigation, runtime, dependency, architecture, config and annotation tools plus the advisory, session-quality, and build-status tools. Importing this module also wires the empty-diagnostic collectors, which is how the diagnostics module gets its dependencies without importing the tools back and creating a cycle.

keyExports.toolHandlers: The complete name-to-handler map for all 18 public tools, including get_build_status.

assumptions: The map is a literal listing every public tool by name; the answerable-name set is fixed by the tool definitions and the map is consulted after that gate.
Every handler receives the same runtime context assembled by the MCP server.
The collector wiring happens as an import side effect, before any handler runs.

sideEffects.description: wiring the empty-diagnostic collectors mutates that module's state at import time

risks: The wiring runs on import, so the effect depends on this module being imported before the diagnostics are used; a second registry would silently overwrite the collectors.
A handler added to a tool's own module but not listed here is unreachable, and nothing reports the omission.
patterns: A single dispatch table, so the set of public tools is readable in one place rather than assembled across registrations.
Dependency injection through the wiring call, which is what lets the diagnostics module ask about entrypoints and config without depending on the tools.
annotation.flowDescription: Side-effect import wires empty-diagnostics collectors; mcp/index executeTool looks up toolHandlers[name] after the not-ready gate for every tool except get_build_status, which mcp/index dispatches through this same map ahead of that gate.
invariants: The map supplies the handler for every public tool, including get_build_status; mcp/index special-cases get_build_status to run ahead of the not-ready gate, but it still calls through this map, not a separate path.
The collector wiring precedes any handler invocation because it is an import-time side effect.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imports every handler under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools, wires the collectors declared in mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/empty-diagnostics with the entrypoint and config-surface libraries, and is looked up by mod:repovine/src/mcp when it executes a tool.
annotation.dataFlow: tool call → name looked up in this map → the handler runs with the runtime context → response envelope.

annotation.summary: The search_context handler: tokenized graph search with an AND or OR strategy, an optional semantic ranking boost, escalation of annotation-matched hits into inspect navigation, and a diagnostic explaining an empty result. It pins one engine state snapshot at entry and threads it through every read, so ranking and graph lookups cannot straddle two graph generations across the embedding await.

keyExports.handleSearchContext: The tool entry: token search with type filters and optional semantic boost, over a single pinned state.
keyExports.isWeakRelaxedSearchMatch: Whether a relaxed match is weak enough that the caller should confirm it by inspecting rather than trusting the hit.

assumptions: The match mode controls how tokens combine. Weak tokens carry reduced weight and a smaller candidate budget; the auto-relaxed OR path suppresses them outright when no strong token hits the index, and reports that as weakTokenOnlySuppressed with an empty result.
Annotation-matched top hits are escalated into inspect navigation, since an annotation match means someone already wrote about the node.
Semantic ranking is available only when embeddings are enabled in the workspace configuration.
Auxiliary config/entrypoint matches are a preview capped at AUX_PREVIEW_CAP (5), not a full paginated result — they carry no separate pagination block, just items and a total.
risks: A relaxed match on a single token is a weak signal that needs confirmation by inspection; treating it as an answer is how a search leads somewhere plausible and wrong.
Semantic ranking silently does nothing when embeddings are disabled, so results differ between workspaces without any indication in the response.
patterns: State is captured once and threaded, rather than re-read per step, which is what makes a concurrent refresh unable to mix one generation's ranking onto another's graph.
The primary orienting tool: it is meant to run before any blind file reading on a fuzzy task.
annotation.flowDescription: Query tokens are searched against the index, optionally re-ranked semantically, merged with auxiliary config and entrypoint matches, and returned with navigation.
invariants: Every read inside one call observes the same engine state generation.
The empty diagnostic is omitted when auxiliary config or entrypoint matches exist, since the result is not truly empty.
annotation.integrationPoints: Searches through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-graph with the pinned state, escalates annotation hits through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-annotation-escalation, and folds in auxiliary matches from the config-surface and entrypoint libraries.
annotation.dataFlow: query → pinned state → optional semantic ranking → graph search fusion on that same state → auxiliary matches → response with navigation and, when empty, a diagnostic.

annotation.summary: Read-only tool returning the domain-config suggestions the build already computed, together with two ready-to-write previews: the merged config that excludes the suggested noise, and the keep config that instead marks those resources as deliberately kept so they stay visible and stop being suggested. It never writes; applying a preview is the user's decision.

keyExports.handleSuggestDomainsConfig: Returns the pending suggestions, the merge strategy, and the two config previews with follow-up navigation.

assumptions: The suggestions are computed during the build and merely read here, so this handler never recomputes them.
The two previews are symmetric alternatives for the same suggestion: exclude the resource, or commit a keep marker for it.
Ids the user wants neither to apply nor to keep seeing are recorded through the shared decline tool rather than here.
Verified 2026-07-23: handleSuggestDomainsConfig and its read of stage2 domains-advisor suggestions plus stage2/domains-schema merge strategy unchanged; content-hash refresh only.
risks: Applying a preview without reading it pollutes the committed domains config, which is why the tool returns a preview rather than writing one.
The keep preview appears only when at least one suggestion is of a keepable kind, so its absence means the suggestions offer no keep option rather than that keeping is unavailable in general.
patterns: A passthrough handler: the advisory computation lives in the build pipeline and this tool only presents it with the two actionable shapes.
annotation.flowDescription: The build computes the suggestions into engine state; this handler reads them and returns the additions alongside both config previews.
invariants: The domains config file is never written by this tool.
The keep preview is surfaced only when the suggestions include a keepable kind.
annotation.integrationPoints: Reads the suggestions produced by the domains advisor in the stage2 pipeline and the merge strategy declared in mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-schema; declines are recorded through the shared advisory decline tool in mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/decline-advisory.
annotation.stateShape: The response carries the additions, the merged config, an optional keep config, the merge strategy and the axis metadata.

annotation.summary: MCP trace_flow handler: projects runtime services/resources/data flows, filters services to the resolved scope before pagination, optionally adds entrypoints, runtime handoff, diagnostics, and navigation.

keyExports.handleTraceFlow: Projects scoped runtime topology and reports service totals/truncation from the filtered service set.

assumptions: Runtime services, resources, flows, and entrypoints originate from stage2 interpreter graph facts.
The public tool does not advertise an unimplemented traversal depth or destination constraint.

Emptiness and confidence are read off the unpaged raw slices (servicesRaw/resourcesRaw/dataFlowsRaw/entrypointPage.total), not the paginated page: an offset past the end must not report the scope itself as empty. emptyOutcome(emptyDiagnostic, 'medium') sets confidence; 'no data flow found' is added to gaps only when the scope is not itself empty (services/resources present, no proven flow is a completeness gap, not an emptiness fact).
risks: Missing interpreter facts yield an empty trace with a diagnostic rather than proving no runtime behavior.
Broad topology projections are bounded by pagination.
patterns: User/runtime flow axis — pair with get_entrypoints for entry discovery.
Filter service scope before slice/total/truncated calculation.
annotation.flowDescription: resolveScope → projectRuntimeTopology(ResolvedScope) → paginate services/resources/flows → optional entrypoints/runtime handoff → envelope and empty diagnostic. The projection decides scope membership; the tool does not filter again.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/empty-diagnostics traceFlowEmptyDiagnostic and emptyOutcome.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + include + offset/limit → topology projection → scoped service page and independent resource/flow pages → response totals, handoff, diagnostics, navigation.

annotation.summary: The contract every server tool handler is written against: the shape of the built repository state, the runtime a handler receives, and the handler signature itself. Types only, with no runtime effects of its own.

keyExports.McpToolRuntime: What a handler is handed: accessors for the state and the configuration, a way to trigger a rebuild, the repository root, the optional per-request cancellation signal, and the context session.
keyExports.RefreshRepoStateOptions: Whether a rebuild should also re-read the configuration.
keyExports.RefreshRepoStateResult: Whether the runtime was actually replaced with one built from reloaded configuration.
keyExports.RepovineState: Everything built per graph build: the graph, the snapshot, the module index, the token and semantic indexes, the annotations, the domain configuration and its suggestions, the resolved analysis thresholds, and when it was built.
keyExports.SemanticSearchRefresh: The four possible outcomes of a semantic index sync.

assumptions: The state is replaced whole on each build rather than mutated, which is why the runtime exposes an accessor instead of the object: a handler that reads it once and holds it across a rebuild is working from the previous graph.
The build timestamp travels with the state so a response can say how old the graph behind it is.

The cancellation signal belongs to one request and is raised when the client cancels; a handler that ignores it simply runs to completion, so honouring it is a property of each long-running operation rather than something enforced here.
The context session identifier is placed on the runtime by the executor because the raw arguments are stripped before a handler runs, so a handler cannot recover it from its own arguments.
Identifier resolution is not here: a caller's scope or node argument is read once by resolveScope in mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve, and handlers pass on the resolved id.

risks.text: This is the contract the entire tool surface is written against: a change to the state or runtime shape reaches every handler and the compliance checks at once. Removing or retyping a field fails the build at every reader and at the site that assembles the state, so the cost is the breadth of the edit. What fails quietly instead are the optional runtime fields, which a handler can omit and still compile.

risks: The cancellation signal is optional on the runtime, so a handler written without it compiles and runs unbounded; nothing marks which operations should be honouring it.
patterns: Accessors rather than values, so a handler always reads the current build instead of a captured one.
One types module for the whole tool surface, which is what keeps thirty-odd handlers agreeing on their context without importing each other.
invariants: The state carries the timestamp of the build that produced it.
A handler never receives the state object directly, only a way to fetch the current one.
annotation.integrationPoints: The state is assembled by the server runtime under mod:repovine/src/mcp and consumed by every handler under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools; its parts come from mod:repovine/src/annotations/store, mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-index, mod:repovine/src/semantic/store, mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains and its advisor, mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/config, and mod:repovine/src/context-quality/session-store.
annotation.dataFlow: a build produces the state → the runtime wraps it with accessors, the request signal and the resolved session → a handler reads the current state, may trigger a rebuild, and returns its result.

annotation.summary: The delivery-mechanics registry: the single place declaring which risk-delivery mechanics exist, in what priority, what primitive each reads, and how each is detected. Array order is the tag priority. Detection predicates are referenced from the rule modules that own them rather than reimplemented here, so the registry stays dispatch and the rules stay where they are defined.

keyExports.DELIVERY_MECHANICS: The ordered mechanic entries; array order is the tag priority.
keyExports.DELIVERY_MECHANIC_PRIORITY: The priority list derived from registry order.
keyExports.HUB_IMPORTER_FLOOR: The absolute importer floor for the hub mechanic, also the floor under the adaptive threshold.
keyExports.deliveryMechanic: Lookup by tag id; total, since every tag has a registered mechanic.

assumptions: The registry declares seven mechanics in this order: risk, boundary, effect, unannotated, wiring, co-change, hub.

Annotation-derived detection is referenced from the rule modules that own it; topology-derived detection is declared in the registry itself, including the hub importer floor that other modules re-export from here.
The consumer mechanic emits the tag named risk; that naming skew is inherited and visible in the API responses.
The co-change mechanic is semantically symmetric, but the direction enum has no symmetric value, so it is declared as propagating to keep it out of push admission.

sideEffects.description: a declarative registry with pure detection predicates

risks: Array order is the tag priority, so inserting or reordering an entry changes the priority for every delivery channel at once.
Detection is all the registry currently dispatches: the channel and direction metadata is descriptive, and the delivery machinery does not yet route through it.
The hub mechanic self-gates to false when no importer count is supplied; the threshold falls back to the floor when no adaptive threshold is supplied.
patterns: Adding a mechanic means declaring an entry at its priority slot; each detect self-gates to false when its primitive is absent, so no core edit is needed.
Each entry records which primitive it reads, which keeps the annotation-derived mechanics distinguishable from the topology-derived ones.
invariants: The priority list is the registry order and is pinned by a unit test, so a reorder fails loudly rather than silently changing tag precedence.
The unannotated mechanic is reserved: its detection always returns false and no channel produces it.
The wiring mechanic fires on a resource-to-handler in-edge or a handler-to-resource out-edge; the resource-side relations belong to flow tracing rather than to this mechanic.
The co-change mechanic fires on an implements edge in either direction.
annotation.integrationPoints: Composes predicates from mod:repovine/src/annotations/format and mod:repovine/src/annotations/side-effect-vocab, takes its tag type from mod:repovine/src/types and its context type from mod:repovine/src/mechanics/types, and is consumed by the investigate-reference resolution and the node inspection tool.
annotation.dataFlow: context (node id, annotation, importer count, edge counts, hub threshold) -> each mechanic's detect in registry order -> emitted tags -> callers cap and order them downstream.

annotation.summary: The contract the mechanics registry implements. A mechanic is one detect-and-deliver unit: its trigger is the primitives it reads plus its detection predicate, and its delivery is the channels it reaches plus whether the signal describes the node itself or obligates its consumers. Detection is what the current version actually dispatches; the channel and direction fields document delivery that each surface still performs itself.

keyExports.CHANNELS: The enumerable list of every Channel value, spelled out because the union type itself isn't walkable at runtime.
keyExports.Channel: The delivery surfaces a signal can reach: pull-self, pull-neighbor, pull-carrier, push and advisory.
keyExports.DeliveryMechanic: One mechanic: emitted tag id, the primitives it reads, its direction, its channels, and its detection predicate.
keyExports.DeliveryMechanicContext: The inputs available to detection; only the node id is guaranteed, with the annotation and the topology accessors optional.
keyExports.Primitive: The graph primitive a trigger reads: the three annotation scopes plus absence, and the in-degree, runtime-edge and implements-edge topology inputs.

assumptions: A mechanic is scoped to a language by reading a primitive only some plugins emit, never by a conditional on language; when that primitive is absent, detection simply returns false.
The registry composes the rule predicates from the annotation modules rather than owning them, and is not their only caller.
Repo-specific judgement lives in annotation content, not in the mechanic definitions.

sideEffects.description: type-only module

risks: The channel and direction fields are descriptive in the current version: a reader who assumes the registry routes delivery will not find that machinery here.
patterns: Universal mechanics read primitives every plugin emits, while language-scoped mechanics read one only some plugins emit, so applicability is declared in data rather than branched on in code.
Every optional context input corresponds to a mechanic that self-gates without it.
invariants: Detection is total: it returns false rather than throwing when the mechanic's primitive is absent from the context.
Only the node id is guaranteed on the context; every other input is optional by contract.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implemented by mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry; the tag and annotation types come from mod:repovine/src/types and the edge vocabulary from mod:repovine/src/graph/model. The context is assembled by the investigate-reference resolution in the MCP layer.
annotation.dataFlow: graph and annotation state -> a context assembled by the caller -> each mechanic's detection -> emitted tags rendered per surface.

annotation.summary: Filesystem layout resolution for the engine: finds the workspace root (REPOVINE_ROOT override, else the nearest ancestor holding .git), names the committed config files, and derives the .repovine artifacts and cache directories. Owns the containment check that keeps a configured annotations path inside the repo. The engine scan-ignore merge previously documented here (mergeScanIgnorePatterns / REPOVINE_ENGINE_SCAN_IGNORE_PATTERNS) is no longer exported by this module — current export set is findRepoRoot, findWorkspaceRootWithin, resolveWorkspaceRoot, domainsConfigFilePath, resolveAnnotationsFilePath, cacheDirFor, repoRoot, packageRoot, ARTIFACTS_DIR_NAME, DOMAINS_CONFIG_FILENAME, ANNOTATIONS_FILENAME, artifactsDir, cacheDir.

keyExports.ARTIFACTS_DIR_NAME: Name of the engine artifacts directory, .repovine.
keyExports.artifactsDir: The .repovine directory for the process workspace root.
keyExports.cacheDir: Cache directory for the process workspace root.
keyExports.cacheDirFor: Cache directory for a given artifacts directory; the per-repoRoot form.
keyExports.domainsConfigFilePath: Absolute path to repovine.domains.json for a repo root.
keyExports.findRepoRoot: Walks parent directories until one contains .git.
keyExports.findWorkspaceRootWithin: Finds a workspace root at or below a starting directory, if any.
keyExports.packageRoot: repovine package root resolved eagerly at module load.
keyExports.repoRoot: Workspace root resolved eagerly at module load.
keyExports.resolveAnnotationsFilePath: Validates a repo-relative annotations path and returns it absolute.
keyExports.resolveWorkspaceRoot: Resolves the workspace root from the REPOVINE_ROOT override, else from the cwd walk.

assumptions: The annotations path is a repo-relative value from workspace configuration; REPOVINE_ANNOTATIONS_FILE overrides it and is validated by the same containment check.
repoRoot and packageRoot are resolved once at module load, which suits CLI and MCP cold start but fixes them for the process lifetime.
A repo is identified by the presence of .git in an ancestor directory.
Engine scan-ignore merging moved out of this module; a caller looking for mergeScanIgnorePatterns should locate it under the stage1 scan-root resolution path instead.

sideEffects.description: findRepoRoot and package-root resolution stat .git and package.json while walking parents
reads REPOVINE_ROOT during workspace root resolution

risks: Using the process-wide cacheDir for a repo root other than the process workspace writes the snapshot cache to the wrong place; cacheDirFor(artifactsDir) is the multi-root form.

risks.text: Callers handling more than one repo root must pass that root explicitly rather than relying on the eagerly resolved repoRoot and cacheDir constants, which are fixed at module load.

patterns: Eager root resolution at module load keeps CLI and MCP cold start free of repeated parent walks.
invariants: resolveAnnotationsFilePath rejects an absolute path and any .. escape that would leave the repo root.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/annotations/store for the annotations file, mod:repovine/src/mcp/context for artifact and cache locations, mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-schema for the domains config path, and stage1 scan-root resolution.
annotation.dataFlow: cwd or REPOVINE_ROOT → resolveWorkspaceRoot → repoRoot → absolute paths for the config, domains and annotations files plus the .repovine artifacts and cache directories.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_ROOT: Overrides the cwd parent walk when resolving the workspace root

annotation.summary: Opt-in build profiler for the repovine graph pipeline. A process-global singleton records RSS and heap deltas per named phase, accumulates PerfCounters over the build (packages, modules, imports/exports, infra, templates, graph nodes/edges, search tokens, snapshot bytes), appends a crash trail to disk, and prints a summary table. Entirely inert unless REPOVINE_PROFILE is set.

keyExports.MemoryProfiler: The profiler singleton reached via ensure(): phase(), setCounter/addCounter, measureJsonBytes, summaryLines(), logSummary(), reset().
keyExports.MemorySnapshot: RSS and heap figures in MB: rssMb, heapUsedMb, heapTotalMb, externalMb, arrayBuffersMb.
keyExports.PerfCounters: Build metric totals accumulated across the pipeline.
keyExports.PhaseRecord: One phase measurement: label, elapsedMs, deltaRssMb, deltaHeapMb.
keyExports.isProfileEnabled: True when the REPOVINE_PROFILE env flag is on.
keyExports.isProfileGcEnabled: True when the REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC env flag is on; forced GC needs node --expose-gc.
keyExports.profilePhase: Sync phase marker wrapping fn with a phase() boundary.
keyExports.profilePhaseAsync: Async phase marker wrapping a promise-returning fn.

assumptions: Profiling is off unless REPOVINE_PROFILE is 1 or true; the flags are read through a helper rather than a static process.env member, so the graph's static env detection only picks up REPOVINE_PROFILE_FILE, not REPOVINE_PROFILE or REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC.
Optional forced GC requires node --expose-gc when REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC is set.
REPOVINE_PROFILE_FILE overrides the crash-trail path; otherwise it falls back to a cwd default.

sideEffects.description: reads REPOVINE_PROFILE, REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC and REPOVINE_PROFILE_FILE at call time
writes and appends the crash-trail file via fs.writeFileSync/appendFileSync
globalThis.__repovineProfiler singleton shared across stage1 and stage2
calls global.gc() between phases when REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC is enabled

risks: Peak heap must stay a reduce rather than Math.max(...phases): the spread throws RangeError on the ~130k-phase arrays a long-lived process accumulates.
reset() must clear counters as well as phases, or a build reports the previous build's searchIndexTokens through the process-global singleton.
Trail truncation is isMainThread-gated so a Stage 2 worker isolate does not wipe the main thread's Stage 1 trail.
Forced GC skews phase timing when enabled, so profiled durations are not comparable to an unprofiled run.
patterns: Zero-cost when disabled: phase markers short-circuit before taking a memory reading.
One globalThis singleton spans stage1 and stage2 so counters survive the pipeline boundary.
invariants: With REPOVINE_PROFILE unset the profiler is a no-op: no counters, no phases, no file writes.
PhaseRecord carries the MemorySnapshot fields plus label, elapsedMs, deltaRssMb and deltaHeapMb.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by mod:repovine/src/stage1, mod:repovine/src/stage2 and mod:repovine/src/mcp/context, which resets at pipeline start and calls logSummary after the last counter is set.
annotation.dataFlow: REPOVINE_PROFILE=1 → profilePhase/profilePhaseAsync mark build boundaries → phase() records RSS/heap deltas → setCounter/addCounter accumulate PerfCounters → crash trail appended → logSummary prints the table.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_PROFILE_FILE: Overrides the crash-trail file path (default under cwd)

annotation.summary: Facade re-export of compareCodeUnits from @repovine/plugin-sdk so every engine sort that touches the graph (package order, node payload lists, persisted artifacts) compares the same bytes as the SDK's own discovery-order sort. Declares no exports of its own.
assumptions: Locale collation must stay out of the projection path; this module exists so engine code never reaches for localeCompare directly, only for the re-exported comparator.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/ordering (compareCodeUnits) verbatim — one import hop, no local logic; see the SDK module for the ICU/locale rationale.

annotation.summary: Single place engine callers read the path vocabulary from. Re-exports six functions declared in @repovine/plugin-sdk (toPosixPath, hostPathKey, repoRelativePosix, normalizeRelPath, lastPathSegment, pathMatchKey, hostKeyedView) and declares one function of its own, resolveRelPath: normalizeRelPath with '.' dropped and '..' resolved against the segments before it.

keyExports.resolveRelPath: (value: string): string — normalizeRelPath output with '.' segments dropped and '..' resolved against preceding segments. Answers 'which file is this', where the unresolved (normalizeRelPath) form answers 'does this string match the pattern the user wrote'.

assumptions: toPosixPath, hostPathKey, repoRelativePosix, normalizeRelPath, lastPathSegment, pathMatchKey and hostKeyedView are declared in @repovine/plugin-sdk, not this file; this module re-exports them so engine callers read the whole path vocabulary from one place instead of importing the SDK directly.

Security-sensitive containment checks (e.g. harness attach path-overlap) must not use the relaxed hostPathKey/resolveRelPath forms; containment keeps its own strict case-sensitive comparison in src/fs/containment.ts.
A config glob is matched against the unresolved path the user wrote (normalizeRelPath), while resolveRelPath produces the resolved file identity; the two deliberately diverge on inputs like 'a/../b'.
risks: resolveRelPath resolves '..' by popping the preceding segment; a value with more leading '..' segments than preceding segments silently drops the extras (pop on an empty array is a no-op) instead of surfacing the out-of-bounds reference as invalid.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports the path vocabulary declared in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/paths and mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/module-id; resolveRelPath is declared here for callers that need the resolved (not just normalized) relative path.

annotation.summary: Text vocabulary for making a value short enough to show (shortenWords/shortenList/omittedNote) and for splitting an identifier into words (splitCamelCase); re-exports the character-budget primitive (SHORTENED_MARKER, shortenText) from @repovine/plugin-sdk so engine callers read the whole vocabulary from one module.

keyExports.omittedNote: Renders an omitted count as ' (+N more)' (leading space), or '' when nothing was dropped.
keyExports.shortenList: First maxItems entries of a readonly array plus an `omitted` count; sized in items, not characters.
keyExports.shortenWords: At most maxWords words, marker (SHORTENED_MARKER) appended when cut; collapses whitespace runs, cuts on word boundaries rather than mid-word.
keyExports.splitCamelCase: Inserts spaces at word boundaries in an identifier via two regex passes (lower-to-upper, and an uppercase run followed by a capitalized word) so acronyms like HTTPServerAdapter read as 'HTTP Server Adapter'.

assumptions: Distinct from src/response/truncation.ts (which reports that a bound was hit) and from scanLinesWithRegex's read-window bound (which reports what was never searched) — this module owns the act of shortening a value that IS being shown, not reporting the cut.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates the character-budget primitive to mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk (SHORTENED_MARKER, shortenText), declared there beside the fact schemas so plugins and the engine cut facts the same way.

annotation.summary: Builds the per-run DeclarationCatalog by merging every active plugin's stamped package.json#repovine declarations across 5 families (dir, value, resource-kind, trigger-type, runtime-action). Each family is keyed compositely (dirKey/valueKey/resourceKindKey/triggerTypeKey/runtimeActionKey); declarations under one key with an identical effect become one record listing every declaring plugin, while declarations under one key with differing effects become a DeclarationConflict and both sides are dropped (no last-write-wins). plugins.retract selectors are applied after merge, removing keys from the decided catalog rather than from one plugin's input.

keyExports.DeclarationCatalog: The merged shape: dirs/values/resourceKinds/triggerTypes/runtimeActions records plus conflicts and retractions.
keyExports.buildDeclarationCatalog: Merges input.catalogs across all 5 families via mergeFamily, then applies input.retract selectors; returns the DeclarationCatalog.
keyExports.catalogResourceKindMeta: Looks up a resource-kind record's effect (service/hasCodeHandler) by (namespace, provider, kind) query.
keyExports.catalogRuntimeActionNamespace: Looks up the namespace a runtime action's effect declares.
keyExports.catalogTriggerTypeMeta: Looks up a trigger-type record's effect by (type, namespace, provider) query.
keyExports.emptyDeclarationCatalog: Returns a DeclarationCatalog with every family/conflicts/retractions empty.

assumptions: Key order and plugin registration order never affect the merged outcome (keys and owners are both sorted before comparison).
A retraction selector matching nothing is still recorded in `retractions` with an empty `removed` array, so a no-op retraction is visible rather than silent.

sideEffects.description: lookupsByCatalog WeakMap memoizes per-catalog key lookups so repeated queries against the same catalog object skip re-deriving the lookup map

risks: Declarations under one key with differing effects drop BOTH sides as a DeclarationConflict rather than picking either; a plugin author expecting last-registered-wins semantics silently loses their declaration entirely.

annotation.summary: Host-provided document loaders (yaml/json/text) that decode a source plugin's raw file bytes into positional LoadedDocument values; a parser names one loader id and never reads the file itself.

keyExports.HOST_DOCUMENT_LOADERS: [yamlLoader, jsonLoader, textLoader] array of DocumentLoader, each id-keyed and returning positional() documents
keyExports.TAG_TOLERANT_YAML_SCHEMA: js-yaml DEFAULT_SCHEMA extended with catch-all scalar/sequence/mapping types that resolve any unknown local tag (e.g. CloudFormation !Ref/!Sub/!If) to its underlying value instead of throwing

assumptions: Documents in a multi-document file are keyed by source position (documentKey = string index) since position is the only identity a multi-document file can promise
risks: TAG_TOLERANT_YAML_SCHEMA discards the unknown YAML tag name itself and keeps only the value underneath, so a document whose meaning depends on which tag was used loses that distinction silently.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implements the DocumentLoader contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/plugin/document-loader

annotation.summary: Host-side registry of the active IaC parsers, document loaders, and kind-to-graph-domain metadata for the current build isolate. installIaCPlugins replaces the whole set atomically per build, so a plugin dropped from config takes its parsers, loaders, and domain metadata with it together.

keyExports.getInfraKindDomain: Maps an infra kind to its declared InfraKindDomain, or a conventional domain:infra-<kind> fallback (via domainLabelSlug/domainNodeId) for kinds no plugin declared metadata for.
keyExports.getParsers: Returns the currently installed IaCParser list.
keyExports.installIaCPlugins: Replaces parsers/documentLoaders/kindDomains from a list of ActiveIaCPlugin; a loader id already held by another plugin is refused and recorded as a LoaderRegistrationConflict rather than silently overwritten; no-op while setParsersForTest has pinned parsers.
keyExports.resolveLoaderForFile: Resolves which document loader decodes a (base, ext) file; a by-name fileMatch claim outranks a by-extension claim, and two equally-specific claims naming different loaders return status 'ambiguous' instead of picking one.
keyExports.setParsersForTest: Test-only: pins the parser list to a caller-built array; returned callback restores the previous list and unpins.

assumptions: Installed order is an inventory, not a precedence: every parser whose fileMatch/supports() claims a document is offered it, and a disagreement is reported (ambiguous/conflict) rather than settled by registration order.

sideEffects.description: module-level mutable registry: parsers, activePlugins, documentLoaders, kindDomains, pinnedParsers

risks: Unknown infra kinds fall back to a per-kind domain:infra-<kind> node rather than a shared default, replacing an earlier behavior that sent unmatched kinds to infra-sam.
