annotation.summary: The single plugin loading path for both the bundled preset and user-installed packages: resolvePluginPackage resolves each package via createRequire (repo root vs the engine's own install), validatePluginManifest/validatePluginRuntimeDescriptor from @repovine/plugin-sdk check the manifest and descriptor, an entry-containment check (isInsidePackage + realpath) rejects an entry that resolves outside its own package directory, importDefaultExport dynamically imports the plugin's default export, wrapUntrustedSourcePlugin/wrapUntrustedParser Zod-validate every emitted module/infra delta before it can reach the graph, and loadPluginSet assembles the per-build PluginLoadReport (loaded/refused/disabled/runtime) by delegating capability installation to source-set.ts and iac-set.ts and runtime assembly to runtime.ts.

keyExports.defaultPluginsConfig: Default PluginsConfigInput for a build with no `plugins` section: { defaults: true, add: [], disable: [] }
keyExports.ensurePluginsLoaded: Fire-and-forget wrapper around loadPluginSet for callers that only need the install side effect
keyExports.getActivePluginIds: Returns currently active plugin ids as { source: string[], iac: string[] }
keyExports.loadPluginSet: Loads a PluginLoadSpec (repoRoot + config), resolves/validates/installs source and IaC plugins, returns PluginLoadReport
keyExports.presetDeclarationCatalog: Builds the declaration catalog contributed by the bundled preset's plugins, reporting packages that failed to resolve

assumptions: A plugin listed in config.plugins.add resolves via Node's createRequire anchored at the analyzed repo's package.json
Bundled preset plugins resolve via the engine's own installation (createRequire(import.meta.url))

sideEffects.description: reads plugin package.json and resolves/verifies entry files via fs.readFileSync/fs.existsSync/fs.realpathSync
dynamic import() of each plugin package's default export, executing third-party code in-process

risks: Arbitrary code from a plugin package executes via dynamic import() once listed in config.plugins.add; manifest/entry-containment validation runs first but the imported code itself is not sandboxed.

annotation.summary: Assembles one build's PluginRuntime from the plugins loaded for it: buildPluginRuntime sorts members/loaders/contributors by owner plugin id (via compareCodeUnits) so config order does not affect the result, merges per-plugin declarations into one DeclarationCatalog through buildDeclarationCatalog, and turns catalog conflicts into published Refusals (DECLARATION_CONFLICT_REFUSAL) instead of picking a side. pluginRuntimeIdentity derives the structural fingerprint (plugin versions, catalog identity, loader/projector ids) that snapshot-reuse decisions compare across builds.

keyExports.PluginRuntime: Interface: { members, catalog, contributors, loaders, refusals }
keyExports.PluginRuntimeInput: Interface: { plugins: [{owner, capabilities, declarations, loaders?, projectors?}], retract? }
keyExports.buildPluginRuntime: Builds a sorted PluginRuntime (members, catalog, contributors, loaders, refusals) from a PluginRuntimeInput
keyExports.emptyPluginRuntime: Empty PluginRuntime for zero-plugin builds or isolates with no loaded plugin code
keyExports.pluginRuntimeIdentity: Structural fingerprint of a PluginRuntime used to decide snapshot reuse across builds

risks: Two plugins declaring the same catalog key with different effects both lose that declaration (published as a conflict Refusal); neither side's declaration is applied and the build proceeds with the rest of the catalog.

annotation.summary: Process-local store for the live (function-valued) half of a build's PluginRuntime, keyed by RepositoryFactsSnapshot object identity in a module-level WeakMap. rememberPluginRuntime records the runtime that produced a snapshot; getPluginRuntime looks it up and falls back to emptyPluginRuntime() when nothing was recorded in this isolate (a snapshot restored from cache, or read inside a different worker than the one that loaded the plugins).

keyExports.getPluginRuntime: Returns the PluginRuntime recorded for a snapshot, or emptyPluginRuntime() if none was recorded in this isolate
keyExports.rememberPluginRuntime: Stores the PluginRuntime that produced a given RepositoryFactsSnapshot, keyed by object identity

sideEffects.description: mutates the module-level WeakMap runtimeBySnapshot (runtimeBySnapshot.set)

risks.text: Callers of getPluginRuntime must verify they run in the same process/isolate that called rememberPluginRuntime for that snapshot; otherwise catalog/contributors/loaders are silently unavailable (emptyPluginRuntime, no error).

annotation.summary: Ambient, process-wide registry of the active SourcePlugin set for the current build isolate. `installSourcePlugins` replaces the module-level `plugins` array (a no-op while a test has pinned it via setSourcePluginsForTest); accessors (getSourcePlugins, getSourcePlugin, getActiveSourcePluginIds) and file-matching (sourcePluginMatchesFile, pickSourcePluginIdForFile) read it. Capability aggregators (getKnownExtensions, getSourceStripSuffixes, getModuleIdStripSuffixes, getSourceIndexBasenames) union each plugin's declared capabilities into path-normalization helpers (stripSourceExtension, stripModuleIdSuffix, stripIndexBasename, hasKnownSourceExtension) and per-plugin flags (pluginHasUiSurfaces, pluginUsesLooseNameSeparators).

keyExports.getKnownExtensions: Union of capabilities.extensions across installed plugins.
keyExports.getSourcePlugins: Returns the currently installed plugin set.
keyExports.installSourcePlugins: Replaces the active plugin set unless a test pin (setSourcePluginsForTest) is in effect.
keyExports.pickSourcePluginIdForFile: First installed plugin's id whose fileMatch claims (base, ext).
keyExports.setSourcePluginsForTest: Test-only: pins the set to given plugins and returns a restore callback that unpins.
keyExports.sourcePluginMatchesFile: True when (base, ext) matches a plugin's fileMatch (fileNames/extensions/fileNamePatterns).

assumptions: Order among installed plugins only matters when two plugins claim the same file; the bundled set uses non-overlapping extensions so order is not load-bearing there.
Every entrypoint is expected to install the plugin set (via src/plugin-host/load.ts) before reading it; nothing here self-installs.

sideEffects.description: module-level `plugins` array and `pinned` flag hold ambient, process-wide plugin-set state read by every isolate

risks.text: Capability/read functions (getKnownExtensions, stripSourceExtension, pluginHasUiSurfaces, etc.) answer over whatever set is currently installed; a caller running before src/plugin-host/load.ts's install step sees an empty/undefined-plugin answer instead of an error.

annotation.summary: CLI dev entry for memory-profiling a cold graph build: validates a writable workspace root, defaults REPOVINE_PROFILE to 1 before static imports, loads engine modules, bootstraps RepovineRuntime with coldSnapshot, and prints node count plus the MemoryProfiler's heap/RSS summary to stdout.
assumptions: Invoked via npm run profile or node --expose-gc dist/profile.js from repo root.
REPOVINE_PROFILE is set before the MemoryProfiler singleton is first constructed; the profiler reads the flag at construction rather than at module load.
Workspace root resolved via paths.repoRoot / REPOVINE_ROOT must be writable.

sideEffects.description: process.exit(1) on invalid or non-writable repo root
mkdir probe under .repovine/.cache
defaults process.env.REPOVINE_PROFILE, enabling MemoryProfiler when the caller has not already set the variable
profiling status and node-count/RSS memory summary

risks: Running from the wrong cwd produces a misleading memory baseline and node counts.
patterns: Cold snapshot build isolates RSS baseline for graph build profiling.
annotation.flowDescription: assertWritableRepoRoot (.repovine/.cache probe) → loadConfig → await RepovineRuntime.create with coldSnapshot → MemoryProfiler table to stdout.
invariants: Dev-only entry — not used by the production MCP server path.
process.exit(1) when the repo root is missing, is not a directory, or is not writable under its artifacts dir.
annotation.integrationPoints: npm run profile CLI entry; mod:repovine/src/perf/memory-profiler (MemoryProfiler.ensure) and mod:repovine/src/mcp/context (RepovineRuntime.create) do the real work.
annotation.dataFlow: assertWritableRepoRoot (.repovine/.cache probe) -> loadConfig -> RepovineRuntime.create with coldSnapshot:true -> node count and MemoryProfiler table to stdout.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_PROFILE: Defaults to '1' at startup before imports. A value inherited from the caller wins, so 0 or empty runs this entry with MemoryProfiler instrumentation off and produces no profile table.

annotation.summary: Closed vocabulary of reasons an MCP response came back empty (the request was answered and the answer is nothing, distinct from a refusal). Declared as a leaf so the diagnostics producer and the context-quality scorer can share one set of string literals without importing each other.

keyExports.EMPTY_DIAGNOSTIC_REASONS: Const tuple of the 24 known reason strings (e.g. 'graph_empty', 'scope_unresolved', 'no_dependency_edges', 'finding_not_found').
keyExports.EmptyDiagnosticReason: Type: the union of EMPTY_DIAGNOSTIC_REASONS members.
keyExports.SCOPE_UNRESOLVED: Const 'scope_unresolved', the one member Context Session Quality matches on by name when counting a session's unresolved scopes off the published response.

assumptions: mcp/response/empty-diagnostics.ts (producer) and context-quality/metrics.ts (consumer) must not import each other; both import this leaf instead so the shared string literal can't drift between them.
annotation.integrationPoints: Named-by-value contract consumed by mcp/response/empty-diagnostics.ts (produces reasons from this set) and context-quality/metrics.ts (matches SCOPE_UNRESOLVED to score sessions).

annotation.summary: One shape (NextCall) for 'the next tool call an answer offers to make', unifying what had grown five separate spellings across the envelope's navigation, attention.next, empty-diagnostics, a finding's nextCalls, and annotation-health prose.

keyExports.NextCall: { tool?, args?, reason } — tool absent means the same tool the caller just used with different arguments; args absent means it takes none; reason is never absent.
keyExports.dedupeNextCalls: Drops repeat tool+args pairs, keeping the first reason given for each.
keyExports.nextCall: nextCall(tool, args, reason) constructor; argument order matches the reading order 'call this, with this, because of that'.
keyExports.renderNextCall: Renders a NextCall as 'tool(args) — reason' text for CLI/text surfaces, or just reason when tool is absent.

invariants: tool absent means same tool, different args; args absent means no arguments needed; reason is never optional.

annotation.summary: Layer-neutral vocabulary for 'how do we know this' tags attached to graph/response facts: a closed ProvenanceMethod enum plus the ProvenanceBasis (declared/computed/inferred/absent) each method maps to.

keyExports.PROVENANCE_METHODS: Array of all ProvenanceMethod keys, derived from BASIS_BY_METHOD so the table stays total.
keyExports.Provenance: Interface { basis: ProvenanceBasis; method: ProvenanceMethod } attached to facts elsewhere in responses.
keyExports.ProvenanceBasis: Type: 'declared' | 'computed' | 'inferred' | 'absent' — the trust grade a reader acts on.
keyExports.ProvenanceSchema: Zod strictObject schema validating a Provenance value against the same basis/method enums.
keyExports.provenance: Builds a Provenance ({basis, method}) from a ProvenanceMethod via the fixed BASIS_BY_METHOD table.

assumptions: basis is always derived from method via BASIS_BY_METHOD, never set independently, so the two cannot disagree.
invariants: BASIS_BY_METHOD covers every ProvenanceMethod key (PROVENANCE_METHODS is Object.keys of it), so provenance() never returns an undefined basis for a valid method.

annotation.summary: Canonical Outcome<T>/Refusal convention: an expected, caller-recoverable failure travels as a value (Refusal) instead of a throw; a broken engine invariant still throws; a successful-but-empty answer is a separate convention (mcp/response/empty-diagnostics.ts). Replaces the engine's prior per-site spellings ({ok:false,error}, {status:'failed',error}, bare undefined, etc.).

keyExports.Outcome: { ok: true, value } | { ok: false, refusal }.
keyExports.REFUSAL_REASONS: Closed list: not-found, unsupported, unreadable, rejected-by-policy, conflict, not-ready, incomplete.
keyExports.Refusal: { reason, kind, message, details? } — kind names which site produced it (among a producer's own refusals); message reaches the user verbatim.
keyExports.delivered: Wrap a value as a successful Outcome.
keyExports.deliveredValue: Unwrap an Outcome's value; throws if refused — used only where the caller already established the outcome is answerable.
keyExports.isRefused: Narrowing predicate for the ok:false arm.
keyExports.publishedRefusalMessage: Read the refusal message off an already-serialized tool result's result.error, so every reader of a published response (transport error flag, session-quality scorer) parses through one function.
keyExports.refused: Build a { ok: false, refusal } Outcome.

invariants: REFUSAL_REASONS is closed — a new reason requires adding to this list, not inventing a synonym at the call site.
deliveredValue throws for a refused Outcome; it is the throw-convention boundary, used only at call sites that already ruled out the refusal case.

annotation.summary: The one shape a bounded/paged MCP answer is reported in: Truncation/TruncationMap types plus constructor functions per remainder-reachability kind (page, arg, narrow, inline, unavailable) and their Zod schemas. Layer-neutral by construction — imports nothing from the graph or MCP response layers.

keyExports.Truncation: { shown, total?, unit, more } — total absent means unknown, never zero.
keyExports.TruncationMap: Record<string, Truncation> keyed by the bounded field name.
keyExports.TruncationMore: Discriminated union: page | arg | narrow | inline | unavailable.
keyExports.TruncationUnit: 'item' | 'char' | 'line' | 'match' | 'name' — the scale shown/total are counted on.
keyExports.argTruncation: Bound whose remainder a different value of a named, tool-schema-declared argument returns.
keyExports.inlineTruncation: Bound whose remainder is already elsewhere in the same response; hint names where.
keyExports.narrowTruncation: Bound whose remainder needs a narrower request (or a tool that traverses without the cap).
keyExports.pageTruncation: Bound a page of a list with a known total; returns undefined once the page reaches the end (decided by nextOffset >= total, not by `shown`); an empty page at a non-zero offset restarts at 0 instead of advancing.
keyExports.truncationMap: Collect several named bounds into one block, dropping any that did not bite; returns undefined if none did.
keyExports.unavailableTruncation: Bound whose remainder no call returns at any price (dropped during extraction, never kept).

invariants: total absent on a Truncation means unknown, never zero.
page's `arg` names its offset argument explicitly because three offset args coexist on some tools (offset, exportOffset, bodyOffset) and a guessed one pages the wrong list.

annotation.summary: Compiles workspace scan include/exclude globs into matcher objects and answers per path whether source or infra walk should descend. Each pattern carries a scope, so a path can be excluded from infra while visible to source. Engine-owned paths always skipped.

keyExports.CompiledScanPattern: A compiled pattern: a GlobMatcher (not regex) and the scope it applies to.
keyExports.CompiledScanPatterns: The compiled include and exclude sets.
keyExports.compileScanPatterns: Compiles configured patterns into scoped sets.
keyExports.shouldScanSourcePath: Gate for source discovery; declaration files scanned only when explicitly included.

assumptions: Include evaluated before exclude.
Engine artifact paths always skipped.
Patterns are scoped per walk.
risks: Over-broad exclude hides modules entirely rather than signaling config error.
Excluding only for infra scope leaves source walk indexing it.
patterns: Compile once, answer per path.
annotation.flowDescription: Configured patterns compile once into scoped include and exclude sets, and each candidate path is then tested against them for the walk that is asking.
invariants: Include is checked before exclude.
The engine-owned path check always applies, whatever the configuration says.
annotation.integrationPoints: Patterns from workspace config via mod:repovine/src/paths; gates applied by stage1 file walk and source plugin discovery.
annotation.stateShape: Two arrays of compiled patterns, each entry pairing a regex with the scope it applies to.

annotation.summary: What a caller's scope argument turned out to be: the ResolvedScope type, the runtime list of every kind it can resolve to, and the whole-repository default. Types and two constants, no runtime behaviour.

keyExports.ALL_SCOPE: The whole repository — what an absent scope argument resolves to.
keyExports.ResolvedScope: The resolved form of a scope argument: raw text, resolved id, kind, and the node/domain/package/query it named.
keyExports.SCOPE_KINDS: Every kind a scope argument can resolve to, as a runtime list.

assumptions: Layer-neutral by construction: this module imports nothing, because the architecture detectors under src/analysis consume a resolved scope and import nothing from src/mcp.
The resolver that produces these values is resolveScope in mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve; it stays in the MCP layer because it needs the runtime state.
patterns: Runtime list plus derived union, so consumers can enumerate the kinds instead of restating them.
invariants: SCOPE_KINDS is the list, ScopeKind is derived from it: a kind cannot exist in the type without existing at runtime.
A kind added here is unanswered by the architecture and topology consumers until each is taught it; test/laws/scope-resolution holds them to answering every kind.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve (produces it), mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/scope and mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/topology (expand or refuse it), and mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope (publishes it).
annotation.dataFlow: caller's scope string → resolveScope → ResolvedScope → detector id sets / runtime-topology membership / response envelope.

annotation.summary: Deterministic natural-language cards for semantic embedding: projectNodeCards walks eligible graph nodes, gates out identifier-only nodes via cardHasSemanticSignal, and buildNodeCard/buildNodeCardProjection fold exports plus annotation summary/invariants/risks/flow/integration/keyExports into a char-budgeted card.

keyExports.NodeCardProjection: Full projection of one card: truncated text, full text, char counts, a truncated flag, and a per-field retained-char breakdown.
keyExports.SEMANTIC_CARD_CHAR_BUDGET: Character budget (1000) the card text is truncated to, sized conservatively under the embedder's roughly 256-token window.
keyExports.SEMANTIC_CARD_NODE_TYPES: Set of node types eligible for a card: module, runtime-resource, template, package, domain (capabilities/export-symbols excluded).
keyExports.SemanticCardField: The named segments a card is built from: identity, description, exports, summary, invariants, risks, flow, integration, keyExports.
keyExports.buildNodeCard: Returns just the truncated card text from buildNodeCardProjection.
keyExports.buildNodeCardProjection: Builds the full card projection for a node: identity/path/description/exports segments plus annotation-derived segments, truncated to the char budget.
keyExports.projectNodeCards: Walks all graph nodes, keeps only ones with semantic signal (cardHasSemanticSignal), and returns nodeId -> card text for the embedding corpus.

assumptions: SEMANTIC_CARD_NODE_TYPES is declared with 'satisfies readonly NodeType[]', so a NodeType rename breaks this file at compile time.
Module graph node id equals ModuleInfo.id (both carry the mod: prefix), so lookups go straight through modulesById.
An identifier-only node (no exports, no annotation-derived segments) is skipped by cardHasSemanticSignal and stays discoverable through the token index instead.
Card text is rebuilt from the graph and annotations on every sync; the embedding store re-embeds only cards whose text hash changed.
risks: Stale annotation prose stays embedded until the node is re-annotated and a semantic sync runs.
patterns: Graph-node RAG: a semantic hit is a node id that plugs directly into inspect_node/analyze_dependencies, not a text chunk.
stringValues folds a structured integrationPoints/dataFlow value (Record<string,string>) into 'key: value' card lines.
annotation.flowDescription: refresh_context's semantic sync calls projectNodeCards, which calls buildNodeCard/buildNodeCardProjection per eligible node to build the nodeId -> card text embedding corpus before the embedding store syncs it.
invariants: Card text is capped at SEMANTIC_CARD_CHAR_BUDGET (1000 chars); MAX_EXPORTS_PER_CARD (30) caps the exports segment.
annotationCardSegments folds summary, invariants, risks, flowDescription, dataFlow, integrationPoints and keyExports, in that fixed order, before the description and exports segments.
Annotating a previously identifier-only node promotes it into the semantic index on the next sync, with no threshold or config flag.
annotation.integrationPoints: Uses mod:repovine/src/annotations/format (normalizeRisks) to render risk lines; consumed by the semantic-index sync step that builds the embedding corpus before the embedding store's sync runs.
annotation.dataFlow: semantic sync -> projectNodeCards (signal gate via cardHasSemanticSignal) -> buildNodeCard/buildNodeCardProjection per eligible node -> nodeId -> card text embedding corpus.

annotation.summary: The local embedding backend behind semantic search. Inference runs in process against a small MiniLM model at full precision (fp32), with no cloud call and no external daemon. The library that provides it (@huggingface/transformers) is an opt-in peer dependency the engine does not pull, because its ONNX runtime is ~700MB, orders of magnitude larger than the engine itself.

keyExports.Embedder: The contract: a stable id and a batch embed() that preserves input order.
keyExports.__setTransformersModuleForTest: Test seam: injects a fake transformers module and clears the pipeline memo.
keyExports.createEmbedder: Returns an embedder for DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL, or null when embeddings are disabled.
keyExports.disposeEmbedderPipelines: Releases every loaded ONNX session and clears the pipeline memo (exit-path hygiene).
keyExports.importTransformersFromWorkspace: Loads the library from a workspace-rooted resolution, unwrapping CJS/ESM interop.
keyExports.localEmbedderId: Builds the cache-invalidation id from model + resolved transformers version + PIPELINE_DTYPE.
keyExports.resolveModelCacheDir: Per-platform model cache dir; REPOVINE_MODEL_CACHE overrides, else the OS cache convention.

assumptions: Lookup is two-step: a bare specifier import first, then a resolution rooted at workspaceRoot. The second step is what makes `npm install @huggingface/transformers` in the workspace take effect when repovine runs from an npx cache that never sees the workspace's node_modules.

The inference serializer (embedSerialize) and the pipeline memo (pipelineByModel) are module-scoped, shared across every embedder instance, not held per instance — a refresh/reloadConfig can leave two generations' embedders live at once; per-instance state would run concurrent ONNX inference and double the model in RAM.
The pipeline memo is keyed by `${workspaceRoot}::${model}`, since resolution itself depends on the workspace.
createEmbedder(false, ...) returns null and never attempts the import, so a workspace without the library pays nothing.
A missing library throws an actionable Error at the first embed (inside loadPipeline), not at createEmbedder/construction time, so startup is unaffected.
localEmbedderId encodes model + transformers runtime version + dtype; an index built under a different id is expected to be discarded by the semantic store rather than reused.

sideEffects.description: dynamically imports @huggingface/transformers and runs ONNX feature-extraction inference in process
downloads/reads MiniLM model weights into resolveModelCacheDir(), once per model then cached
routes all pipeline loads and embed() calls through one process-wide serializer (embedSerialize)

risks: Workspace resolution (importTransformersFromWorkspace) loads and executes whatever version of the library the analyzed repository itself installed, not necessarily the range repovine was tested against.
The first embed() call downloads the model, so a cold start pays both download and pipeline load before any result.

onnxruntime-node 1.21 SIGABRTs at process exit on macOS (libc++ mutex-lock abort in its native teardown); mitigated by single-threaded darwin session_options plus disposeEmbedderPipelines, but the actual floor documented is requiring transformers 4.x / onnxruntime 1.24.3 (docs/platform-support.md), not the mitigation code alone.

Sharing embedSerialize/pipelineByModel at module scope is load-bearing, not an optimization: making them per-instance would reintroduce concurrent inference and duplicate model memory across generations.
patterns: Opt-in and degradable: without the library, token search still works and only fuzzy/semantic ranking is absent.
The heavy dependency is reached through a dynamic import specifier so it is never a load-time cost when disabled.
Deterministic graph tools stay deterministic; embeddings only rank fuzzy search_context queries.
invariants: enabled=false means no import of the transformers package is attempted.
Two different workspaceRoot values never share a pipeline memo entry.
Inference never runs concurrently within one process (single embedSerialize queue).
annotation.integrationPoints: Constructed by the server runtime's semantic index sync (mod:repovine/src/mcp) with the config flag and workspace root; embedSerialize's primitive comes from mod:repovine/src/semantic/serialize (createSerializer); DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL from mod:repovine/src/config; vectors are stored/keyed by mod:repovine/src/semantic/store (cardHash).
annotation.dataFlow: config flag + workspaceRoot -> transformers resolved beside repovine or in the workspace -> feature-extraction pipeline loaded once per (workspaceRoot, model) -> texts embedded through the shared serializer -> pooled, L2-normalized vectors returned in input order.

envDependencies.LOCALAPPDATA: Base cache dir on Windows when REPOVINE_MODEL_CACHE is unset.
envDependencies.REPOVINE_MODEL_CACHE: Overrides the model cache directory entirely.
envDependencies.XDG_CACHE_HOME: Base cache dir on Linux when REPOVINE_MODEL_CACHE is unset.

annotation.summary: Shipped semantic-search relevance/fusion policy defaults shared by search_context, scope recovery, tests, and offline calibration, calibrated on the 25-query Archestra relevance corpus.

keyExports.DEFAULT_SEMANTIC_FUSION_POLICY: Object.freeze'd SemanticFusionPolicy built from the four constants above; semanticRankBoost's default policy.
keyExports.SEMANTIC_COSINE_WEIGHT: Const 0 — weight given to raw cosine score in fusion (currently unused/zeroed).
keyExports.SEMANTIC_MIN_COSINE: Const 0.3 — minimum cosine similarity for a semantic hit to count.
keyExports.SEMANTIC_RRF_K: Const 1 — the k constant in the RRF boost formula.
keyExports.SEMANTIC_RRF_WEIGHT: Const 15 — weight applied in the RRF boost formula.
keyExports.SemanticFusionPolicy: Interface { minCosine, rrfWeight, rrfK, cosineWeight } describing a fusion policy.
keyExports.semanticRankBoost: RRF-style boost for a semantic hit at rank: policy.rrfWeight / (policy.rrfK + rank).

assumptions: The four constants are in-sample defaults calibrated on one 25-query corpus (Archestra), not universal probability thresholds; semantic-only hits are treated as low-confidence advisory by callers.

annotation.summary: Bounded-concurrency admission-control primitive for resources with no other cap (ONNX inference, transient worker threads). createLimiter(n) runs at most n tasks at once and FIFO-queues the rest; a queued task whose AbortSignal fires leaves the line immediately instead of waiting for admission.

keyExports.Limiter: <T>(task, signal?) => Promise<T> — the callable admission gate.
keyExports.createLimiter: Returns a Limiter capping concurrency at max(1, floor(n)); a rejecting task frees its slot, a pre-aborted signal rejects before running, and an abort while queued removes the waiter without ever consuming a slot.
keyExports.createSerializer: createLimiter(1) — tasks run one at a time in submission order.

assumptions: Callers rely on FIFO admission order and on the abort-while-queued fast path.
A task's own rejection surfaces to its caller only and does not stall the queue.

sideEffects.description: counting semaphore with a FIFO waiter queue

risks: An aborted queued task relinquishes its place without having incremented the active count — the accounting must stay balanced or the limiter leaks or under-counts concurrency.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/semantic/embedder (one module-scoped serializer shared across embedder generations) and mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/node-body (bounded grep-worker pool).

annotation.summary: The file-backed vector index over graph node cards. It loads persisted vectors, re-embeds only the cards whose text changed, drops entries for nodes that left the graph, and answers a query by scanning every vector. There is no vector database, because the corpus is thousands of nodes rather than millions of chunks and a full scan takes milliseconds.

keyExports.SEMANTIC_INDEX_FILENAME: The file the index persists to ('semantic-index.json').
keyExports.SemanticHit: One result: the node id and its similarity score.
keyExports.SemanticIndex: The index itself: static load(), sync() against current cards, embedQuery(), query()/queryDetailed().
keyExports.SemanticQueryReport: A query's hits plus indexed/compared counts and dimensionMismatches.
keyExports.SemanticSyncOptions: An optional onProgress(done, total) callback during embedding.
keyExports.SemanticSyncReport: What a sync did: embedded, reused, removed and the resulting total.
keyExports.cardHash: The content key: embedder identity and card text hashed together (NUL-separated) via sha256Hex.
keyExports.semanticIndexFileExists: Whether an index file is present for a cache dir.
keyExports.semanticIndexFilePath: That file's path inside a cache directory.

assumptions: The embedder identity is part of the content key (cardHash), so changing the model invalidates every vector rather than mixing incompatible ones.

A persisted file from a different embedder id or a different `version` is discarded whole (SemanticIndex.load), rather than partially reused; an unreadable/missing file just starts an empty index that the next sync() rebuilds.
Vectors are L2-normalized on the way in (normalize()), which is what makes the similarity score a plain dot product.
sync() throws when the embedder fails rather than swallowing it, leaving the caller to decide whether a stale index is still worth serving.
Entries are written in compareCodeUnits-sorted order so the persisted file diffs stably between builds.
Entries whose vector length does not match the query's are skipped during search (dimensionMismatches++), which keeps a partially migrated index usable rather than broken.

sideEffects.description: SemanticIndex.load reads the persisted index file
save() writes the index atomically (writeJsonObjectStreamed) after embedding or pruning
sync()/embedQuery() call the injected Embedder to embed pending cards in batches

risks: save() streams entries one at a time rather than a single JSON.stringify, because the base64 vectors make this the second-largest cache artifact — a whole-file stringify would both stall the event loop and risk hitting the engine's string-length ceiling.
queryDetailed() scans every entry linearly, so query cost grows with graph size; acceptable at the intended node-count scale, not at a text-chunk scale.

A failed sync() throws after any already-processed batches were applied and pruned entries already removed — the index can end up partially updated, and only the caller's own handling decides whether to keep serving it.
patterns: Content-keyed incremental sync: only changed cards are re-embedded, and cards for nodes no longer present are pruned in the same sync() call.
No external service and no database — the whole feature is a local file plus the injected Embedder.
invariants: Every entry's key includes the embedder identity (via cardHash), so an index built by a different model is never partially reused.
The persisted file is written atomically and in a stable (compareCodeUnits) order.
Stored vectors are L2-normalized.
annotation.integrationPoints: Embedder comes from mod:repovine/src/semantic/embedder; atomic streamed write from mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic (writeJsonObjectStreamed); stable ordering from mod:repovine/src/platform/ordering (compareCodeUnits); hashing/HASH_WIDTH from the published @repovine/plugin-sdk contract.
annotation.dataFlow: node cards (Map<nodeId,text>) -> content hash compared against persisted entries -> changed cards embedded in batches, absent nodes pruned -> index streamed to disk -> a query vector is embedded and scored (dot product) against every entry, top-k returned.

annotation.summary: Diagnostic-only probe for whether the optional @huggingface/transformers peer is installed and where it resolves from, without ever importing it (importing pulls in a large ONNX runtime).

keyExports.TransformersInstallInfo: Interface { resolved: boolean; source?: 'repovine'|'workspace'; entryPath?: string; version?: string }.
keyExports.describeTransformersInstall: Tries resolving the peer next to repovine first (source:'repovine'), then from workspaceRoot (source:'workspace'); returns TransformersInstallInfo with resolved/source/entryPath/version, or { resolved:false }.
keyExports.resolveTransformersFromWorkspace: Resolves @huggingface/transformers as the given workspaceRoot would (via createRequire against workspaceRoot/package.json); undefined if unresolvable.

assumptions: Deliberately a dependency-free leaf: a probe cannot live next to config.ts's DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL without creating an import cycle with embedder.ts.

The package's exports map blocks resolving './package.json' directly (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED), so version is read by walking up parent dirs from the resolved entry path (up to 6 levels) looking for a package.json named @huggingface/transformers.

sideEffects.description: createRequire(...).resolve() and fs.readFileSync of package.json while walking up from the resolved entry path

risks: createRequire/CJS resolution can differ from ESM import() conditions in exotic setups, so describeTransformersInstall's answer is a diagnostic approximation, not a guarantee an import() would succeed.

annotation.summary: The first build stage: apply plugin configuration, discover packages and files through language plugins, extract them inline or across a worker pool, then add infrastructure and templates and assemble the facts snapshot. Fails loudly — any extraction failure ends the run before a partial snapshot is finalized or cached.

keyExports.STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION: The snapshot shape version; a stored snapshot whose version does not match invalidates the cache. Currently 1 — the count starts at the first release and increments only when the snapshot shape itself changes.
keyExports.collectRepositoryFactsAsync: Main orchestrator: prepares plugin config, discovers packages/files, extracts in shards (inline or pooled), adds infra/templates, assembles snapshot.
keyExports.dedupByModuleIdPreservingOrder: Dedup pending modules by resolver priority, preserving order.
keyExports.mergeResults: Merges shard results and reuse/rescan counts.

assumptions: Extraction inline when worker count is ≤1, pooled otherwise.
Cancellation is cooperative and checked before each package and after each await.
Worker sizing accounts for container memory limit, not just host memory.
Reusing a prior snapshot requires shape version AND engine build identity match.

sideEffects.description: runs pooled extraction across worker threads
reads snapshot cache and sizing calibration
writes sizing calibration after run

risks: Engine build identity is development-only and absent from installed packages, so in production only shape version guards reuse.
A plugin not registered is skipped with warning, so its modules are absent rather than reported as failure.
Failure is all-or-nothing: one unparseable package ends the whole build.
patterns: Fail loud rather than degrade: a partial snapshot is never finalized or cached, because a quietly incomplete graph is worse than no graph.
The engine stamps ownership rather than trusting plugins to self-report, so a plugin that omits its own identifier still yields correctly owned modules.
Sizing is measured and remembered: a calibration from previous runs advises the worker count for the next.
annotation.flowDescription: plugin configuration → discovery → sharding → inline/pooled extraction → infra/templates → snapshot assembly.
invariants: Any shard error aborts before snapshot is finalized or cached.
Every module carries owning package's plugin identifier.
annotation.integrationPoints: plugin-loader, source/registry, source/extract-runner, worker-pool, calibration, stage1/infra, stage1/templates.
annotation.stateShape: The snapshot carries packages, modules, infrastructure modules, the analysis version, and optionally the linking configuration and the bundle handler map.
annotation.dataFlow: plugin configuration → per-plugin discovery → package jobs and shards → inline or pooled extraction with cancellation checkpoints → fail on any shard error, otherwise merge → infrastructure and templates → facts snapshot, plus an updated sizing calibration.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_MAX_PACKAGE_WORKERS: Caps the worker pool when the option is not supplied

annotation.summary: Portable repository-facts snapshot cache with sync/async load/save and two SHA-256 guards: snapshotContentFingerprint (analysis/build/extraction-config identity, order-preserving) drives the dirty-skip write guard, while extractOutputFingerprint (sorted id+contentHash, excluding version fields) preserves the CI golden contract. saveAsync streams the write so no full-snapshot JSON string is held in memory.

keyExports.SnapshotCache: load/loadAsync/save/saveAsync/exists over the full RepositoryFactsSnapshot JSON.
keyExports.createFileCache: Factory for cacheDir+repoRoot; rewrites module filePath to portable repo-relative form around save/load; saveAsync streams the write so no full-snapshot JSON string is ever held in memory.
keyExports.extractOutputFingerprint: CI golden-guard fingerprint: SHA-256 over sorted-by-id module/template/infra id+contentHash only, excluding analysisVersion/engineBuildId; changes exactly when extract output changes.
keyExports.snapshotContentFingerprint: P2 dirty-skip guard: SHA-256 over analysisVersion + engineBuildId + each module/template/infra id+contentHash in original (unsorted) order; a match means the on-disk snapshot is already current and the write can be skipped.

assumptions: Module filePath is the only absolute field in a snapshot; toPortable/toAbsolute round-trip it repo-root-relative so the on-disk cache transfers across worktrees/CI checkouts/containers with identical content.
The portable-path rewrite in writeSnapshot/saveAsync is synchronous (no await between rewrite and revert), so nothing else on the event loop observes a mid-rewrite snapshot.

sideEffects.description: load()/loadAsync() read repository-facts-snapshot.json under cacheDir
save() writes atomically via writeFileAtomicSync; saveAsync() streams via writeJsonObjectStreamed (no full-snapshot JSON string)

risks: Large monorepos produce a multi-hundred-MB JSON string; writeSnapshot's JSON.stringify can hit Node's >512MB string-length cliff — its finally block still restores absolute filePaths if stringify throws.

risks.text: extractOutputFingerprint's exact hash shape (sorted mod/tpl/infra id+contentHash, excluding analysisVersion/engineBuildId) is the CI golden-guard's byte contract over a fixed fixture corpus.

patterns: Two independent SHA-256 fingerprints: snapshotContentFingerprint (order-preserving, includes analysisVersion+engineBuildId) for the on-disk dirty-skip guard; extractOutputFingerprint (sorted by id, excludes both) for the CI golden guard.
invariants: Requires raw.modules to be an array on load or the cache is rejected (returns null).
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by a caller that loads a previousSnapshot and passes it into mod:repovine/src/stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync, then saves the returned snapshot back (cache functions are not called directly from stage1/index.ts itself); uses mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic (writeFileAtomicSync/writeJsonObjectStreamed) and mod:repovine/src/perf/memory-profiler phases.
annotation.dataFlow: Caller loads previousSnapshot via SnapshotCache.load()/loadAsync() → passed as SnapshotOptions.previousSnapshot into stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync → returned RepositoryFactsSnapshot saved back via save()/saveAsync().

annotation.summary: Zod-validated Stage-1 calibration persistence and advice: atomically stores finite positive build observations and clamps worker/shard recommendations to finite positive integers.

keyExports.adviseFromCalibration: RAM-budget 70% rule + cpuCount-1 cap; user maxPackageWorkers override wins.
keyExports.saveCalibration: Writes lastRun observed metrics after a build completes.

assumptions: saveCalibration called at end of successful graph build with MemoryProfiler peak.
Schema version 1; unknown versions are ignored.

sideEffects.description: loadCalibration reads build-calibration.json
saveCalibration mkdir + writeFileSync calibration JSON

risks: Stale calibration after hardware change skews ETA.
patterns: Persists timing samples under .repovine for ETA advice.
invariants: Calibration is best-effort — missing file uses defaults.
annotation.integrationPoints: .repovine calibration files; cli/build ETA estimates.
annotation.dataFlow: prior build timings persisted → adjust stage1 ETA in build-controller messages.

annotation.summary: Dev-only engine-build identity for stage1 snapshot-reuse gate. Fingerprints the engine's dist/ when running in dev (REPOVINE_DEV=1 or git checkout), else undefined for installed packages, preventing silent reuse of stale snapshot caches. Reviewed against current source: 5-export surface unchanged from the prior note.

keyExports.__resetEngineBuildIdMemo: Test-only: clears the per-process memoized id.
keyExports.computeEngineBuildId: Pure decision core: returns fingerprint when dev-mode detected, else undefined; deps injected for testability.
keyExports.currentEngineBuildId: Memoized per-process id: finds engine package root, detects git checkout, fingerprints dist/**/*.js files (path + size + mtime) via SHA-256[:16].
keyExports.engineBuildMatches: Reuse-gate predicate: true when current is undefined (release mode); else requires stored === current (dev mode).

assumptions: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync to gate snapshot reuse alongside STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION.
currentEngineBuildId() memoized for process lifetime; dist/ rebuild mid-process not detected without __resetEngineBuildIdMemo().

sideEffects.description: Walks up from module to find engine package.json, checks for .git, hashes every .js file in dist/ (size + mtime)

risks: In release mode (no REPOVINE_DEV, not a git checkout), currentEngineBuildId() returns undefined and engineBuildMatches is a no-op; reuse guard relies solely on STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION.
invariants: engineBuildMatches always returns true when current is undefined (release mode).
fingerprintDist uses SHA-256[:16] over sorted-by-name .js file metadata (path, size, mtimeMs).
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync imports currentEngineBuildId/engineBuildMatches for previousSnapshot reuse gating.
annotation.dataFlow: currentEngineBuildId() supplies real fs/git/fingerprint deps to computeEngineBuildId(deps), memoized in `memo` → stage1/index compares it against a loaded previousSnapshot.engineBuildId via engineBuildMatches.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_DEV: When set to '1', forces dev-mode fingerprinting even outside a git checkout.

annotation.summary: Engine-owned Stage-1 source-extraction boundary: reads each shard file once and fingerprints it, hands the raw text+hash to the source plugin's extract(), then assembles the plugin's SemanticModuleDelta results into full ModuleInfo records in pending order.

keyExports.RunSourceExtractionArgs: Input shape for runSourceExtraction (plugin, repoRoot, packages, pendingModules, prevByAbsPath, absPathToId, extractContext, analysisVersion)
keyExports.RunSourceExtractionResult: Output shape (modules, reused, rescanned, facts, factRefusals)
keyExports.runSourceExtraction: Reads pendingModules' files (fs.readFileSync + sha256Hex), calls plugin.extract(), assembles ModuleInfo[] in pending order, and takes the plugin's published facts via takePublishedFacts

assumptions: A shard file that fails fs.readFileSync is simply absent from sourceByModuleId, so the plugin emits no delta for it and it drops out deterministically.
A transient delta (delta.transient) is assembled with an empty contentHash sentinel so it never matches a real hash and is always rescanned next run.

sideEffects.description: fs.readFileSync each pending module's source file

risks: Both extraction paths (main thread and worker thread) must route through this module so the ModuleInfo[] boundary type crossing the worker bridge has exactly one assembly point.

annotation.summary: Computes one digest standing for every input that can change what extraction produces without any source byte changing: the scan patterns, the identity of the active plugins, the directory-layout table extraction walked by, and the per-plugin context carrying things like compiler options. The snapshot reuse gate stores this digest, so a configuration change forces a full extraction rather than reusing facts derived under different settings.

keyExports.ExtractionConfigFingerprintInput: The inputs that go into it: repository root, scan include/exclude patterns, active source plugins, infrastructure plugin ids, the per-plugin context map, and an optional plugin-runtime identity.
keyExports.computeExtractionConfigFingerprint: Returns the sha256 digest (truncated to HASH_WIDTH.config hex characters) of the stably-serialized payload.

assumptions: The repository root is stripped from every string before hashing, in both native and posix path spellings, so the same checkout moved or cloned elsewhere yields the same digest and its cache stays usable.
Serialization is structural and order-independent where order carries no meaning: object keys sort, map entries sort by serialized key, sets sort.
Plugin order is preserved rather than sorted, because the first plugin to claim a file owns it and a reordering genuinely changes the outcome.

A plugin contributes its declared identity — id, apiVersion, fileMatch, capabilities and requires — rather than anything derived from its implementation; packageMarkers is deliberately excluded here because it is folded in from the directory-layout table instead.
Recursion is guarded via an onStack Set, so a context holding a cycle serializes to '[Circular]' instead of looping.

The directory-layout table (pruned dirs, test-layout markers, packageMarkers) is included because which directories were skipped and which filenames marked a package root both decide which modules exist.
risks: Only the declared plugin identity is hashed, so a plugin whose extraction logic changes while its descriptor stays the same produces an unchanged digest and the gate reuses facts built by the older logic.
Functions serialize to their name alone, so a context carrying a callback yields the same digest whatever the callback now does.

The digest covers only what callers pass in, so a plugin-specific input left out of the context map makes reuse more permissive than it looks, and the failure appears later as facts that quietly do not match the configuration.
patterns: Paths are made portable before hashing rather than after, which is what separates 'the configuration changed' from 'the checkout moved'.
One digest stands for many heterogeneous inputs, so the reuse gate compares a single value instead of re-deriving each condition.
invariants: The same configuration under a different repository root produces the same digest.
A change to a scan pattern, a compiler option or the active plugin set changes the digest.
Serialization is deterministic for equivalent structures regardless of insertion order (object keys, map entries and set entries are all sorted before joining).
annotation.integrationPoints: The digest is stored on the facts snapshot (RepositoryFactsSnapshot.extractionConfigFingerprint) and compared by the first-stage reuse gate; scan pattern shapes come from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters, the plugin shape from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types, and HASH_WIDTH/sha256Hex from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk.
annotation.dataFlow: scan patterns, plugin identities, directory-layout table and per-plugin contexts -> root-relative normalization -> stable structural serialization -> sha256 digest stored on the snapshot and compared on the next build.

annotation.summary: Finds infrastructure definitions during the first build stage and turns them into records. It walks the repository for files any registered parser claims, reads each one in the format its kind implies, then offers every document to the parsers in registration order until one takes it. The parsers supply the infrastructure meaning; the identity, the file reference and the fingerprint are stamped here.

keyExports.InfraScanOptions: The repository root, optional packages, the compiled scan patterns, and an onPruned callback.
keyExports.InfraScanResult: The scan output: modules found, refusals, and published facts.
keyExports.collectInfraModules: Runs the scan and returns one record per infrastructure module found, plus refusals and facts.

assumptions: The parsers are registered by importing the bootstrap for its side effect, so the registry is populated before the first scan.
Structured formats are parsed and the rest is handed over as raw text, which is how a container definition and a template can share one dispatch path.
The template format is read with a schema tolerant of the intrinsic tags cloud templates use, so those files parse instead of failing on unknown tags.
One fingerprint is computed per file and shared by every document that file yields, since the documents come from the same bytes.
An unreadable file yields an empty fingerprint rather than a wrong one, so a later run treats it as changed and reads it again.
Records sharing an identity come from the same file, so merging them only concatenates their resources.
The packages option is accepted and ignored: discovery here is driven from the filesystem, not from the package list.

sideEffects.description: walks the tree and reads candidate infrastructure files

risks: The first parser that both matches the filename and claims a document takes it, and the search stops there whether or not the parser produced anything — a parser that claims a document and returns nothing silently prevents any later parser from seeing it, and the resource simply does not appear.
Because claiming is ordered, registration order decides the outcome for a document more than one parser recognizes; a reordering changes classification with nothing failing.
A file that cannot be read or parsed is skipped, and the warning appears only when verbose output is enabled, so a malformed template is invisible in a normal run.
Directory exclusions are by name anywhere in the tree and include ordinary words such as test and build, so definitions kept under such a directory are never discovered.
patterns: Parsers own the semantics, the engine owns the identity and the fingerprint, which keeps a parser from having to know how modules are addressed.
Discovery, format dispatch and claiming are three separate steps, so adding a format does not touch the walk.
invariants: A parse failure never aborts the build.
Every record's fingerprint is the hash of the whole file it came from.
Records with the same identity fold their resources rather than replacing each other.
annotation.integrationPoints: Parsers are registered through mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/bootstrap and resolved from mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/registry; the tolerant template schema comes from mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/yaml-schema; path filtering from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters; the record shape from mod:repovine/src/types, and the result is placed on the build snapshot by the first stage.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root -> candidate walk -> scan-pattern filter -> format-specific read -> first claiming parser per document -> engine-stamped record, merged by identity.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Logs per-file read and parse failures

annotation.summary: LayoutSkipCollector aggregates pruned-directory reports from every Stage 1 source-plugin discovery walk (plus the engine's own walks) into per (reason,name) counts, so a build's layout table can state what it pruned without keeping one entry per path.

keyExports.LayoutSkipCollector: Class with a `sink` field (the PrunedDir callback handed to producers' SourceDiscoveryOptions.onPruned and the engine's own walks) and a `summary(catalog)` method that returns LayoutSkip[] sorted by reason:name, joining each name's owning plugin ids from the DeclarationCatalog.

assumptions: Aggregation key is `${reason}:${name}`; callers rely on counts being grouped by that pair, not per path.
DeclarationCatalog entries are read via keys prefixed `dir:`; summary() strips that prefix to match against collected names.

sideEffects.description: sink() mutates an in-memory Map of stop counts on the collector instance; summary() reads DeclarationCatalog.dirs to join ownership.

annotation.summary: Normalizes repovine.config build.linking into a deduped NormalizedLinkingConfig (handler search roots, bundle scripts/autoDetect), persisted on RepositoryFactsSnapshot.linkingConfig for stage-2 infra→code linking.

keyExports.NormalizedLinkingConfig: { handlers: { searchRoots: string[] }, bundles: { scripts: string[], autoDetect: boolean } }.
keyExports.hasLinkingConfig: True when the normalized handlers.searchRoots or bundles.scripts arrays are non-empty.
keyExports.normalizeLinkingConfig: Dedupes array fields and defaults bundles.autoDetect to true unless the input explicitly sets it false.

assumptions: bundles.autoDetect defaults to true: normalizeLinkingConfig only turns it off when the input explicitly sets autoDetect:false.
handlers.searchRoots and bundles.scripts are deduped through uniqueStrings, which also drops empty-string entries.
risks: Typo in handlers.searchRoots leaves Lambda handlers unlinked in stage-2 graph.
patterns: Shared normalization for CLI build and MCP RepovineRuntime snapshot paths.
annotation.flowDescription: repovine.config build.linking → normalizeLinkingConfig → snapshot.linkingConfig for stage2 runtime-links and bundle-output-loader.
invariants: hasLinkingConfig is true when either normalized section has non-empty values.
bundles.autoDetect defaults true when omitted.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage1/index snapshot assembly; stage2 runtime-links; mod:repovine/src/stage2/bundle-output-loader reads bundles.scripts/autoDetect from this normalized shape.
annotation.stateShape: NormalizedLinkingConfig has two sections: handlers.searchRoots[], and bundles.scripts[] + autoDetect boolean.
annotation.dataFlow: repovine.config build.linking → normalizeLinkingConfig → snapshot.linkingConfig → stage2 runtime-links and bundle-output-loader.

annotation.summary: Named-once registry of Stage 1 build refusal `kind` string constants, so MCP/CLI readers of a Refusal.kind match against a shared constant instead of a retyped string literal that silently drifts from the producer.

keyExports.DECLARATION_CONFLICT_REFUSAL: 'declaration-conflict' — two plugins declared one catalog key with different effects; neither is in force.
keyExports.FILE_CLAIMED_TWICE_REFUSAL: 'file-claimed-twice' — two source plugins claimed one file; the first is indexed; carries {count, sample}.
keyExports.GRAPH_VALIDATION_REFUSAL: 'graph-validation' — composition did not take every record the scan produced.
keyExports.IAC_DOCUMENT_CLAIM_CONFLICT_REFUSAL: 'iac-document-claim-conflict' — a parser claimed a document exclusively and another parser also contributed from it.
keyExports.IAC_LOADER_AMBIGUOUS_REFUSAL: 'iac-loader-ambiguous' — two equally specific parser claims asked for different loaders.
keyExports.IAC_LOADER_CLAIMED_TWICE_REFUSAL: 'iac-loader-claimed-twice' — two plugins registered one loader id; the second is refused.
keyExports.IAC_LOADER_UNKNOWN_REFUSAL: 'iac-loader-unknown' — a parser named a document loader no plugin registered.
keyExports.OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE_REFUSAL: 'outside-workspace' — candidate resolves outside the workspace root; carries {count, sample}.
keyExports.PLUGIN_FACT_REJECTED_REFUSAL: 'plugin-fact-rejected' — a Stage 1 producer published a fact the boundary would not take.
keyExports.PLUGIN_UNLOADABLE_REFUSAL: 'plugin-unloadable' — a plugin named in repovine.config.json could not be loaded.
keyExports.PROJECTION_BATCH_REJECTED_REFUSAL: 'projection-batch-rejected' — one projection batch was refused whole.
keyExports.PROJECTION_CONFLICT_REFUSAL: 'projection-conflict' — two contributions named one thing and disagreed; carries both owners and values.
keyExports.PROJECTION_CONTRIBUTOR_FAILED_REFUSAL: 'projection-contributor-failed' — a projector threw, returned the wrong shape, or blew its batch budget; carries the owner.
keyExports.RESOURCE_IDENTITY_CONFLICT_REFUSAL: 'resource-identity-conflict' — one file emitted two resources under one identity with different content; neither is kept.
keyExports.SOURCE_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE_REFUSAL: 'source-plugin-unavailable' — a source plugin's prerequisite is absent, so its files are not indexed.

annotation.integrationPoints: Populates Refusal.kind (mod:repovine/src/response/refusal) for every Stage 1 producer; MCP/CLI layers read these constants rather than the raw string.

annotation.summary: Finds server-side template files during the first build stage and records what each one declares about its neighbours. It walks the repository, keeps files that sit under a templates directory and carry a recognized extension, hashes the content, and pulls the parent, include and block names out of the body by regular expression. The second stage turns these into template nodes and the edges between them.

keyExports.collectTemplates: Walks the repository and returns one record per template file, sorted by path, carrying the content hash and the body hints.
keyExports.parseTemplateBodyHints: Pulls the parent template, the included templates and the declared block names out of a template body.

assumptions: A file counts as a template only when it sits under a templates directory, which is what keeps stray markup in static, docs or coverage output from being picked up.
Recognized extensions are the markup pair and the three Jinja-family ones.
The engine is recorded only when the extension names it; plain markup is ambiguous across engines, so the field is left off rather than guessed.
Literal sections and comments are removed before the hints are read, so a tag shown as documentation inside a template is not mistaken for a real one.
Hints come from regular expressions rather than a parse, which is enough for the static forms and nothing more.
Directory entries are sorted during the walk and the result is sorted by path, so the same tree always produces the same records.

sideEffects.description: walks the repository tree and reads template files

risks: A template that cannot be read becomes an empty one rather than an error: the walk continues, the record is still emitted, and the hash is the hash of nothing, so the file looks present and empty instead of unreadable.
An include or extends whose target is a variable or an expression yields no hint, so the edge is simply absent from the graph rather than reported as unresolved.
The skip list and the extension set are literal, so a repository using another template extension or nesting templates below a skipped directory produces no template nodes and no diagnostic.
patterns: The templates directory acts as the anchor, which is what makes discovery precise without any per-repository configuration.
Discovery mirrors the infrastructure-module path: stage one collects file records, stage two projects them into nodes.
invariants: The first record wins for a given path, so a repeated visit never overwrites an earlier one.
Output is ordered by path, which keeps the content hash comparison stable between builds.
annotation.integrationPoints: Emits the record type defined in mod:repovine/src/types; path filtering comes from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters; the records are projected into template nodes against mod:repovine/src/graph/model in the second stage.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → sorted directory walk → extension, directory and scan-pattern filters → read and hash → body hints → one template record per file, sorted by path.

annotation.summary: AST-free Stage 1 identity and path helpers shared by the orchestrator and source plugins: package job keys and deterministic module-collision priority declared here, plus re-exports of the SDK's module-id minter (as makeModuleId) and package-name extractor (extractPackageName) so Stage 1 need not import @repovine/plugin-sdk directly for these two.

keyExports.modulePathResolverPriority: Ranks extension and slash-spelled /index form when multiple discovered files collapse to one module id; lower wins; unmatched extensions score 9999.
keyExports.packageJobKey: Combines sourcePluginId, package name, and package path (NUL-joined) into a collision-resistant job identity for a discovered package entry.

assumptions: The resolver priority is the engine's fixed collision order (MODULE_PATH_EXT_PRIORITY), not a language-plugin capability.
makeModuleId and extractPackageName are re-exported from @repovine/plugin-sdk rather than declared here, so this file itself has no AST/toolchain dependency.
TypeScript tsconfig discovery normally supplies forward-slash paths even on Windows, while filesystem-walk producers may retain backslashes.
The index-form penalty is keyed to the '/' spelling; extension rank alone is separator-independent.
risks: The index-form penalty recognizes only forward slashes; a backslash-spelled index path can tie with or outrank a file-form collision according to extension rank alone (documented in-source as a real drift risk between the priority list and the matching pattern).
Changing extension priority changes which physical file owns a stable module id and can alter downstream graph identity.
patterns: Keep identity helpers free of TypeScript AST dependencies so Stage 1 can load them without a language toolchain.
Use numeric resolver priority with a stable discovery-order tie break.
invariants: The module has no ts-morph or typescript runtime import.
All ranked extensions have distinct priorities and unknown extensions sort after known index forms.
Only slash-spelled /index.<ext> receives the index-form penalty.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by Stage 1 deduplication and TypeScript discovery/resolution; imports PackageInfo through the shared types surface and re-exports the SDK's mintModuleId (as makeModuleId) and extractPackageName.
annotation.dataFlow: package facts → packageJobKey job identity; discovered candidate paths → modulePathResolverPriority → deterministic pending-module winner; bare import specifiers → extractPackageName (re-exported) → package names.

annotation.summary: Stage-1 worker_threads entry point. Loads this isolate's plugin set once (awaited before every job, not at module scope, so an early message never races an empty set), then runs registered source extraction for a package shard and posts assembled modules or a serialized error message+stack back to PackageWorkerPool. Its shutdown handler reaps any in-flight plugin subprocess (e.g. python AST child) via SourcePlugin.terminateInFlight before closing parentPort.
assumptions: Worker receives a package slice via workerData (WorkerInit) and returns a ModuleInfo batch per JobMessage.
Extract errors are captured per shard as a serialized message+stack (JobErrorMessage) without aborting the worker or the isolate.
console.log is redirected to console.error and the pipeline log sink silenced, because stdout is the JSON-RPC channel when the MCP server spawned this process.

A worker script read from disk at spawn time against an older/rebuilt engine can arrive with no pluginSpec; that path rejects pluginsReady with an actionable message instead of throwing on a destructure, and the rejection is swallowed at the top level (each job handler awaits it itself).

sideEffects.description: worker_threads child runs source extraction via runSourceExtraction; shutdown handler reaps plugin subprocesses via terminateInFlight before parentPort.close()
loadPluginSet registers this isolate's source plugins (queried later via getSourcePlugin/getSourcePlugins)

risks: A shutdown message must reap the plugin's OS child subprocesses (via SourcePlugin.terminateInFlight) before parentPort.close(), or the pool's Worker.terminate() orphans them.
A missing sourcePluginId registration (no plugin loaded for job.sourcePluginId) fails the shard with an error reply rather than silently skipping it.
patterns: WorkerInit's absPathToId/extractContext arrive as serialized [key,value][] entries and are rehydrated into Maps once per worker isolate at module scope.
pluginsReady is created once and awaited per message, not top-level-awaited, so composition order doesn't depend on when the first job message arrives.
annotation.flowDescription: JobMessage -> await pluginsReady -> getSourcePlugin(sourcePluginId) -> runSourceExtraction (stage1/extract-runner.ts) -> postMessage result|error.
invariants: No public exports — worker_threads entry only, side-effecting on import.
Throws synchronously if parentPort is missing (must be spawned via worker_threads, not required directly).
annotation.integrationPoints: Extraction delegated to mod:repovine/src/stage1/extract-runner (runSourceExtraction); plugin registry lookups via mod:repovine/src/plugin-host/source-set (getSourcePlugin/getSourcePlugins) and mod:repovine/src/plugin-host/load (loadPluginSet); dispatched by mod:repovine/src/stage1/worker-pool (resolveWorkerScriptUrl loads this file as worker.js); log routing via mod:repovine/src/cli/ui (setPipelineLogSink); a source plugin's teardown hook lives on the plugin itself, e.g. mod:@repovine/plugin-source-python/src/extract.
annotation.stateShape: Module-scope: packages, absPathToId, extractContextByPlugin, repoRoot, analysisVersion (from workerData) and the single pluginsReady promise; parentPort carries JobMessage/ShutdownMessage in, JobResultMessage/JobErrorMessage out.
annotation.dataFlow: workerData (WorkerInit) -> module-scope state + pluginsReady -> parentPort message (job) -> runSourceExtraction -> postMessage(result|error); message (shutdown) -> terminateInFlight on every loaded plugin -> parentPort.close().

annotation.summary: Persistent worker-thread pool for stage-1 package shards. Each slot tracks one job, so a crash rejects that job and marks the slot dead. No respawn: capacity degrades until destroy()+recreate. Shutdown asks each worker to exit on its own (reaping any plugin subprocess, e.g. python AST) within a grace period before force-terminating.

keyExports.PackageJob: One shard: package, owning plugin, pending modules, previous entries, shard position, optional solo flag.
keyExports.PackageJobResult: Shard modules, reuse/rescan counts, facts/factRefusals, or an error string.
keyExports.PackageWorkerPool: The pool: submit(job), each worker fed via resolveWorkerScriptUrl's worker.js, destroy() to tear down.
keyExports.chooseWorkerCount: Parallelism heuristic: min(cpuCap = floor(cpus/2), ramCap = floor(floor(totalRam/2)/3GiB)), floor 1; an explicit maxPackageWorkers overrides both (clamped to >=1).
keyExports.effectiveTotalMemBytes: min(host RAM, cgroup constraint) when the constraint is a positive number; falls back to host RAM when process.constrainedMemory() reports 0 or is unavailable.

assumptions: A worker replies exactly once per dispatched job; the reply is matched to a slot by currentJobId and to a job by jobId.
Job payloads (pkg, pendingModules, prevModuleEntries, etc.) must survive structured cloning across the worker_threads boundary.

resolveWorkerScriptUrl finds worker.js by trying, in order: adjacent to this file, a src->dist path swap, cwd/dist/stage1/worker.js, cwd/repovine/dist/stage1/worker.js — throwing if none exist (module must be built).
Graceful shutdown window is SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS (3000ms) by default, overridable via PackageWorkerPoolOptions.shutdownGraceMs; workers are force-terminated only on overrun.

sideEffects.description: spawns and terminates worker threads; dispatches jobs and receives replies by postMessage

risks: effectiveTotalMemBytes treats process.constrainedMemory() returning 0 (undeterminable) or an unconstrained cgroup v2 'max' sentinel the same as 'no container limit', falling back to host RAM — a container whose cgroup limit can't be read is sized as if unconstrained, which can over-provision workers and invite an OOM/container kill.
A dead slot is never respawned; a build that loses workers (crash/OOM/unexpected exit) runs with fewer slots for the rest of that build, and if every slot dies the whole backlog is rejected.
postMessage failure to a dying/non-cloneable-payload worker surfaces as a rejected job (then fails that slot) rather than a retry.
patterns: One in-flight job per slot, tracked by jobId; a stray/duplicate reply for a different jobId does not free a busy slot.
Solo jobs (large packages, via soloThreshold) mutually exclude each other but never block non-solo jobs from dispatching.
invariants: drainQueue dispatches only to slots that are both non-busy and non-dead.
Solo jobs are mutually exclusive with each other; a non-solo job is never blocked by an in-flight solo job.
annotation.integrationPoints: Constructed and driven by mod:repovine/src/stage1/index.ts, which also supplies effectiveTotalMemBytes()/chooseWorkerCount() for sizing; each worker thread runs mod:repovine/src/stage1/worker.ts (resolved via resolveWorkerScriptUrl); PluginLoadSpec comes from mod:repovine/src/plugin-host/load; job/result shapes cross the @repovine/plugin-sdk HostPath/ReadonlyFactRecord boundary.
annotation.stateShape: Per-slot WorkerSlot (worker handle, busy, runningSolo, dead, currentJobId); pendingByJobId map; an in-memory FIFO queue of not-yet-dispatched InternalJob.
annotation.dataFlow: shard job -> submit() queues it -> drainQueue picks a free live slot (respecting solo mutex) -> postMessage to the worker -> worker replies result|error -> resolved/rejected back to the caller.

annotation.summary: The second build stage: turn facts snapshot into the served graph. Interpreter layers contribute structural and infrastructure edges first, inert resources are optionally pruned, then domain passes tag and classify. An asynchronous form runs composition in a worker.

keyExports.composeRepositoryGraphAsync: Composition in a worker, falling back to inline when unavailable.

assumptions: Interpreters run before domain tagging because domain passes depend on edges they contribute.
One mutable graph runs through every pass; no patch handed between them.
Entrypoints carried explicitly across worker boundary rather than via side table.
Worker path resolved lazily and remembered; absent when compiled worker unavailable; offload failure falls back to inline.

sideEffects.description: builds and mutates one in-memory graph through every pass
asynchronous form runs composition in worker isolate

risks: Silent inline fallback on worker error; REPOVINE_STAGE2_WORKER_STRICT turns it into failure.
Graph validation warns outside development; a pass that drops record or leaves dangling edge degrades graph quietly in release.
patterns: Contribute, then prune, then classify: each stage sees a graph the previous finished with.
annotation.flowDescription: Stage-2 orchestrator: interpreters enrich the graph first (modules, runtime resources, infra links, entrypoint fragments), then multi-pass domain tagging and classification mutate the same in-memory RepositoryGraph.
invariants: Interpreter composition always precedes domain tagging.
Pruning runs between interpreter layers and domain passes.
Every snapshot record projects into graph and no edge dangles.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage2/interpreter/bootstrap, composer, entrypoint-store; stage2/prune-inert-resources, graph-validate; stage2/domains; worker beside this module.
annotation.dataFlow: facts snapshot → interpreter contributions and entrypoint fragments → inert resources pruned → domain, content, propagation, classification and subdomain passes → validation → the served graph.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_DEV: Turns graph-validation problems into a failure instead of a warning
envDependencies.REPOVINE_STAGE2_INLINE: Forces inline composition, skipping the worker
envDependencies.REPOVINE_STAGE2_WORKER_STRICT: Turns an offload failure into a failure instead of an inline fallback
envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Reports per-domain counts and offload availability

annotation.summary: Stage 1 snapshot helper living under src/stage2/: regex-parses bundle build script source (esbuild/webpack/rollup entry-to-output literal maps) and auto-detects conventional scripts/bundle.{js,ts} plus per-package script conventions expanded from root package.json workspace globs. buildSnapshot stamps the resulting bundle-output-to-source map onto RepositoryFactsSnapshot.bundleOutputHandlerMap; the infra-runtime-links interpreter reads it during Stage 2 composition. The mechanism is bundler-shaped, not provider-shaped: it recognises three bundler config forms and names no cloud vendor.

keyExports.loadBundleOutputHandlerMap: Merges explicit build.linking.bundles.scripts configs with autoDetect candidates, reads each script that exists inside the workspace root, and returns the merged output-to-source map.
keyExports.parseBundleOutputScript: Regex-parses a build script's source without eval; recognizes esbuild (entryPoint/outputFile), webpack (entry/output) and rollup (input/file) key patterns in either declaration order.

assumptions: Bundle scripts use string-literal entry/output pairs recognizable via regex; scripts requiring evaluation to resolve their paths are not covered.

autoDetect reads root package.json and expands workspace entries ending in '/*' one directory level deep; both the array and { packages: [] } workspaces shapes are accepted. Literal paths and deeper globs contribute no candidates.
Configured script paths are repo-root-relative and are read only when they resolve inside the workspace root.

sideEffects.description: reads configured bundle scripts on every build; autoDetect additionally pulls workspace globs from root package.json to widen the candidate set

risks: Bundle formats outside the three recognized literal-pair shapes produce no output-to-source alias; handler resolution falls back to path-shape lookup and loses linkage only where the bundle renames the entry relative to its output.
A configured script path that resolves outside the workspace root is skipped silently, so a typo pointing past the root yields no mappings rather than an error.
patterns: Optional pass: when no scripts configured and autoDetect finds nothing, proceeds without bundle mappings.
Containment is applied before the stat, because path.join normalizes a parent segment away instead of rejecting it.
invariants: Only establishes a mapping entry when entryBase and outBase both resolve to a non-empty, differing path after extension stripping.
A candidate script is read only when it resolves inside the workspace root and is an existing file.
Vendor-neutral by construction: the parser keys off bundler config vocabulary, never a cloud provider's.
annotation.integrationPoints: Stage 1 buildSnapshot reads config path build.linking.bundles.scripts and the autoDetect flag; containment guard from mod:repovine/src/fs/containment; the resulting map rides the snapshot into the stage2 graph build, where the infra-runtime-links interpreter consumes it as handlerPathMap.
annotation.dataFlow: bundle script source -> parseBundleOutputScript (regex sweep over esbuild/webpack/rollup key pairs) -> per-script output-to-source map -> loadBundleOutputHandlerMap merges across configured + auto-detected scripts that pass containment -> RepositoryFactsSnapshot.bundleOutputHandlerMap.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: gates a console warning when reading a bundle script that exists on disk throws

annotation.summary: The single alphabet a domain label is written in: every mint of a domain node id (domain:<label>, domain:<parent>/<sub>), repovine.domains.json key, or hand-typed scope argument routes through here so the three always agree on spelling.

keyExports.domainLabelSlug: Splits a label on '/' (the one character outside domainSlug's alphabet that survives, for parent/sub subdomains), slugs each segment, drops empty segments, rejoins with '/'; an all-empty label returns ''.
keyExports.domainSlug: Lowercases, replaces any non [a-z0-9-] run with '-', collapses repeats, trims leading/trailing '-'. A segment with no admissible characters (e.g. '___', non-ASCII 'ünï') slugs to '' — a refusal, not a best-effort transliteration.

assumptions: Non-ASCII letters are dropped, not transliterated, because the alphabet is what node ids are compared in and per-language transliteration is not the engine's job.
invariants: domainSlug is idempotent: applying it to its own output returns the same string, so a caller can never mint a label that itself re-slugs to something different.

annotation.summary: Stage-2 domain tagging engine: path-segment tags, basename heuristics (suffixes like .controller, .service), import-graph cluster propagation via label propagation, repovine.domains.json pattern/alias matching, package labels, infra resource exclude/keep matching, and heavy vs lightweight classification into module domain tags and tagged edges.

keyExports.collectAllDomainTags: Primary entry: returns {tagsByModule Map, classification Map} — heavy/lightweight domain tiers.
keyExports.evaluateBasenameCandidate: Promotes stem from suffix files (.controller, .service) when graph connectivity threshold met.
keyExports.getClusterDomains: Label propagation on import graph for emergent package-adjacent domains.
keyExports.getPathBasedDomains: Directory-segment domain tags excluding structural dirs.
