keyExports.resolveDomainToCanonical: Maps config aliases to canonical domain id strings.

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types unchanged; domain logic unchanged.

sideEffects.description: loadDomainsConfig reads repovine.domains.json during collectAllDomainTags

risks: Overlapping repovine.domains.json patterns can double-tag modules.
Cluster propagation may over-merge unrelated modules in dense import hubs.
patterns: Tagged edge tagSource distinguishes path, package, cluster, and pattern origins.
Basename suffixes and PascalCase stems evaluated with graph connectivity gates.
invariants: Domain tags are additive — a module may carry multiple domain labels.
Lightweight domains (1-2 modules) hidden from anomalies unless explicitly included.
annotation.integrationPoints: repovine.domains.json via domains-schema; stage2 graph build; map_context domain scopes; domains advisor.
annotation.dataFlow: repovine.domains.json patterns + path/cluster heuristics -> module domain tags -> tagged edges -> domain: scopes in map_context and annotation roll-ups.

annotation.summary: First-run domains advisor: scans snapshot infra resource suffix histograms (INFRA_NOISE_SUFFIXES), witness-aware mixed-suffix patterns (infra.excludePatterns), PascalCase module basename ratio, and infra folder path clusters to propose repovine.domains.json additions. Returns mergedConfig (accept/exclude preview) and keepConfig (committed infra.keep preview); applyDomainsSuggestion/applyDomainsKeep merge without writing disk.

keyExports.applyDomainsKeep: Symmetric to applyDomainsSuggestion: maps infra suffix/pattern suggestions to infra.keep.suffixes/patterns so resources stay visible and stop being proposed.
keyExports.applyDomainsSuggestion: Merges accepted additions into DomainsConfigFile (excludeSuffixes, excludePatterns, basename.pascalCase, domains.paths).
keyExports.computeDomainsSuggestion: Runs infra suffix/pattern, PascalCase basename, and infra folder path heuristics; filters declined ids; builds mergedConfig and keepConfig previews.
keyExports.readDomainsConfigFile: Reads repovine.domains.json via DomainsConfigSchema; returns {} on missing/invalid.

assumptions: Never writes repovine.domains.json without explicit user approval.
Mixed suffix buckets emit infra.excludePatterns with spared witnessed labels instead of blanket excludeSuffixes.

sideEffects.description: readDomainsConfigFile reads repovine.domains.json

risks: Auto-applying infra excludeSuffixes/patterns without review can hide legitimate domain tags on noisy resource labels.
keepConfig commits survive .repovine/ wipe unlike declined cache — user must understand keep vs decline.
patterns: INFRA_NOISE_SUFFIXES list drives infra.excludeSuffixes suggestions from runtime-resource label histogram.
computeInfraDomainPathSuggestions proposes domains axis entries for ^infrastructure/<folder> patterns.
annotation.flowDescription: Suffix histogram + graph module paths -> computeDomainsSuggestion -> formatDomainsConfigFile preview for MCP/CLI onboarding.
invariants: basename.pascalCase suggestion requires >=12 PascalCase modules and ratio >=0.25.
Non-infra axes are no-ops in applyDomainsKeep.
annotation.integrationPoints: MCP suggest_domains_config and decline_domains_config_suggestions; cli domains-advisor; RepovineRuntime domainsSuggestions after build.
annotation.stateShape: DomainsSuggestionAddition discriminated by axis infra.excludeSuffixes | infra.excludePatterns | basename.pascalCase | domains; DomainsSuggestion wraps additions[], axes[], declinedHidden, mergedConfig, keepConfig previews.
annotation.dataFlow: RepositoryFactsSnapshot infraModules + module basenames -> computeDomainsSuggestion -> DomainsSuggestion with mergedConfig preview -> suggest_domains_config MCP / CLI onboarding.

annotation.summary: Schema and loader for repovine.domains.json. Validates with a strict Zod schema (domains paths/aliases, infra exclude/keep/pruneInert, basename rules, package grouping, structural dirs), compiles globs via the shared compileGlob from @repovine/plugin-sdk/src/glob (avoiding regex catastrophic backtracking) to GlobMatcher and aliases to a lookup map, hands stage2 the compiled DomainsConfig for domain tagging and inert-resource pruning.

keyExports.DOMAINS_CONFIG_MERGE_STRATEGY: Marks infra.pruneInert as set-once during a setup merge.
keyExports.DomainsConfig: DomainsConfigFile plus compiled caches: _aliasToCanonical Record, _fileAsDomainInclude/Exclude GlobMatcher[], _structuralDirs Set.
keyExports.DomainsConfigFile: type DomainsConfigFile = z.infer<typeof DomainsConfigSchema> — the raw parsed shape before compiled caches are attached.
keyExports.DomainsConfigSchema: Strict Zod schema for domains{paths,aliases}, infra{excludeSuffixes,excludePatterns,keep,pruneInert}, basename, packages, structuralDirs.
keyExports.loadDomainsConfig: (repoRoot: string): DomainsConfig | null — reads and validates repovine.domains.json.

assumptions: Missing repovine.domains.json is normal: loadDomainsConfig returns null.
infra.pruneInert defaults off; infra.keep is the per-resource opt-out.
Alias lookup is case-insensitive; canonical names and aliases are lowercased in the map.

sideEffects.description: loadDomainsConfig reads repovine.domains.json from repo root
reports schema validation and parse failures

risks: pruneInert=true drops unwitnessed runtime-resource nodes; a misconfigured keep marker silently hides resources.

risks.text: Callers must treat null as 'no config' not an error; must not assume compiled cache fields are present on a hand-built config.
repovine.domains.json is a committed config contract: one unknown top-level key fails validation and the file is discarded. A key must exist in DomainsConfigSchema before consumers can write it.

patterns: compileGlob (from @repovine/plugin-sdk/src/glob) is shared between this loader and the domains advisor preview, so suggestions match loader behavior.
Compiled caches are computed once at load and carried on the config object.
annotation.flowDescription: Zod-parse repovine.domains.json, compile globs to a matcher plus an alias map and a structural-dirs set, then expose the DomainsConfig used for stage2 domain tagging.
invariants: The schema is strict: unknown top-level keys are rejected rather than ignored.
DOMAINS_CONFIG_MERGE_STRATEGY marks infra.pruneInert as set-once during a setup merge.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by stage2 domain tagging/inert pruning, MCP suggest_domains_config advisor, CLI domains flow; resolves config path through mod:repovine/src/paths; compiles globs via mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/glob.
annotation.stateShape: DomainsConfigFile (DomainsConfigSchema): optional domains record {paths?,aliases?}, infra {excludeSuffixes?,excludePatterns?}, basename {pascalCase?,files{include?,exclude?}}, packages {enabled?,exclude?,rename?,merge?}, structuralDirs?; DomainsConfig extends with compiled caches _aliasToCanonical, _fileAsDomainInclude/_Exclude GlobMatcher[], _structuralDirs Set.
annotation.dataFlow: repoRoot → repovine.domains.json → Zod safeParse → compiled aliases/globs/structural dirs → DomainsConfig → stage2 tagging and pruning.

annotation.summary: Read-only post-composition integrity gate: validateComposedGraph checks that every stage1 snapshot module/template projects to a stage2 graph node and no edge references a missing node; summarizeGraphValidationProblems formats results. Wired into composeRepositoryGraph — warns by default, throws under REPOVINE_DEV.

keyExports.summarizeGraphValidationProblems: One-line summary of the first N problems for log/throw.

assumptions: Runs after composeRepositoryGraph's interpreter composer, inert-resource prune and domain passes complete, so it treats the graph as structurally final at call time.

A node dropped together with all its edges (e.g. pruneInertRuntimeResources) is a by-design blind spot: it never produces a dangling-edge finding on its own, only a missing-module/-template finding when the snapshot record itself is checked.
risks: If composeRepositoryGraph changes its pruning/mutation passes, re-verify invariants still hold.
Node dropped together with all its edges yields no dangling edge; missing-module still catches it, but co-dropped pairs are a by-design blind spot.
invariants: Never mutates the graph; intentional inert-resource pruning leaves a consistent graph.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by stage2/index composeRepositoryGraph after domain passes; consumed by FindingF3 audit gate.

annotation.summary: Built-in interpreter bootstrap. Imports INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS from interpreters/index and registerInterpreter each into stage2/interpreter/registry; auto-invoked on import before stage2 compose.

keyExports.bootstrapInternalInterpreters: Registers all built-in interpreters from INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream interpreters and registry; bootstrap side-effect still accurate.

sideEffects.description: Populates interpreter registry on first import

risks: Missing interpreter in INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS silently omits graph or entrypoint contributions.
patterns: No manifest ceremony — built-ins register directly like source plugins.
annotation.integrationPoints: interpreters/index INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS; stage2/index imports bootstrap side-effect before compose.
annotation.dataFlow: import bootstrap → registerInterpreter for each INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS entry.

annotation.summary: Runs the interpreter layers over the built graph. It decides which interpreters apply to this repository, orders them by declared phase, then lets each contribute graph changes and entrypoint fragments. Interpreters that do not apply are recorded rather than run, so an enrichment that produced nothing is distinguishable from one that never ran.

keyExports.ComposeInterpretersOptions: The graph and snapshot to work on, the module index, the domain configuration, an optional interpreter override and an optional logger.
keyExports.InterpreterCompositionResult: The applied and skipped identifiers plus the collected entrypoint fragments.
keyExports.composeInterpreters: Filters, orders and runs the interpreters, returning which ran, which were skipped, and the entrypoints collected.

assumptions: Two independent conditions gate an interpreter: any of its requiresSemanticHints keys must be present on some module's semanticHints, and every one of its requiresSnapshotFacts slots must be non-empty on the snapshot.
The hint check walks a dotted path and gates on the key being present, so an interpreter whose required hint no module emits never runs. A slot present but empty still enables it.
Ordering is purely by declared phase (INTERPRETER_PHASES: nodes then links), not by an inter-interpreter dependency graph; within a phase the input order is preserved but carries no meaning.

Graph contributions are applied on the trusted path: the schema check exists but is switched off here, so a node with a bogus type or a foreign data shape reaches the graph unchecked and the interpreter is still reported as applied. The application step enforces only referential rules — a node id already present is skipped, an edge whose endpoints are absent is dropped without a warning.
Both hooks are optional; an interpreter may contribute graph changes, entrypoints, or neither.
A duplicate interpreter id among the composed set throws rather than silently overwriting.
The interpreter list can be supplied directly, which is what lets tests compose a known set instead of the registry.

sideEffects.description: applies validated deltas to the graph passed in

risks: The skipped list records the identifier but not the reason, so an interpreter missing because the repository lacks its language looks identical to one missing because a hint was never produced — the two need very different fixes.
A skip is silent in the sense that the pipeline succeeds: the enrichment is simply absent from the graph, and nothing downstream can tell it was expected.
The applied list names every interpreter that was ordered, including one that implements neither hook, so it reports what was enabled rather than what actually contributed.
patterns: Filter, order, then run: applicability is decided before anything touches the graph.
One shared context serves both hooks, so an interpreter sees the same view whichever it implements.
invariants: An interpreter that fails either gate is recorded and never invoked.
An empty interpreter set returns an empty result rather than failing.
A duplicate interpreter id in the composed set throws before anything runs.
annotation.integrationPoints: The registered interpreters come from mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/registry; the hook contracts from mod:repovine/src/interpreter/types; validation and application from mod:repovine/src/graph and mod:repovine/src/graph/delta; the domain configuration from mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains; entrypoint fragments carry the slot marker defined in mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-slots.
annotation.dataFlow: registered interpreters -> language/hint and snapshot-fact gates -> phase order (nodes then links) -> per interpreter, a validated graph delta and any entrypoint fragments -> applied and skipped identifiers with the collected fragments.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Enables informational logging from the default logger

annotation.summary: The shared vocabulary that lets independent interpreter layers label the entrypoints they produce. Each produced entry carries a hidden slot marker naming the kind of entrypoint it is. The server shell later replays entries slot by slot to reproduce a fixed public ordering, then removes the marker so what callers see matches the older inline shape exactly.

keyExports.EntrypointSlot: The eight slot names an entry can carry: api-route, file-api, jsx-route, tanstack-route, angular-route, conditional, file-page, service-trigger.
keyExports.LAYER_ENTRYPOINT_SLOT_KEY: The hidden field name the marker is stored under.
keyExports.SlottedEntrypointFragment: An entrypoint fragment that carries the marker.
keyExports.stripEntrypointFragmentInternals: Returns a shallow copy of an entry with the marker removed, for public output.

assumptions: This lives outside every layer on purpose, so the frontend, backend and infrastructure producers can all use the same slot names without importing one another.
Ordering authority belongs to the server shell, not to the layers: producers only label their entries and the shell decides the sequence.
The marker is an internal detail with a reserved-looking name, which is why it is stripped rather than documented.

risks.text: Slot names are matched as strings by the replay index rather than resolved through types, so callers depending on entrypoint ordering must verify their slot set against the replay list rather than assume a rename propagates.

risks: The strip is shallow, so nested objects stay shared with the original entry and a later mutation of the returned copy reaches the source.
patterns: A neutral vocabulary module breaks what would otherwise be cross-imports between sibling layers.
Producers label, one consumer orders: the layers stay unaware of the public sequence.
invariants: The marker never appears in public output; it is removed on the way out.
Every slotted fragment carries exactly one slot name.
annotation.integrationPoints: The slot names are attached by the interpreter layers that produce entrypoints (ui-entrypoints, server-entrypoints, infra-runtime-links) and consumed by the server-side entrypoint index, which replays by slot and then calls the strip before returning; the fragment type comes from mod:repovine/src/interpreter/types.
annotation.dataFlow: layer produces a fragment -> marker attached -> shell indexes fragments by slot -> replays them in the fixed order -> marker stripped -> public entrypoint list.

annotation.summary: In-memory entrypoint store keyed by RepositoryGraph. rememberInterpreterEntrypoints saves interpreter collectEntrypoints output; getInterpreterEntrypoints supplies mcp/lib/entrypoints replay during get_entrypoints and trace_flow.

keyExports.getInterpreterEntrypoints: Returns fragments stored for this graph instance.
keyExports.rememberInterpreterEntrypoints: Attaches collected EntrypointFragment[] to graph WeakMap.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream interpreter/types and types; WeakMap entrypoint store unchanged.

sideEffects.description: WeakMap entry per RepositoryGraph for collected entrypoints

risks: Replacing graph object without re-compose yields empty get_entrypoints until refresh_context.
patterns: Graph-scoped side store — not persisted in .repovine cache JSON.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage2/interpreter/composer; mcp/lib/entrypoints getInterpreterEntrypoints replay.
annotation.dataFlow: composeInterpreters collectEntrypoints → rememberInterpreterEntrypoints → getInterpreterEntrypoints in mcp/lib/entrypoints.

annotation.summary: Stage-2 interpreter plugin registry. registerInterpreter collects built-in Interpreter objects; getInterpreterRegistrations returns the list for composer orchestration; setInterpretersForTest supports unit tests.

keyExports.getInterpreterRegistrations: Readonly view of registered Interpreter plugins.
keyExports.setInterpretersForTest: Test hook replacing registry with restore teardown.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream mod:repovine/src/interpreter/types; registry API and integrationPoints unchanged.

sideEffects.description: Mutates in-memory interpreters array

risks: Duplicate interpreter ids are not rejected at register time — composer must detect conflicts.
patterns: Singleton registry symmetric to detector-registry and source plugin registry.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage2/interpreter/bootstrap registerInterpreter loop; interpreter/composer getInterpreterRegistrations.

annotation.summary: Shared display helper for graph module and infra-module node labels. Produces a compact two-segment tail (…/dir/file) for deep relative paths so MCP navigation stays readable without losing local context. Neutral utility extracted from the old stage2 inline passes for use by code-structure and infra-runtime-links interpreters.

keyExports.shortModuleLabel: Compact display label: …/parent/file for deep paths, full path when ≤2 segments; strips the module-id suffix via plugin-host/source-set's stripModuleIdSuffix before splitting.

assumptions: Used for graph node labels in MCP map_context and inspect_node — not full paths.

Suffix stripping is delegated to the registry-driven stripModuleIdSuffix rather than a hardcoded extension list, so the label reduces a path the same way the module id itself is built (global.d.ts → global, index.ts/index.mjs → index).
Paths with ≤2 segments are returned whole; longer paths show an ellipsis prefix plus the last two segments.
risks: Two-segment collision possible for unrelated files sharing the same parent/name suffix — acceptable for display-only labels.
Does not strip .cpp/.py extensions — only the suffixes stripModuleIdSuffix's registry recognizes.
patterns: Extracted from the former inline copy in stage2/index.ts so code-structure and infra-runtime-links layers share one implementation.
invariants: Pure function — no I/O or global state.
Always returns forward-slash joined segments even on Windows inputs.
annotation.integrationPoints: interpreter code-structure graph pass2Modules; interpreter infra-runtime-links graph pass2Infra; any layer adding module nodes with compact labels.
annotation.dataFlow: mod.relativeFilePath → shortModuleLabel → graph module/infra node label in code-structure and infra-runtime-links layers.

annotation.summary: The two-phase projection composer: runs every enabled plugin contributor against an immutable fact view, buffers its batches, validates them, builds one global reference index, settles references and key conflicts against it, then applies survivors (resources/nodes, then links, then entrypoints, then extensions) in a stable order.

keyExports.BatchOutcome: interface { batchId: string; status: BatchStatus; reason?: string }.
keyExports.ContributorOutcome: interface { pluginId: string; contributorId: string; status: ContributorStatus; reason?: string; batches: BatchOutcome[] }.
keyExports.ProjectionCompositionInput: interface { contributors: readonly ProjectionContributorRegistration[]; input: ReadonlyProjectionInput; knownModuleIds: ReadonlySet<string>; knownNodeIds: ReadonlySet<string>; knownResourceIds?: ReadonlySet<string> }.
keyExports.ProjectionCompositionResult: interface { delta: GraphDelta; entrypoints: EntrypointFragment[]; extensions: ExtensionRecord[]; contributors: ContributorOutcome[]; refusals: Refusal[] }.
keyExports.composeProjections: (input: ProjectionCompositionInput) => ProjectionCompositionResult. Contributors run in pluginId+contributor.id sorted order (registration order decides nothing). A contributor that throws, returns a non-array, or exceeds PROJECTION_BUDGETS.maxBatchesPerContributor is marked 'failed' and loses only its own output. Each batch is validated (shape/budgets/spelling, duplicate local keys, reused batchId, a minted resource id already in the graph), then a settle loop repeatedly checks dangling references and same-key conflicting content, rejecting offending batches until the surviving set is stable (each round only rejects, so it terminates).
keyExports.emptyProjectionCompositionResult: () => ProjectionCompositionResult with delta:{nodes:[],edges:[]}, entrypoints:[], extensions:[], contributors:[], refusals:[].

assumptions: Order independence: every reference resolves against one global index built after every contributor's batches are buffered, so a reference to a not-yet-registered contributor's output resolves exactly like one to an earlier one — there is no contributor DAG.

Atomicity is per batch (one module or one infra document): a batch that fails validation, carries a dangling reference, or conflicts with another contribution's key contributes nothing, leaving the contributor's other batches and every other contributor's work untouched.

Two contributions sharing a key (resource namespace/localKey, entrypoint id, or plugin+schema+extension localKey) must carry identical content or both are refused as a conflict (PROJECTION_CONFLICT_REFUSAL).
A projected resource id colliding with an id already in knownNodeIds is refused — a projection mints an id, it never claims one that exists.

annotation.summary: Converts an accepted EntrypointContribution (from a plugin projector) into the stable id and EntrypointFragment shape every entrypoint reader already consumes, so a projected route lands on the same entry as a built-in that produced the equivalent execution start.

keyExports.CONVERTED_ENTRYPOINT_KINDS: const, set to ENTRYPOINT_CONTRIBUTION_KINDS (from @repovine/plugin-sdk) — the contribution kinds this converter answers for.
keyExports.projectedEntrypointId: (contribution: EntrypointContribution) => string. Switch over contribution.kind: 'api-route' => `entrypoint:api:${moduleId}:${path}:${method}`; 'file-route' => `entrypoint:file:${moduleId}:${path}:${fileType}` plus `:${method}` when present; 'ui-route' => `entrypoint:route:${moduleId}:${path}`; 'conditional-render' => `entrypoint:conditional:${moduleId}:${component}`; 'resource-trigger' => `entrypoint:${triggerKind}:${makeResourceId(resourceRef)}:${discriminator}`.
keyExports.toEntrypointFragment: (contribution: EntrypointContribution) => EntrypointFragment. 'resource-trigger' contributions map to { id, kind: triggerKind, layer:'backend', serviceId: makeResourceId(resourceRef), discriminator, handlerModule?, label?, source:'projection' }; other kinds map through FRAGMENT_KINDS to { id, kind, moduleId, label?, source:'projection', layer:'backend'|'frontend', ...kind-specific fields (path/method/fileType/component) }.

assumptions: FRAGMENT_KINDS mapping (verbatim, excludes 'resource-trigger'): 'api-route' -> 'api', 'file-route' -> 'route', 'ui-route' -> 'route', 'conditional-render' -> 'conditional-render'.
The fragment `kind` vocabulary is narrower than the contribution vocabulary by design: distinct contribution kinds that start execution the same way share one fragment kind.
The switch over contribution.kind is total by construction: a kind added to ENTRYPOINT_CONTRIBUTION_KINDS without a matching arm here is a compile error.

annotation.summary: Builds the immutable ReadonlyFactView a projection contributor reads: indexes RepositoryFactsSnapshot modules/infraModules by id, buckets published facts by schema (sorted for reproducible order), and exposes hasModule/moduleIds/module/hasResource/infraModules/select as read-only queries. Carries no producer id, so a contributor cannot ask 'who published this fact'.

keyExports.FactViewInput: Input shape: snapshot, optional facts and resourceIds.
keyExports.createFactView: Builds the ReadonlyFactView from a FactViewInput (snapshot/facts/resourceIds).

assumptions: select() filters by selector.field only for object, non-array fact values.

annotation.summary: Bridges the published contract's kebab-case SemanticLinkRelation names to the graph's own underscore-spelled EdgeKind. RELATION_EDGE_KINDS is the one total map between the two vocabularies; relationEdgeKind looks a relation up in it; PUBLISHED_RELATIONS re-exposes the contract's relation list in contract order.

keyExports.PUBLISHED_RELATIONS: The published relations, in contract (plugin-sdk SEMANTIC_LINK_RELATIONS) order.
keyExports.RELATION_EDGE_KINDS: Frozen total map: every SemanticLinkRelation to its internal EdgeKind.
keyExports.relationEdgeKind: Looks up a relation's EdgeKind in RELATION_EDGE_KINDS.

risks: RELATION_EDGE_KINDS is total over plugin-sdk's SEMANTIC_LINK_RELATIONS; adding a relation to that contract without adding a case here is a compile error, not a silently-dropped link.

annotation.summary: Builder-level witness rule: after the graph composer finishes, drops runtime-resource nodes that carry only structural contains/tagged edges (no load-bearing witness). Gated by infra.pruneInert (off by default); infra.keep suffixes/patterns opt out per resource label via matchesInfraResourceExclude.

keyExports.pruneInertRuntimeResources: Mutates RepositoryGraph in place — deletes unwitnessed runtime-resource nodes and incident edges; returns pruned count (0 when pruneInert disabled or nothing to prune).

assumptions: Must run after every load-bearing edge is added (post interpreter composer) and before graph consumers.
Inert resources only carry contains/tagged, so pruning never orphans load-bearing edges.

sideEffects.description: Mutates graph.nodes, graph.byType, graph.edges, graph.outEdges, graph.inEdges in place

risks: Enabling pruneInert without reviewing keep markers can remove resources agents expect in topology queries.
Misconfigured keep patterns may fail to protect intended resources.
invariants: No-op (returns 0) unless config.infra.pruneInert is true.
Resources matching infra.keep suffixes/patterns are never pruned.
annotation.integrationPoints: matchesInfraResourceExclude comes from mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains; isWitnessedNode/nodesOfType from mod:repovine/src/graph; runs as part of the stage-2 build pipeline after the interpreter composer, gated by the loaded domains config's infra.pruneInert.

annotation.summary: Phase 3.1 projection layer: maps enriched semanticHints.routes with source:'file' into legacy FileBasedRoute records for MCP get_entrypoints replay. Canonical file-route inference lives in source-plugins/typescript collectFileRoutes; this module only filters (framework + fileType present) and shapes, stateless and graph-free.

keyExports.FileBasedRoute: Legacy MCP shape: path, framework, moduleId, fileType.
keyExports.fileBasedEntryKind: Maps fileType strings (page, layout, default → page; api, server, server-api, route → api; else route).
keyExports.inferFileBasedRoutes: Iterates snapshot.modules; keeps routes where declaredIn==='layout' and both framework and fileType are set.

assumptions: A route is kept only when its declaredIn is 'layout' and both framework and fileType are present; a route missing either field is dropped rather than emitted with defaults.
fileBasedEntryKind has a catch-all 'route' fallback for any fileType string outside the recognized page/api sets, so a new framework's fileType never throws.
risks: Routes missing framework or fileType are silently skipped — under-reporting when plugins omit fields.
Novel framework fileType conventions may mis-classify via fileBasedEntryKind heuristics.
patterns: Thin compatibility shim between stage-1 RouteInfo hints and MCP entrypoint consumers.
annotation.flowDescription: snapshot.modules[].semanticHints.routes (source:file) → FileBasedRoute[] → ui-entrypoints file-page slot and mcp/lib/entrypoints file-api/file-page replay keys.
invariants: inferFileBasedRoutes is stateless and graph-free.
fileBasedEntryKind returns only page | route | api.
annotation.integrationPoints: source-plugins/typescript collectFileRoutes (upstream inference); ui-entrypoints collectUiRouteEntrypoints; mcp/lib/entrypoints fileApiLayerKey/filePageLayerKey replay.
annotation.stateShape: Stateless pure functions — no module-level mutable state; input snapshot modules are read-only.
annotation.dataFlow: collectFileRoutes (stage-1) → RouteInfo with source:file → inferFileBasedRoutes → fileBasedEntryKind → interpreter slots → MCP replay.

annotation.summary: Stage-2 infra-to-code linking helpers: resolves the repo-relative directory holding a resource's code from its infra template attributes (SAM CodeUri or a Terraform/archive filename), and builds the deduplicated list of search roots stage-2 handler resolution walks to find a runtime entrypoint module.

keyExports.resolveArtifactRoot: Derives the repo-relative artifact root from a resource's codeUri attribute or an archive filename attribute (stripping .zip/.jar/.war), relative to the infra template's own directory; returns undefined when attributes are missing or the location is an absolute URL.
keyExports.runtimeEntrySearchRoots: Builds the deduplicated search-root list for handler resolution: the artifact root (if resolved), the linking config's configured handler search roots, and each package's root and src directory.

assumptions: normalizeLinkingConfig applies build.linking defaults before its handlers.searchRoots are read.
snapshot.packages is already populated (by stage 1) when runtimeEntrySearchRoots runs.
codeUri is tried before filename when a resource's attributes carry both.
risks: A codeUri or filename matching an absolute URL scheme (e.g. `s3://...`) is treated as unresolvable and contributes no artifact root, so a resource whose code location is a URL is invisible to handler search.
patterns: Falls back through multiple search roots (artifact root, configured handler roots, each package's root and src dir) rather than requiring the handler module to sit at one exact predicted path.
invariants: resolveArtifactRoot returns undefined when attributes is absent or neither codeUri nor filename resolves to a usable path.
An archive filename (.zip/.jar/.war) is stripped before its directory is taken as the root.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used during stage-2 graph build linking to resolve infra-to-handler-module search paths; normalizeLinkingConfig comes from mod:repovine/src/stage1/linking-config, path helpers from mod:repovine/src/platform/paths.
annotation.dataFlow: infra resource attributes (codeUri/filename) + infra template path + snapshot.linkingConfig + snapshot.packages -> resolveArtifactRoot / runtimeEntrySearchRoots -> deduplicated repo-relative directories for handler-module search.

annotation.summary: Maps an IaC service trigger record to the MCP entrypoint-kind string used by get_entrypoints and infra-runtime-links, using registered trigger-type metadata from the IaC plugin registry so Lambda/API Gateway/SQS/etc. triggers classify consistently across ecosystems. Falls back to a 'webhook' sub-kind when the catalog resolves 'api' and the trigger path looks like a webhook. Lives in stage2/runtime (not MCP) so interpreters own entrypoint construction without importing MCP internals (handoff T5).

keyExports.triggerEntryKind: Maps trigger { type?, path? } + DeclarationCatalog + carrier { namespace?, provider? } to an entrypoint kind string (api, webhook, schedule, unknown, ...).

assumptions: trigger.type missing, catalog omitted, or the type unregistered in the catalog all resolve to 'unknown'.
carrier.namespace/provider are forwarded to catalogTriggerTypeMeta only when defined, so the lookup narrows to the resource's own ecosystem rather than matching across providers.
The webhook sub-kind only applies when the catalog resolves entrypointKind to 'api' and trigger.path, lowercased, contains 'webhook'.
risks: Webhook detection via substring match on path may false-positive.
Unknown trigger types collapse to 'unknown' — entrypoint filtering may hide them.
patterns: Neutral stage2 runtime helper extracted for handoff T5 — decouples the infra-runtime-links interpreter from the MCP shell.
invariants: Returns 'unknown' when trigger.type is missing or unregistered.
Pure over its arguments — no graph access, no I/O.
annotation.integrationPoints: Trigger-type metadata from stage1/iac plugin registry (catalogTriggerTypeMeta); consumed by mcp/lib/entrypoints and the infra-runtime-links interpreter to build service-trigger entrypoints.
annotation.dataFlow: runtime-resource node trigger → triggerEntryKind → mcp/lib/entrypoints service-trigger slot keys; infra-runtime-links/entrypoints collectServiceTriggerEntrypoints.

annotation.summary: worker_threads isolate entry for the Stage 2 compose offload: reloads the plugin set the snapshot names (so a build with plugin projectors composes off the control plane instead of degrading to inline), runs composeRepositoryGraph inside the worker so the synchronous compose never blocks the MCP control plane, and posts the graph plus interpreter entrypoints, composed refusals, graph extensions, and the projection report back to the parent by postMessage.
assumptions: Spawned only via worker_threads with { snapshot } in workerData and a live parentPort; throws otherwise.

Loads the plugin set from snapshot.plugins (falling back to defaultPluginsConfig()) through the same loadPluginSet path the control plane used, then remembers its runtime via rememberPluginRuntime(snapshot, report.runtime) before composing.
modulesById is rebuilt from snapshot.modules inside composeRepositoryGraph — only the serializable snapshot crosses the boundary.

sideEffects.description: reloads the plugin set and runs Stage 2 compose in a worker isolate; unref's parentPort so it exits after replying
reroutes console.log → stderr and silences the pipeline log sink to protect the parent's JSON-RPC stdout channel

risks: The reply carries { type:'ok', graph, entrypoints, refusals, extensions, contributors }; entrypoints and composed refusals are posted EXPLICITLY because their process-local WeakMap/Map sidecars (keyed by the graph object) do not survive structured clone — dropping either field silently yields empty entrypoints/refusals in the parent.
console.log lands on stdout by default, which would corrupt the parent's JSON-RPC stream — the reroute is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
The worker reloads the plugin set independently of the parent's own load; a plugin config mismatch between the two processes would only surface here, inside the isolate.
annotation.integrationPoints: Spawned by mod:repovine/src/stage2/index (runStage2InWorker); the parent re-keys the posted entrypoints and refusals onto the cloned graph via mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store and mod:repovine/src/stage2 respectively; plugin set reload goes through mod:repovine/src/plugin-host/load and mod:repovine/src/plugin-host/runtime-store; extensions and the projection report come from mod:repovine/src/graph/build-artifact.

annotation.summary: Central repovine type hub for plugin facts, graph taxonomy, MCP views, and annotations. Snapshot config identity (analysisVersion, engineBuildId), original Kubernetes kind, capped-link pagination, and bounded-grep metadata are explicit typed contracts; stage1/plugin-sdk types are re-exported, graph-stage types are defined here.

keyExports.AnnotationContent: Writable annotation field bag; sideEffects typed as SideEffect[].
keyExports.GraphDelta: Interpreter patch {nodes, edges} validated by mod:repovine/src/graph/delta.
keyExports.GraphNode: Discriminated union keyed by NodeType with NodeDataByType payloads.
keyExports.NodeViewDetail: MCP inspect payload: NodeView plus optional body/grepMatches/pagination.
keyExports.RepositoryFactsSnapshot: Stage-1 snapshot: modules[], infraModules[], templates?, linkingConfig?, bundleOutputHandlerMap? (bundle output path to source entry path), outsideRepoPaths? (candidates refused for resolving outside the workspace root), analysisVersion? (manual cache-invalidation version), engineBuildId? (dev-only reuse-gate fingerprint, mod:repovine/src/stage1/engine-build-id).
keyExports.RepositoryGraph: In-memory graph container {nodes, edges} consumed by MCP tools.
keyExports.StoredAnnotation: Persisted note with contentHash, importBaseline, schemaVersion, provenance.
keyExports.TagEdgeSource: Provenance for tagged edges: path | package | cluster | pattern.

assumptions: Stage-1/plugin-sdk types are re-exported from @repovine/plugin-sdk; graph-stage types are defined in this file.
AnnotationContent.sideEffects uses SideEffect[] from mod:repovine/src/annotations/side-effect-vocab.
risks: Wide fan-in (~63 downstream) on GraphNode, NodeType, or RepositoryFactsSnapshot changes.
keyExports must reference symbols exported from this module graph node, including re-exports tracked by the builder.
patterns: Shared contract hub — breaking changes ripple stage1, stage2, MCP, annotations, and plugins.
Producer/engine split: Semantic*Delta types carry language/infra semantics; engine stamps ids/paths/hashes.
annotation.flowDescription: Stage-1 modules populate ModuleInfo → stage2 graph nodes/edges → annotations attach to graph node ids.
invariants: SemanticModuleDelta.transient=true forces empty contentHash so poisoned extractions are not cached.
Re-exported plugin-sdk types must stay compatible with mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types.
extensionPoints: NodeDataByType and DomainNodeData tier/weight fields extend graph metadata without new NodeType values.
Open-string InfraKind/WebFramework slots allow additive plugin vocabulary.
annotation.integrationPoints: Hub for stage1 finalize, stage2 runtime-links/domains, MCP inspect_node/search, annotations read/write; re-exports mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types.
annotation.dataFlow: Plugin-sdk types re-exported → stage1 fills RepositoryFactsSnapshot → stage2 builds RepositoryGraph/GraphNode → MCP emits NodeView/NodeViewDetail → StoredAnnotation keyed by graph node id.

annotation.summary: Compose service `cli` (profile cli) in examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.yaml: one-shot `node scripts/langgraph-cli.mjs` run for CI/local debug. Shares the egress-gw network namespace, NODE_OPTIONS heap guardrail, and the hardened x-harness-app settings (read-only rootfs, cap_drop ALL). Command args pass through to langgraph-cli.mjs; exits non-zero unless the task completes and passes compliance.
assumptions: Profile cli: docker compose --profile cli run --rm cli --goal "..." (also invocable via npm run docker:cli -- --goal ...).
Command args pass through to langgraph-cli.mjs after the image entrypoint.
Depends on workspace-init completing and egress-gw being healthy, inherited from the x-harness-app anchor.
Exits non-zero when compliance fails or credentials block the worker.

sideEffects.description: Runs the full Delivery Protocol cycle (validate-assignment → worker → validate-result → compliance) via invokeGraph
Writes artifacts under .harness in the bind-mounted sandbox

risks: Missing provider credentials yield blocked runs with exit 1.
Long multi-agent runs can hit HARNESS_MEM_LIMIT despite NODE_OPTIONS if subprocess memory grows.
Stale local .env ALLOW_DOMAINS blocks HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK's npm install/build/test unless npm is added to ALLOW_DOMAINS.
patterns: Compose profile isolates CLI runs from http/tg-bot long-running services.
invariants: One-shot container — not a long-running service.
Shares the egress-gw network namespace for controlled outbound access.

This service is the sandbox half of the pair: resource:generic:cli-attach runs the same entrypoint against a mounted host worktree, and only this one waits on workspace-init and mounts the managed .workspace.
annotation.integrationPoints: examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.yaml profile cli; scripts/langgraph-cli.mjs; mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow invokeGraph; x-harness-app Dockerfile build.
annotation.dataFlow: compose run cli → shared harness-app image → langgraph-cli.mjs → invokeGraph → .harness artifacts on bind-mounted sandbox.

annotation.summary: Compose service `cli-attach` (profile attach-cli) in examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.attach.yaml: the attach-mode counterpart of `cli`. Mounts a pre-created host Git worktree at /workspace instead of the managed sandbox, and runs one-shot `node scripts/langgraph-cli.mjs` as the worktree owner so writes land with the operator's uid and gid.
assumptions: scripts/attach-launcher.mjs is the supported entrypoint: it runs the fail-closed preflight and creates the state layout before any docker call.

The YAML merge is wholesale per key: declaring local volumes, depends_on or environment replaces the anchor's value entirely, which is how attach avoids mounting .workspace and avoids waiting on workspace-init.
HARNESS_TARGET_MODE=attach and HARNESS_REPO_ROOT=/workspace mark the run for the target-repo policy; HOME points at the container state dir.

sideEffects.description: writes into the operator's mounted worktree as the operator's uid/gid
runs the full Delivery Protocol cycle through a provider worker

risks: A direct `docker compose --profile attach-cli up` with hand-set environment bypasses the launcher preflight. That is a deliberate operator override, unsupported and not prevented here.

Attach vars deliberately avoid the `${VAR:?}` required form in compose.yaml itself, because Compose interpolates the whole file before profile filtering and a required-var error would break every sandbox invocation; the overlay confines `${VAR:?}` to attach so an unset var fails container create instead of Docker auto-creating a root-owned host directory.
annotation.integrationPoints: Launched through scripts/attach-launcher.mjs; shares the harness-app image and the egress-gw network namespace with mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/target-repo deciding attach policy.

annotation.summary: Compose service egress-gw: Alpine sidecar with dnsmasq, ipset, iptables, GitHub CIDR bootstrap, and startup/healthcheck egress probes. Harness containers attach via network_mode:service:egress-gw for fail-closed provider, Telegram, npm, and GitHub release-asset egress. Declared twice: full definition in compose.yaml plus a profiles-only stub in compose.attach.yaml.
assumptions: ALLOW_DOMAINS, UPSTREAM_DNS, GITHUB_CIDR_BOOTSTRAP, and EGRESS_SELF_TEST* come from compose/.env; defaults cover OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, Telegram, npm, github.com/api.github.com, and common githubusercontent release asset hosts.
LLM_PROVIDER selects the default provider self-test URL; EGRESS_SELF_TEST_ALLOW_URLS can override the provider probe list.
Publishes HARNESS_HTTP_PORT on loopback via this service because http/bot/harness use network_mode: service:egress-gw.
Only this sidecar holds NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW; harness apps keep cap_drop ALL.

sideEffects.description: Configures iptables/ipset default-deny egress filtering for the shared harness netns
Fetches api.github.com/meta at startup when GitHub CIDR bootstrap is enabled
Runs dnsmasq and curl-based startup/healthcheck probes for allowed npm/provider egress and blocked example.com

risks: Misconfigured ALLOW_DOMAINS blocks provider APIs, Telegram long-poll, npm installs, or GitHub-hosted binary/release downloads.
Over-broad domain allowlist weakens fail-closed egress posture.
GitHub meta/bootstrap outage falls back to DNS allow-list only, which is less robust for runtime_check binary fetches.
Provider, npm, or upstream DNS outages make the gateway fail startup self-test or become unhealthy.
invariants: Only this sidecar holds NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW; every harness app keeps cap_drop ALL and reaches the network through this namespace.

Both halves of the topology attach here: the sandbox services and their attach-mode counterparts share this namespace, so the egress posture is identical whether the run targets a managed sandbox or a mounted host worktree.
annotation.integrationPoints: docker/egress-gw Dockerfile (curl, jq, dnsmasq, ipset, iptables); all harness-app services depend_on egress-gw healthy; .env.example documents allowlist/self-test knobs.

annotation.summary: Runtime resource for the harness image build (examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/Dockerfile), built by infra:dockerfile:examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/Dockerfile and used as the build target for every harness-app service in compose.yaml (cli/http/tg-bot/harness-base).
assumptions: Runs as the base image's unprivileged node user; no Docker access, no host docker.sock.
risks: Image CMD is scripts/langgraph-cli.mjs --help; the cli/http/tg-bot services in compose.yaml each override entrypoint to their own script.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/scripts/langgraph-cli (default entrypoint script this image runs)

annotation.summary: Runtime resource for the egress-gateway image (examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/docker/egress-gw/Dockerfile), built by infra:dockerfile:examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/docker/egress-gw/Dockerfile and run as the egress-gw service in compose.yaml; the harness container shares its network namespace so all harness traffic passes its dnsmasq/ipset/iptables allow-list.
assumptions: ALLOW_DOMAINS/EGRESS_ALLOW_TELEGRAM/UPSTREAM_DNS env bindings come from the egress-gw service block in compose.yaml, not from this Dockerfile.
risks: entrypoint.sh is the container ENTRYPOINT and owns the iptables/ipset/dnsmasq setup; it and proxy.mjs are plain scripts with no package.json, outside the npm/TS module graph.

annotation.summary: Base compose service in examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.yaml (profile 'harness-base', never requested — inert by design). Exists so cli-attach/http-attach/tg-bot-attach in compose.attach.yaml can `extends: {file: compose.yaml, service: harness-base}` to inherit build context, resource ceilings, read_only, cap_drop, tmpfs, and network_mode from the shared x-harness-app anchor without inheriting the sandbox workspace mount or workspace-init depends_on gate (this service's own volumes/depends_on are empty).
assumptions: Consumers extend this service rather than running it directly; its own profile is never selected.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/scripts/attach-host-adapter owns the preflight logic (mount-table enumeration, fs-type proof) that must pass before attach services built on this base are allowed to mount host paths.

annotation.summary: Compose service `http` (profile http) in examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.yaml: long-running `langgraph-http.mjs` REST handle exposing /task (alias /goal), /ask, /status, /reset. Shares the egress-gw network namespace, NODE_OPTIONS heap guardrail, and hardened x-harness-app settings. The external port is published on egress-gw (127.0.0.1:8080 by default), not on this service; PORT and HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN are set directly on top of the harness-env anchor. Bearer auth is enforced only when HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN is set.
assumptions: Profile http: docker compose --profile http up -d http (or npm run docker:http).
PORT and HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN set in this service's environment block, merged on top of the harness-env anchor.
Port published on egress-gw (127.0.0.1:8080 by default), not on the http service itself.
Depends on workspace-init completing and egress-gw being healthy before start.

sideEffects.description: HTTP server on PORT with JSON /task (or /goal) invokeGraph, /ask runAsk, and /reset endpoints; GET /status for health
Provider-backed Delivery Protocol graph and ask runs via shared harness-app env

risks: Unset HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN exposes /task, /goal, /ask and /reset on the published egress port.
Depends on egress-gw healthy — http cannot start without the sidecar passing health probes.
Long multi-agent runs can hit HARNESS_MEM_LIMIT despite NODE_OPTIONS.
patterns: HTTP channel shares the harness-app image and env with cli/tg-bot services.
invariants: Single-flight locks return 409 for concurrent /task or /ask on the shared sandbox.
Bearer auth enforced when HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN is set.

This service is the sandbox half of the pair: resource:generic:http-attach serves the same endpoints against a mounted host worktree, and only this one waits on workspace-init and mounts the managed .workspace.
annotation.integrationPoints: scripts/langgraph-http.mjs; mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/channels/http-adapter startHttp; examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.yaml profile http.
annotation.dataFlow: Client HTTP → egress-gw published port → http container langgraph-http.mjs → startHttp → invokeGraph/runAsk.

annotation.summary: Compose service `http-attach` (profile attach-http) in examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.attach.yaml: the attach-mode counterpart of `http`. Serves the long-running REST handle against a pre-created host Git worktree mounted at /workspace instead of the managed sandbox, running as the worktree owner.
assumptions: scripts/attach-launcher.mjs is the supported entrypoint: it runs the fail-closed preflight and creates the state layout before any docker call.
Local volumes, depends_on and environment keys replace the anchor's values wholesale, which is how attach avoids mounting .workspace and avoids waiting on workspace-init.
The published port still belongs to egress-gw, since the service shares that network namespace.

sideEffects.description: writes into the operator's mounted worktree as the operator's uid/gid
serves the REST endpoints on the shared egress-gw published port

risks: A direct compose invocation with hand-set environment bypasses the launcher preflight — a deliberate operator override, unsupported and not prevented here.

The bearer token guard is the same one the sandbox http service uses, so leaving it unset exposes the endpoints on the published port against the operator's real worktree rather than a disposable sandbox.
annotation.integrationPoints: Launched through scripts/attach-launcher.mjs; serves mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/channels/http-adapter with attach policy from mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/target-repo.

annotation.summary: Compose service `tg-bot` (profile tg-bot) in examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.yaml: long-running `langgraph-tg-bot.mjs` Telegram channel (outbound long-poll, no published HTTP port). Shares the egress-gw network namespace, NODE_OPTIONS heap guardrail, and hardened x-harness-app settings. Requires TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS via harness-env; an empty allow-list fails closed at startup. Depends on egress-gw healthy before start.
assumptions: Profile tg-bot: docker compose --profile tg-bot up -d tg-bot (or npm run docker:tg-bot).
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_IDS required via the harness-env anchor.
No published HTTP port — outbound Telegram long-poll only.
Depends on workspace-init completing and egress-gw being healthy before start.
Liveness is a heartbeat file (/tmp/harness-tg-bot.alive) the poll loop touches each iteration; a wedged loop fails the healthcheck and the restart policy recycles it.

sideEffects.description: Telegram Bot API long-poll and message sends
Provider-backed Delivery Protocol graph and ask runs via shared harness-app env

risks: Unset provider credentials block task runs but the bot can still start.
Provider/npm/DNS outage or a narrow ALLOW_DOMAINS makes egress-gw unhealthy and blocks startup.
Long multi-agent runs can hit HARNESS_MEM_LIMIT despite NODE_OPTIONS.
patterns: Long-running bot service sharing the harness-app image with cli/http.
invariants: This service is the sandbox half of the pair: resource:generic:tg-bot-attach polls the same way against a mounted host worktree, and only this one waits on workspace-init and mounts the managed .workspace.
annotation.integrationPoints: scripts/langgraph-tg-bot.mjs; mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/channels/telegram-adapter startTelegram; examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.yaml profile tg-bot.
annotation.dataFlow: Telegram long-poll → tg-bot container langgraph-tg-bot.mjs → startTelegram → invokeGraph/runAsk → replies via Bot API.

annotation.summary: Compose service `tg-bot-attach` (profile attach-tg-bot) in examples/delivery-protocol-harness-demo/compose.attach.yaml: the attach-mode counterpart of `tg-bot`. Polls the messaging API and runs the graph against a pre-created host Git worktree mounted at /workspace instead of the managed sandbox, as the worktree owner.
assumptions: scripts/attach-launcher.mjs is the supported entrypoint: it runs the fail-closed preflight and creates the state layout before any docker call.
Local volumes, depends_on and environment keys replace the anchor's values wholesale, which is how attach avoids mounting .workspace and avoids waiting on workspace-init.
The identity allowlist is the same fail-closed one the sandbox bot uses: empty means the bot refuses to start.

sideEffects.description: writes into the operator's mounted worktree as the operator's uid/gid
polls the messaging API and sends replies through the shared egress-gw namespace

risks: A direct compose invocation with hand-set environment bypasses the launcher preflight — a deliberate operator override, unsupported and not prevented here.
A publicly messageable bot now drives edits in the operator's real worktree rather than a disposable sandbox, so a wrong identity in the allowlist costs more here than in sandbox mode.
annotation.integrationPoints: Launched through scripts/attach-launcher.mjs; serves mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/channels/telegram-adapter with attach policy from mod:repovine-delivery-protocol-harness-demo/lib/target-repo.

annotation.summary: One-shot Alpine init container in agent-harness-demo compose: chowns bind-mounted HARNESS_WORKSPACE_DIR to uid 1000 before cli/http/tg-bot start, fixing Docker auto-created root-owned host paths. Verified against current compose.yaml: unchanged (profiles cli/http/tg-bot, cap_add CHOWN, entrypoint docker/init-workspace.sh).
assumptions: Profiles cli, http, tg-bot only — not started for egress-gw alone.
Runs as root (user 0:0) with CAP_CHOWN to fix ownership on bind mount.
Entrypoint is docker/init-workspace.sh mounted read-only from demo tree.

sideEffects.description: chown on /workspace bind mount before harness services start

risks: Missing or wrong HARNESS_WORKSPACE_DIR leaves node user unable to write sandbox.
Init failure blocks all profile services via depends_on service_completed_successfully.
patterns: Pre-flight ownership fix for unprivileged harness-app containers (uid 1000 node).
invariants: Must complete successfully before cli/http/tg-bot start.
restart: no — single-shot init, not a long-running service.
annotation.integrationPoints: compose.yaml x-harness-app depends_on; HARNESS_WORKSPACE_DIR env; docker/init-workspace.sh.
annotation.dataFlow: compose up profile → workspace-init chowns mount → exits 0 → egress-gw healthy → harness app services start.
